Once per enemy Field wait up A companion further than Wait Up Distance behind a moving leader Aid given A heal or buff cast says this instead of the art's name Aid Given Chance of the time Aid received One ally a heal or buff reached thanks the caster, once the cast's line has finished Enemy reinforcement Another enemy joins a fight already Reinforcement After Seconds old Reaction The leader calls a Break, Topple or Daze landing on an enemy (off in the shipped rules)

docs.title: Pacing: the rules table
docs.text:
Seven voices could easily talk over each other; XC3 was criticised for exactly that. Every voice therefore follows these rules, all set in DT_XenoCore_VoiceRules:

  • One line at a time. A request at or below the priority of the line playing is dropped, not queued; a higher one cuts in. Rows with Overlaps (grunts, hurt) are the exception.
  • A gap (Gap Seconds on the config, 0.8 s) follows every line. It holds back lines of equal or lower priority than the one that ended; a more urgent line (Downed, a revive) goes straight through.
  • Chance applies to the player-controlled character; AI Chance to companions. With Scale With Party Size on, the AI chance is multiplied by Reference Party Size / active members, so a party of seven says less per head than a party of three.
  • Speaker Cooldown stops one character repeating a category; Category Cooldown stops anyone.
  • A rule covers its children. The XenoCore.Voice.Field row paces every field category, so a new category inherits sensible pacing until it gets its own row. A category with no rule anywhere is never said, and the log names it.
Shipped priority Category 100 Downed 90 Revive 80 Victory 70 Talent ready 60 Art 55 Battle start, take control 45 Reactions (off) 40 Low HP 35 Party Gauge 30 Critical 25 Enemy status 20 Aid 15 Miss, evade 10 Level up 5 Field banter

docs.title: Adding a category of your own
docs.text:
A boss taunt or a quest beat needs no C++:

  1. Add the tag under XenoCore.Voice, e.g. XenoCore.Voice.Boss.PhaseTwo: open Project Settings › Project › GameplayTags, click Add New Gameplay Tag, and save it to a tag file of your own project rather than XenoCore's (a template update replaces XenoCore's).
  2. Optionally add a rules row. Without one it uses XenoCore.Voice's.
  3. Add rows with that category to the characters who should say it.
  4. Call Speak from the Blueprint where it happens: the boss's phase change, a trigger volume, a quest step.

Speak (Xeno Core Battle Voice Subsystem) takes a Speaker, a Category and, optionally, an Art and an Addressee. It returns whether a line started. Call it as often as you like; the rules decide.

docs.title: Recording lines
docs.text:
The shipped lines were generated with a text-to-speech service, then trimmed, levelled and given lip-sync keys. To add your own recording:

  1. Level it like the shipped takes: about -16 dB average loudness, peaks under -1 dBFS.
  2. Drag the WAV into the Content Browser, next to the character's voice table. Import it as mono: a stereo file cannot pan with the speaker.
  3. Open the new sound wave and set its Sound Class to SC_XenoCore_Dialogue, so it follows the player's Dialogue volume.
  4. In the character's voice table, add it to a row's Takes.

A hand-imported take has no lip-sync keys, so the mouth uses the generic flap described in The face.

Test it

Start the gym, then type XenoCore.Voice.Speak Kael <Category> in the console with your row's category. Log LogXenoVoice Verbose explains a line that did not play.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: XenoCore.Voice.Message.Spoke is sent the moment a line starts. Payload XenoCoreVoiceSpokeMessage: Speaker, Category, Take (with its lip-sync keys), Expression, Expression Weight, Subtitle, Duration. Use it for subtitles or a speaking indicator. See Events you can listen to.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text: Command Does XenoCore.Voice.Describe Prints the config, every rule and each active member's table XenoCore.Voice.Speak <Member> <Category> [Art] Asks a member for a line, exactly as gameplay does. The category may omit XenoCore.Voice.; e.g. XenoCore.Voice.Speak Kael Art DA_XenoCore_BackSlash Log LogXenoVoice Verbose Logs why each request was or was not said (cooldown, chance, gap, priority, no row)

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: • Victory replies (an ally answering the victory line) have a category but no lines.

docs.title: Characters
docs.text:
All · 15 min read · No code

Every character that fights carries its own ability system on its pawn: its own attributes, its own arts, its own active effects. Party members and the player's pawn share one C++ base, AXenoCoreCombatantCharacter, whose only job is to wire that ability system up without a player state. Enemies do the same wiring on a separate class, and NPCs deliberately have none of it. The one idea: a character's identity is its Blueprint (mesh, pawn data, statline, starting level), and anything that must outlive the body, such as its level, is stored elsewhere and read back when the body spawns.

At a glance

In play: every fighter has its own body, stats, level and Arts; a party member at 0 HP kneels (downed) instead of dying.

What you can change, no code:

  • A character's starting level, name and portrait: Your first change
  • Their stats at each level: Give a character its own statline
  • Body shape and movement style: Choose an animation style
  • A whole new member: Add a VRoid party member
  • Every setting on this page: What you can change

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
The class tree, from C++ to the Blueprints you open:

  • ALyraCharacterWithAbilities (Lyra: a character that owns its ability system)
    • AXenoCoreCombatantCharacter: party-playable pawns
      • Game/B_XenoCore_PlayableCharacter_Base (Blueprint)
        • Game/B_XenoCore_Player: the bootstrap pawn, used only when the party has no starting roster. Not in the shipped roster
      • AXenoCorePartyCharacter: adds equipment, AI perception and footstep components in C++
        • Characters/Party/B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base (Blueprint)
          • Characters/VRoid/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_Base: the base for VRoid members
            • Characters/VRoid/<Name>/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_*: the sample party, seven members (Kael, Mira, Nia, Dorran, Isolde, Sabine, Tamsin), one folder each
          • B_XenoCore_Party_Quinn, B_XenoCore_Party_Manny and the other colour variants: Mannequin-bodied examples kept on disk, not in the shipped roster
    • AXenoCoreEnemyCharacter: enemies (see Enemies and AI)
  • ACharacter
    • AXenoCoreNpcCharacter: townspeople, Characters/NPC/B_XenoCore_Npc

Two names for the same idea on enemies

Enemies are not on the combatant base, so their settings have their own names: Enemy Pawn Data and Enemy Level instead of Combatant Pawn Data and Combatant Level. They mean the same thing.

Who is in the party

The sample cast is the seven VRoid members. A new game starts with two, Kael and Mira; the other five (Tamsin, Dorran, Sabine, Nia and Isolde) are recruited from NPCs on Gaur Plain, and every member who joins fights (Max Active Members is 7). The colour variants (PartyMember_Quinn, PartyMember_Blue and the rest) stay on disk as working examples of a Mannequin-bodied member; they are not in the cast. See Set the starting party and Recruit a party member from an NPC.

Each sample member has its own statline and its own experience curve: a stats effect per character (Battle/Attributes/GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_<Name>, reading the <Name>.* rows of Battle/Attributes/CT_XenoCore_PartyStatlines), and a row in Game/DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves picked by the member definition's Experience Curve. See Give a character its own statline and Tune levelling.

Pawn data (ULyraPawnData) is the list of ability sets and input config a character gets. Each party Blueprint points at one, for example Characters/Party/PawnData_XenoCore_Party_Quinn (the seven sample VRoid members share Characters/VRoid/PawnData_XenoCore_Party_VRoid), which grants AbilitySet_XenoCore_PartyMember and uses the tag relationships in Game/TagRelationships_XenoCore. The player's pawn uses Game/PawnData_XenoCore_Player, which grants AbilitySet_XenoCore_Hero.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Spawn. When the party spawns a body, the body sets itself up as it spawns, in this order:

  1. Sets its Combatant Pawn Data on the pawn extension component.
  2. Initialises its ability system. Only now can it take damage and die.
  3. Grants every ability set in the pawn data.
  4. Applies its Stats Effect at its level. A party member's level comes from the progression component; anything without a roster entry uses Combatant Level.
  5. Grants the art palette stored for this character (see Arts).

The player's bootstrap pawn, spawned by Lyra's game mode before the party exists, does the same steps through its hero component instead, because Self Initialise Ability System is off on B_XenoCore_Player.

Statline. A statline is a Gameplay Effect whose modifiers read curve tables at the effect's level. Applying it again at a new level is what a level-up is. See Stats and damage.

Possession. Every party body is born under AI control. When the player takes one over, its hero component binds input and the camera. When the player hands a body back to the AI and later takes it again, input is re-bound explicitly, because Lyra only binds on the first possession.

A body with AI Steering on moves more softly while the AI drives it: a lower turn rate, a slower start and a longer stop, so a companion has weight instead of snapping and spinning like a player-driven body. When the player takes it over, the Blueprint's own movement values (the Character Movement component's Rotation Rate, Max Acceleration and Braking Deceleration Walking) are put back from the class defaults, so the player's feel is never changed by it.

Down, not dead. Health reaching zero on a party member does not kill it. The party's ability sets grant Battle/GA_XenoCore_Downed in place of Lyra's GA_Hero_Death: the member kneels (Characters/Core/Animations/Downed/AS_XenoCore_DownedKneel_*), cannot act, and waits for a revive or the end of the battle. See Party Gauge, downed and revive.

Who What happens at 0 HP Party member (sample party and colour variants) Goes downed: kneels in place with its weapon, greys out on the HUD, gets up on a revive. When every active member is down the party is wiped. A party pawn (AXenoCorePartyCharacter) whose ability sets grant GA_Hero_Death instead The death performance: one of Death Montages at random, a wait between Ragdoll Delay Min and Ragdoll Delay Max, a ragdoll with an impulse on Ragdoll Impulse Bone, and its weapons hidden. Enemy Its own sequence, then EXP, a chest and a vanish. See Enemies and AI.

Keep Body On Death keeps the body, and its ability system, after a real death so it can be brought back with Revive. It is on for the party bases and B_XenoCore_Player, and off (Lyra's behaviour) for anything else.

Fails silently: a pawn with no pawn data cannot die

Death and damage come from abilities that the pawn data grants. A character Blueprint with Combatant Pawn Data empty spawns with no abilities, no stats, and cannot be killed. An error naming the pawn is logged, and UXenoCorePartyMemberDefinition also flags it in the Content Browser when you validate the member asset.

Fails silently: no Stats Effect

With Stats Effect empty the character runs on attribute defaults (mostly zero) and an error is logged on every spawn. It still moves and animates, so it looks fine until it fights.

A destroyed body takes its ability system with it

The ability system lives on the body. When the body is destroyed, its attributes, arts and active effects go with it. Level, EXP and the art palette survive because they are stored on the progression component and re-applied to the next body. Anything else you keep only on a character's ability system (a buff, a custom attribute) is lost on death unless Keep Body On Death is on. A downed member keeps its body, so nothing is lost while it waits for a revive.

docs.title: Appearance: cosmetic parts and body meshes
docs.text:
XenoCore uses Lyra's cosmetic system. Each playable Blueprint has a Cosmetic Part variable. On begin play, if it is set, the Blueprint adds that part through Lyra's character-parts component.

  • Characters/Core/Cosmetics/B_XenoCore_Cosmetic_Masculine and _Feminine are parts with no mesh. They exist only to carry a tag, Cosmetic.AnimationStyle.Masculine or .Feminine.
  • The character-parts component's Body Meshes rules read that tag and set the body mesh: masculine to SKM_Manny, feminine to SKM_Quinn.
  • The same tag picks the animation layer when the weapon is drawn or stowed, so a feminine character uses Lyra's feminine clips. See Animation.

So the colour variants differ only by material, and body shape plus movement style come from one tag.

VRoid members use the same pattern the other way round: Body Meshes point at the invisible SKM_Manny_Invis / SKM_Quinn_Invis, and a VRoid cosmetic part (B_XenoCore_Cosmetic_VRoid_*) carries the visible mesh, retargeted from the invisible Mannequin. Gameplay, montages and sockets all stay on the Mannequin skeleton. See Add a VRoid party member.

No invisible pawns. Lyra's character-parts component sets the body mesh from Body Meshes every time a part is added or removed, and when no rule matches the parts' tags it uses Body Meshes › Default Mesh. With no default, the body is set to nothing and the character turns invisible. XenoCore closes this three ways:

  • Every shipped pawn has a Default Mesh: SKM_Manny on B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base and B_XenoCore_PlayableCharacter_Base, the invisible Mannequin on the VRoid pawns.
  • At Begin Play, before the Blueprint adds its part, a combatant character with no Default Mesh uses the mesh it spawned with for this session, and logs a LogXenoCosmetics warning once per class.
  • Saving a pawn Blueprint runs an editor check: a missing Default Mesh or a rule with no mesh is a warning; a Cosmetic Part whose tags match no rule is a warning, or an error on a pawn that is not a XenoCore combatant and so has no runtime guard.

An unmatched style tag gives the default body

A part whose tags match no Body Meshes rule no longer hides the pawn, but it silently gives it the Default Mesh instead of the body you meant. Give every style tag a rule, and leave Cosmetic Part empty rather than pointing it at a class with no tag.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text: Setting Where it lives What it does Combatant Pawn Data Character Blueprint › XenoCore › Combatant Ability sets and input config. Required. Combatant Level Character Blueprint (also per placed instance) › XenoCore › Combatant Starting level. For a party member it only seeds the saved level the first time. Stats Effect Character Blueprint › XenoCore › Combatant The statline effect applied at the character's level. Self Initialise Ability System Character Blueprint › XenoCore › Combatant Off only on the bootstrap player pawn. The party component forces it on for bodies it spawns. Keep Body On Death Character Blueprint › XenoCore › Combatant Keep the body (and its ability system) after a real death so it can be revived. On for the party. Art Learn Table Character Blueprint › XenoCore › Arts The character's learnset: a Data Table of XenoCoreArtUnlock saying which arts they learn, at what level, in which starting slot. Empty means keep whatever the ability sets grant. See Arts. Skill Tree Character Blueprint › XenoCore › Skills The character's skill branches: a Data Table of XenoCoreSkillBranchRow. Empty means no skills. See Skills and Add a skill or a skill tree. Death Montages, Ragdoll Delay Min/Max, Ragdoll Impulse Bone, Ragdoll Impulse Strength Party Blueprint › XenoCore › Death The death performance, for a member that really dies rather than going downed. Cosmetic Part Character Blueprint variables The tag-carrying part that decides body mesh and animation style. AI Steering Character Blueprint › XenoCore › Movement Softer turning, acceleration and braking while an AI drives the body. Enabled is on for party bodies and B_XenoCore_Player, off otherwise; defaults 420°/s, 1500 and 1100. See Companion AI. Body Meshes Character Blueprint › character-parts component Which mesh each cosmetic tag selects, and the Default Mesh used when none matches. Starting equipment Character Blueprint › equipment component The gear a character is first dressed in. See Equipment.

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
• A new party member: make a child Blueprint of Characters/VRoid/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_Base (a VRoid body, like the sample party) or of Characters/Party/B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base (a Mannequin body), in Content/MyGame/. Give it its own pawn data and stats effect, then make a member definition for it. See Add a VRoid party member and Add a party member.
  • A new statline: duplicate a party stats effect and change its curve rows. See Give a character its own statline.
  • A townsperson: place B_XenoCore_Npc, or make a child Blueprint of it for a reusable type. It has no ability system and cannot fight.
  • To add a component to every party member, open B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base, click Add in the Components panel, then Compile and Save: every child gets it.
For programmers: components on the party base

Never add components to B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base from an editor script: a scripted component crashed play twice on a null owner. Add them in the editor or in a C++ subclass. The equipment component is created in C++ on AXenoCorePartyCharacter for this reason.

The player's pawn is on a different branch

B_XenoCore_Player derives from B_XenoCore_PlayableCharacter_Base, not from the party base, and has its own editor-added equipment component. Changes you make to B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base do not reach it. Its death graph was removed when the party moved to downed. Its arts also come from AbilitySet_XenoCore_Hero; it has no Art Learn Table.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers: the design reasons

Lyra's hero component only knows how to find an ability system on a player state. A party of characters that each keep their own stats would need a player state each. Instead XenoCore uses Lyra's ALyraCharacterWithAbilities, the same shape as Epic's damageable test dummy, and performs the one initialisation call Blueprint cannot make (InitializeAbilitySystem) in C++. The base does nothing else: no drop table, no ragdoll, no follow logic, so a subclass never inherits behaviour it did not ask for.

The statline is applied from C++ rather than granted by an ability set because an ability set applies its effects at one fixed level for every character that uses it.

docs.title: The combat loop
docs.text:
All · 20 min read · No code

Break lands on the target; the Arts palette sits at the bottom, the party plates on the left.

A fight is a chain of gameplay abilities talking through gameplay tags and events. Nothing is a central "battle manager". Target mode starts the fight on the player's side, drawing the weapon puts the party in battle, the auto-attack swings on its own while the target is in reach, and each landed hit sends the victim an event it reacts to. The one idea: Status.XenoCore.InBattle on the leader means "the party is fighting", and the party AI, the HUD, the animation layers and the Party screen all read that one tag.

At a glance

In play: lock on, the party draws and auto-attacks; hits flinch and push the target; misses dodge, blocks guard; when the last enemy falls the party sheathes and celebrates.

What you can change, no code:

  • Swing reach, speed and clips: Tune auto-attack
  • Shake, rumble, numbers and the critical line: Add hit feedback
  • Knockback, flinch, guard and dodge clips: What you can change and Give a character its own combat animations
  • Block and hit chances: Stats and damage

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Stage Ability or asset Tag it holds Lock on Battle/Targeting/GA_XenoCore_TargetMode Status.XenoCore.TargetMode Draw / sheathe Battle/GA_XenoCore_Arm_v2 Status.XenoCore.Arming while playing; toggles Status.XenoCore.InBattle Auto-attack Battle/GA_XenoCore_AutoAttack (UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_AutoAttack) Ability tag Ability.XenoCore.AutoAttack Damage Battle/Attributes/GE_XenoCore_Damage Fires the cue GameplayCue.XenoCore.DamageTaken Talent charge Battle/Attributes/GE_XenoCore_TalentCharge Fills Talent Gauge Flinch Battle/GA_XenoCore_Player_HitReact (UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_HitReact) Triggered by XenoCore.Event.HitReact Guard (you blocked) Battle/Defence/GA_XenoCore_Guard (UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_GuardReact) Triggered by XenoCore.Event.Combat.Block; holds Status.XenoCore.Defence.Guard Recoil (you were blocked) Battle/Defence/GA_XenoCore_Recoil (UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_RecoilReact) Triggered by XenoCore.Event.Combat.Blocked; holds Status.XenoCore.Defence.Recoil Dodge (you evaded) Battle/Defence/GA_XenoCore_Evade (UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_EvadeReact) Triggered by XenoCore.Event.Combat.Evade; holds Status.XenoCore.Defence.Evade Swing and hit feel GameplayCues/GCN_XenoCore_Swing, GCN_XenoCore_Hit GameplayCue.XenoCore.Swing, .Hit Battle text UXenoCoreBattleNotifySubsystem + UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_BattleNotify Message XenoCore.Battle.Message.Notification Numbers Lyra's number pop + UXenoCoreDamageNumberSubsystem See below

The player's and party members' abilities come from Game/AbilitySet_XenoCore_Hero and Characters/Party/AbilitySet_XenoCore_PartyMember, plus the shared Game/AbilitySet_XenoCore_Input for every button-driven ability. Arts are a separate system layered on this loop: see Arts and Reactions and statuses.

docs.title: 1. Engagement
docs.text:
• The player presses Target Next (R bumper). That sends XenoCore.Event.SwitchTarget, which starts target mode on the nearest enemy near the centre of the screen and brings up the battle HUD: target badge, player plate and arts palette. See Targeting.
  • An enemy wanders or patrols near home until it is attacked or it notices the party by its Detection (sight, sound of running, or a nearby ether art; a passive enemy only reacts to being hit). If it belongs to a spawner's squad, the rest of the squad joins in. It then chases whichever party member holds the most aggro on it, which may be a companion. An enemy Ignore When Levels Below (6) or more levels below the leader never notices the party, but still fights back when hit. Outrun it and it gives up, heals and walks home. See Targeting and Enemies and AI.
  • Companions join in when the leader carries Status.XenoCore.InBattle, or when an enemy near the party is already fighting one of them. Each draws its weapon where it stands, a short random moment after the fight starts, and only then closes in. What they attack follows the party tactics (by default the leader's target). See Companion AI.

Locking on is not the same as fighting. Status.XenoCore.TargetMode means a target is selected; Status.XenoCore.InBattle means the weapon is drawn.

docs.title: 2. Drawing the weapon
docs.text:
Choosing Attack (or an art) on the palette draws the weapon first. GA_XenoCore_Arm_v2 plays the draw montage and flips Status.XenoCore.InBattle on its way. The weapon actor moves from back to hand on the frame marked by the AN_XenoCore_WeaponHandoff notify in the montage.

  • While the draw plays, the ability holds Status.XenoCore.Arming. The flinch ability refuses to run under that tag, so a hit during the draw still does damage but cannot interrupt it.
  • The draw stops movement (Gameplay.MovementStopped); the sheathe does not.
  • The same ability toggles, so it is only ever asked to run when the tag says the state is wrong.

The one-time camera ease towards the target happens here, when the fight starts.

docs.title: 3. The auto-attack loop
docs.text:
The auto-attack is one long-running ability, not one ability per swing:

  1. It waits until the weapon is drawn (Requires Arming).
  2. If the target is within Attack Range, it plays the next montage from Attack Montages (or Attack Montages Stationary when standing still), at Montage Play Rate, and plays the swing cue.
  3. The montage's UXenoCoreAnimNotify_GameplayEvent fires XenoCore.Event.MeleeHit on the contact frame. Only then is the hit resolved: reach is re-tested (with Contact Reach Tolerance), the hit roll is made, and on a hit the damage effect, the talent charge and any Additional Effects are applied.
  4. The next swing is scheduled from the montage's length plus Swing Recovery.
  5. If the target is out of range it pauses and re-checks every Out Of Range Retry seconds. It does not end.

Moving does not stop the loop. A full-body swing is handed back to the legs if you start moving (Cancel Full Body On Move).

Fails silently: a swing that never hurts

Damage happens only on the montage's gameplay-event notify. An attack montage with no XenoCore.Event.MeleeHit notify plays its animation and deals no damage, with nothing logged. Every montage in Attack Montages needs that notify on its contact frame.

Fails silently: an enemy that never swings

Requires Arming must be off for anything that has no draw ability. Enemies are not granted GA_XenoCore_Arm_v2, so with it on they wait for a draw that never comes.

docs.title: 4. A landed hit
docs.text:
When a swing connects, in this order:

  1. Contact roll. The swing misses, is blocked, or hits. A miss shows MISS over the target, makes it dodge, and stops here. Out-of-reach at contact is also shown as a miss. A block shows BLOCKED and carries on with the changes described in Blocks and dodges.
  2. Damage, through the damage execution. See Stats and damage.
  3. Talent charge: the attacker's Talent Charge Per Hit is added to its own Talent Gauge.
  4. Riders: the ability's Additional Effects, such as a reaction or a debuff. Each effect's own application requirements decide whether it takes (which is how Break → Topple → Daze is ordered).
  5. Hit feel: GameplayCue.XenoCore.Hit (camera shake and controller rumble).
  6. Flinch and knockback: XenoCore.Event.HitReact is sent to the victim, which plays a directional additive flinch on the AdditiveHitReact slot and is knocked back, straight away from the attacker, by its hit-react ability's Push Distance x the attack's Force Multiplier. The flinch layers over whatever the victim is doing, so as in XC1 an ordinary hit never cuts off an attack or an art: only a reaction such as Topple or Daze does. The victim does not react while drawing, using an art, Toppled or Dazed, and then it is not pushed either. A blocked hit sends no flinch: the victim guards instead, and is not pushed. This works both ways: an enemy's hits knock the player back. Untick Flinch On Hit on a hit-react ability to drop the flinch animation; the knockback still applies. Set Push Distance to 0 to drop the knockback. ⚠️ A flinch montage must be additive and on the AdditiveHitReact slot, and that slot must be registered on the character's skeleton in its own slot group (AdditiveGroup). A normal montage, or an unregistered slot, puts the flinch in the attack's slot group and it cuts the swing off again. See Add a new enemy for a new skeleton.

Arts aimed at enemies make the same contact roll for every hit and every target, and every hit flinches and knocks back the same way, using the Art's own Force Multiplier. See Arts.

docs.title: Blocks and dodges
docs.text:
Blocking and dodging are rolls, not buttons. When a hit is blocked or misses, both bodies react on their own:

Outcome The defender The attacker Blocked Plays its guard (GA_XenoCore_Guard), and takes no damage by default Recoils (GA_XenoCore_Recoil) for about 0.65 s Missed Ducks or sidesteps, picked at random each time (GA_XenoCore_Evade) Nothing more: the swing simply whiffs

While a guard, recoil or dodge plays, the character:

  • cannot move (Gameplay.MovementStopped);
  • does not auto-attack: Status.XenoCore.Defence is in the auto-attack's Incapacitated Tags, so the loop pauses and a swing already in flight does not connect;
  • cannot use an Art: TagRelationships_XenoCore blocks Ability.XenoCore.Art on Status.XenoCore.Defence.

A block also changes the hit itself:

  • No Topple. A blocked hit skips any rider that would Topple. Break still lands.
  • A blocked Art ends. The recoil cancels the attacker's Art, so the rest of a multi-hit Art never lands.

A party member's duck and sidestep play on the Defence slot of ABP_XenoCore_Base. While the weapon is drawn, the body and legs come from the clip but the arms stay in the weapon stance, so the hands never leave the sword's grip. With the weapon sheathed, the clip's own arms play. Both clips move the character with root motion: the duck steps back and the sidestep moves to the side, even straight after a swing made on the move.

The minion has its own copies (Characters/Enemies/Minion/GA_XenoCore_Minion_Guard, _Recoil, _Evade), because it is on its own skeleton (SK_Minion_Core) and its clips are retargeted from the player's. The minion's dodge is still the directional one: it moves away from the attacker.

docs.title: 5. Hit feedback: which side plays it
docs.text:
Camera shake and rumble need a local player controller. So the attacking ability plays GCN_XenoCore_Hit on whichever side has one: on the attacker when you hit an enemy, and on you when an enemy hits you.

Fails silently: shake and rumble from a damage effect

A cue triggered by a Gameplay Effect has no player controller to find, so camera shake and force feedback on a GE-driven cue never play (sparks and sounds still do). Put anything that shakes the camera or rumbles the pad on a cue your ability executes itself, the way the auto-attack does.

No rumble on keyboard

Lyra only plays force feedback when the current input device is a gamepad and the player's setting allows it. To test with a keyboard, use the console command LyraPC.ShouldAlwaysPlayForceFeedback 1.

docs.title: 6. Numbers and battle text
docs.text:
What Who draws it Damage the party deals (yours and every ally's) XenoCore's damage cue GameplayCues/GCNL_XenoCore_DamageTaken (a copy of Lyra's), through B_XenoCore_NumberPopComponent, DamagePopStyle_XenoCore and NS_XenoCore_DamageNumbers. A critical hit draws gold. Damage you take UXenoCoreDamageNumberSubsystem, drawing NS_XenoCore_DamageNumbers_Taken Heals UXenoCoreDamageNumberSubsystem Show Heal Number, drawing NS_XenoCore_HealNumbers MISS, CRITICAL HIT!, BLOCKED, BREAK, TOPPLE, DAZE, status names UXenoCoreBattleNotifySubsystem, drawing W_XenoCore_BattleNotify

Anything can raise a battle line with the Notify node (target, text, colour, scale, punch). Punch above 1 makes the line arrive that many times larger and snap down to its size, the way CRITICAL HIT! does. The critical line's text, size, punch and an optional hit-stop are under Project Settings › Game › XenoCore Content › Critical Hit; see Tune hit feedback.

Fails silently: a damage effect that fires Lyra's cue

The dealt-damage number, the hit-confirm sound and the kill sound come from XenoCore's own copy of Lyra's damage cue, GCNL_XenoCore_DamageTaken, which knows that XenoCore's attackers are pawns and that allies' hits count. Lyra's own GCNL_Character_DamageTaken is left untouched, and it does not work with XenoCore's characters: a damage effect of your own that fires GameplayCue.Character.DamageTaken shows sparks but no number and no hit sound. Duplicate GE_XenoCore_Damage for new damage effects, so they keep GameplayCue.XenoCore.DamageTaken. See Hit numbers or hit sounds are missing.

Fails silently: a hit with no location

The damage cue places its number and sparks at the effect's hit result, with no fallback. The auto-attack builds a hit result at the target's surface. If you apply GE_XenoCore_Damage yourself without one, the number appears at the world origin, where nobody sees it.

docs.title: 7. Disengaging and death
docs.text:
Target mode ends when you press Target Mode Exit, or when the lock becomes invalid (out of range, out of sight, or the wrong team). Ending it sheathes the weapon and cancels the auto-attack.

When the locked target dies, the fight is not over if other enemies are still fighting the party: the lock moves to the next one (one on screen first, then the one with most aggro on the leader, then the nearest), and the weapon stays drawn. Only when no enemy is still fighting does target mode end.

Winning. The battle is won when an enemy dies and no living enemy is still fighting the party. UXenoCoreBattleVictorySubsystem decides this, in one place, and a retreat never counts. It then:

  1. Broadcasts XenoCore.Battle.Message.Won and plays Victory Fanfare (Project Settings › Game › XenoCore Content › Battle; cleared means no fanfare).
  2. Ends target mode and the auto-attack, and has every living member sheathe its weapon.
  3. As each member finishes sheathing, plays its own victory emote, from Victory Montages on its anim profile. A character with none does not celebrate. Moving, jumping or a new fight stops the emote.

A downed member does not celebrate; it sheathes once the battle-over revive stands it up. The console command XenoCore.Battle.Victory runs the whole sequence without a fight.

Recovering. Once no enemy has been engaged for Battle Over Grace (1 s) and the party is not in battle, every member recovers Out Of Battle Regen Per Second (0.1, a tenth of max HP a second) after Out Of Battle Regen Delay (1 s), benched members included. Both are on BP_XenoCore_Party › XenoCore › Party › Recovery; 0 turns recovery off. A party fleeing with enemies on its heels recovers nothing. Heal Arts work only in battle, so this is how the party gets back to full between fights.

When an enemy dies it awards EXP to the party, broadcasts XenoCore.Enemy.Message.Defeated and drops a chest after Chest Drop Delay. A party member at 0 HP is downed: they kneel until the leader revives them for a bar of the Party Gauge, or until the battle ends and they get up at 1 HP. When the whole active party is down, the party is wiped: "Defeated" shows, the screen fades, the party returns to the last save point visited (or the map's player start) at full health, and every enemy stands down. See Party Gauge, downed and revive, Characters, Party, Loot and Progression.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
Setting Where it lives What it does Attack Range GA_XenoCore_AutoAttack › XenoCore › AutoAttack Reach at swing start (420). Contact Reach Tolerance same › XenoCore › Attack Extra reach allowed at the contact frame (60). Attack Montages, Attack Montages Stationary same › XenoCore › AutoAttack The swing clips, cycled in order. Montage Play Rate, Swing Recovery same Swing speed and the gap between swings. Damage Effect, Additional Effects same What a landed hit applies. Talent Charge Effect same › XenoCore › Talent Effect that adds to the attacker's gauge. Target Source same Target Lock (the player's selection) or Nearest Hostile (enemies). Requires Arming same Wait for the weapon draw before the first swing. Face Target On Attack, Face Target Turn Rate same Turn to face the target while swinging (off for the player). Force Multiplier same › XenoCore › Attack How hard each landed swing knocks its target back, as a multiple of the target's Push Distance (1). 0 = no knockback. Lunge Multiplier, Lunge same › XenoCore › Attack Lyra's melee lunge: each landed swing also drives the attacker into its target. Lunge Multiplier 0 (off) by default; Lunge holds Lyra's values (2200 cm/s for 0.05 s, scaled by the gap). Push Distance, Push Time Any hit-react ability › XenoCore › HitReact › Push How far a hit at Force Multiplier 1 knocks this body back (60 cm) and over how long (0.12 s). It then stops dead. Lower Push Distance for a heavy enemy; 0 means it is never pushed. Push Strength Over Time same Optional curve shaping the knockback across Push Time (X 0-1). Empty is a constant push. Directional Montages Any reaction ability (flinch, guard, recoil, dodge, Topple, Daze) › XenoCore › Reaction Front, Back, Left, Right: the side the other body is on. A dodge fills each slot with the clip that moves away from it. Random Montages same If any are set, each activation plays one of these at random and Directional Montages is ignored. GA_XenoCore_Evade lists AM_XenoCore_Evade_Duck and AM_XenoCore_Evade_Dodge. Empty (the default on every other reaction) uses Directional Montages. A character's anim profile still overrides both. Front Back Half Angle same How wide "front" and "back" are (45°). Hold Until Montage Ends same Keep the ability active for the whole montage. On for knockdowns, guards, recoils and dodges; off for flinches. Flinch On Hit GA_XenoCore_Player_HitReact, GA_XenoCore_Minion_HitReact › XenoCore › HitReact On for both: play the additive flinch. Off: no flinch at all. Hits never interrupt either way. Guard, recoil and dodge clips GA_XenoCore_Guard, _Recoil, _Evade and the minion's copies › Directional Montages (and Random Montages on GA_XenoCore_Evade) Montages in Characters/Core/Animations/Defence (player) and Characters/Enemies/Minion/Animations/Defence (minion). Block damage, hit and block chances BP_XenoCoreDamageExecution See Stats and damage. Shake and rumble GCN_XenoCore_Hit CS_Character_DamageTaken and FFE_Character_Damage by default.

See Tune the auto-attack and Change the hit feedback.

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
• A different weapon feel: right-click GA_XenoCore_AutoAttack, choose Create Child Blueprint Class, save the child in Content/MyGame/, change its montages and ranges, and grant the child in your character's ability set instead.
  • Something that should not flinch: give its hit-react ability's blocked tags the state you want, or grant it no hit-react ability.
  • Guards and dodges for a new character: make a child Blueprint of GA_XenoCore_Guard, _Recoil and _Evade (or the minion's, if your character is on the minion's skeleton), set your own montages in Directional Montages (or Random Montages, for a pick-one-at-random set), and grant the children beside the hit react in its ability set. On the party skeleton, put a dodge montage on the Defence slot to keep the arms on the weapon while armed; on FullBody the clip's own arms play in both stances. The rules (trigger, held tags, cancelling an Art) come with the parent class; the copy only holds clips.
  • A character that never guards or dodges: grant it none of the three. It still blocks and is still missed, without an animation.
  • A new kind of reaction: make a C++ child of UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_Reaction and set its trigger in the constructor. That base has the montage machinery (direction, hold, follow-up) and nothing else, so a new reaction inherits no rules it has to undo.
  • Hold still during something: add a state tag and a row in Game/TagRelationships_XenoCore that blocks the abilities you want stopped, rather than cancelling them from your code.

A Blueprint array replaces the C++ one

The hit-react base class blocks itself while Status.XenoCore.Arming and Status.XenoCore.ArtExecuting are present. A Blueprint child that sets its own Activation Blocked Tags replaces that list entirely, so it must list those two tags again alongside its own. GA_XenoCore_Player_HitReact lists all four (Arming, ArtExecuting, Topple, Daze). The same applies to the guard, recoil and dodge classes, which set their own lists in C++: a Blueprint copy that sets Activation Blocked Tags or Activation Owned Tags replaces them, and the character can then move or swing while it guards.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers: the design reasons
  • The animation decides when a hit lands. A timer beside a montage drifts, and the target takes damage while the blade is still winding up. Tying damage to a notify on the clip keeps them in step when a clip is retimed.
  • The victim decides whether to react. The attacker only sends an event. A heavy enemy, a guarding one or a dead one ignores it without the attacker knowing anything about it.
  • The roll decides, the reaction only animates. The attacking ability rolls the miss and the block, and sends an event to each side. The guard, recoil and dodge never change an outcome, so removing one costs an animation, not a rule.
  • One battle tag. A second "in combat" flag somewhere else would eventually disagree with this one.
  • State tags block abilities as data. Lyra's tag relationship mapping turns "while this tag is present, this ability cannot start" into a table row, so no ability has to know about another.

docs.title: Companion AI and aggro
docs.text:
Designer · 15 min read · No code · Last tested: 2026-10-01

Companions fight the way the player does. They use the same target, the same auto-attack, the same arts at the same levels, the same cooldowns, and they take the same reactions and statuses. The AI decides when to do those things; it never gets a separate, simplified copy of them. Enemies, in turn, decide who to attack by aggro, so a companion can draw an enemy off the player.

Out of a fight, companions do not wait in a line for you to move. Each one looks around, wanders, turns to talk to a companion and pulls faces, on its own timer, so the party never acts in unison. That half is covered in Out of battle: a party on its own clock.

This page explains how both work and which numbers you can change. To change them step by step, see Tune companion AI and Give a character its own idle breaks and faces.

Where the knobs are

Nearly every number on this page lives in one of four places: an Art definition (when an art is used), a party member definition (AI Profile: pacing and target choice), the party StateTree Characters/Party/AI/ST_XenoCore_PartyMember (movement, gaze, rest), and BP_XenoCore_Party (tactics and spawn). The table below says which.

docs.title: The short version
docs.text: What the player sees What drives it Where you change it Companions attack what you attack The leader's target lock, through the Attack tactic Party tactics (in play: tap or hold X / F) They fan out round the enemy The EQS query EQ_XenoCore_CompanionCombatSpot The EQS editor They use their arts Each art's Companion AI section The art definition They pace themselves The character's AI Profile The party member definition They walk behind for Back Slash The art's positional bonus + Seek Positional Bonus Both of the above They heal when someone is hurt Heal Threshold The party member definition Enemies turn on whoever hits hardest Aggro, on every enemy Each art's Threat Companions look around, at you and at each other The XenoCore Party Gaze task ST_XenoCore_PartyMember At rest they stroll, chat and pull faces The XenoCore Party Hold task ST_XenoCore_PartyMember Each has its own fidgets and temperament The character's Anim Profile (Idle, Face) The anim profile asset They start and stop with some weight AI Steering The party pawn Blueprint

docs.title: Aggro
docs.text:
Every enemy keeps a running score for each party member and attacks whoever is highest. These are XC1's rules:

Action Aggro change Dealing damage + damage × 0.5 Healing anyone + the heal's amount × 1.25 on every enemy already fighting, even if the target was at full health Using an art + the art's Threat × (user's level + 14), which drains at 75 per second Being hit − damage × 2 on the enemy that hit you

A fight opens with every party member at 1 and the leader targeted. A tie never changes the target. A Dazed enemy gains no aggro. A member who goes down is forgotten, and an enemy that walks home or wins forgets everyone.

So, by default: a companion that out-damages you draws the enemy off, a healer who over-heals makes themselves the target, and whoever is being hit sheds aggro over time.

Watch it live

Type log LogXenoThreat Verbose in the console. Every aggro change and every time an enemy switches target is printed with the running total.

docs.title: What a companion does in a fight
docs.text:
The companion battle state is in Characters/Party/AI/ST_XenoCore_PartyMember. When the party is in battle, it runs two tasks side by side:

  • XenoCore Fight Target takes the party's target and keeps the companion's auto-attack running. The auto-attack pauses while the target is out of reach or the companion is toppled, and picks up again after an art, exactly as it does for you.
  • XenoCore Use Best Art decides on arts.

Draw first, then close in. A companion draws its weapon where it stands, Draw Delay Min–Max (0.15–0.6 s, rolled per member) after the party enters battle, and only then walks in. The follow task holds a sheathed member still for up to Max Hold For Draw (1.5 s) so it does not jog during the wait. The delays are parameters on the XenoCore Fight Target task and the hold on XenoCore Party Follow, both in ST_XenoCore_PartyMember.

Meanwhile XenoCore Party Follow walks the companion to a combat spot. An EQS query picks a point on a ring round the enemy, away from the other party members and from the spots they have already claimed, so bodies do not pile onto one point. Only one member's spot query runs at a time, first come first served: a spot counts as claimed only once its query answers, so two queries in flight together could otherwise pick the same point.

What a companion attacks, and whether it uses arts, follows the party tactics. With Stay Back on, it keeps Stay Back Distance (750 cm, on BP_XenoCore_Party) from the target instead of taking a melee spot.

When the battle is won the companions sheathe, play their victory emotes, and go back to following you (see The combat loop). A companion still armed out of battle for Sheathe Reassert Delay (1.5 s) is asked to sheathe again.

docs.title: How a companion chooses an art
docs.text:
Every Decision Interval (1.5 s by default, ± 30 % so companions do not act in lockstep) the companion looks at the arts on its body:

  1. Only arts slotted in its Arts menu, at their learned levels, plus its weapon's Talent Art. An art that is learned but not on the bar is not on the body at all, so it can never be used.
  2. Only arts the player could use right now. The art must be off cooldown, the target in its reach, and nothing blocking it. These are the same checks the palette makes for you.
  3. Each usable art gets a score: its AI Priority, plus the Bonus of every optional condition that passes. A required condition that fails removes the art. A Talent Art gets +1.
  4. The highest score is used. On a tie, the earlier palette slot wins.

After using an art the companion waits its Post-Art Cooldown (3 s) before considering another. This is the main thing that stops a large AI party out-performing a player, and it is a per-character number.

See every decision

log LogXenoAI Verbose prints each decision with every usable art and its score, for example decision - Turn Strike=4.0 Back Slash=1.0. Tune against that line, not against a guess.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
An art's Companion AI › AI Conditions list reads live state:

Condition Passes when Target has tag / lacks tag The enemy carries (or does not carry) a tag: a reaction such as Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Break, a status, an aura … Still Active On Impact (Has tag only.) The tag will still be there when this art's hit lands, so a Topple is not fired into a Break that runs out mid-swing Target health below / above % The enemy's health compared with Percent I hold / do not hold the target's aggro The enemy is (or is not) attacking this companion Target is / is not facing me The companion is (or is not) in front of the enemy An ally is below my heal threshold Any living party member is below this companion's Heal Threshold Recipient lacks tag Whoever the art lands on does not already have the buff

Ticking Required makes a condition a gate. Unticking it makes it a bonus worth Bonus points.

A heal art needs no condition: one with no "ally below heal threshold" condition is given one automatically, so a companion never heals a full-health party.

The shipped Break arts (Air Slash, Stream Edge, Turn Strike) have one optional condition, Target lacks tag Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Break worth +2, so a companion opens the reaction chain rather than re-breaking a broken enemy.

docs.title: The reaction chain
docs.text:
A Topple or Daze art needs no AI conditions at all. The companion reads the art's Effects: a Topple effect only lands on a Broken enemy, and a Daze effect only on a Toppled one. From that:

  • The art is held until its reaction can land. A companion never spends Wild Down on an enemy that is not Broken. If it did, it would get a weak hit and a 25-second cooldown, and the next Break would go unanswered. Untick AI Wait For Reaction on an art whose damage is worth using on its own.
  • The art jumps the queue when its reaction can land. It scores AI Chain Bonus (+3) extra while the enemy is Broken (for Topple) or Toppled (for Daze). It also needs the reaction to still be there when the hit lands, so it never fires into a Break that is about to run out.

The chain works across the party: anyone's Break lets any companion Topple. Mira ships with XC1 Reyn's Wild Down (Topple) and Shield Bash (Daze) to show it.

See why a reaction did not land

log LogXenoArts Verbose prints every art's roll (hit, MISS, BLOCKED) and every status it applied or had refused. A missed hit carries no statuses, and a blocked hit cannot Topple.

docs.title: Moving into position
docs.text:
An art with a positional bonus (Back Slash from behind), or an effect that only lands from the side or behind (Slit Edge, Air Slash), is worth moving for. When it wins a decision and the companion is not in position, the companion holds the art and walks behind or beside the enemy, using no art meanwhile. It uses the art when it arrives, or after Positional Timeout (2 s) wherever it is.

It never does this while the enemy is attacking it, and it tries once per art per enemy. Untick Seek Positional Bonus for XC1 behaviour, where companions use these arts from the front.

docs.title: Enemies use the same AI
docs.text:
An enemy fights with the same two tasks as a companion. The only difference is its target: an enemy goes after whoever holds the most aggro on it, and a companion goes after the party's target.

To give an enemy arts:

  1. Author each art as an ordinary Art Definition and fill in its Companion AI section. Priority, conditions and the chain bonus work as described above.
  2. Add the arts to the enemy Blueprint's Arts list. They are granted at level 1. Enemy arts do not level; the enemy's own level scales its damage through its stats.
  3. Tune the enemy's pacing in its AI Profile (decision interval, post-art cooldown). Seek Positional Bonus is off for enemies by default, because XC1 enemies fight from where they stand.

The sample minion has two arts:

  • Rend is a Break, with +2 priority while you are not Broken.
  • Sweep is a Topple. It is held until you are Broken.

So a minion that Breaks you follows up with a Topple, the same chain your party runs on it.

Out of a fight, a placed enemy walks its Patrol Points (drag them in the viewport). It waits Patrol Wait seconds at each point and walks at Patrol Speed. An enemy from a spawner wanders inside its spawner's Wander Radius instead. Either way it walks back home after a fight. See Enemies and AI.

docs.title: Seeing who an enemy is after
docs.text:
While an enemy is fighting, a red ring sits under its target. The Aggro Indicator component on the enemy draws it. Its settings:

Setting Default What it does Ring System NS_XenoCore_AggroRing The effect. Clear it to hide the ring. Ring Lift 8 cm How far above the ground the ring starts. Hide Grace 0.4 s How long the ring stays up after the target is lost, so a target switch does not flicker.

The ring's size is the Ring Size user parameter on NS_XenoCore_AggroRing. Y and Z are the diameter (220 cm). X is how deep it projects; keep that shallow, or the ring tints the legs of the character it sits under.

docs.title: Out of battle: a party on its own clock
docs.text:
A group of people does not move, stop and look around on the same beat. What gives a robotic party away is synchrony: everyone stopping together, fidgeting together, staring straight ahead together. So every timer below is rolled per member, and nothing waits for the leader except the decision to follow.

All of it runs in Characters/Party/AI/ST_XenoCore_PartyMember. The numbers are parameters on the tasks in that tree. To change them, duplicate the tree and set it on your own child of Characters/Party/BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember; Party AI has the steps.

docs.title: Where they look
docs.text:
XenoCore Party Gaze runs on the Active state, beside the movement task, so it works in and out of battle. It turns only the head and neck; the body keeps doing whatever it was doing.

Out of battle, every Glance Interval Min–Max seconds (1.8–5 s) the member picks something new to look at, by relative chance:

Look at Chance Notes The leader Leader Chance (2.5) Another member Ally Chance (2.5) × Eye Contact Multiplier (2.5) if that member is already looking back An enemy that has not noticed the party Enemy Chance (2) Only inside Enemy Notice Radius (22 m) The view View Chance (1.5) A point View Distance out, within View Yaw Range of the body's facing Straight ahead Ahead Chance (1.5) × Walking Ahead Multiplier (4) while walking: eyes go where the feet go

Nothing beyond Max Gaze Distance (20 m) is looked at. In battle the head stays on the party's target, with a quick glance at an ally Battle Glance Chance (20 %) of the time.

The head turn itself is on the host anim Blueprint, ABP_XenoCore_Base: see Animation. A player-controlled body has no gaze and looks straight ahead, so the leader you drive is never turned by this.

Make a member look at something

From any Blueprint, take the member's body, call Get Controller, Cast To BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember, and call Request Attention with an actor and a number of seconds. That beats whatever the gaze task would pick, which makes it the call for a cutscene beat or a scripted line. Set Gaze Target and Clear Gaze Target point the head without a time limit.

docs.title: What they do while they wait
docs.text:
XenoCore Party Hold is the travel state a member is in while the leader is close. It no longer just stands still.

Slack. Each time a member comes to rest it rolls its own leash: Follow Start Distance (5.2 m) plus up to Leash Jitter (2.6 m). A small step by the leader moves nobody. A real departure sets members off one at a time, nearest leash first, each after its own Reaction Delay Min–Max (0.2–1 s). Past Immediate Follow Multiplier (1.6) times its leash, a member goes at once.

Activities. Every Activity Interval Min–Max seconds (3.5–9 s) a resting member picks one, by relative chance:

Activity Chance What you see Stroll Stroll Chance (3) Ambles Stroll Min Distance–Max Distance (1–3.2 m) to a free spot inside the group, at Amble Speed Social Social Chance (3) Steps up to a companion within Social Max Partner Distance (9 m), stops Social Stand Distance Min–Max (1.15–1.65 m) away, and the two look at each other for Social Attention Min–Max (3–6 s). Each may pull one of its Social Expressions Solo Solo Chance (1) Pulls one of its Solo Expressions, alone Stay Stay Chance (2) Nothing. Standing is also something people do

No new activity starts while the leader moves faster than Leader Moving Speed (60 cm/s), and a stroll in progress is dropped if the leader walks off. Min Separation (1 m) keeps strolls and social spots off other members.

Turning to face someone. When a resting member's attention target (a companion talking to it, one it is talking to) is more than Turn To Attention Angle (55°) off its facing, it takes one short step toward them. When it is already too close to step, it turns on the spot at Turn In Place Rate (140°/s). There is no turn-in-place clip, so keep that rate gentle.

The faces and fidgets are per character, in the character's anim profile. See Give a character its own idle breaks and faces.

docs.title: Who is speaking
docs.text:
When a voiced line has an Addressee, the speaker and the addressee look at each other for the line, plus Attention Linger (1.5 s) so a reply lands while they still face each other. Other companions within Listener Radius (9 m) glance at the speaker Listener Glance Chance (60 %) of the time. A field exchange only pairs two members within Exchange Max Distance (5 m), so a conversation is never shouted across the party.

These are on the voice config, Audio/Voice/DA_XenoCore_BattleVoiceConfig, under Who Is Speaking. Writing the lines themselves is Battle voices and banter.

docs.title: How they move
docs.text:
Catch-up pace. XenoCore Party Follow Leader never runs faster than the leader's speed × Catch Up Ratio (1.5) + Catch Up Margin (120 cm/s), and eases its pace toward the target at Pace Smoothing (3 per second). Behind a walking leader, companions walk a little faster instead of sprinting, stopping and walking again. Once the leader stops they come in at Arrive Speed.

AI Steering. On the pawn Blueprint, XenoCore › Movement › AI Steering gives a body softer movement while the AI drives it: Rotation Rate Yaw (420°/s), Max Acceleration (1500) and Braking Deceleration Walking (1100). The player's numbers are tuned for a hand on the stick and look robotic on a body nobody steers. When the player takes the body over, the Blueprint's own movement values come straight back. It is on for B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base, B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_Base and B_XenoCore_Player, and off (untick Enabled) for anything that does not opt in, enemies included.

Crowd avoidance. Out of battle, members follow their paths straight; Detour Crowd avoidance is switched off. With it on, members re-steer round each other every frame and the whole party wobbles as it walks, at every quality setting. In battle it is always on, because members converge on one enemy and need to get round each other. To have it while travelling as well, tick Crowd Avoidance While Travelling on BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember (XenoCore › AI › Crowd). The same category holds Crowd Avoidance Quality, Crowd Anticipate Turns, Crowd Separation Weight and Crowd Collision Query Range.

docs.title: Where they appear
docs.text:
When the party first spawns, members land on a loose scatter behind the leader rather than in a formation. The settings are on BP_XenoCore_Party under XenoCore › Party › Spawn:

Setting Default What it does Spawn Inner Radius 190 cm Distance of the nearest member from the leader Spawn Radius Step 55 cm Each later member lands this much further out, on average Spawn Radius Jitter 45 cm Random spread on each radius Spawn Arc Degrees 240° The arc behind the leader members are scattered across. 360 surrounds it Spawn Min Separation 120 cm No two members closer than this Spawn Face Leader 0.35 0 faces where the leader faces, 1 faces the leader Spawn Facing Jitter 40° Random turn on each member's facing

docs.title: What companions do not do yet
docs.text:
• They do not revive you or each other, and do not help a toppled ally up. Reviving is the player's move, paid from the Party Gauge.
  • They do not react to Visions. In XC1, warning an ally is the player's move.
  • They never start a fight. Even with the Attack tactic on At Will, a companion only picks enemies that are already fighting the party. See Party tactics.

docs.title: Time of day and weather
docs.text:
All · 10 min read

XenoCore keeps a clock that runs while you play: the sun rises and sets, night falls with a moon and a starry sky, and each area rolls its own weather, from clear skies to rain and storms. The time and the weather sit on the minimap, and the menu's Change Time entry jumps the clock to any hour. The one idea: the clock and the weather are game-wide state; one placed actor per map turns them into light. A map with no director still has a clock and weather (anything that asks for them gets an answer); its sky just does not change.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
• Day and night and weather on a map of yours: Give a map its time of day and weather.
  • How fast the clock runs, the phase hours, the start hour: Project Settings › Plugins › XenoCore Environment (Settings).
  • Which weather an area gets, and how often: the area's weather table (The weather).
  • What rain or a storm looks and sounds like: rows of World/DT_XenoCore_WeatherTypes.
  • How a day looks (sun arc, sky colour, fog, night brightness): a sky profile data asset.
  • Night music: Give a map its music.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text: Piece Class / asset Job Clock Built in, game-wide The time, 00:00 to 23:59, and the phase. Survives map travel; saved with the game Weather Built in, game-wide The current weather, rolled from the area's weather table. Saved with the game Settings Project Settings › Plugins › XenoCore Environment Clock speed, phase hours, the hour a new game starts at, the Change Time fade, the weather types table Weather types World/DT_XenoCore_WeatherTypes One row per kind of weather (Clear, Rain, Storm): its name and icon, how long it lasts, and how it changes the sky, lights, music and wind Area weather odds A Data Table (row structure XenoCoreWeatherChanceRow) on the area's Area Definition, for example Maps/Areas/DT_XenoCore_Weather_GaurPlain on DA_XenoCore_Area_GaurPlain The chance of each weather in this area Environment director XenoCore Environment Director (in Place Actors), one placed per map Moves the map's own sun, sky light, fog and clouds with the clock, and adds rain, lightning, ambience and the night sky Sky profile World/DA_XenoCore_SkyProfile_Default (data asset) How a day looks: sunrise and sunset hours, the sun's and moon's arcs, per-hour curves for sky light, exposure, fog colour and saturation, the night exposure floor Change Time screen XenoCoreChangeTimeScreen, the menu's Change Time entry A 24-hour dial; confirm and the screen fades while the clock jumps Minimap The HUD's Minimap widget The sun or moon on the rim (noon at the top, midnight at the bottom) and the time and weather icon beside the area name

docs.title: The clock
docs.text:
Pace. One real second is one in-game minute, so a whole day takes 24 minutes. Change it with Minutes Per Second. A new game starts at New Game Start Hour (10:00).

Phases.

Phase Hours (defaults) Morning 05:00 to 06:00 Day 06:00 to 17:00 Evening 17:00 to 19:00 Night 19:00 to 05:00

Each start hour is a setting (Clock › Phases). Morning, Day and Evening count as daytime, Night as nighttime, which is what the night music asks.

When it stops. The clock runs on game time, so it stops whenever the game pauses (every menu) and slows with slow motion. It also stops during conversations (Pause During Dialogue) and whenever a Blueprint holds it with Add Clock Hold (XenoCore › Time), naming a Reason; Remove Clock Hold with the same reason releases it.

Change Time. From the menu, pick an hour on the dial and confirm. The screen fades out, the clock jumps to the start of that hour, the weather re-rolls, and the screen fades back in. The fade timings are in Clock › Change Time.

The screen draws in C++, so its look is on the class: Font Family (Orbitron by default, used by any of its fonts left without one) and the dial's Sun Texture / Moon Texture (the minimap rim's icons, used when Sun Icon / Moon Icon have no image). All three are soft references loaded when the screen is built. To change them, make a Blueprint child of XenoCoreChangeTimeScreen and point the menu's Change Time entry at it (see UI shell and HUD).

docs.title: The weather
docs.text:
Per area. Each area's Area Definition (the one the map's XenoCore Map Area actor points at, see Minimap) has a Weather Table: rows of a weather and its Percent. Whatever the rows leave under 100 is Clear, so an area with no table is always clear. Gaur Plain rolls Rain 5% and Storm 2%. A row can be limited to some Phases (none ticked means any phase).

When it re-rolls. When the current weather's duration runs out (Duration Minutes, in in-game minutes), when the clock jumps, and when the phase changes to one the current weather is not allowed in. Travelling to another area keeps the weather if that area allows it.

What it changes. Every look field on a weather type is a scale on top of the time of day: rain at dusk is dusk and rain. A weather type can dim the sun and sky light, thicken the fog, close and darken the clouds, grey and darken the picture, and blow the grass harder (Wind Strength). Rain and Storm also:

  • lower the music (Music Volume Scale, applied to every area music track);
  • play an ambience loop (Ambient Sound);
  • spawn rain round the camera, which stops at the ground and at any roof above, and splashes where it lands;
  • (Storm only) flash lightning with thunder after it.

A change of weather blends in over Blend Seconds; a clock jump or arriving in a map snaps straight to it.

docs.title: Night
docs.text: At night the sun's light becomes the moon's: one directional light plays both. The director also draws a moon disc and a starry sky with the Milky Way, and lifts the darkest exposure the camera may pick (Night Exposure Floor EV100 on the sky profile), so night reads as night rather than as a dim afternoon. Area music can switch to a night field track at nightfall: see Give a map its music.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Setting Where What it does Minutes Per Second Project Settings › Plugins › XenoCore Environment › Clock Clock speed. 1 is a 24-minute day; 0 stops the clock New Game Start Hour same The time a new game starts at Pause During Dialogue same Stop the clock while a conversation is open Morning / Day / Evening / Night Start Hour … › Clock › Phases The phase boundaries Change Time Fade Out / Hold / Fade In Seconds … › Clock › Change Time The Change Time fade Weather Types … › Weather The weather types table. Defaults to DT_XenoCore_WeatherTypes Weather Table The area's Area Definition › Weather That area's odds Profile The placed director › Environment Which sky profile the map uses. Empty uses the C++ defaults, a complete day Light Step Minutes The sky profile › Performance The sun rotates in steps of this many in-game minutes, because each rotation re-renders its shadows. Brightness, fog and sky colour refresh separately, at most every 0.1 s of real time Sun Actor, Sky Light Actor, Fog Actor, Sky Atmosphere Actor, Cloud Actor The placed director › Environment › Lights / Clouds Which of the map's actors to drive. Empty finds the map's first of each Wind Collection The placed director › Environment › Wind The material parameter collection your foliage's wind reads Precipitation Spawn Rate, Rain Color, Splash Color and the Height Map settings The placed director › Environment › Weather How much rain, its colour, and the overhead capture that stops it under cover

docs.title: Console commands
docs.text:
Command Does XenoCore.Time.Set <hour> [fade] Set the clock (re-rolls the weather). fade runs the Change Time fade XenoCore.Time.Scale <multiplier> Run the clock faster: 60 is an hour a second, 1 is normal XenoCore.Time.Describe Log the time, phase and weather XenoCore.Weather.Set <Clear\|Rain\|Storm> [lock] [snap] Force the weather. lock holds it until XenoCore.Weather.Reroll; snap skips the blend XenoCore.Weather.Reroll Release a lock and roll the area's table XenoCore.Weather.Lightning Flash lightning now XenoCore.Weather.Tune [Field] [Value] List or change the current weather's and the director's numbers live XenoCore.Environment.Freeze 1 Stop the director writing lights, to compare with the map as authored XenoCore.Environment.NightFloor <EV100> Try a night exposure floor without editing the profile

See Console commands.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The clock broadcasts XenoCore.Time.Message.PhaseChanged, XenoCore.Time.Message.HourBlockChanged (every three in-game hours) and XenoCore.Time.Message.Jumped; the weather broadcasts XenoCore.Weather.Message.Changed (old and new weather, and whether it snapped). A Blueprint that should react to nightfall or rain listens for these rather than polling. See Events you can listen to.

Fails silently: a sun that is not Movable

The director can only move a directional light whose Mobility is Movable. A Static or Stationary sun stays where it was placed: the clock runs, the minimap shows the right time, and the sky never changes. A warning is logged at Begin Play. Set the sun to Movable.

Fails silently: a weather name with no row

An area's Weather Table row whose weather has no row in the weather types table rolls, shows nothing on screen and lowers no music. The log shows only the ordinary XenoCoreWeather: … -> … line. Every weather an area can roll needs a row in DT_XenoCore_WeatherTypes, with the same Tag.

  • Wet surfaces and a distant rain curtain.

docs.title: Enemies and AI
docs.text:
All · 15 min read

What the player sees: enemies patrol or wander, notice the party by sight, sound or ether, fight with an auto-attack and their own Arts, give up and walk home if you run far enough, and drop a chest when the last one of a group falls. A lvl.N label over each one is coloured by how dangerous it is compared with your party leader.

Everything that makes one enemy different from another (mesh, level, stats, Arts, loot, how it notices you) is a setting on its Blueprint or a data asset it points at. The AI that drives every enemy is shared, so a new enemy type needs no AI of its own: the enemy's data decides what it can do, and the shared AI decides when. An enemy fights with the same AI as a companion; only where its target comes from differs.

See the Glossary for Engage, disengage, Detection, Aggro, Squad and Pawn data.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
• A new enemy type: a child Blueprint of the sample minion. See Add an enemy and Your first enemy.
  • Where enemies stand, patrol and respawn: Place enemies.
  • Its stats at each level: Enemy statline.
  • Its Arts and how it chooses them: Give an enemy Arts.
  • What it drops: Build a drop table.
  • Its hit, knock-down and death clips: Give a character its own combat animations.
  • How it notices you, how far it chases, its rewards: settings on the enemy Blueprint, in the tables below.

Ability sets on the sample minion:

Ability Tag the AI uses Notes GA_XenoCore_Minion_Attack Ability.XenoCore.AutoAttack Auto-attack. An Art pauses it; the fight task restarts it afterwards GA_XenoCore_Minion_HitReact none Directional flinch GA_XenoCore_Minion_Topple, GA_XenoCore_Minion_Daze none Knock-downs, triggered by the reaction tag arriving and held for as long as it lasts. The minion's two Arts are not in the ability set. They are Art definitions on the enemy Blueprint's Arts list, granted at level 1 when it spawns: the same kind of Art the party uses. Like a party Art, an enemy Art roots the enemy for the length of its animation.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Spawn. The enemy receives the abilities in its Enemy Pawn Data and applies its Stats Effect at its Enemy Level. The controller records the pawn's start position as home and gives the pawn its team (2 by default). An enemy made by a spawner rolls its level from the spawner's range, and its home is where it spawned.

Waiting. Until it is provoked its aggro target is empty and the StateTree keeps it in Freeroam: it walks its Patrol Points back and forth at Patrol Speed (105 cm/s, its walk), pausing Patrol Wait (2 s) at each point; with no points it wanders within Wander Radius of home, or stands still if that is 0. A spawner sets the wander radius for its squad.

Noticing. An enemy is provoked by taking damage, or by its Detection:

Detection Provoked when… None (passive) never; only damage provokes it Sight the party leader is inside Sight Radius (1400) and the view cone (Sight Half Angle, 55°; 180 sees all round) Sound the leader runs (faster than the controller's Running Speed, 280 cm/s) inside Sound Radius (1000). Walking past is safe Ether the party uses an ether art inside Ether Radius (1500), even a harmless one

Detection obeys the level rule: an enemy Ignore When Levels Below (6) or more levels under the party leader does not notice the party at all. The rule never applies to being attacked: hit an under-levelled enemy and it fights back. A Unique Monster, or a controller with Always Aggro, skips the rule.

Link aggro. An enemy made by a spawner belongs to a squad. When one member is provoked, every living member within the spawner's Link Radius is provoked too. This is XC2/XC3's documented behaviour, chosen for XenoCore; XC1's own rule for groups is not sourced. Untick Link Aggro on a spawner for a loose group whose members fight only when each one is provoked.

Engaging. Once provoked, the controller's aggro target is the party member holding the most aggro on it (see Aggro), so a companion who hits harder than you can draw the enemy off. It engages while that pawn is within Engage Radius (1600). Once engaged, the radius grows by Disengage Radius Scale (2.5 ×) so the enemy does not flicker in and out at the edge. Each of these, and Leash Radius, is the controller's default unless the enemy sets its own override (below).

Fighting. The tree's Fight state chases the target, keeps the auto-attack swinging at it, and every Decision Interval scores the Arts on the enemy's Arts list, using the best one that is ready. Scoring is the companions' (see How a companion chooses an art): a Topple Art is held until the target is Broken, so the minion opens with Rend (Break) and follows with Sweep (Topple). Its AI Profile paces it; Post-Art Cooldown is the brake. When aggro moves to another party member, the enemy turns on them.

Moving. The minion's anim Blueprint plays a 2D blend space over Direction and Ground Speed, so it walks on patrol, jogs in a chase, and strafes or backs off with side and back clips while it shuffles round its attackers. A hit's knockback is not treated as movement: while the shove lasts the legs hold their pose and the body slides underneath, with the flinch on the torso.

Knocked down. While the enemy is Toppled or Dazed it plays its knock-down, stops chasing, does not auto-attack, and uses no Arts. It picks up where it left off when the reaction ends. A Dazed enemy gains no aggro.

Giving up. If the enemy strays more than Leash Radius (7000) from home, or the party outruns it (the target leaves the disengage radius), it disengages, forgets it was provoked and its aggro, recovers to full health (Heal On Give Up), and walks home at the chase task's return speed. It then resumes its patrol or wander. A party wipe does the same to every enemy at once. A Blueprint can do it to one enemy with the controller's Reset Aggro node (XenoCore › AI).

Dying. On death the enemy announces its defeat (see Events), awards the party EXP, Art Points and Skill Points through the progression component (Experience Reward, Art Point Reward and Skill Point Multiplier, scaled by level difference), rolls a chest tier and spawns the chest hidden for Chest Drop Delay, plays one of its Death Montages, ragdolls after a random Ragdoll Delay Min–Max, then vanishes after Death Vanish Delay with its Death Effect. The effect is a soft reference: it starts loading when the enemy is first provoked, so idle enemies on a map do not hold it in memory. In a squad, only the last member killed drops a chest, upgraded to at least silver. A spawner brings fallen members back after its Respawn Delay, only while the party is out of sight of the spot and not fighting that squad.

Widgets. Every enemy wears a lvl.N label with a chevron, coloured by how its level compares with the party leader's. It fades out with distance and is always shown in battle. A Unique Monster's label is gold, carries its name and shows from further away. The text, the colour bands and the distances are in Project Settings › Game › XenoCore Enemies › Level Label. The HP bar is hidden until the enemy is engaged. Neither widget costs anything while it has nothing to show: the label switches itself off beyond its fade distance (re-checked every Label Tick Check Interval, 0.4 s). While the enemy fights, a red ring lies under whoever it is after. No line is drawn between the enemy and its target. See Seeing who an enemy is after.

docs.text:
Settings marked per placement can also be changed on a placed enemy in the level.

Per placement Display Name XenoCore › Enemy Name on the target badge. Per placement Unique Monster XenoCore › Enemy Skips the level rule; gold, named label. Tick Always Gold Chest too. Per placement Wander Radius XenoCore › AI › Patrol With no Patrol Points: wander this far from home. 0 = stand still. A spawner overrides it. Per placement Leash Radius Override XenoCore › AI This enemy's leash radius. -1 uses the controller's.
