docs.title: On the AI controller (BP_AIC_XenoCore_Enemy, Class Defaults)
docs.text:
Setting Category What it does Engage Radius XenoCore › AI How close the target must be to fight. Default 1600 Leash Radius XenoCore › AI Distance from home at which the enemy gives up. Default 7000 Disengage Radius Scale XenoCore › AI Engage radius multiplier once fighting. Default 2.5 Ignore When Levels Below XenoCore › AI Ignore a party this many levels higher. Default 6 Always Aggro XenoCore › AI Skip the level rule. Noticing the party still needs a Detection other than None Running Speed XenoCore › AI › Detection Leader speed above which Sound detection hears it. Default 280 Detection Interval XenoCore › AI › Detection How often, in seconds, the enemy checks whether it has noticed the party. Default 0.2 Heal On Give Up XenoCore › AI Restore full health when the enemy gives up a fight. Default on Team Id XenoCore › Teams Team the pawn joins. Default 2

The three radii here are the defaults for every enemy the controller possesses. One enemy type, or one placed enemy, can differ through its own … Override settings above, with no new controller. -1 means "use the controller's"; 0 is a real value (an engage radius of 0 never engages, even when provoked). An override changed while the game runs applies on the next check. In a Blueprint, Get Effective Engage Radius, Get Effective Leash Radius and Get Effective Disengage Radius Scale on the controller return the values in force.

docs.title: In the StateTree
docs.text:
The tree ST_XenoCore_EnemyFreeroam has two states:

State Entered when Runs Fight The controller has an aggro target XenoCore Chase Aggro Target, XenoCore Fight Target, XenoCore Use Best Art Freeroam It has none XenoCore Enemy Patrol Node Parameters What it does XenoCore Has Aggro Target (condition) Invert The controller has a target XenoCore Chase Aggro Target (task) Acceptable Radius (140), Repath Interval, Chase Speed (380), Return Speed (150), Home Tolerance Chases, then walks home when the target is gone XenoCore Fight Target (task) Retry Interval Keeps the auto-attack swinging at the target; never restarts it under an Art XenoCore Use Best Art (task) none Scores and uses the enemy's Arts, paced by its AI Profile XenoCore Enemy Patrol (task) none Walks the enemy's Patrol Points back and forth; hands over to Fight the moment the enemy is provoked

The tree reads its numbers from the enemy (patrol route, Arts, AI Profile), so one tree serves every enemy type. The older nodes XenoCore In Attack Range, XenoCore Ability Ready, XenoCore Target Has Tag and XenoCore Activate Ability By Tag are still available for a tree of your own.

Fails silently: an enemy Art that borrows the auto-attack's montage

Using an Art stops the auto-attack's swing by montage. An Art playing the same montage asset is stopped on its first frame: no hit, nothing logged. Give every Art its own montage copy.

Fails silently: a Stats Effect using Add

Every modifier on a stats effect must use Override. Re-applying it on a level change would otherwise stack the numbers.

The enemy won't fight

Check, in order: its Detection (None waits to be hit; Sound only hears running); is it 6 or more levels below the party leader (then it notices nothing, but still fights back when hit); is it further than Engage Radius.

docs.title: The sample enemy types
docs.text:
The seven types in Characters/Enemies/Minion/Variants/ are empty child Blueprints of B_XenoCore_Minion_Melee. They change only class defaults (name, detection, mesh, material, stats effect, drop table, rewards), so every fix to the minion reaches all of them.

Blueprint Name Detection Body B_XenoCore_Minion_Grunt Plains Grunt Sound Melee B_XenoCore_Minion_Grunt_Rust Rust Grunt Sight Melee, rust skin B_XenoCore_Minion_Skirmisher Skirmisher Sight Ranged B_XenoCore_Minion_Skirmisher_Jade Jade Skirmisher Ether Ranged, jade skin B_XenoCore_Minion_Bulwark Bulwark None (passive) Siege B_XenoCore_Minion_Brute Brute Sight Super B_XenoCore_Minion_Brute_Violet Violet Brute Sight, all round Super, violet skin

Skins are material instances of the minion material, not new textures. The ranged, siege and super bodies are on skeletons that share the melee body's bone chain and are marked compatible with SK_Minion_Core, so they run the melee minion's anim Blueprint, montages, abilities and Arts unchanged. The tougher types use their own stats effects (GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_Minion_Skirmisher, _Bulwark, _Brute), which read the same Minion_Melee.* rows of CT_XenoCore_EnemyStats times per-type multipliers on the effect: Strength ×0.9, ×1.15 and ×1.45, and HP ×0.8, ×1.9 and ×3.0, for Skirmisher, Bulwark and Brute (each also shifts Agility, and Ether or the defences). The rows themselves are anchored on an early XC1 field enemy: a level 1 minion has 900 HP and 69 Strength, plus 100 HP and 10 Strength a level.

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
• A new enemy type: right-click B_XenoCore_Minion_Melee and choose Create Child Blueprint Class, in your own folder, as the seven sample types do. Duplicate its pawn data, ability set and stats effect only if it needs different ones (those are data assets). See Your first enemy, Add an enemy, Enemy statline and Place enemies.
  • Different Arts: put different Art definitions on the enemy's Arts list, and steer them with each Art's Companion AI settings. See Give an enemy Arts.
  • A squad: place a XenoCore Enemy Spawner. See Place enemies.
  • A patrol: set Patrol Points on a hand-placed enemy. See Place enemies.
  • A unique monster: tick Unique Monster on a spawner (with a Unique Name) or on a placed enemy, and override Enemy Level, Experience Reward and Always Gold Chest as needed.
  • Never edit B_XenoCore_Enemy_Base, BP_AIC_XenoCore_Enemy or the shared StateTree in place.
For programmers: a C++ enemy

AXenoCoreEnemyCharacter and AXenoCoreEnemyController are exported, so your own module can subclass them. Enemies do not derive from AXenoCoreCombatantCharacter (the party's base); both derive from Lyra's ALyraCharacterWithAbilities. The pawn owns its own Ability System Component and has no PlayerState.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers
  • No PlayerState. Lyra's PlayerState route would give every enemy the experience's default pawn data (the player's kit), because the only per-pawn hook, ALyraGameMode::GetPawnDataForController, is not virtual. Deriving from ALyraCharacterWithAbilities gives the pawn its own ASC. It is the same shape as Lyra's own B_ShootingTarget, and it lets enemies simply be placed in a level.
  • Two small C++ classes. The pawn exists to call InitializeAbilitySystem, which is not a UFUNCTION; without it the health component never initialises. The controller exists because Lyra's team interface cannot be implemented in Blueprint, and a pawn's team must come from its controller.
  • Level on the instance. Ability sets apply effects at a level fixed on the asset, so a per-placement level needs its own stats effect path.
  • Data, not states, in the tree. One tree serves every enemy. What an enemy can do is on the enemy (its Arts and AI Profile), and cooldowns are asked of GAS rather than duplicated in the tree.
  • One AI for both sides. Enemies and companions share the fight and art tasks, so an Art behaves the same whoever uses it.

docs.title: Equipment
docs.text:
All · 15 min read

The equipment screen: slots, the character preview and the stat panel.

What the player sees: each character wears gear in six slots (Weapon, Head, Chest, Arms, Legs and Feet), chosen on the Equipment screen from the party's shared bag. A weapon shows on the character's back, moves to the hand when a battle starts, and goes back when it ends. Each piece adds its numbers to the character sheet, and weapons and some armour carry gems in sockets.

Equipping does not move an item out of the bag (see Items and inventory); a slot only points at it. Every number an item adds is a setting on the item itself, so a new item is pure data: no effect asset or graph of its own.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
• A new weapon: Add a weapon.
  • New armour: Add armour.
  • A gem: Add a gem.
  • A new stat on equipment (for example a speed bonus): Add an equipment stat.
  • What a character starts wearing and which weapon types it may wield: its equipment component (see Settings).
  • How a weapon looks drawn and sheathed: its weapon type and weapon instance; see Animation.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Piece Class / sample asset Job Equipment component The equipment component (class XenoCoreEquipmentComponent), in the Components panel of each character Blueprint Six named slots; starting gear; equip, unequip and swap; the capped gem effect Item definition Weapons/GreatSword/ID_XenoCore_JunkSword, Inventory/Armour/ID_XenoCore_* Slots allowed, stats, which equipment definition to use Equipment definition (weapon) Weapons/ED_XenoCore_Sword_Base › GreatSword/ED_XenoCore_JunkSword, BlueSword/ED_XenoCore_BlueSword and one per sword Weapon actor to spawn, instance class, ability sets to grant Weapon actor Weapons/B_XenoCore_Sword_Base › B_GreatSword, B_BlueSword… The mesh you see Weapon type Weapons/Types/DA_XenoCore_WeaponType_Greatsword The kind of weapon: its name in menus, its drawn and sheathed stances, draw and sheathe montages, auto-attack swings and reach. An item names its type; a character lists the types it may wield Equipment definition (armour) Inventory/Armour/ED_XenoCore_Armour Shared by every armour piece. Spawns nothing Weapon ability sets Weapons/AbilitySet_XenoCore_SwordCommon (granted by the sword base), plus a Talent set such as GreatSword/AbilitySet_XenoCore_JunkSword Common: GA_XenoCore_EquipmentStats and GA_XenoCore_WeaponDrawSync. Talent set: the sword's Talent Art, for example GA_XenoCore_TurnStrike Armour ability set Inventory/AbilitySet_XenoCore_EquipmentStats GA_XenoCore_EquipmentStats only Stats ability Inventory/GA_XenoCore_EquipmentStats Applies the stats effect when the item is equipped. Names no stat of its own Stats effect Inventory/GE_XenoCore_EquipmentStats Infinite effect; SetByCaller modifiers onto the character's stats Weapon instance Weapons/B_WeaponInstance_Base → GreatSword/B_WeaponInstance_GreatSword Drawn and stowed sockets, SetDrawn, animation layers Draw sync Weapons/GA_XenoCore_WeaponDrawSync Draws or sheathes the weapon when battle starts or ends Arming Battle/GA_XenoCore_Arm_v2, AM_GreatSword_Unsheathe / _Sheathe Plays the draw or sheathe montage Screens UserInterface/W_XenoCore_EquipmentScreen, W_XenoCore_ItemSwapList, W_XenoCore_EquipConfirm Loadout, candidate list, "take from another character" confirm

The sample swords (Junk, Blue, Green, Red, Amber, Gold, Ivory and Violet, one folder each under Weapons/) are all children of the two sword bases, share B_WeaponInstance_GreatSword and the Greatsword type, and differ only in their item, mesh or material, and the Talent Art their ability set grants. Junk, Blue, Green, Red and Gold share AbilitySet_XenoCore_JunkSword (Turn Strike); Amber, Ivory and Violet grant their own. Weapons/IronBlade holds only a mesh and material. See Add a weapon.

Each character wields one weapon type. An item's type is Weapon Type on its XenoCoreFragment_EquipSlots fragment; a character's allowed types are its equipment component's Allowed Weapon Types. A weapon of the wrong type is refused (Wrong Weapon Type) and is hidden from that character's swap list. An empty value at either end allows anything. Every sample party member is a Greatsword user today.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Starting gear. When a character's ability system is ready, its equipment component first adds its Starting Inventory to the party bag, then equips each Starting Equipment entry (adding the item to the bag first). A character that has been benched and redeployed comes back in what the player last put on it, picking its own items back up from the bag rather than adding copies.

Equipping. Equip Item To Slot checks the item first. Get Equip Blocker returns why it would fail:

Blocker Meaning None It would equip No Item Nothing passed Not Equippable No InventoryFragment_EquippableItem, or one with no equipment definition Wrong Slot The item's Allowed Slots does not include this slot Worn In Another Slot This character already wears it elsewhere Worn By Another Another character wears it. Pass Take From Other Character to strip it from them (the screen asks first) Wrong Weapon Type The weapon's type is not in this character's Allowed Weapon Types

If allowed, whatever was in the slot is unequipped, the weapon actor (if any) spawns, and the equipment definition's ability sets are granted. One of those, GA_XenoCore_EquipmentStats, copies the item's stat numbers (its InventoryFragment_SetStats values) onto the character at once, so the character sheet is right the moment the item goes on. Which stats it copies is the list of Modifiers on Inventory/GE_XenoCore_EquipmentStats: one row per stat. An item stat with no row there is ignored, with a warning in the Output Log (LogXenoCoreEquipmentStats). Screens hear about the change through the XenoCore.Equipment.Message.SlotChanged message.

Which body holds it. A VRoid member's own mesh is an invisible Mannequin, so its weapon goes to the visible VRoid body instead, whenever that body's skeleton has the socket being used (XC_WeaponGrip_R in the hand, XC_WeaponStow_Back on the back). Move those sockets in the VRoid skeleton's editor to fit the weapon to each character. A body without them keeps the weapon on the Mannequin's own sockets.

What a weapon type changes. A weapon's type (a data asset such as Weapons/Types/DA_XenoCore_WeaponType_Greatsword, picked on the item's Equip Slots fragment) decides who may wield it, and can also bring its own stance, draw and sheathe montages, auto-attack swings and reach. Any of those left empty on the type falls back to the greatsword's. A weapon's Type row in the menus shows its type's Display Name (armour shows Light, Medium or Heavy there instead).

Unequipping. Unequip Slot takes the item's stats off the character, despawns the weapon actor and removes the granted abilities. The item stays in the bag.

Leaving the field. When a character's pawn is destroyed (benched, or killed and cleared), every slot is unequipped, so its gear sits loose in the shared bag.

Drawing the weapon. When a battle starts or ends, GA_XenoCore_Arm_v2 plays the draw or sheathe montage, and GA_XenoCore_WeaponDrawSync moves the weapon between its back and hand sockets as the montage plays and swaps the character's stance animations (see Animation); the character cannot move while drawing, and neither direction can be interrupted by a flinch.

docs.title: Gems
docs.text:
A weapon or armour piece can carry gems in its sockets, XC1-style. A gem is an ordinary item (Inventory/Gems/ID_XenoCore_Gem_<Type>_<Rank>: Strength Up, Ether Up, Agility Up, Ether Def Up, Muscle Up and Critical Up, ranks I to III), and its exact strength is rolled when the gem is created, within its rank's range.

  • Sockets travel with the item. Socketing writes the gem onto the host item, so a weapon handed to another character keeps its gems. A gem not listed in Inventory/Gems/DA_XenoCore_GemRegistry is refused.
  • How many sockets. A weapon has its weapon type's Default Gem Slots (2 on the Greatsword); tick Override Gem Slots on the item's Equip Slots fragment to give one weapon a different count. Armour uses that fragment's Gem Slots: 0 on the Colony starter pieces, 1 on the rest.
  • Caps are per character. The gems a character wears are summed across every piece and capped per gem type (Strength Up at 150, as in XC1), then added to the character's stats, refreshed on every equip, unequip and socket change. An item's own stats, and the comparison in the swap list, never include its gems.
  • On screen. The equipment screen shows each piece's sockets as coloured icons and names them on a line under the piece; the gem popup sockets and removes gems, and previews the change on the character sheet as you highlight a gem.

Gems come from quests and the shop, never chests; Kael starts a new game with one. See Add a gem.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Where it lives What it does Starting Equipment Character Blueprint › Components › equipment component › Details › XenoCore › Equipment Slot and item definition pairs worn at start Starting Inventory Same Loose items (and Count) the party starts with Allowed Weapon Types Same Weapon types this character may wield. Empty allows any Allowed Slots, Equip Type Item › XenoCoreFragment_EquipSlots Which slots; Light / Medium / Heavy label Stat numbers Item › InventoryFragment_SetStats XenoCore.Stat.* tags and values Equipment Definition Item › InventoryFragment_EquippableItem Which equipment definition equips it Actors To Spawn, Instance Type, Ability Sets To Grant Equipment definition (Lyra) What equipping spawns and grants Draw and stow sockets, animation layer sets Weapon instance Blueprint See Animation

Stats the shared effect carries: Strength, Ether, Agility, PhysicalDefence, EtherDefence, BlockRate, CriticalRate, WeaponAttackMin, WeaponAttackMax and Weight, each fed by the matching XenoCore.Stat.* tag.

Weight. Armour carries XenoCore.Stat.Weight. It is subtracted from Agility whenever Agility is used for a hit roll: the wearer is easier to hit and misses more. The character sheet still shows Agility and Weight as separate rows; the subtraction happens only in the roll.

On the stats ability (GA_XenoCore_EquipmentStats, Class Defaults, XenoCore › Equipment):

Setting Shipped What it does Equipment Stats Effect GE_XenoCore_EquipmentStats The effect applied while worn. Its Set By Caller modifiers decide which stats reach which attributes Percent Stat Tags empty Extra stats authored as whole percent (15) and applied as a fraction (0.15). Critical Rate and Block Rate are already percent in the stat list, so they need no entry

Unequip rules. On the loadout, the unequip prompt appears only for a filled slot that is not the Weapon slot. Can Unequip Slot returns false for Weapon: every party member must carry a weapon. An empty slot's row shows the slot's name.

Fails silently: armour with no stats ability

GA_XenoCore_EquipmentStats is granted only through an ability set on the equipment definition. Armour that points at an equipment definition without AbilitySet_XenoCore_EquipmentStats equips, fills its slot, shows its name, and adds zero stats with nothing logged. Point every armour piece at ED_XenoCore_Armour.

Fails silently: the armour ability set must not draw

AbilitySet_XenoCore_EquipmentStats must not include GA_XenoCore_WeaponDrawSync, or armour tries to draw itself. The weapon's set carries both.

Fails silently: a new item created blank

A new item definition has no equipment definition, so Get Equip Blocker returns Not Equippable: the row shows, the click does nothing, nothing is logged. Duplicate a working item.

Fails silently: removing Ability Sets To Grant from a weapon

The weapon's ability set grants the draw sync as well as the stats. It is granted with the equipment instance as its source, which is the only way the draw ability finds its weapon. Removing it breaks drawing and sheathing without an error.

Fails silently: listing an item in both Starting lists

Starting Equipment adds its own copy of each item. Listing the same item in Starting Inventory as well gives the party two: one worn, one loose.

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
• A new weapon: duplicate a sword's item, equipment definition and actor Blueprint into your own folder. See Add a weapon.
  • New armour: duplicate an ID_XenoCore_* armour item and keep Equipment Definition at ED_XenoCore_Armour. See Add armour.
  • A new equipment stat: one modifier row on GE_XenoCore_EquipmentStats plus a XenoCore.Stat.* tag. No graph edit. Two parts need a programmer: a brand-new attribute, and making the menus draw the stat at all (the list of stats the menus show is in C++). See Add an equipment stat.
  • A new slot needs a programmer, plus a change to every screen that lays out six slots.
  • Do not add a separate stats effect per item: the one shared effect is filled from each item's own numbers, so an item is pure data.
For programmers: classes and extension points

The component is UXenoCoreEquipmentComponent, a subclass of ULyraEquipmentManagerComponent. The stats ability's C++ parent is UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_EquipmentStats: it calls Get Item For Equipment, then fills every Set By Caller tag named by the effect's own modifiers from the item instance's stat tags (0 where absent, percent stats divided by 100). Weapon attachment to a VRoid body goes through Get Weapon Attach Parent; the weapon instance's SetDrawn asks it on every draw and sheathe. Weapon types are UXenoCoreWeaponTypeDefinition; the arm ability asks Get Weapon Arm Montage and SetDrawn asks Resolve Weapon Anim Layer. The stats the menus draw are UXenoCoreInventoryStatics::GetStatDefinitions (XenoCoreInventoryStatics.cpp); slots are EXenoCoreEquipSlot (XenoCoreEquipmentComponent.h).

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers
  • Subclass, not a sibling component. Lyra's own code finds the equipment manager with FindComponentByClass<ULyraEquipmentManagerComponent>, which finds ours. A second component beside Lyra's would have left those lookups finding the wrong one.
  • On the pawn. Equipment spawns the meshes animation depends on, so it stays with the body. Inventory is data, so it lives on the controller.
  • One SetByCaller effect. One effect asset per item would be two hand-made assets per item, and would make the comparison screen price an item by equipping it. The stats come from the item's own InventoryFragment_SetStats, which Lyra already writes onto the instance.
  • Get Item For Equipment. Lyra's EquipItem spawns the instance and grants its abilities in one call, so the stats ability runs before the slot is recorded. The component remembers the item for the length of that call, so the ability can find it immediately rather than a frame later, which once showed a new weapon's name with zero attack.
  • Weight in the roll only, so the sheet and the item that caused it never disagree.

docs.title: Events you can listen to
docs.text:
Designers and programmers · 10 min read · Simple Blueprints

Who this is for: anyone making a Blueprint react to the game (a HUD element that updates when the party changes, a door that opens when a quest is turned in). The Sent by column and the notes marked For programmers are for C++ readers; a designer needs only the channel and payload.

When something changes in the game (the bag, the party, a quest, the locked-on target), XenoCore announces it on a gameplay message channel, using Lyra's Gameplay Message Router. A channel is a gameplay tag; a message carries a small struct. Any Blueprint can listen without knowing who sends it, which is how every XenoCore screen and HUD element stays current. The idea that makes the rest make sense: each channel has exactly one sender, and most messages only say "this changed, read it again", so a listener always re-reads the owning component rather than trusting a copy.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
• Sender: one XenoCore system per channel announces the change. Each tag below is broadcast from one place only.
  • Listener: a Blueprint uses the Listen for Gameplay Messages node (below).
  • Channels are gameplay tags, so they appear in the tag picker.
For programmers

Senders call UGameplayMessageSubsystem::BroadcastMessage; C++ listeners use UGameplayMessageSubsystem::RegisterListener. The channel tags are native, declared in Source/XenoCoreRuntime/Public/XenoCoreGameplayTags.h.

docs.title: The channels
docs.text:
Channel Payload struct and fields Sent by When XenoCore.Inventory.Message.Changed XenoCoreInventoryChangedMessage: Owner (the controller holding the bag), Item Def, New Count, Delta (negative for a removal) UXenoCoreInventoryStatics (also UXenoCoreInventoryWatchSubsystem, for a change made around it) Every add or remove made through the inventory statics: pickups, chest takes, quest turn-ins, shop and trade, save restore XenoCore.Equipment.Message.SlotChanged XenoCoreEquipmentSlotChangedMessage: Owner (the character), Slot, Item (empty when the slot was emptied) UXenoCoreEquipmentComponent on that character Something was equipped into, or removed from, a slot XenoCore.Party.Message.Changed XenoCorePartyChangedMessage: Owning Controller, Active Count UXenoCorePartyComponent A member joined, left, was benched or brought in, or the leader changed XenoCore.Party.Message.Wiped XenoCorePartyWipedMessage: Owning Controller, Phase (Defeated or Respawned), Respawn Transform UXenoCorePartyComponent Twice per party wipe: Defeated when every active member is down, before the fade (the respawn point is already decided, so a "defeated" card can name it); Respawned when the party stands again at full health and the fade back in starts. Nothing in the plugin listens; use it for a defeat card or a "returned to..." line XenoCore.Party.Message.TacticChanged XenoCoreTacticChangedMessage: Owning Controller, Member (empty for the whole party), Tactic, Value (-1 when a member went back to following the party) UXenoCorePartyComponent A party tactic changed, for the party or one member XenoCore.PartyGauge.Message.Changed XenoCorePartyGaugeChangedMessage: Old Points, New Points, Max Points, Points Per Bar, Reason (a XenoCore.PartyGauge.Reason.* tag; empty for the out-of-battle drain) UXenoCorePartyGaugeComponent The Party Gauge moved. Unlike most channels it carries the numbers, so a HUD can animate from old to new XenoCore.PartyGauge.Message.Refused XenoCorePartyGaugeChangedMessage (old and new points are equal) UXenoCorePartyGaugeComponent The player asked for bars the gauge does not have, such as a revive with less than one bar. The gauge widget shakes its short bars XenoCore.Progression.Message.Changed XenoCoreProgressionChangedMessage: Owning Controller, Levelled Count, Experience Awarded, Gains (a list of Member, Experience, Art Points, Skill Points) UXenoCoreProgressionComponent Experience, Art Points or Skill Points were banked, anyone levelled, gold changed, or skill progress changed. A kill sends one message for its EXP, AP and SP together XenoCore.Progression.Message.LevelUp XenoCoreLevelUpMessage: Owning Controller, Levelled (a list of Member, Level Before, Level After) UXenoCoreProgressionComponent Once per award that levelled at least one character. One message for the whole party XenoCore.Skills.Message.SkillLearnt XenoCoreSkillLearntMessage: Member, Branch (row name), Index (0 to 4), Skill Name UXenoCoreProgressionComponent A character learnt a skill, once per skill. Nothing in the plugin listens to it; the "Skill Learnt" float is drawn directly. See Skills XenoCore.Enemy.Message.Defeated XenoCoreEnemyDefeatedMessage: Enemy Class, Display Name, Level AXenoCoreEnemyCharacter An enemy's death starts. Display Name is empty if the enemy has none authored XenoCore.Battle.Message.Won XenoCoreBattleWonMessage: Celebrants (every living party body told to sheathe and celebrate) UXenoCoreBattleVictorySubsystem A battle was won: an enemy died and no living enemy is still fighting the party. Never sent for a retreat. The fanfare, the disarm and the victory emotes follow; area music fades its battle track on it XenoCore.Quest.Message.Changed XenoCoreQuestChangedMessage: Owning Controller UXenoCoreQuestComponent Any quest was accepted, declined, progressed, turned in, restored, or the tracked quest changed XenoCore.Quest.Message.TurnedIn XenoCoreQuestTurnedInMessage: Quest, Quest Title, Gold, Experience, Items UXenoCoreQuestComponent A quest was handed in. Carries what it paid XenoCore.Targeting.Message.TargetChanged XenoCoreTargetChangedMessage: Seeker, New Target, Old Target The target mode ability (UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_TargetMode) The locked-on target changed. New Target is empty when target mode ends XenoCore.Battle.Message.Notification XenoCoreBattleNotification: Target, Text, Colour, Scale, Punch UXenoCoreBattleNotifySubsystem (anyone may call its Notify) A word pops over a character: the damage calculation raises MISS, CRITICAL HIT! and BLOCKED XenoCore.Loot.Message.ChestOpened XenoCoreChestOpenedMessage: Chest, Tier, Offered (item definitions) AXenoCoreTreasureChest A chest was opened and its contents rolled, before anything enters the bag XenoCore.Collectable.Message.Collected XenoCoreCollectableCollectedMessage: Item Def, Instance, Orb AXenoCoreCollectableOrb A collectable orb was picked up XenoCore.Voice.Message.Spoke XenoCoreVoiceSpokeMessage: Speaker, Category, Take (sound and lip-sync keys), Expression, Expression Weight, Subtitle, Duration UXenoCoreBattleVoiceSubsystem A party member's voice line starts. See Battle voices XenoCore.Time.Message.PhaseChanged, .HourBlockChanged, .Jumped XenoCoreTimeChangedMessage: Minutes, Old Phase, New Phase, Hour Block, Jumped UXenoCoreTimeOfDaySubsystem The phase changed (Morning, Day, Evening, Night); a new three-hour block began; the clock was jumped (Change Time, a load). A jump across several phases sends one message with the final phase. See Time of day and weather XenoCore.Weather.Message.Changed XenoCoreWeatherChangedMessage: Old Weather, New Weather, Instant UXenoCoreWeatherSubsystem The weather changed. Instant is true when it snapped rather than blended

The Owner of an inventory message is the player controller, because the party bag lives there. The Owner of an equipment message is the character wearing the gear.

docs.title: Listening from Blueprint
docs.text:
1. In any Blueprint with a world (a widget, an actor, a component), add Listen for Gameplay Messages. Do it once, for example on Event Construct or Begin Play.
  2. Set Channel to the tag, for example XenoCore.Quest.Message.Changed.
  3. Set Payload Type to the matching struct from the table. It must match exactly.
  4. From On Message Received, use the Payload pin, split or break it, and react.
  5. For a "changed" message, re-read the owning component (for example Get Party Quests then Get Status) rather than reading details from the message.

Match Type can be left at Exact Match. Partial Match would also receive child tags, which no XenoCore channel has today.

The wrong Payload Type drops the message

If Payload Type does not match the struct the sender uses, your node never fires. The only sign is a Struct type mismatch on channel error in the Output Log, easy to miss during play. Copy the struct name from the table.

Fails silently: listening again every time a screen opens

CommonUI reuses screens. If you start listening in On Activated, each visit adds another listener and the handler runs several times. Listen once, from Construct.

docs.title: The rule for the bag
docs.text:
Every change to the party bag goes through the XenoCore inventory nodes

Add and remove items with the XenoCore › Inventory nodes (Add Item to Party, Remove Item from Party, Consume Items From Party and the rest), never with the Lyra inventory component's own functions such as Add Item Definition. The statics broadcast XenoCore.Inventory.Message.Changed at once, honour carry caps and never take a worn item. A change made any other way is caught by a watcher that broadcasts it a frame later, but it gets none of those protections.

Two consequences worth knowing:

  • Lyra's own inventory message does not fire here. Lyra's Lyra.Inventory.Message.StackChanged is only sent from replication callbacks, which a single-player game never runs. That is why XenoCore has its own channel.
  • Item costs go through the statics. The Party Item (XenoCore) ability cost spends items with Consume Items From Party, so an item spent as a cost sends the message too. (Lyra's own Inventory Item cost is switched off in stock Lyra and never lets an ability activate.)

The same one-sender rule holds for gold (through the progression component), the party (the party component) and quests (the quest component).

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
• A new channel for your own system: add a tag in Project Settings › Project › GameplayTags (for example MyGame.Door.Message.Opened), make a Blueprint Structure for the payload, and send it with Lyra's Broadcast Message node from exactly one place. Listeners use Listen for Gameplay Messages with that structure. Prefer "this changed, re-read me" messages; add details only when a listener cannot reconstruct them, as the quest turn-in payout does. (In C++: a native tag and a USTRUCT(BlueprintType) with BlueprintReadOnly fields.)
  • Raising a battle notification from a Blueprint: call the Notify node (XenoCore › Battle) with a target actor, text and colour. The message and the popup follow.
  • The full list of tags is on Gameplay tags, and the payload structs with every field on Gameplay messages.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers
  • Lyra's router, not delegates. A message needs no reference between sender and listener, so a HUD widget can react to the party component without ever finding it, and a new screen needs no change to the system it watches. It is the same router Lyra uses for its own events.
  • One sender per channel. If two systems broadcast the same channel, a listener cannot know which view of the world is current. Keeping one broadcaster per channel is what makes "re-read on message" safe.
  • Thin messages. A message carrying a snapshot can be stale by the time it is read. A message saying "read again" cannot. The two exceptions (turn-in payout, level-up list) carry facts that cannot be re-read afterwards.

Next: Reference: gameplay messages · Quests

docs.title: Input and camera
docs.text:
All · 12 min read · No code

What the player sees: every button does one thing at a time, depending on the moment: A jumps, talks to an NPC, or uses the selected Art; the triggers switch the party leader; buttons go quiet behind a menu. The camera follows the leader on a boom, recentres on a button, blends to a new leader on a switch, and frames both speakers in a conversation.

XenoCore uses Lyra's input chain unchanged: a key is mapped to an input action by a mapping context, the action raises an input tag (a gameplay tag), and the tag starts whichever ability was granted with it. So almost every button in XenoCore is a small input ability named GA_XenoCore_*. The camera is built with Unreal's Gameplay Cameras plugin: a camera component on each playable character runs a camera asset, which runs a rig. The idea that makes the rest make sense: the input you press never talks to a system directly. It raises a tag, and the ability system decides whether anything may happen right now. That is also why a menu, a conversation or target mode can switch buttons off without touching the bindings.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
• Which key does what: the rows of Input/Mappings/IMC_XenoCore (Settings).
  • A new button with an on-screen prompt: Add an input action with a button prompt.
  • The exploration and conversation camera: Tune the camera.
  • When a button is blocked (in a menu, in a conversation): rows of Game/TagRelationships_XenoCore.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:

docs.title: Camera
docs.text: Piece Job Cameras/CA_XenoCore_Player The camera asset. A single-rig director that always runs the explore rig Cameras/CameraRig_XenoCore_Explore The exploration camera: boom arm, collision push, position and rotation damping, offset, field of view Cameras/CameraRig_XenoCore_Dialogue The conversation camera: field of view and the XenoCore Dialogue Framing node, blended in and out Gameplay camera component on Game/B_XenoCore_Player and Characters/Party/B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base Runs CA_XenoCore_Player for that character

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
A press. Enhanced Input fires the action. Lyra's hero component turns it into the input tag, and the ability system activates the ability granted with that tag, unless something blocks it.

One press, one activation. Every IA_XenoCore_* action carries a Pressed trigger. Without a trigger, Enhanced Input fires every frame the key is held. An ability that ends on the same frame it starts (most input abilities do) would then run again on each of those frames, so one tap became several presses.

Blocking by state. TagRelationships_XenoCore blocks abilities while a state tag is on the player. Its rows:

Ability tag Blocked while the body has Ability.Type.Action.Jump (Lyra's jump) Status.XenoCore.Looting (the prompt holds A), .TargetMode, .Dialogue, .Downed Ability.XenoCore.Art Status.XenoCore.Dialogue, .Defence Ability.XenoCore.AutoAttack, Ability.XenoCore.TargetMode, Ability.XenoCore.ToggleMenu Status.XenoCore.Dialogue Ability.XenoCore (every XenoCore ability) Status.XenoCore.Downed

A row keyed on a parent tag such as Ability.XenoCore.Art covers every Art, including ones you add later. An ability with no ability tags cannot be reached by any row.

Tap and hold on one key. The triggers carry two input actions each. IA_XenoCore_PartySwitchPrev (LT, Z) and IA_XenoCore_PartySwitch (RT, C) have a Tap trigger; IA_XenoCore_PartySelect (all four keys) has a Hold trigger. Both use 0.25 s, so a short press switches and a long one opens the party cursor. The three switch abilities differ only in Mode (Next, Previous, Select) in their Class Defaults, and they live in the leader-only set, so only the body you drive holds them. While the cursor is open the D-pad (arrow keys) moves it instead of the Arts palette; left, right and confirm do nothing, so a stray press cannot fire an Art.

Fails silently: a one-shot Hold trigger

IA_XenoCore_PartySelect's Hold trigger has Is One Shot off. With it on, the trigger reports a release on the frame after it fires, so the cursor opens and commits at once and the hold looks like a tap. Keep it off on any hold-to-open input.

Menus. While a menu screen is open, IMC_XenoCore and IMC_Default switch off, so nothing in the game world can react to a key behind a menu. That is set project-wide in Config/DefaultInput.ini (the default mapping-context query asks for InputMode.Game), and needs no setting on each mapping context.

Enter and Space click. Config/DefaultGame.ini sets CommonUI's Common Button Accept Key Handling to TriggerClick (Project Settings › Plugins › Common UI Framework › Button), so Enter and Space press the focused menu button, as the pad's A does.

X is shared with Trade. While the interaction prompt offers a second verb (Trade, at a trader NPC), tap X is Trade and does not change the tactic.

The camera runs on every playable character all the time, but only the character the player is viewing steers the view. Switching the party leader switches which one that is: the view blends from where it was over Switch Camera Blend Time (0.35 s, on BP_XenoCore_Party). In battle it then turns onto the locked enemy; out of battle it turns to face the new leader's forward.

  • Recentre: GA_XenoCore_CameraReset sweeps the view round behind whichever character you are driving: over Recentre Duration (0.35 s) it turns toward the character's facing at Recentre Pitch (−10°). It works for whichever character leads. To recentre on something else, such as the locked target, make a child Blueprint of GA_XenoCore_CameraReset and override its Get Recentre Rotation function.
  • Conversations stop look input, so the camera cannot turn while a line is on screen, and blend in CameraRig_XenoCore_Dialogue: over the player's shoulder at the NPC, close enough to read, held still until the conversation ends. See Interaction, NPCs and dialogue.

docs.text:

Copy the context rather than editing Lyra's Action to tag InputData_XenoCore › Native Input Actions, Ability Input Actions Which tag each action raises Tag to ability AbilitySet_XenoCore_Input › Granted Gameplay Abilities › Input Tag Which ability a tag activates, for every playable body at once Blocking rules TagRelationships_XenoCore Which states block which abilities Boom length, offset, damping, collision, field of view CameraRig_XenoCore_Explore Exploration camera feel Focus Bias, Distance, Orbit Angle, Elevation, Box Headroom, field of view, blend times CameraRig_XenoCore_Dialogue › XenoCore Dialogue Framing node, Field of View node, transitions The conversation shot. The camera backs off from Distance only as far as it must to fit both heads and the box over them Dialogue Camera Rig Project Settings › XenoCore Content › Dialogue Which rig conversations use. Clear it to leave the camera alone Party-switch keys and tap/hold time IA_XenoCore_PartySwitch, IA_XenoCore_PartySwitchPrev, IA_XenoCore_PartySelect › Triggers Which keys switch and open the cursor, and how long a press must be to count as a hold (0.25 s) Switch Camera Blend Time BP_XenoCore_Party › XenoCore › Party › Switch The camera blend on a leader switch. 0 cuts Recentre Duration, Recentre Interp Speed, Recentre Pitch Input/Abilities/GA_XenoCore_CameraReset › XenoCore › Camera The recentre sweep: its length (0.35 s; 0 snaps), speed (8) and final pitch (−10°)

See Tune the camera and Add an input action with a button prompt.

Several keys are shared

Pad A is Jump, Interact and Palette Confirm; Space is Jump and Palette Confirm; pad B is Crouch and Leave Target Mode. Each trigger carries a tap action and a hold action on purpose. Which one wins depends on state and on the blocking rules above. InputData_XenoCore also maps Lyra's Crouch.

Fails silently: a new one-shot action with no trigger

If you add an input action without a Pressed trigger and bind it to an ability that ends at once, one tap fires the ability several times. Nothing is logged. Add the Pressed trigger to every new button action.

IMC_XenoCore's priority is load-bearing

IMC_XenoCore is added at priority 2, above Lyra's IMC_Default (1) and any context at 0 another plugin adds on the same keys. Lowering it to 0 lets such a context win the tie, and the pad's look stick can stop working.

Fails silently: an input ability granted twice

Granting an input ability in AbilitySet_XenoCore_Input and in AbilitySet_XenoCore_Hero or AbilitySet_XenoCore_PartyMember gives that body two copies, and one press activates both. Grant input abilities only in AbilitySet_XenoCore_Input.

Button prompts. A prompt on a menu's action bar comes from a CommonUI action row, such as the rows in UserInterface/Foundation/DT_XenoCore_Actions, not from an Enhanced Input action. Some of those rows exist only to draw a glyph for an Enhanced Input button (the quest tracker toggle on View/Back and J, dismissing a banner). Such a row must name the same key as the mapping context; nothing checks it at runtime, so a mismatch is a prompt that lies.

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
• A new button: create an input action with a Pressed trigger, add a key row to your copy of the mapping context, add an action-to-tag row to the input config, and grant an ability with that tag in AbilitySet_XenoCore_Input, once. See Add an input action with a prompt.
  • Rebinding keys: edit IMC_XenoCore (a XenoCore asset). For Lyra's keys, make your own mapping context and add it in your own Experience or game feature rather than editing IMC_Default.
  • A different camera: duplicate CameraRig_XenoCore_Explore and CA_XenoCore_Player into Content/MyGame/Cameras/, change the rig, and point the camera components at your camera asset.
  • An Art close-up for another Art: copy the start and stop camera-modifier nodes from GA_XenoCore_TurnStrike.
For programmers: classes

The full-screen minimap ability is UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_MinimapOverlay; the three switch abilities are Blueprint children of UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_PartySwitch; the recentre is a child of UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_CameraRecentre. Menus filter mapping contexts through Enhanced Input's mode filtering: DefaultMappingContextInputModeQuery and DefaultInputMode in Config/DefaultInput.ini both carry InputMode.Game, which CommonUI adds and removes. The conversation camera is started as a global camera modifier rig, and look input is held with SetIgnoreLookInput.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers
  • Lyra's chain, untouched. Input actions to tags to abilities is Lyra's own design, so every Lyra rule (blocking, relationships, cooldowns) applies to XenoCore buttons for free.
  • Blocking by state, not by input. A state tag plus a relationship row is data: the widget or system that owns the state knows nothing about which buttons it blocks.
  • Menus filter contexts. CommonUI already reports Game and Menu modes to Enhanced Input. The project default query makes gameplay contexts listen to it, with no change to Lyra's assets.
  • Gameplay Cameras. Rigs are data assets a designer tunes in the editor, and a camera modifier rig layers a close-up on top without replacing the exploration camera.

Next: Events you can listen to · Targeting

docs.title: Interaction, NPCs and dialogue
docs.text:
All · 15 min read · No code

What the player sees: walking up to something usable shows a prompt beside the character ("A Talk", "A Open", sometimes "X Trade"), and the button does exactly that. Talking to someone frames the two speakers with the camera, shows each line in a box over the speaker's head, and waits for A between lines.

Every interactable thing decides its own prompt word and range, and XenoCore picks the nearest one in range. An NPC's On Interact event (in its Blueprint graph) decides what talking does: play some lines, offer a quest, open a shop, recruit a party member. The idea that makes the rest make sense: what the prompt shows is exactly what the button does, because the press acts on whatever the prompt last offered.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
• A talking NPC: Make an NPC talk.
  • A conversation with choices: Branch a conversation.
  • An NPC who gives a quest, or is a quest's target: Quests, Give a quest to defeat enemies, talk to someone, or go somewhere.
  • An NPC who joins the party: Recruit a party member from an NPC.
  • A shopkeeper or trader: Open a shop, Set up a trade.
  • A lever, door, sign or pickup: Add an interactable object.
  • How the prompt, name plate and dialogue box look: Extending it.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Piece Kind Job Interaction system Built in, nothing to place Picks the nearest interactable in range every 0.2 s, draws the prompt, routes the button XenoCoreInteractableActor Parent class for your Blueprints A door, lever, sign or pickup. Two verb fields; Can Interact, On Interact, On Focused, On Unfocused events UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_InteractPrompt Widget, set by Interact Prompt in XenoCore UI settings The "button + verb" chips beside the player. It can draw four; the subsystem sends it at most two Input/Abilities/GA_XenoCore_InteractPress and GA_XenoCore_InteractPressSecondary Input abilities Call Handle Interact Press with verb 0 (A) or verb 1 (X) Characters/NPC/B_XenoCore_Npc NPC Blueprint A townsperson: name plate, quest marker, idle clip, the On Interact event. Starts blank: no lines, no quest, no marker Characters/NPC/B_XenoCore_Npc_Sample Child of B_XenoCore_Npc A finished example carrying the sample lines and the sample quest DA_XenoCore_Quest_Collection01 UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_NpcLabel Widget The name, chevron and quest bubble over an NPC's head, as one widget Dialogue system Built in, nothing to place Shows one line at a time over the speaker, waits for A, holds the player still Characters/NPC/BP_XenoCore_DialogueAnchor Actor Blueprint, set by XenoCore Content › Dialogue Anchor Carries the dialogue box and attaches it to whoever is speaking UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_DialogueBox Widget The speech box itself Cameras/CameraRig_XenoCore_Dialogue, set by XenoCore Content › Dialogue Camera Rig Camera rig (Field of View + XenoCore Dialogue Framing node) Moves the camera in over the player's shoulder for a conversation and back out after Show Dialogue, Play Dialogue, Close Dialogue Blueprint nodes (XenoCore › Dialogue) One line and wait; a whole list of lines then close; close the box and release the player

The treasure chest (see Loot) is found the same way. Lyra's own interaction ability, Input/Abilities/GA_XenoCore_Interact, is still granted by Game/AbilitySet_XenoCore_Interact, but it no longer decides what A does. It still traces for Lyra interactables and, while it finds one, holds Status.XenoCore.InteractAvailable, which stops Palette Confirm; the gameplay event it waits on (XenoCore.Event.Interact) is sent by nothing.

The interaction abilities reach the player through the party, not through the pawn data: AbilitySet_XenoCore_Interact is the party's Leader Only Ability Set, granted to whichever body the player drives. (Experiences/B_XenoCore_Experience also grants it to LyraPlayerState, where it does nothing.)

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Registering. An NPC, a chest or a child of XenoCoreInteractableActor signs itself up when the level starts playing and signs off when it is removed. Nothing to set up.

Choosing. Every 0.2 seconds XenoCore looks at every interactable, skips any that say they are unavailable (an opened chest, for example), and takes the nearest one within that actor's own range, measured from the player character's location to the actor's origin. The prompt then shows the actor's verbs: the main verb on A and the first extra verb on X. Any further verbs are dropped (see below). When the chosen actor changes, the old one is told it lost focus and then the new one that it has it. While the prompt is up, A does not also jump, and that lasts 0.5 s after the prompt goes away, so a held button does not turn into a jump.

Hidden prompt. The prompt hides whenever the world is covered: a menu is open, a quest reward or level-up banner is showing, or a panel has suppressed it (the loot panel, a conversation).

Pressing. The press runs in a fixed order:

  1. If a conversation is on screen, A advances it. Nothing else happens.
  2. If the world is covered by a banner, A dismisses the newest banner early.
  3. Otherwise A acts on whatever the prompt is currently offering, and nothing else. No prompt, no interaction.

Talking. Before the graph runs, an NPC with a Quest Id counts as talked to for every active quest whose Talk To NPC objective names it (so a last step at the quest giver hands in during the same conversation). Then its Blueprint event On Interact runs, with the pressed verb's index. The shipped B_XenoCore_Npc graph branches on Is Trade Verb, plays dialogue, offers or turns in its quest, recruits its Member To Recruit if it has one, and opens a shop at the end of the conversation if it has a Shop Table (see Quests and Shops and trade).

Recruiting. An NPC with Member To Recruit set adds that character to the party at the end of the talk (or after a turn-in, when Recruit After Quest names a quest that must be complete first). The member arrives at least at the party's level, their body steps into the NPC's place, and the NPC leaves. On every other NPC this does nothing. See Recruit a party member from an NPC.

Party members are interactables too: out of battle, stopping beside a companion offers Talk (a voiced line, see Battle voices), and a downed ally offers Revive (see Party Gauge, downed and revive).

A conversation. The first line puts the player on hold:

  • The player cannot move or turn the camera, so the camera cannot swing the box around.
  • The dialogue camera blends in (0.6 s) to frame the player and the NPC, and holds that shot for the whole conversation; replies move the box, never the camera. When the conversation closes it blends back (0.5 s) to exactly where the camera was.
  • The player and the NPC turn to face each other (XenoCore Content › Dialogue Turn Seconds, 0.3 s). After the conversation the NPC turns back to how it was placed; the player stays facing it.
  • Arts, the auto-attack and target mode are blocked (by rows in Game/TagRelationships_XenoCore).
  • The interaction prompt and the NPC's own name plate hide.

Each line appears over the speaker's head. The first A press finishes the typing effect, the next advances. Close Dialogue releases all of it. It does nothing when no conversation is open, so it is safe to end every branch with it.

A conversation left open. A conversation that is open, has no line waiting for A, and has no quest, trade or shop panel covering the box can never move on: A has nothing to advance. The dialogue system checks for exactly that state 2 seconds after each A press, after a panel closes, and after an NPC's On Interact returns. If it finds it, it logs a LogXenoDialogue warning naming the NPC and closes the conversation, so the player is never stuck. The check waits 2 seconds because a graph may do other work between two lines; a pause longer than that closes the box and the next line reopens it.

docs.text:
