Each dialogue line has three fields: Speaker (the name on the plate; empty means "use the actor's own name"), Line (keep it under 165 characters or a warning is logged), and Source (Npc or Player: whose head the box sits over).

On Blueprint class defaults:

Setting Where it lives What it does Overhead Widget Class, Overhead Height B_XenoCore_Npc › XenoCore › NPC › Overhead The plate widget and where its bottom edge sits Box Height BP_XenoCore_DialogueAnchor › XenoCore › Dialogue How far above the speaker the dialogue box's bottom edge sits. Default 120 Box Widget Class BP_XenoCore_DialogueAnchor › XenoCore › Dialogue The dialogue box widget. Empty uses XenoCore UI › Dialogue Box Bob Amplitude, Bob Speed W_XenoCore_NpcLabel › XenoCore › NPC The chevron's bounce

A Show Dialogue chain that never closes

Show Dialogue does not close the box, and Play Dialogue does. End every branch that uses Show Dialogue with Close Dialogue. A branch that forgets is closed for you after 2 seconds, with a LogXenoDialogue warning: "conversation with ... was left open with no line waiting - closing it." The player is released, but the last line hangs on screen for those 2 seconds, so treat the warning as a bug in the graph.

Branch on Is Trade Verb, never on Verb Index

Trade is inserted before your Extra Interact Verbs, so the verb numbers move when you add one. A graph comparing Verb Index to 1 opens the wrong thing without any error.

Only two verbs: a third is dropped

Only A (IA_XenoCore_Interact, verb 0) and X (IA_XenoCore_InteractSecondary, verb 1) have inputs. Every interactable's list is cut to two before the prompt draws it, and the press checks the same list, so a third verb is neither drawn nor pressable. It logs one warning per actor (LogXenoInteract: "offers N verbs but only 2 interact inputs exist (A, X) - dropping ..."). An NPC with a Trade Offers table already uses X for Trade, so its Extra Interact Verbs are all dropped.

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
• A new NPC: place B_XenoCore_Npc (or your own child of it under Content/MyGame/) and fill in the per-instance fields. It starts blank; copy settings from B_XenoCore_Npc_Sample if you want a worked example. A town is one class with many placed actors, not a Blueprint per person. See the recipe Make an NPC talk.
  • A place a quest sends you to: place a XenoCore Quest Location (in Place Actors) and give it a Location Id matching the objective's Target Id. It counts when the leader walks in; it has no prompt. See Give a quest to defeat enemies, talk to someone, or go somewhere.
  • Branching conversations: replace the Play Dialogue node in On Interact with a chain of Show Dialogue nodes and ordinary Blueprint branches. See Branch a conversation.
  • Anything else the player can use (a lever, a door, a sign): create a Blueprint Class with XenoCoreInteractableActor as its parent, set Interact Verb, Secondary Interact Verb and Interact Range, and handle On Interact. It registers itself. Set Interact Enabled switches it off and makes the prompt re-decide at once; override Can Interact for conditions. See Add an interactable object.
  • Restyling: duplicate W_XenoCore_InteractPrompt, W_XenoCore_DialogueBox or W_XenoCore_NpcLabel into your own folder and change the look. Point Project Settings › Game › XenoCore UI › Interact Prompt or Dialogue Box at your copy (the name label is set on the NPC's Overhead Widget Class). The dialogue anchor itself is XenoCore Content › Dialogue Anchor. Keep the parent class, and see The two settings pages for the cooking caveat.

Never edit the chest's Lyra side or Lyra's interaction ability; the chest's behaviour lives in XenoCore.

For programmers: classes

UXenoCoreInteractionSubsystem (world subsystem) keeps the registry, picks the nearest actor, draws the prompt and routes the press (Handle Interact Press, called by GA_XenoCore_InteractPress / GA_XenoCore_InteractPressSecondary with verb 0 or 1; the list is capped by MaxPressableVerbs in Get Offered Verbs). Anything with a prompt implements IXenoCoreInteractable and registers in BeginPlay / unregisters in EndPlay; AXenoCoreInteractableActor does that for Blueprint children, and a C++ class implementing the interface directly must do it itself. The NPC is AXenoCoreNpcCharacter (its Interact calls On Interact), the label UXenoCoreWorldLabelBase, the prompt UXenoCoreInteractPromptBase, dialogue UXenoCoreDialogueSubsystem with AXenoCoreDialogueAnchor. The chest implements both IXenoCoreInteractable and Lyra's IInteractableTarget. While the prompt is up the player holds Status.XenoCore.Looting; a conversation adds Gameplay.MovementStopped, Status.XenoCore.Dialogue and SetIgnoreLookInput.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers
  • Proximity, not aim. Lyra's interaction ability scans with a camera line trace, which answers "what am I looking at". Every prompt here means "what is near me", so XenoCore uses a registry and a distance check instead. Lyra's option list is also protected on an unexported class, so C++ outside Lyra cannot read it.
  • One owner for the button. A is also Jump (Lyra) and Palette Confirm, so the subsystem both shows the prompt and claims the button. A second system drawing its own prompt would be a second owner of the same button.
  • A base class for designers, not a Blueprint interface. Making the interface Blueprint-implementable would have left every Blueprint responsible for registering itself, and forgetting reads as "my lever has no prompt" with nothing logged. AXenoCoreInteractableActor registers in its own Begin Play, which a child's Begin Play runs inside.
  • Two verb fields, not a list. Only two interact buttons exist, so the base cannot express a third one nobody can press.
  • Each actor owns its range. The prompt, the name plate and the press all read one number from the actor, so nothing can show at one distance and act at another.
  • Blueprint decides what happens. C++ decides when someone was talked to; the NPC's On Interact graph decides what happens. Blueprint is already a branching editor with breakpoints, so there is no custom dialogue-tree asset.
  • The box is attached, not projected. The dialogue box is a screen-space widget component on an anchor actor that attaches to the speaker, so it moves in step with the rendered frame.
  • Holding the camera as well as the pawn. Gameplay.MovementStopped only reaches the movement component. Look input goes straight to the controller, so the dialogue subsystem also calls SetIgnoreLookInput. Both are counters, and the subsystem balances them.

Next: Quests · Shops and trade · Events you can listen to

docs.title: Items and inventory
docs.text:
All · 15 min read

The Items menu, with rarity-coloured names.

What the player sees: one bag shared by the whole party. The Items menu sorts it into tabs (Equipment, Items, Collectables, Key, Gems, Crystals, Materials, Art Manuals), every item name is coloured by its rarity, an "Obtained" badge appears when something is picked up, and any character can equip from the bag.

An item is a small Blueprint (an item definition) whose Details panel holds a few fragments: blocks of settings for its menu tab, description, rarity, equipment slot and stats. Making an item is duplicating one that is close and changing those settings.

The one rule for Blueprints that give or take items: use the XenoCore inventory nodes (XenoCore › Inventory, such as Add Item To Party), not Lyra's. They keep every menu current, honour carry limits and never take an item someone is wearing.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
• A new consumable, material or key item: Consumable item.
  • A new weapon or piece of armour: Add a weapon, Add armour.
  • A gem: Add a gem.
  • Rarity tiers and how they look: Set and style item rarity.
  • Y-to-sort on a list: Add Y-to-sort to an item list.
  • Category glyphs: UserInterface/Foundation/DA_XenoCore_ItemIcons (see Settings).
  • What a new game starts with: Starting Inventory on a party member (see Equipment).

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text: Piece Class / sample asset Job The bag ULyraInventoryManagerComponent on the player controller, added by the plugin's Game Feature (XenoCore) Holds item instances Finding the bag Node Get Party Inventory (XenoCore › Inventory) The only way to find the bag from a Blueprint Item parent Inventory/BP_XenoItemDefinition Parent Blueprint of the shipped items Items Inventory/Items/ID_XenoCore_*, Inventory/Armour/ID_XenoCore_*, Inventory/Gems/ID_XenoCore_Gem_*, Weapons/*/ID_XenoCore_* One Blueprint per item XenoCore fragments XenoCoreFragment_EquipSlots, XenoCoreFragment_ItemCategory, XenoCoreFragment_ItemDisplay, XenoCoreFragment_Gem Slots, weapon type and sockets; menu tab, carry cap and rarity; description and icon; what a gem adds Lyra fragments InventoryFragment_EquippableItem, InventoryFragment_SetStats What equipping spawns and grants; the item's stat numbers Category icons UserInterface/Foundation/DA_XenoCore_ItemIcons One glyph per category or slot for items with no icon of their own Menus UserInterface/W_XenoCore_ItemMenu, W_XenoCore_EquipmentScreen Browse the bag, equip from it HUD UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_ItemBadge "Obtained" badge

docs.title: Fragments on an item
docs.text:
Fragment Settings Notes XenoCoreFragment_ItemCategory Category, Max Carried, Sell Value, Sort Order, Rarity Category picks the Items menu tab: Equipment, Items, Collectables, Key, Gems, Crystals, Materials, Art Manuals. Max Carried 0 = uncapped. Rarity is Common, Rare or Legendary; empty is Common. See Set and style item rarity XenoCoreFragment_ItemDisplay Description, Icon, Symbol, Symbol Colour See the warning on Symbol below XenoCoreFragment_EquipSlots Allowed Slots, Equip Type, Weapon Type, Override Gem Slots, Gem Slots, Fixed Gems Only on equipment. Empty means "not equipment". Equip Type is Light, Medium, Heavy or None. Weapon Type decides who may wield a weapon; the gem fields set its sockets. See Equipment XenoCoreFragment_Gem The gem's stat, rank and strength range Only on gems. Its strength is rolled when the gem is created. See Equipment › Gems InventoryFragment_EquippableItem (Lyra) Equipment Definition Only on equipment. See Equipment InventoryFragment_SetStats (Lyra) Initial Item Stats (tag → number) Stats under XenoCore.Stat.*, such as XenoCore.Stat.PhysicalDefence

An item with no category fragment falls back to Items. A non-equipment item such as ID_XenoCore_EtherCrystal carries only the category and display fragments; a piece of armour such as ID_XenoCore_BattleArmour carries all five.

docs.title: Checks on save
docs.text:
Saving an item definition (an ID_ asset), or running Asset Actions › Validate Assets on it, checks its fragments for setups that otherwise fail silently in play:

Check Result An empty entry in the fragment list Error Equip Slots but no Equippable Item fragment, or no Equipment Definition on it Error: the item would list in the swap menu and the click would do nothing An Equippable Item fragment but no Equip Slots fragment, or no Allowed Slots Error: the item could never be placed in a slot A weapon with no Weapon Type Warning: any character could wield it Equipment whose Category is not Equipment Warning: it shows on the wrong Items menu tab No display name Warning A gem with no Stat Tag, a Gem Id of 0, or Min Value above Max Value Error

The results appear in the Message Log window and the Output Log.

docs.title: Rarity
docs.text:
Xenoblade 3's model: Common, Rare and Legendary, drawn white, gold and purple with one to three pips (UserInterface/Items/T_XenoCore_RarityPip) in every menu that names an item. Names carry a thin dark outline and a soft shadow so a coloured name reads on a pale row, and every details pane has a labelled Rarity row.

  • Rarity is a property of the item definition. Nothing rolls it per drop, so the save format, quest counting and shop prices are unchanged. A Rare and a Common version of the same thing are two items, as in Xenoblade 3.
  • What a rarity looks like is a row of UserInterface/Items/DT_XenoCore_ItemRarities, set in Project Settings → XenoCore UI → Item Rarity Table.
  • Every screen colours names through the same rarity nodes (below), so no widget chooses a colour itself.
  • Apply Item Rarity / Apply Item Instance Rarity colour a name and fill a pip box.
  • Apply Item Rarity To Button does the same for a button labelled with Set Button Text.
  • Prefix With Item Rarity gives "Rare · Heavy".
  • A screen's own state colours win. An unaffordable row keeps its rarity colour, dimmed. A "(no room)" line stays red.
  • Rarity changes no price, as in Xenoblade 3.
  • A new game starts with one item of each tier in the leader's Starting Inventory.

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text:
Pressing Y on the Items menu or the equipment swap list cycles the list's order. The Items menu offers Default, Rarity, Name, Value and Most Recent. The swap list offers Default, Stat (Attack or Physical Def), Rarity, Name and Most Recent.

Each screen carries a UserInterface/Foundation/W_XenoCore_ItemSortControl, a placed widget that owns the Y prompt and re-sorts the list in place. Its Sort Items node sits between Get Items For … and Set List Items, so each list opens already sorted.

See Add Y-to-sort to an item list. The shop and trade screens have their own sort, through the merchant base.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Where the bag comes from. The plugin adds Lyra's inventory component to the player's controller. Get Party Inventory always returns that bag, whichever character asks. Do not look for a bag on an AI party member's controller: it is not the party's.

Starting contents. Each character's equipment component adds its Starting Inventory (loose items) and then its Starting Equipment (items it immediately wears) to the party bag when the character's ability system is ready. See Equipment.

One entry per item. Twelve Ether Crystals are twelve entries in the bag. Quantity is counted, not stored: Get Party Item Count counts entries. A list still shows "Ether Crystal x12"; only the storage is one per item.

Adding and removing. Always through the statics:

Node What it does Add Item To Party (Item Def, Count) Adds up to Count, honouring Max Carried. Returns how many went in Add One Item To Party Adds one and returns the new instance, or null if the cap left no room Remove Item From Party (Item Def, Count) Removes what is there, up to Count, and returns how many went Get Party Item Count How many of a definition the party holds Is Item Equipped By Anyone, Find Equipment Holding Whether, and by whom, an instance is worn, asked across the whole party Find Free Item By Definition A copy of an item that nobody is wearing Get Free Party Item Count How many of a definition the party holds that nobody is wearing: what can be spent or sold Remove Item Instance From Party (Item) Removes that exact item. Refuses and returns false if someone is wearing it or it is not in the bag Consume Items From Party (Item Def, Count) Spends exactly Count, or nothing at all. Returns false, removing nothing, when fewer than Count are free. Never takes a worn item

All of these are under XenoCore › Inventory. Every add and remove broadcasts XenoCore.Inventory.Message.Changed with the item definition, the new count and the change (positive gained, negative spent). A change of zero broadcasts nothing. Open menus, the item badge and quest counters listen for it. Chests and collectable orbs add through the same functions, so they update everything too.

Changes made another way. XenoCore compares the bag with what it last saw every frame (paused menus included). When something other than the XenoCore nodes changed it (Lyra's own inventory nodes, or Lyra's pickup interface), it broadcasts the same change message on that change's behalf and logs a line to LogXenoBagWatch: "The party bag changed outside the XenoCore inventory functions (+1 ...); announcing it on their behalf." So menus stay current. What it cannot do is undo a change: see the warnings below.

Items as an ability cost. An ability that spends items (a potion, an Art Manual) uses the Party Item (XenoCore) cost in its Additional Costs list. Set Item Definition and Quantity (a scalable float keyed on ability level; fractions round down). The ability cannot activate unless the party holds that many copies nobody is wearing, and it spends them through Consume Items From Party, so the change message fires. The cost looks up the party bag whoever casts, including an AI party member.

Equipped state. An item in the bag may be worn by one character in one slot. The bag does not move items when they are equipped; the equipment component only points at them.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Where it lives What it does Display Name Item Blueprint › Class Defaults (Lyra) The name shown everywhere Fragment settings Item Blueprint › Fragments See the table above Category Icons DA_XenoCore_ItemIcons › XenoCore › Inventory Glyph per category. An unmapped category draws no icon, never a default Slot icons DA_XenoCore_ItemIcons Glyph per equipment slot, for the merchant tabs

An item's own Icon wins over the category glyph. None of the shipped items sets one, so every icon you see in the sample comes from DA_XenoCore_ItemIcons.

Lyra's Remove Item Instance can take an item someone is wearing

Lyra's Remove Item Instance removes the item you give it even if a character is wearing it. The character keeps showing it in its slot, but the bag, and therefore the save, no longer holds it. The watcher cannot put it back; it logs an Error to LogXenoBagWatch naming the item and the wearer. Use Remove Item Instance From Party, which refuses. The same risk applies to Lyra's Consume Items By Definition, which takes the first entries it finds; use Consume Items From Party.

Lyra's Add Item Instance crashes

Lyra's Add Item Instance node is not implemented in stock Lyra and stops the editor or the game when it runs. There is no way to put an existing item instance back into the bag. Add by definition with Add Item To Party instead.

Fails silently: Lyra's Inventory Item cost never lets the ability run

Lyra's own Inventory Item ability cost is switched off inside stock Lyra 5.8, so its check always fails and an ability carrying it can never activate. Nothing is logged. Use Party Item (XenoCore) instead.

Fails silently: Symbol draws as a box

Symbol on the display fragment is authored as text, and the UI font only covers Latin letters and basic punctuation. Anything else draws as a missing-glyph box. Use Icon or the icon set instead.

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
• A new item: duplicate a shipped item of the same kind into your own folder (Content/MyGame/Items) and change its fragments. See Consumable item, Add a weapon and Add armour.
  • A new equipment item must be duplicated, never created blank: a blank definition has no equipment definition, so it lists but cannot be equipped, and nothing is logged.
  • A new category (Items menu tab) needs a programmer: the list of tabs is fixed in C++. See the note below.
  • Something that gives items (a quest reward, a shop, a script) should call Add Item To Party so the change message fires.
  • Reacting when the bag changes: listen for the XenoCore.Inventory.Message.Changed message. See Events.
  • Never rename or delete the fragments on shipped items in place; duplicate first.
For programmers: classes and adding a category

The bag is a stock ULyraInventoryManagerComponent on the player controller, found by UXenoCoreInventoryStatics::GetPartyInventory. Every bag change goes through UXenoCoreInventoryStatics; changes made elsewhere are caught by UXenoCoreInventoryWatchSubsystem. Rarity colouring is UXenoCoreItemRarityStatics, the item cost is UXenoCoreAbilityCost_PartyItem, and the message payload is FXenoCoreInventoryChangedMessage. A new category is a value appended to EXenoCoreItemCategory (XenoCoreItemFragments.h): append at the end, never reorder or insert, because saved items store the number.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers
  • One entry per item because Lyra counts entries. GetTotalItemCountByDefinition adds one per entry and never reads StackCount, and ConsumeItemsByDefinition removes one entry per unit. Merged stacks would make Lyra's counting under-report and break item ability costs. Lyra knowledge a buyer already has stays correct.
  • The bag on the controller because Lyra's inventory consumers, such as the quick bar, look for it there, and because the party, not a character, owns it. The controller survives switching the leader.
  • One resolver because "which bag" has one right answer in single-player, and writing that assumption down in exactly one function means only that function changes if it ever stops being true.
  • Our own change message because Lyra's Lyra.Inventory.Message.StackChanged is only sent from replication callbacks, which never run in a standalone single-player game.
  • A watcher as well as a rule. Designers reach for Lyra's inventory nodes, because they are the first ones the node menu offers. The watcher keeps menus current when that happens; it is cheap because an untouched bag compares equal in one pass. It is a net under the rule, not a replacement: only the statics honour carry caps and refuse worn items.
  • Our own item cost because Lyra's is compiled out, and even restored it would look for the bag on the casting character's own controller (wrong for an AI party member) and could spend a worn item.
  • Fragments in C++ because C++ cannot read variables defined on a Blueprint class, so data that both menus and gameplay code need has to live on a native fragment.

docs.title: Loot
docs.text:
All · 12 min read

A chest's offer: Take All or Take None.

When an enemy dies it leaves a treasure chest where it fell. The chest's tier (Wooden, Silver or Gold) is decided at death, so you can see it on the ground; its contents are decided only when you open it, from the enemy's drop table. Opening shows a panel that asks you to take everything or nothing. Chests stay in the world until opened, across area changes and save and load. Separately, collectable orbs sit in the level and give their item when you walk into them. The idea that makes the rest make sense: a chest holds a drop table and a tier, never a list of items.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
• What an enemy drops, and how often each chest tier appears: Build a drop table.
  • How rare an item is, and its colour: Set and style item rarity.
  • A chest placed by hand, an orb to walk into: drag BP_XenoCore_TreasureChest or B_XenoCore_CollectableOrb into the level and fill in the settings in Settings.
  • How the chest looks and opens: the chest Blueprint's Presentation settings, or a child Blueprint using its three events (see Extending it).

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text: Piece Class / sample asset Job Drop table (data asset) Inventory/Loot/DA_XenoCore_Drops_Grunt, _Skirmisher, _Bulwark, _Brute (one per minion family), DA_XenoCore_Drops_Minion (base minion and dummy) Tier odds, and a pool of weighted items per tier Enemy loot settings Enemy Blueprint · Drop Table, Chest Class, Always Gold Chest, Chest Drop Delay Which table, which chest, forced gold, reveal delay Chest Inventory/Loot/BP_XenoCore_TreasureChest Holds tier and table, rolls on open, offers the contents Open ability Inventory/Loot/GA_XenoCore_OpenChest Granted near a chest by Lyra's interaction system Chest label Inventory/Loot/W_XenoCore_ChestLabel Floating label near a closed chest Popup UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_LootPopup Lists the items; Take All or Take None. Shown automatically when a chest opens Collectable orb Inventory/Collectables/B_XenoCore_CollectableOrb Walk-in pickup that respawns Icons UserInterface/Foundation/DA_XenoCore_ItemIcons Category glyphs on each popup row

docs.title: Drop table settings
docs.text:
Setting What it does Gold Chance Chance of a gold chest, checked first. Default 0.02 Silver Chance Chance of silver if gold did not land. Default 0.25. Otherwise wooden Pools One entry per tier (Wooden, Silver, Gold) Pool › Min Items, Max Items How many items a chest of that tier rolls. Default 1–2 Pool › Entries › Item Def, Weight Candidate items. Weights are relative, not percentages; 0 parks an entry without removing it Pool › Entries › Min Level, Max Level A level band: the entry only drops from an enemy inside it. The level is the dying enemy's, stored on the chest. 0 means no bound Pool › No Duplicate Equipment A piece of equipment comes out of one chest at most once. Materials still repeat. If the pool runs out of drawable entries, the chest holds fewer items rather than repeating one Pool › Guarantee One Of Rarity Empty by default. When set, a chest from this pool always holds at least one item that rare. If the roll found none, its last pick is redrawn from the qualifying entries. Xenoblade 1's silver and gold chests always hold one rare material

Each item in a chest is rolled independently, so the same material can appear twice (equipment too, unless No Duplicate Equipment is on).

The sample tables give each minion family its own common and rare material, a silver chance between 18% and 34%, and level-banded armour in the gold pool: the Legendary Vanguard Plate only drops from a level 10+ enemy. Gems are never in a chest; they come from quests and shops. To see what a table really pays out, run XenoCore.Loot.Simulate <table> [level] [chests] in the console.

Each Item Def is a soft reference. Holding a drop table (every enemy and chest does) loads none of its items; only the items actually rolled load, when the chest is opened.

Chest tier and item rarity are separate. The tier is the chest, and its odds come from the drop table. Rarity belongs to each item; see Set and style item rarity.

They meet in three places:

  • Each rarity's Lowest Chest Tier (Common → Wooden, Rare → Silver, Legendary → Gold). A drop table warns, but does not error, when an item sits in a lower pool than that.
  • The chest beam, coloured by the rarity its tier stands for, so a gold chest glows Legendary purple. Turn this off with the chest's Use Rarity Beam Colour.
  • The loot panel, which lists the rarest items first.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
At death. If the enemy has a Drop Table, it rolls the tier (gold if Always Gold Chest is ticked), spawns its Chest Class on the floor where it died, turned to face the player, and tells the chest its table, tier and the enemy's level. The chest hides itself for Chest Drop Delay (2 s) so it does not appear in the middle of the death animation, and cannot be opened until then. No Drop Table means no chest.

Squads. An enemy that belongs to an enemy spawner squad follows Xenoblade Chronicles' squad rule (the spawner's Squad Loot Rule, on by default):

  • Only the last member killed drops a chest. The others drop nothing, and their loot is not added to it: a squad is worth one chest, not one per member.
  • The chest is gold at three times the usual chance (the spawner's Squad Gold Multiplier, 3), and otherwise silver, never wooden. A table with no silver pool falls back to wooden.
  • Its contents come from the squad leader's drop table and level, whichever member died last. The leader is the first enemy of the spawner's first Members entry, so put the type whose loot the squad should give first.

Waiting. An unopened chest stays in the world. It has no timer and nothing despawns it, and it survives leaving the map and saving and loading. The save subsystem keeps a record for every map the party has visited:

Chest What is remembered How it comes back Dropped by an enemy, unopened Chest class, position, drop table, tier, source level Respawned when the map begins play. It still rolls its contents on open, so a reload gives a new roll Placed in the level Only what has happened to it: emptied, or opened with items left in it The level brings the actor back; on its own BeginPlay it asks the save for its record, then removes itself or restores its leftovers Opened, holding items the bag had no room for The leftover items themselves, not a table Offers exactly those items again, never a re-roll

Leaving a map sweeps its dropped chests into the record; a save writes every map's records; a load replaces them; a new game clears them. Placed chests report their own changes as they happen, so a World Partition cell that streams out and back in is still correct.

Opening. Walk up to a chest and the interact prompt offers its verb. Pressing it opens the chest: the lid plays, the chest rolls its contents now from the table and tier, and after the lid the XenoCore.Loot.Message.ChestOpened message announces the offered items (see Events). Nothing has entered the bag yet.

Choosing. W_XenoCore_LootPopup appears, focused on Take All:

  • Take All adds each item to the party bag, one at a time, and every menu updates. Anything over an item's Max Carried stays in the chest: the panel shows those rows in Rejected Colour with "(no room)" after them, and the hint line reads "No room for the items in red. They will stay in the chest." The chest stays open-able until it is empty, and offers exactly the leftovers next time.
  • Take None discards everything the chest offered, leftovers included, and the chest is finished.

Back (B or Escape) does nothing on this panel: you must answer it. While it is up, the interact button belongs to the panel and the character cannot jump.

After. A chest that has nothing left to offer fades and removes itself after Despawn Delay.

Collectable orbs. Walking within Collect Radius of an orb adds its Item To Grant to the bag, broadcasts XenoCore.Collectable.Message.Collected, and hides the orb. If Respawns is on, it comes back after Respawn Seconds (300).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Where it lives What it does Drop table settings Drop table asset See the table above Drop Table, Chest Class, Chest Spawn Height Enemy Blueprint › XenoCore › Loot Loot source, chest Blueprint, clearance above the floor Always Gold Chest Enemy Blueprint › XenoCore › Loot Force gold. Can be set per placement Chest Drop Delay Enemy Blueprint › XenoCore › Enemy › Loot Reveal delay. Can be set per placement Drop Table, Tier, Source Level A chest placed in a level › XenoCore › Loot For hand-placed chests. Source Level is the level the table's bands roll against Lid Open Angle, Lid Open Time, Flip Hinge Side, Front Yaw Offset, Lid Open On Spawn Chest Blueprint › XenoCore › Loot › Presentation The lid Beam Height, Beam Width, Beam Intensity, Beam Opacity, Beam Fade Time Chest Blueprint › XenoCore › Loot › Presentation The tier-coloured light beam Despawn Delay, Offer Delay After Lid Chest Blueprint › XenoCore › Loot › Presentation Timing after the answer and before the popup Label Height, Label Range Chest Blueprint › XenoCore › Loot The floating label On Tier Set, On Opened, On Resolved Chest Blueprint events Your own tier colours, sounds and effects Row Colour, Row Font Size, Rejected Colour Popup widget › XenoCore › Loot Popup look; Rejected Colour marks the "(no room)" rows Item To Grant, Collect Radius, Respawns, Respawn Seconds, Orb Effect, Collect Sound Placed orb › XenoCore › Collectable The orb

Fails silently: a chest tier with no pool opens empty

Every tier a chest can roll needs its own pool with entries. A missing pool gives an empty chest rather than falling back to another tier. Only a warning in the Output Log says so. The sample minion can roll all three tiers, so its table needs all three.

Fails silently: renaming a placed chest resets it

A hand-placed chest's save record is keyed by the actor's name in the level. Rename it, delete and re-place it, or duplicate the level, and existing saves no longer match it: a chest the player emptied comes back full, and nothing is logged. Settle placed chests' names before you ship, and do not rename them in an update.

Fails silently: the chest must answer the interaction trace channel

A custom chest whose collision does not respond to Lyra_TraceChannel_Interaction is never found: no prompt and no way to open it, with nothing logged. Build chests from BP_XenoCore_TreasureChest.

Fails silently: the chest's open ability must be the exact Blueprint

The chest's interaction option names GA_XenoCore_OpenChest. Lyra finds that ability by exact class, so pointing it at a parent class makes the option disappear.

Fails silently: an orb on an interaction collision profile

An orb's volume must overlap pawns only. On an Interactable_* profile, the chest's interact prompt starts offering the orb.

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
• Your own drop table: duplicate DA_XenoCore_Drops_Minion into your own folder (Content/MyGame/Loot), fill all three pools, and set it on your enemy. See Drop table.
  • A hand-placed chest: drag BP_XenoCore_TreasureChest into a level and set its Drop Table, Tier and Source Level.
  • A different chest look: right-click BP_XenoCore_TreasureChest, choose Create Child Blueprint Class, and use its three events (On Tier Set, On Opened, On Resolved). Do not build a chest from a plain Actor: only the shipped chest can be opened with the interact button.
  • Not built yet: taking specific items from a chest (only Take All and Take None exist). Outside a spawner squad, every enemy with a table drops its own chest.
  • Do not build a pickup on Lyra's own pickup system: it puts items in the bag behind XenoCore's back, so carry limits are skipped.
For programmers: classes

Drop table UXenoCoreDropTable; chest AXenoCoreTreasureChest (C++ because Lyra's IInteractableTarget cannot be implemented in Blueprint); popup UXenoCoreLootPopupBase, shown by UXenoCoreLootPopupSubsystem on XenoCore.Loot.Message.ChestOpened; orb AXenoCoreCollectableOrb. The chest answers Lyra_TraceChannel_Interaction and grants GA_XenoCore_OpenChest; the popup blocks jumping with Status.XenoCore.Looting. Do not implement Lyra's IPickupable: it adds to the bag directly (only the bag watcher announces it, and carry caps are skipped) and passes a stack count, which the one-entry-per-item bag does not use.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers
  • Roll on open. Deciding contents at open rather than at death is the genre's behaviour, and it means a chest only needs a table pointer and a tier.
  • Chests persist, so no "encounter ended" signal is needed to decide when to hand out loot.
  • The drop table is a data asset, not a component: it is static, shared by every enemy of a type, and read once, at death.
  • The chest is C++ because Lyra's IInteractableTarget cannot be implemented in Blueprint. It is shaped on ShooterCore's ALyraWorldCollectable.
  • The popup cannot be backed out of because closing it without an answer would leave a rolled, opened chest with no way back in. It consumes the back action rather than ignoring it, so back reaches nothing underneath either.
  • Everything enters the bag through the inventory statics, so menus, badges and quests update.

docs.title: Minimap
docs.text:
All · 10 min read

The minimap is the circle in the top right of the HUD. It shows the area around the party leader, which way the leader faces, which way the camera looks, nearby enemies, quest givers, shops and whatever the active quest needs. The area's name sits under the circle. It follows the XC1 field minimap: north-up by default, with turning the map with the camera as an option. Pressing L3 (keyboard M) fades the same map in over the whole screen, see-through and fading out toward the edges, as in XC1's Definitive Edition.

Everything you change is data: a placed actor, a data asset, a Data Table and properties on the HUD. No Blueprint graph is involved.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
• A minimap for a new map: Give a map its minimap.
  • A new kind of marker, or a marker on your own Blueprint: Show something on the minimap.
  • The legend's words and each marker's look: rows of UserInterface/HUD/Minimap/DT_XenoCore_MapMarkers.
  • Size, range, north-up or rotating, colours, fonts: the Minimap widget's Details panel (Settings).

docs.title: What it shows
docs.text:
On the minimap Meaning Comes from Yellow arrow, centre The party leader, pointing the way they face Always drawn Pale wedge Where the camera is looking: brightest at the arrow, fading out toward the rim Always drawn Soft dot A living enemy, coloured by its danger: the same colour as the lvl.N over its head. It pulses while the enemy is fighting the party Every XenoCore enemy, automatically Ring A living unique enemy, coloured by danger the same way An enemy with Unique Monster ticked Red ! on a white tag An NPC with a quest to give or to take back A XenoCore NPC whose quest is offerable or ready to hand in House An NPC who runs a shop A XenoCore NPC with a Shop Table Blue dot Something the active quest wants Enemies a Defeat Enemy objective still needs, the NPC of a Talk To NPC step, the Quest Location of a Reach Location step, and the quest giver once the quest is ready to hand in

Blue dots stay pinned to the rim when they are out of range, pointing the way. Every other marker disappears beyond the edge.

The rim also carries the time of day: a sun or moon that travels round it, noon at the top and midnight at the bottom. The line under the circle reads the area name, the current weather's icon and the time, for example "Gaur Plain 21:40". See Time of day and weather.

The arrow and the wedge can point different ways

They show two different things, as in XC1: the arrow is the way the character faces, the wedge is the way the camera looks. With the camera behind the character they line up; turn the character toward the camera and the arrow points back down the wedge. Neither is a bug.

No treasure chests, by design

XC1's own manual lists no minimap icon for chests or collectables, so XenoCore draws none. To add one, see Show something on the minimap.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
• The image is a picture of the whole area seen from straight above, stored on an Area Definition data asset with the rectangle of the world it covers (Maps/Areas/DA_XenoCore_Area_*). XenoCore bakes it from the map into an XC1-style plan: tan ground tinted olive where it is grassy and pale where it is sandy, dark rock, blue water, outlines between levels, faint contour lines every 3 m of height, higher ground casting a soft shadow to the south-east and lit along its north-west edges, all on a light paper texture. You can also paint your own in any image editor.
  • One XenoCore Map Area actor per map says which Area Definition the map uses. In the editor it draws that rectangle as an orange box, so you can see exactly where the image lands. Its Fit Bounds To Landscape button sizes the rectangle to the map's landscape (for a hand-painted image), and Map Check flags a missing area, a missing image or backwards bounds.
  • Markers are drawn for every actor that asks to be. XenoCore enemies and NPCs ask automatically; any other actor can ask with one Blueprint node.
  • What each marker looks like is one row of UserInterface/HUD/Minimap/DT_XenoCore_MapMarkers. Each row is keyed by a XenoCore.Map.Marker.* gameplay tag.
  • The minimap itself is the Minimap widget in UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_HUDLayout. The full-screen view is a second one there, MinimapOverlay.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Select Minimap (or MinimapOverlay) in W_XenoCore_HUDLayout's hierarchy. Everything below is in its Details panel.

Setting Category What it does World Radius Minimap How far the map reaches from the centre to the edge, in cm. The corner minimap uses 9000 (90 m) Rotate With Camera Minimap Off (XC1's default): north is always up and the arrow turns. On: the map turns so the camera always looks up Minimap Size Minimap The widget's size on screen Overlay Minimap On for MinimapOverlay only: draw only while L3 has the overlay open Overlay Fade Seconds Minimap Overlay only: how long it takes to fade in and out (0.15) Fill Widget Minimap Fill the whole widget, fading toward every edge, instead of a circle. On for MinimapOverlay Vignette Start, Backdrop Dim Minimap › Look Fill Widget only: where the edge fade begins, and how much the game behind is darkened Rim Width, Rim Color Minimap › Look The thin band round the edge Edge Shade Minimap › Look How much the disc darkens toward its rim Shadow Width, Shadow Opacity Minimap › Look The soft shadow outside the rim Map Opacity, Map Brightness Minimap › Look How solid and how bright the map image is Background Color Minimap › Look Drawn where there is no image Leader Icon, Leader Icon Size, Leader Tint Minimap › Leader The arrow. 24 at the corner minimap's size: about a tenth of the circle, as in XC1 Camera View Color, Camera View Half Angle Minimap › Leader The camera wedge, which lightens the map under it. Its colour's alpha is how strong it is Camera View Softness, Camera View Outer Strength Minimap › Leader How far the wedge's sides fade out (degrees), and how strong it still is at the rim compared with the arrow. XC1's is brightest at the arrow and fades out Marker Styles Minimap › Markers Which marker table to use Rim Clamp Inset Minimap › Markers How far inside the rim a pinned marker sits Marker Scale Minimap › Markers Multiplies every marker's size. 1.6 on the overlay Area Name Strip Minimap › Text Height of the strip under the circle for the area's Display Name. 26 on the corner minimap, whose Minimap Size is 240 × 266. 0 = no name Show Header And Legend Minimap › Text Fill Widget only: the area name across the top and a legend of marker kinds bottom-left Area Name Font, Header Font, Label Font, Text Color Minimap › Text The name, the header, and the legend and NPC names Leader Label Minimap › Text The legend line for the arrow (You). Empty = left out Show Time And Weather, Weather Icon Size, Time Weather Separator Minimap › Time And Weather The weather icon and clock after the area name Show Day Night Dial, Sun Icon, Moon Icon, Dial Icon Size Minimap › Time And Weather The sun or moon that rides the rim

Changing the legend's words

Every other legend line is the Label column of that kind's row in /XenoCore/UserInterface/HUD/Minimap/DT_XenoCore_MapMarkers: open the table, edit Label, save. The shipped lines are Enemy, Unique Enemy, Shop, Quest and Objective. Clear a Label to leave that kind out of the legend. Row names and marker tags (Monster, XenoCore.Map.Marker.Monster) are internal and never shown to the player, so they do not need renaming.

Under the minimap, MinimapPrompt shows the overlay button and Map: the left-stick-click glyph on a gamepad. It draws the MinimapOverlay row of UserInterface/Foundation/DT_XenoCore_Actions.

Both prompts have icons on every device: XenoCore ships its own keyboard keycap icons, set by Keyboard Key Icons in Project Settings › Game › XenoCore UI.

To change the overlay button:

  1. Edit IA_XenoCore_MinimapOverlay's keys in Input/Mappings/IMC_XenoCore.
  2. Set the same keys on the MinimapOverlay row of DT_XenoCore_Actions.

Fails silently: the prompt shows the old button

The prompt only draws what the table row says; it never reads the input mapping. Change one without the other and the HUD tells players to press a button that does nothing. Nothing warns, so press the button in Play after every change.

L3 was Lyra's Dash

Lyra's own IMC_Default binds the left stick click to Dash, which XenoCore has no use for. IMC_XenoCore runs at a higher priority, so the minimap overlay wins the button.

docs.title: Testing from the console
docs.text:
Command Effect XenoCore.Minimap.Rotate 1 / 0 / -1 Force rotate with camera / north-up / back to the widget's setting XenoCore.Minimap.Hide 1 / 0 Hide / show the corner minimap. The L3 overlay is unaffected

There is no options-menu entry for these yet.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
• Give a map its minimap: set up a new area, bake or paint its image.
  • Show something on the minimap: a new kind of marker, or mark a Blueprint actor.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers
  • One native widget. UXenoCoreMinimap is a UMG widget like UImage, with no Blueprint. It paints the disc, every marker and the leader in one OnPaint, so nothing re-lays out, and a marker costs one draw call.
  • The disc is one material. M_XenoCore_Minimap is built in C++ by UXenoCoreMinimapTools::BuildMinimapMaterial, never by hand. One Custom HLSL node pans, zooms, rotates, masks and rims it, and draws the camera wedge clipped to the circle.
  • Markers are a registry, not a component. UXenoCoreMapMarkerSubsystem (a world subsystem) holds weak pointers. Actors that implement IXenoCoreMapMarkerSource answer their kind every frame, which is how a dead enemy or a taken quest disappears with nothing to unregister.
  • One actor per map, not World Settings, because Lyra's World Settings is host code. It is not spatially loaded, so it is never streamed out.

docs.title: Party Gauge, downed and revive
docs.text:
All · 15 min read · No code · Last tested: 2026-10-01

A party member who runs out of HP is downed, not killed. They kneel where they fell, and the leader can stand over them and press A - Revive, which spends one bar of the Party Gauge, the blue three-bar meter above the leader's HUD row. The party gauge is filled by playing well: critical hits and art bonus effects. A downed member also gets up on their own, at 1 HP, once the battle is over. Only when every active member is down is the battle lost, and then the party wakes at the last respawn point and keeps everything it earned.

That is XC1's revive, one bar and no healer, combined with XC3's rule that only a whole-party knockout loses the fight.

What you can change, no code

  • What a revive costs, how much HP it gives back and how close you stand: Tune revive and defeat
  • The defeat beat, the fade and where the party wakes: the same recipe, and Party wipe
  • How fast HP recovers between fights: Recovering HP between fights
  • What fills the gauge and how big it is: What you can change

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Piece What it is Where it lives Party Gauge UXenoCorePartyGaugeComponent, on the player controller beside the bag Added by the XenoCore GameFeatureData (Add Components) Gauge readout UXenoCorePartyGaugeWidget, three framed bars Placed in UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_PartyMemberPlate, shown on the leader's row only Downed GA_XenoCore_Downed, triggered by Lyra's death event Battle/GA_XenoCore_Downed, granted by AbilitySet_XenoCore_Hero and AbilitySet_XenoCore_PartyMember Revive The downed body is an interactable, like an NPC or a chest AXenoCoreCombatantCharacter, priced and run by BP_XenoCore_Party End of battle and defeat Party-wide battle state, the wipe and the defeat beat Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party

The revive uses the same prompt and button as Talk and Trade (Interaction), so what is offered and what A does are one answer.

docs.title: Filling the gauge
docs.text:
The gauge holds 300 points as three bars of 100. Battle actions add points by reason:

Reason Points A critical hit by a party member 10 An art's bonus effect lands 20

Enemies never fill it. Out of battle it drains at 2 points a second. A bar that fills flashes; when all three are full the readout pulses and plays a particle burst, because a Chain Attack would be ready.

Reasons with no system yet

The table also prices Burst Affinity (50, or 75 perfectly timed), auto-attacks at very high Tension (5) and a kill during a Chain Attack (100). None of those mechanics exist yet, so those rows are waiting for a caller.

docs.title: Going down
docs.text:
When a party member's HP hits 0, GA_XenoCore_Downed runs instead of a death:

  1. They kneel and hold the pose. They cannot move, jump, auto-attack or use arts, and enemies stop seeing them.
  2. Their HUD row greys out: the portrait dims, the name, level and HP turn grey, and the empty health bar stops blinking.

docs.title: Reviving
docs.text:
Stand on top of the downed ally. The prompt appears within Revive Range (110 cm), which is deliberately tight so a crowded fight never offers the wrong body. Then:

  • With a full bar: press A. One bar is spent, the leader plays a short gesture, a ring of green motes rises from the ally with a chime, and they stand up with 30% of their HP, shown as a green heal number.
  • Without a full bar: the prompt still shows, and pressing A is refused. The line Party Gauge not full appears over the ally, the gauge readout shakes with its empty bars flashing red, and a short "no" sound plays. Nothing is spent.

While A - Revive is on screen, A revives and nothing else: the arts palette's confirm, which is also A, is held off.

The player cannot revive their own body. A downed leader can be left: switch to a standing member (battle switching) and revive from there. Otherwise a downed leader waits for the battle to end or for the whole party to fall.

docs.title: The end of the battle
docs.text:
Battle state is party-wide: the party is in battle while the leader has their weapon drawn, or while an enemy within 30 m is fighting any member. The battle ends when no enemy has been engaged for Battle Over Grace (1 second). At that moment every downed member gets up at 1 HP.

Sheathing alone is not enough. Fleeing with the palette's Flee does not revive anyone while an enemy is still chasing the party.

docs.title: Recovering HP between fights
docs.text:
Out of battle, every party member's HP climbs back to full on its own. XC1 has no healing items and its arts work only in battle, so this is the only way to recover between fights. A member the battle just stood up at 1 HP recovers the same way. Benched members recover too.

Recovery uses the same end-of-battle rule as the revive: nothing heals while an enemy is still chasing the party. Two settings on BP_XenoCore_Party, under XenoCore > Party > Recovery:

Setting Default What it does Out Of Battle Regen Per Second 0.1 Fraction of max HP recovered each second. 0 turns recovery off. Out Of Battle Regen Delay 1 s Wait after the battle ends before recovery starts.

XC1 never states the rate. The 10% per second default is XC2's, the closest sourced number. Console: XenoHurtParty 0.3 drops every standing member to 30% so you can watch it climb.

docs.title: Defeat
docs.text:
When every active member is down, the party is wiped:

  1. The defeat beat. Time slows to 35%, the world drains of colour, Defeated fades in, bold and red, in the middle of the screen, and Lyra's end-of-round sting plays.
  2. The camera fades to black with the word still showing.
  3. Under black, the party is moved to the respawn point and restored to full health. Enemies forget the fight.
  4. The fade lifts. Experience, items, gold and gear are all kept.

The respawn point and the fade timings are covered under Party wipe.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
Setting Where it lives What it does Revive Bar Cost BP_XenoCore_Party › XenoCore › Party › Revive Bars a revive spends (1). 0 makes reviving free. Revive Health Fraction same HP a revived member stands up with, as a fraction of max (0.3). Revive Range same How close the reviver must stand, in cm (110). Revive Gesture Montage same Played on the reviver. Default: Lyra's upper-body heal gesture. Revive Refused Text, Colour, Scale same The line over the ally when the gauge is short. Empty shows nothing. Revive Refused Sound same Played when a revive is refused. None plays nothing. Battle Over Grace BP_XenoCore_Party › XenoCore › Party Seconds with no engaged enemy before the battle counts as over and the downed get up. Defeat Banner Class, Defeat Text BP_XenoCore_Party › XenoCore › Party › Wipe › Defeat The defeat banner widget and its line. None turns the banner off. Defeat Time Dilation, Defeat Saturation, Defeat Desaturate Seconds, Defeat Sound same The slow motion, how grey the world goes and how fast, and the sting. 1.0 dilation and 1.0 saturation turn those parts off. Grey When Downed, Downed Portrait Tint, Downed Text Colour, Downed Health Bar Opacity W_XenoCore_PartyMemberPlate, on each placed row How a downed member's HUD row looks. Refused Colour, Refused Seconds, Refused Shake The gauge widget inside W_XenoCore_PartyMemberPlate The gauge's shake and red flash when a spend is refused. Bar Count, Points Per Bar, Fill Points, Out Of Battle Drain Per Second UXenoCorePartyGaugeComponent The gauge's size and what fills it. See below. Downed pose Characters/Core/Animations/Downed/ AS_XenoCore_DownedKneel_Enter, _Loop and _GetUp, shared by every character.

The gauge's settings have no Blueprint to edit

The XenoCore Game Feature Data adds the C++ class XenoCorePartyGaugeComponent directly, so there is no asset holding Fill Points or Bar Count, and changing them on the running component in play is lost when play stops. To retune them:

  1. In your own folder, right-click and choose Blueprint Class. Under All Classes, search for XenoCorePartyGaugeComponent, pick it, and name the Blueprint BP_MyPartyGauge.
  2. Open it, set XenoCore › PartyGauge › Bar Count, Points Per Bar, Fill Points and Out Of Battle Drain Per Second, then Compile and Save.
  3. Open the XenoCore asset at the top of XenoCore Content (the Game Feature Data). Under Actions, expand the Add Components action, then its Component List, and find the entry whose Component Class is XenoCorePartyGaugeComponent. Set it to BP_MyPartyGauge. Save.

A template update replaces the XenoCore asset, so note this change to re-apply after updating.

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
• Something new fills the gauge. Call Add Party Gauge For Reason with the actor that earned it and a new XenoCore.PartyGauge.Reason.* tag, then add a Fill Points row for that tag. An enemy causer is ignored, so you never need to check whose hit it was.
  • Something new spends the gauge. Check Can Afford Bars, then Spend Bars. When the player asked for it and it cannot be paid, call Notify Cannot Afford so the readout shakes. Do not call it from AI or from code that is only probing.
  • React to the gauge. Listen for XenoCore.PartyGauge.Message.Changed (it moved) or XenoCore.PartyGauge.Message.Refused (a spend was refused). On the readout widget, the On Bar Filled, On Gauge Full and On Spend Refused events are there for extra sound or flourish. On a party row, On Downed Changed fires when it greys out or comes back.
  • A different defeat screen. Make a Blueprint child of XenoCoreDefeatBannerBase with its own layout (name the text block DefeatText) and set it as Defeat Banner Class. For something bigger, listen for XenoCore.Party.Message.Wiped.

Do not give the party back a death ability. Downed is what keeps the body in the world to be revived; a death ability ragdolls it and removes it.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers: the design reasons
  • Downed is Lyra's death, stopped halfway. GA_XenoCore_Downed triggers on GameplayEvent.Death, as Lyra's death ability does, and calls StartDeath but never FinishDeath, so the health component reports dead while the body stays.
  • Revive is an interaction, not an ability. The prompt, the range check and the button are UXenoCoreInteractionSubsystem's, the same path Talk and Trade use. A downed body is just one more interactable that the leader is not driving.
  • The prompt shows even when the gauge is short. Hiding it left the player standing on an ally with no prompt and no reason, which read as a bug. Refusing on the press can say why.
  • The gauge lives on the controller with the bag, quests and progression, because it belongs to the party, not to whichever character is leading.
  • The battle ends on "no enemy engaged", not on sheathing, so fleeing cannot buy a free revive.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Party AI does not revive anyone yet. Only the character the player controls can revive.
  • Battle switching skips downed members: you cannot switch onto one, but you can switch away from a downed leader.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
