  • Interaction, NPCs and dialogue: the prompt a revive shares.
  • Tune revive and defeat

docs.title: Party tactics
docs.text:
Designer · 10 min read · No code · Last tested: 2026-10-04

The Party Tactics panel, opened mid-fight.

Tactics are standing orders for the companions: who they attack, and how they use their arts. The player sets them at any time, in the field, locked on or mid-fight. They stay set until changed, and they are saved with the game. Orders can be given to the whole party or to one member, as in Xenoblade Chronicles X.

At a glance

In play: tap X (F) to switch the party between fighting your target and picking their own; hold it for the full list of orders.

What you can change, no code: the starting orders, which tactics the list shows and their wording, and how a companion picks a target on At Will. See What you can change and Tune companion AI.

Control Pad Keyboard Switch Attack between Focus and At Will for the whole party Tap X Tap F Open the Party Tactics list (open while held) Hold X Hold F ...move the highlight D-pad Up / Down Up / Down ...change the highlighted tactic's value D-pad Left / Right Left / Right ...give the orders to the next / previous member RB / LB Tab / Q

While an NPC's prompt is offering Trade, X is Trade instead. The prompt on screen shows which.

                                [M] Map
                      [X] Party Tactics     <- always shown
                     Focus · Heal First     <- shown for a few seconds, then fades

            PARTY TACTICS                   <- the list, while X is held
  [LB]      (portrait) Mira      [RB]
  ------------------------------------
  | Attack              < Regroup >
    Stay Back           < PARTY  >
    Prioritise Healing  < PARTY  >
    Arts                < PARTY  >

Under the minimap's [M] Map, in the same style, the hint [X] Party Tactics is always on screen, so the button is never a secret. The party's orders appear on a card below it for a few seconds and fade, rather than cluttering the HUD - when they change (a tap of X, or closing the list), when a battle starts, and once when the game loads. The card wraps to the minimap's width and only ever breaks between two orders. The battle line over the leader also announces every change, as XC1's group commands do. The list appears only while X is held, sized to its longest row. No text in it scrolls.

docs.title: The tactics
docs.text:
Tactic Values Series Attack Focus: the leader's target. At Will: each companion picks its own (see below). Regroup: stop attacking and gather by the leader, weapons drawn - the leader fights alone until it is changed XC1 Focus attacks! / Engage at will! / Come to me!; XC3 Focus Attacks and Follow Leader Stay Back OFF / ON: hold a distance from the target and fight with what reaches from there - heals, buffs, long arts. With swords only, a member on Stay Back mostly heals and supports XCX Use ranged attacks! Prioritise Healing OFF / ON: heal arts become eligible sooner and outscore attack arts Ours; no Xenoblade tactics list has one Arts All: every art. No Talent: never the Talent Art, so the gauge stays full. Auto Only: no arts at all, heals included No Talent: ours, XCX's Keep your tension up! is the nearest. Auto Only: XCX Assemble! behaviour

Attack and Arts are one tactic each with three values because their answers exclude each other: a companion told to follow you cannot also be focusing your target, and one on auto-attacks only is already holding its Talent Art. The default is Attack: Focus, Arts: All, everything else OFF.

docs.title: One member's orders
docs.text:
Pressing RB while the list is open moves it from Whole Party to the first companion, shows their portrait, and puts a white ring under them. On a member's list every tactic has one extra value, PARTY: "same as everyone". Stepping a tactic away from PARTY gives that member their own order; stepping it back to PARTY hands it back to the party.

Changing a tactic for the whole party clears every member's own order for that tactic, so "everyone" always means everyone.

docs.title: Who a companion attacks on At Will
docs.text:
Each companion scores every enemy fighting the party and takes the best. Only enemies already in the fight count: as in every Xenoblade, companions never start a battle themselves - and with squads that link aggro, one that did would pull the whole squad onto you. The weights are on the character's AI Profile › Target Choice (party member definition), so a defender and a healer can choose differently:

Field Default Effect Attacking Me Weight 3 Fight whatever is attacking this character Attacking Ally Weight 1.5 Peel enemies off the rest of the party. Raise on a defender Leader Target Weight 1 Lean toward the player's fight Current Target Weight 2 Stick with the current target rather than flip-flop Per Ally On Target Weight -1 Each other companion already on an enemy makes it less attractive, which spreads the party Distance Penalty Per Metre 0.1 Prefer the nearer enemy Target Reconsider Interval 1 s How often the choice is re-made; a dead target is replaced at once

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
Everything is on the party component: open Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party, click Class Defaults, and look under XenoCore › Party › Tactics:

Property What it does Default Tactics The orders a new game starts with Tactic Info Per tactic: its Label and Description, and its Values in order - each with its own label on the list, battle line, word in the orders under the prompt (empty = not shown) and colour - plus a sound Tactics List Which tactics the list shows, top to bottom. Leave one out to hide it Heal First Threshold / Heal First Bonus How early, and how strongly, Prioritise Healing heals (70%, +3) Stay Back Distance How far from its target a Stay Back member holds (750 cm - past every melee art and the auto-attack). Each member holds on its own side of the target, so several spread round it Regroup Ends With Battle Turn every Attack: Regroup back to Focus when a fight ends. Off by default: orders stand Follow Party Line The battle line when a member goes back to PARTY Tactics Panel Class The widget that draws the prompt and the list. Set a Blueprint child of XenoCoreTacticsPanelBase to restyle it

The panel widget's own Details hold its look: Tactics › Layout (position, minimum width, portrait sizes, fade and slide), Prompt (the hint on or off, the orders card's width, how long it shows and its fade, which moments show it - a change, a battle start, a load - and Always Show Prompt to keep the card up), Text (fonts, their shared Font Family, and every word it prints) and Colour (accent, rim, shadow, header band, value pills, highlight). A child that authors its own widget tree keeps it, and gets On Tactics Refreshed after every change to draw from.

The glyphs - X on the prompt, LB / RB on the list - are the rows PartyTactics, TacticsScopePrev and TacticsScopeNext in DT_XenoCore_Actions (the panel's Action Table, drawn with its Glyph Class, Lyra's InputActionWidget). Glyph Class, Action Table and Font Family are soft defaults on the class: they load when the panel is first built, and a Blueprint child can point them elsewhere.

Fails silently: remapping the tactics button

The glyph rows store their own keys; they are not read from the input mapping. If you rebind the tactics input in Input/Mappings/IMC_XenoCore, also open UserInterface/Foundation/DT_XenoCore_Actions and change the PartyTactics, TacticsScopePrev and TacticsScopeNext rows' keys to match, or the prompt keeps showing the old button.

The buttons are Blueprint children of XenoCoreGameplayAbility_PartyCommand in /XenoCore/Input/Abilities (GA_XenoCore_PartyTacticFocus, ..._PartyTacticsPanel, ..._TacticsScopeNext/Prev). The tap's Tactic, Value A and Value B say what it flips between; to put another tactic on its own button, duplicate it, change those, and map an input to it.

Fails silently

A tactic that is not in Tactics List cannot be changed from the list, and nothing says so. It still works if a button or a Blueprint sets it (Set Tactic on the party component).

If companions stand around while you fight

Hold X and look at Attack. On Regroup they are doing what they were told - set it back to Focus. Orders are saved with the game, so a Regroup set once comes back with the save.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: After changing tactics, the companion AI or an art's AI settings, start a fight in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and set each value in turn from the list (hold X / F). Watch what the companions do: who they target, whether they swing, how far from you they stand, which arts they use and whether a hurt ally is healed. log LogXenoAI Verbose in the console prints every art decision (see Companion AI).

docs.title: Saving
docs.text: Tactics are saved by name - "Attack: AtWill", never a number - so tactics and values can be reordered or added without breaking a save. Each member's record holds only the orders they do not take from the party. A save made before tactics existed loads Default Tactics.

docs.title: For Blueprint
docs.text: Get Tactic Value, Get Attack Order, Is Tactic On, Set Tactic, Toggle Tactic, Clear Member Tactic and Clear Member Tactics on the party component take an optional member definition (empty = the whole party). Every change is broadcast on XenoCore.Party.Message.TacticChanged.

docs.title: Party
docs.text:
All · 15 min read · No code

The party is owned by one component on the player controller, UXenoCorePartyComponent, set up as the Blueprint Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party. It holds three things: the roster (everyone recruited), the active members (everyone fielded) and the leader slot (which active member the player drives). It spawns a body for each active member and despawns benched ones. The one idea: the leader is an index into the active list, not a different kind of character. Every active member has the same class, the same spawn path and an AI controller ready to take the body back; switching leader is only the player controller letting go of one body and possessing another. The player can do that at any time, in battle too, with the triggers (XC3-style).

At a glance

In play: up to seven characters fight together; you drive one and the rest follow and fight on their own. Tap a trigger to take control of another, in or out of battle.

What you can change, no code:

  • Who you start with, and how many fight at once: Set the starting party
  • A new character: Add a party member
  • Recruiting someone by talking to them: Recruit a party member
  • The defeat screen and where the party wakes: Tune revive and defeat
  • How companions follow and fight: Tune companion AI
  • Every setting on this page: What you can change

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Piece Asset What it decides Party component Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party Starting roster, party size, leader slot, leader-only abilities, spawn spacing. Added to the player controller by the plugin's Game Feature Data. Member definition Characters/VRoid/<Name>/PartyMember_VRoid_* for the seven sample characters (UXenoCorePartyMemberDefinition); the colour mannequins' Characters/Party/PartyMember_* are kept as samples Name, role, portrait, which Blueprint to spawn, which AI controller drives it. One per recruitable character. Member Blueprint Characters/VRoid/<Name>/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_*, children of Characters/VRoid/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_Base Everything about the character itself. See Characters. AI controller Characters/Party/BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember (AXenoCorePartyMemberController) Carries the team and runs the StateTree. Party AI Characters/Party/AI/ST_XenoCore_PartyMember Following out of battle, fighting in battle. Recruit trigger AXenoCorePartyRecruitTrigger (place it in a level) Adds a character to the roster when the player walks in, or when called. Join banner UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_PartyJoinBanner in the HUD layout "joined the party" / "left the party". Party screen UserInterface/W_XenoCore_PartyManager Swap members, change leader. In battle, change leader only. Switch abilities Input/Abilities/GA_XenoCore_PartySwitch, GA_XenoCore_PartySwitchPrev, GA_XenoCore_PartySelect Tap a trigger to switch, hold one for the party cursor. Granted through the Leader Only Ability Set.

The member definition is deliberately thin. It does not hold pawn data, a statline or a level; those belong to the member's Blueprint, so each fact has one home.

docs.title: The roster, active and reserve
docs.text:
• Roster: everyone recruited. Adding to the roster is idempotent, so a story event that fires twice does not duplicate anyone.
  • Active members: the first Max Active Members of the roster, in order, unless changed. The leader counts towards the number.
  • Reserve: everyone else in the roster. A reserve member has no body at all: no pawn, no ability system, no equipment component. Their level, EXP and arts live on the progression component, and what they were wearing is remembered by the party component, so the Party screen can still show them.

Reserve members gain EXP at the progression component's Reserve Experience Rate. The sample's Game/BP_XenoCore_Progression sets it to 0, so a benched member earns nothing (the C++ default is XC1's 90%). Recruits with Join At Party Level catch up when they join. See Progression.

The sample's Starting Roster is Kael and Mira. The other five characters are recruited in Gaur Plain by talking to them. Max Active Members is 7 on BP_XenoCore_Party, so every recruit joins active and the reserve stays empty until you recruit an eighth or lower the number. The C++ default is 3.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Start. On begin play the component either restores a save or adds every Starting Roster member in order. Starting members are the party you already have, so they raise no join banners.
  2. Spawn. As soon as the player controller has a pawn, the component records where that pawn stands, then spawns each active member. The leader's body lands exactly on that spot; the others are scattered loosely in an arc behind it, each at its own distance and facing, so the party never appears in a neat formation (the Spawn settings, see Where they appear). Each gets its own AI controller, set to the leader's team before possession.
  3. Hand-over. The player possesses the body in Leader Slot. The Leader Only Ability Set (interaction, in the sample) moves to that body and is taken away from the previous one.
  4. Changes. Every change (recruit, remove, swap, clear, set leader) edits the lists and then re-syncs bodies through one spawn path, then broadcasts XenoCore.Party.Message.Changed. The message carries no detail; listeners re-read the component.
  5. Notices. Joins and leaves are queued rather than shown immediately, because party changes are made from a paused menu. UXenoCorePartyNoticeSubsystem drains the queue once the game is running again and plays the banner, leavers first.
  6. Defeat. The component watches every body it spawns. A member who runs out of HP is downed, not killed: they kneel and can be revived for a bar of the Party Gauge, and they get up at 1 HP when the battle ends. See Party Gauge, downed and revive. When every active member is down, the party is wiped (see below).

docs.title: Party wipe
docs.text:
When the last active member falls (a member with no body counts as down):

  1. XenoCore.Party.Message.Wiped is broadcast with Phase Defeated and the Respawn Transform the party is about to be sent to, so a "defeated" card can name the place.
  2. The defeat beat plays across Wipe Fade Delay (2.5 s): time slows, the world drains of colour, Defeated fades in in bold red, and a sting plays. Then the camera fades to Wipe Fade Colour over Wipe Fade Out Duration, with the word still on screen. Every part of the beat is a setting; see Tune revive and defeat.
  3. Under black, every active body is replaced by a fresh one at the respawn point: no reactions, no battle state, no target mode. Every enemy forgets the fight and walks home.
  4. After Wipe Hold Duration every active member is set to full health, the camera fades back in, and the message is broadcast again with Phase Respawned.

Experience, levels, items and gear are kept: none of them live on the bodies that were replaced. The respawn point is, in order: the point last recorded by Set Party Respawn Point, else the map's player start, else where the party was standing. A save point records itself when the player steps on it (unless its Is Respawn Point is off), so in practice the party returns to the last save point visited this session. To answer from anything else, such as a story checkpoint, override the Get Wipe Respawn Transform function in BP_XenoCore_Party (in the My Blueprint panel, Functions › Override), or call Set Party Respawn Point from your own Blueprint when the checkpoint is reached.

For a battle the story means the player to lose, call Begin Party Wipe to run the same flow. Is Party Wiped and Is Wipe In Progress let other systems stay out of the way meanwhile.

Fails silently: the party respawns inside the floor

The respawn point is a capsule centre, like a player start, and the leader is placed exactly there with no collision adjustment. A Get Wipe Respawn Transform override or a Set Party Respawn Point call that passes a point on the ground puts the party half into it. Raise the point by the capsule's half-height (about 100). Save points already do this with their Respawn Offset.

A fallen leader is not a wipe

By default only the whole active party going down wipes it. If the leader falls while others still stand, the player can switch to a standing member with the triggers and fight on (see Switching the controlled character). Nothing switches automatically: if the player does not, the leader kneels until the battle ends, or the fight is lost when the rest fall too. Party AI does not revive the leader yet. Tick Wipe When Leader Falls on BP_XenoCore_Party to end the fight the moment the leader goes down.

docs.title: Swapping and the leader
docs.text:
Blueprint node What it does Refused in battle? Add To Roster (Member, Activate Immediately, Join At Party Level) Recruit. Fields them straight away if there is room and Activate Immediately is ticked. With Join At Party Level, a new recruit arrives at least at the leader's level. No Remove From Roster The character leaves the story. No Set Active Members Replace the fielded list wholesale. Ignores anyone not in the roster, with a warning. No Swap Member (Active Slot, Member) Put a roster member into a slot. If they are already active elsewhere, the two trade places. Yes Clear Slot Bench whoever is in a slot. The list compacts: later slots move up. Yes Set Leader (Active Slot) The player drives that member. The new leader moves to slot 0 and everyone they passed moves down one. No, but it obeys the switch rules below Switch Leader By (Direction) The next (1) or previous (−1) member who can take control, as a trigger tap does. No Switch Leader To (Member) The player drives that body, as the party cursor does. No Can Change Party False while the leader carries Status.XenoCore.InBattle (weapon drawn). Can Assign To Slot (Active Slot, Member) Whether a Swap Member with these arguments would be accepted right now. Use it to grey out rows.

The in-battle rule is enforced by the component, not the screen, so any caller obeys it. Swap Member between the leader's slot and another active member is a leader change, not a composition change, so it is allowed in battle; that is how the Party screen picks a leader. Story events (add, remove, set) are deliberately not gated, so a cutscene recruit never fails because a fight was running. Show Party Locked Message raises Lyra's own confirmation dialog explaining the refusal.

Slots move when you clear one, and when the leader changes

Clear Slot compacts the active list, so the member who was in slot 2 is now in slot 1. A leader change also reorders it, because the leader always ends up in slot 0. Never store a slot number across a change; store the member definition and look up its slot again.

docs.title: Switching the controlled character
docs.text:
The player can take control of any active member at any time, in battle or out, XC3-style. Control changes hands; nobody joins or leaves.

Input What happens Tap RT (C) Control passes to the next member down the party column. Tap LT (Z) Control passes to the previous member, up the column. Hold LT or RT (Z or C) The party cursor opens on the leader's row. The D-pad (arrow keys) moves it; releasing the trigger takes control of the member under it. Releasing on the leader cancels.

What you see. The party cursor is a highlight on the member's HUD row plus a small white ring on the floor under their body. Out of battle the party column slides in while the cursor is up. When control lands, the white ring flashes under the new leader and fades, the word Leader appears over them, the camera blends to their view, and the HUD rows slide into their new places. Out of battle the column then stays up for a moment and slides away.

The column reorders. The leader is always the top row. A trigger tap or the cursor rotates the column: the chosen member goes to the top and everyone above them moves to the bottom, in order, so repeated taps walk the whole party. A pick in the Party screen cascades: the chosen member goes to the top and only those they passed move down one.

In battle, the fight carries over. The new leader draws their weapon if it is sheathed and locks the enemy the old leader had locked. The old leader keeps their weapon out and their swing going, and the party AI takes them over. Cooldowns, gauges and statuses belong to each body, so nothing resets.

When a switch is refused, "Can't switch" appears over the leader and Switch Refused Sound plays. A switch is refused:

  • away from a leader who is toppled or dazed;
  • while an ally-targeted Art is choosing its target (the cursor is busy);
  • during a party wipe;
  • when nobody else can take control.

Members who are downed, toppled, dazed or in the air are skipped by a tap and cannot be chosen with the cursor. A downed leader can be switched away from, which is how the player carries on fighting. Nothing switches automatically, and the battle is lost only when every active member is down (unless Wipe When Leader Falls is ticked).

The Party screen in battle allows a leader pick only: select the leader's row, then another active member. Bench swaps, clearing a slot and reordering other members stay locked until the fight ends.

The same cursor is used by Arts that target one ally, such as Light Heal: confirming the Art opens the cursor on the caster, the D-pad moves it, and confirming again casts. See Targeting.

Fails silently: switch abilities granted outside the leader-only set

The three switch abilities live in AbilitySet_XenoCore_Interact, the Leader Only Ability Set, which moves to whichever body the player drives. Do not also grant them in a member's own ability set: the switch moves the leader-only set on the next frame, and a second copy on another body is never removed, so it answers the trigger from a body the player is not driving.

Fails silently: a party member that nothing can hurt

A party member is only on a team if its controller is AXenoCorePartyMemberController or a child of it. A plain Blueprint AI controller leaves the member on no team: enemies ignore it and your own attacks pass through it, with no error. Keep Controller Class empty (to use the component's Default Controller Class) or point it at a child of BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember.

Fails silently: a member who never spawns

A member definition with Member Class empty is logged as an error when it should spawn and simply never appears. Run Validate Assets on your member definitions: missing Member Class, a pawn with no pawn data, a missing display name or portrait are all reported there.

docs.title: Party AI
docs.text:
Companions are driven by ST_XenoCore_PartyMember on the StateTree component of their controller. It has two branches, chosen by XenoCore Party In Battle (the leader carries Status.XenoCore.InBattle):

  • Travel. Three states in a loop:
    • XenoCore Party Hold rests near the leader until it is Follow Start Distance away - strolling, chatting with a companion or pulling a face on its own clock (see What they do while they wait).
    • XenoCore Party Follow Leader trails the leader at Trail Distance plus Per Slot Spacing per slot, matching the leader's speed instead of stopping and starting.
    • XenoCore Party Recalculate Position runs once the leader stops: it settles, picks a resting spot on the member's own side of the leader, steps onto it, and returns to Hold.
  • In battle. One state running two tasks, XenoCore Fight Target (target and auto-attack) and XenoCore Use Best Art (arts). XenoCore Party Follow walks the member to a spot an EQS query chose around the target, so the party spreads out instead of piling up. A companion fights the leader's target; with none, the nearest enemy already fighting the party. The whole battle side is its own page: Companion AI and aggro.

The party counts as in battle when the leader has drawn its weapon, or when an enemy within 30 m is already fighting the party, so companions defend themselves even before the player locks on.

XenoCore Party Follow also teleports a member that falls more than Teleport Distance behind.

All of the distances above are parameters on the tasks inside the StateTree asset. To tune them without changing the shipped tree:

  1. In Characters/Party/AI, right-click ST_XenoCore_PartyMember and choose Duplicate. Move the copy into your own folder, for example MyGame/AI.
  2. Open your copy, select a state (for example Travel), select the task in the Details panel and change its numbers. Save.
  3. In Characters/Party, right-click BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember and choose Create Child Blueprint Class. Move the child into your folder and open it.
  4. In its Components panel select StateTreeAI, and in the Details panel set its AI › State Tree to your copy. Compile and Save.
  5. Open BP_XenoCore_Party, click Class Defaults, and set XenoCore › Party › Default Controller Class to your child (or set Controller Class on one member definition, for one character only).

See Recruit by talking. Travel and battle distances ST_XenoCore_PartyMember task parameters Follow spacing, speeds, teleport distance.

Fails silently: the cursor ring overlaps the aggro ring

Party Cursor Ring Diameter is kept well inside the aggro ring (220 cm) so the two nest under a member an enemy is after. Make it 220 or larger and the rings overlap into one shape, with nothing to tell the player which is which.

Fails silently: a cursor ring material without the right parameters

The ring writes its tint to a Colour parameter and the switch flash fades it through an Opacity parameter. A material of your own without them draws the ring in its own colour, and the flash stays at full strength until it vanishes instead of fading. Nothing is logged. Copy both parameters from Effects/Aggro/M_XenoCore_AggroRing.

Fails silently: interaction on an AI body

Anything in Leader Only Ability Set is granted only to a player-controlled body. Lyra's interaction scan asserts if it runs without a player controller, which is why interaction lives there. If you add your own ability that needs a player controller, put it in that set, not in a member's pawn data.

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
• Add a character: a Blueprint plus a member definition, no code. See Add a party member and Set the starting party.
  • A flourish on a switch: implement On Switch Slide (From Slot) on your party row widget; it fires on each row whose character arrived from another row.
  • Recruit by talking to someone: set Member To Recruit on a placed NPC. See Recruit a party member by talking to them.
  • Recruit from a story event: call Add To Roster on Get Party Component, or place an AXenoCorePartyRecruitTrigger and call its Recruit node from a cutscene. A Blueprint child of the trigger can implement On Recruited for a sound or a line of dialogue.
  • Different AI: duplicate the StateTree ST_XenoCore_PartyMember (it is data), and make a child Blueprint of BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember that uses your tree. A child keeps the C++ controller the team depends on.
  • Do not keep your own list of party pawns. Ask Get Active Member Pawns or Get Pawn For Member, and listen for XenoCore.Party.Message.Changed.

Console commands

XenoSetLeader, XenoDownMember, XenoWipeParty, XenoReviveMember and XenoHurtParty run in development builds. See Diagnostics.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers: the design reasons
  • On the controller because the party must survive changing which body the player drives, and because Lyra's own party-wide systems (quick bar, item costs) look there.
  • Spawning lives with the lists because "who is active" and "who has a body" are one fact. Two components each owning half would disagree.
  • The leader is a slot so the Party screen, the HUD and the save all describe the leader the same way as everyone else. An earlier design kept the leader outside the list and every screen needed special cases for it.
  • Switching is a free action (XC3): it interrupts neither character, so the fight is handed over rather than ended and restarted. Every rule lives on the party component, so the triggers, the Party screen and the console all obey the same ones.
  • An empty roster still plays. Until you author your first member, the player keeps the pawn Lyra's game mode spawned. Nothing in the component names a character, so you can delete every shipped character without touching C++.

docs.title: Loading and ticking
docs.text:
Designers and programmers · 10 min read · No code

Who this is for: anyone adding content who wants it to stay cheap. The first half (which references to make soft, and when to tick) is for designers working in Blueprints and Details panels; the warning boxes marked For programmers are for whoever writes C++.

Two things decide most of what XenoCore costs at run time: what an asset drags into memory when it loads, and what runs every frame. A property that points straight at another asset (a hard reference) loads that asset, and everything it points at, whenever its owner loads. A Blueprint with a live Event Tick runs a Blueprint call every frame for every copy in the world. The idea that makes the rest make sense: load an asset when it is needed, not when something that might need it loads; and run code when something changes, not every frame in case it did.

docs.title: Hard and soft references
docs.text:
A soft reference stores the asset's path only. In the Details panel it looks and works exactly like a hard one: the same picker, the same thumbnail. The difference is that nothing loads until code asks for it.

Hard is right when the owner cannot do its job without the asset the moment it is used:

  • a character's meshes, anim Blueprint and the montages it always plays;
  • its Pawn Data and ability sets;
  • the widget classes a screen builds on open.

Soft is right when the asset is optional, situational, one of many, or large and needed later:

  • drop pools, shop and trade stock, quest targets, learnable Arts, rare effects;
  • a default that a Blueprint child is expected to override (fonts, glyph widgets, textures).

These XenoCore properties are soft. Existing data converted on its own; you set them the same way as before.

Property Where Loads when Enemy Target Quest objective Never by the quest. Kills are matched against enemies already in the world. See Quests Art Art learnset rows (DT_XenoCore_ArtLearnset_*) The character learns it: at spawn or level-up. See Arts Item Def Drop table entries A chest is opened, and only the items rolled. See Loot Item (offers, overtrade bonus) Shop and trade tables The shop or trade screen opens. See Shops and trade Death Effect Enemy The enemy is first provoked, so it is ready by the time the body vanishes. See Enemies and AI Glyph Class, Action Table, Font Family Tactics panel (XenoCoreTacticsPanelBase) The panel is first built. See Party tactics Font Family, Sun Texture, Moon Texture Change Time screen (XenoCoreChangeTimeScreen) The screen is first built. See Time of day and weather

Blueprint graphs that read these fields

A graph reading one of the properties above now gets a soft reference. Load it with Load Class Asset Blocking / Load Asset Blocking at a pause (below), or Async Load Class Asset / Async Load Asset if it can wait. (For programmers: in C++, the shop and trade rows have LoadItem().)

docs.title: Where to load a soft reference
docs.text:
• At a natural pause: a menu opening, a chest opening, a level-up, the moment an enemy is provoked. The player expects a beat there, and one load is invisible.
  • Never per frame or per hit. Loading from a tick or a damage path is a path lookup every call at best, and a disk read at worst.
  • Cache what you load. Keep the loaded pointer (or the async handle) while it is in use, so the second call is free and garbage collection does not unload it mid-fight.

The XenoCore Content and XenoCore UI project settings already work this way: each setting is resolved the first time it is read and then kept. Editing a setting clears the cache.

Fails silently in the editor: caching an asset on a settings object

For programmers. In a cooked game, settings objects created at startup sit in a memory pool the garbage collector never walks, so an asset cached on one is not kept alive by it. The editor never shows this. A Development build halts on the title screen ("breaking Disregard for GC assumptions"); a Shipping build frees the asset under the pointer. XenoCore's own caches go through XenoCoreSettingsCache::KeepAlive; do the same in any settings class you add, and test a packaged build.

docs.title: Ticking
docs.text:
• Prefer events and timers. React to a gameplay message, a delegate or a timer. Most "is it time yet?" checks run perfectly well every 0.2 to 0.5 s.
  • Throttle what must poll. XenoCore's own polls run on intervals: the enemy's label decides whether to tick every Label Tick Check Interval (0.4 s), and the environment director refreshes brightness, fog and sky colour at most every 0.1 s.
  • Turn tick off when idle. A widget or component with nothing to do should stop ticking and start again when something changes. Enemy health bars and labels do this.
  • No per-frame searches. Get Component by Class, Get All Actors of Class and similar iterators belong in Begin Play or behind a timer, with the result cached.

Fails silently: an Event Tick that only calls its Parent

A Blueprint whose Event Tick (or Event Blueprint Update Animation) is wired only to Parent: Tick does nothing extra, but it still makes every copy run a Blueprint call each frame. Nothing warns. Delete the node; the parent's tick still runs without it. A greyed-out Event Tick placed by default and left unconnected costs nothing.

docs.title: Measuring
docs.text:
What an asset drags in. Right-click an asset in the Content Browser and choose Size Map: it shows everything the asset loads with it, by size. Reference Viewer (same menu) shows which property holds each reference. Compare a whole play session rather than single assets: one asset's cost overstates the saving when the map or the party loads the same content anyway.

Which Blueprints tick. Open a Blueprint's Event Graph and look for a connected Event Tick; see the warning above.

For real numbers, in Play In Editor or a packaged build, open the console:

Command Shows stat game Time spent in game-thread tick, per category stat unit Frame, game, draw and GPU time dumpticks Every registered tick function, enabled or not memreport -full Memory by class and asset, written to Saved/Profiling/MemReports

Unreal Insights (run with -trace=default) shows which ticks and loads cost what, frame by frame.

docs.title: Looked at and kept
docs.text:
These came up and were deliberately left alone, so there is no need to look again:

Candidate Why it stays Body Meshes on the party base classes The template pawn already loads both Mannequin bodies, so a soft reference saves nothing Member Class on party member definitions Every starting member spawns at New Game, and the party and progression screens read benched members' class defaults Lyra's fonts Already set to Lazy Load Gaur Plain's map size The fix is converting the map to World Partition, not trimming references. See Build a world-partition map

docs.title: Progression
docs.text:
All · 15 min read · No code

The level-up panel after a fight.

Levels, experience, Art Points, learned arts, art palettes, skill progress and the party's gold are all owned by one component on the player controller, UXenoCoreProgressionComponent, set up as the Blueprint Game/BP_XenoCore_Progression. The one idea: progress is stored per character, keyed by the member definition, not by the pawn. A benched character has no body, but still has a level. When a body is spawned, it reads its level from here and applies its statline at that level.

At a glance

In play: kills pay EXP, Art Points and SP; a level-up banner lists everyone who levelled; each level raises the character's stats and fully heals them.

What you can change, no code:

  • How much EXP each level needs, per character: Tune progression
  • What an enemy pays: Experience Reward and Art Point Reward on the enemy Blueprint
  • Whether benched members earn, the starting gold, palette slot unlock levels: Game/BP_XenoCore_Progression › Class Defaults. Listed under What you can change.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Piece Asset What it does Progression component Game/BP_XenoCore_Progression Holds every character's record and the purse. Added to the player controller by the plugin's Game Feature Data. EXP curves Game/DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves (Data Table, row structure XenoCoreExperienceCurveRow) EXP needed to go from level X to X + 1. One row per curve: XC1 (the default) and one per sample character. A member definition's Experience Curve picks its row. Reward curve Battle/Attributes/CT_XenoCore_RewardLevelDiff, row Reward.LevelDiffMultiplier EXP multiplier by (party level − enemy level). Enemy reward Each enemy's Experience Reward, Art Point Reward and Skill Point Multiplier Base EXP, AP and SP scaling for a kill. Statline Each character's Stats Effect Re-applied on level-up. See Stats and damage. Level-up banner UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_LevelUp (UXenoCoreLevelUpBannerBase) One panel listing everyone who levelled, with HP rolling up.

Each character's record holds: Level, Experience (progress into the current level), learned arts, the art palette, each art's level and level cap, Art Points, and skill-tree progress (see Skills). The first time a character is seen, its record is seeded from its Blueprint's Combatant Level; after that the Blueprint value is never read again for that character.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
An enemy dies. The enemy calls Award Experience For Kill on the party's progression component, which pays three things:

  • EXP: the enemy's Experience Reward × its Experience Level Scale row at the enemy's level (if set) × the reward curve at (leader's level − enemy level), rounded. The sample minions read CT_XenoCore_EnemyStats › Minion.ExperienceScale, so a same-level kill is worth the same share of a level at every level. Enemies well below the party give little; enemies above give more.
  • Art Points: Art Points Base + Art Points Per Enemy Level × the enemy's level (2 + 2 × level by default), times the same reward-curve multiplier. An enemy whose Art Point Reward is 0 or more pays that amount instead of the formula (still times the multiplier).
  • Skill Points: a band from the Skill Point Reward Table by level difference, paid into each character's selected skill branch. See Skills.

EXP is banked. The award walks the whole roster:

  • Active members get the full amount; reserve members get Reserve Experience Rate of it. The sample sets it to 0, so a benched character earns nothing; the C++ default is XC1's 0.9. The same rate applies to a kill's Art Points.
  • A character recruited with Join At Party Level is raised to the party's level when they join, so a mid-story recruit does not arrive at level 1.
  • A character's skills can raise their own share: a kill asks for their battle-EXP and AP skill bonuses, a quest turn-in for their quest-EXP bonus.
  • Only kills pay Art Points. Award Experience (used by quest rewards and the XenoAwardExp cheat) pays EXP alone.
  • Each member levels up as many times as the EXP covers, up to the level cap. Levelling stops if the curve returns 0 for a level.

A member levels up.

  1. Arts whose unlock level has been reached are learned (added to the character's list, not equipped).
  2. If the member has a body, its statline is re-applied at the new level from its own Stats Effect, and its palette is re-granted (a new level can open a palette slot).
  3. Because every statline overrides Health as well as Max Health, a level-up fully heals the character. This is intended.
  4. A benched member has no body; the new level is simply read when it next spawns.

Messages. After the award, the component broadcasts XenoCore.Progression.Message.Changed (levelled count, EXP awarded, and Gains: what each member was paid in EXP, AP and SP, benched members included; a kill sends one message for all three), then, if anyone levelled, XenoCore.Progression.Message.LevelUp carrying each member with their level before and after. The level-up banner listens for the second. It shows everyone in one panel, waits for any quest reward banner to finish first, and leaves on its own after Hold Time plus Hold Per Member for each line. Pressing the interact button while it is up dismisses it.

A level-up heals only because the statline overrides Health

The full heal is not code; it comes from the Health modifier on every GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_*. If you remove that modifier, or change it to Add, level-ups stop healing and nothing reports it. For the same reason, never re-apply a statline for any other purpose: each application is a free full heal.

An EXP curve must cover every level up to the cap

Each row of DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves lists the cost of every level in turn. Past its last entry a character is at the cap and stops levelling. An entry of 0 would freeze a character at that level, so Data Validation rejects it on save, and warns about a row shorter than Max Character Level.

Level-up does not revive

A downed party member stays down until revived or the battle ends; a level-up records the new level but does not stand them up.

docs.title: Gold
docs.text: The purse is Gold on the same component, 3,000 at the start of a new game. Award Gold adds and broadcasts XenoCore.Progression.Message.Changed; Spend Gold is all-or-nothing and returns false if the party cannot afford it. Gold is not an attribute and no Gameplay Effect can change it. Shops and quest rewards go through these two nodes. See Shops and trade.

docs.title: Arts and Art Points
docs.text:
Setting Default Meaning Default Art Level Cap 4 An art's level cap until something raises it (Raise Art Level Cap). Art Level Cost Multipliers 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 18, 25, 33, 42, 53, 65 Cost multiplier for raising an art to level 2, 3 ... 12, times the art's base cost. Art Points Base 2.0 The flat part of a kill's AP. Art Points Per Enemy Level 2.0 AP per level of the defeated enemy, added to Art Points Base. Art Slot Unlock Levels 1, 1, 1, 12, 20, 28, 34, 40 Character level at which each palette slot opens. Eight entries means eight slots. Entries are in unlock order, not screen order: the bar fills from the centre out (slot 0 left of the Talent Art, slot 1 right, slot 2 next left...), so keep the list ascending. Default Art Ability Class Battle/Arts/GA_XenoCore_Art_Base The ability every art runs as unless its definition names another.

An enemy's own Art Point Reward (XenoCore › Enemy, default -1) overrides the formula for that enemy; -1 means use it. Level Up Art spends a character's own Art Points. Learning, equipping and the palette are covered in Arts.

All slots from the start

Set every entry of Art Slot Unlock Levels to 1 to give characters their full palette immediately.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
Setting Where it lives What it does Default Experience Curve BP_XenoCore_Progression › XenoCore › Progression The EXP curve for a character with none of its own: a row of DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves. Experience Curve Member definition › XenoCore › Progression This character's own EXP curve. Empty uses the default. Reward Multiplier Curve BP_XenoCore_Progression › XenoCore › Progression Level-gap EXP multiplier table. Reserve Experience Rate BP_XenoCore_Progression › XenoCore › Progression Benched members' share of EXP and kill AP (0 in the sample). Gold BP_XenoCore_Progression › XenoCore › Progression Starting purse. Art settings BP_XenoCore_Progression › XenoCore › Arts See the table above. Experience Reward Enemy Blueprint or placed enemy › XenoCore › Enemy Base EXP per kill: the enemy TYPE's weight. Experience Level Scale Enemy Blueprint › XenoCore › Enemy A curve-table row that multiplies Experience Reward at the enemy's level. Empty = the same EXP at every level. Raise Member To Level Progression component, Blueprint node Raise a character to at least a level (never lowers). What a recruit joining at the party's level uses. For a walkthrough, see Tune progression.

docs.title: Console commands
docs.text:
These work in PIE and development builds (they are cheat-manager commands):

Command Effect XenoAwardExp 5000 Award EXP to the party, as a kill or quest would. XenoAwardGold 500 Add gold. XenoGiveAP 1000 Art Points for the leader. XenoGiveSP 500 Skill Points into the leader's selected branch. XenoSkills Print the leader's branches and progress. XenoArts Print the leader's learned arts and palette. XenoSetArt 2 AirSlash Put an art into a palette slot. XenoCastArt AirSlash Use an equipped art the way the palette does.

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
• To reward EXP or gold from anything (a landmark, a cutscene), call Award Experience or Award Gold on Get Party Progression.
  • To show progression on a new screen, read Get Member Level, Get Member Experience and Get Member Experience Fraction for a member definition, and refresh on XenoCore.Progression.Message.Changed.
  • To buff the whole party, apply a separate effect on top of each statline. Never replace the statline with a shared one: every character would then take the same numbers on their next level.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers: the design reasons
  • On the controller and keyed by definition because the party levels together, and half the roster has no body at any given time. A level stored on a pawn would not exist for a benched character.
  • The statline comes from the character, never from the component, so a level-up and a respawn produce the same numbers by calling the same function.
  • One level-up message carrying everybody because the party levels at once, and a banner needs the whole set to draw one panel.
  • Messages carry the amount awarded because afterwards the component only knows the running total; "you gained 200" cannot be reconstructed from "you have 1,400".

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
All · 15 min read · No code

What the player sees: an NPC with a "!" bubble offers a quest on a screen with its title, who is asking, the objectives and the reward. Accepting it puts it in the Quest Log and on the HUD tracker; the minimap marks what it still wants; and talking to the giver when it is done pays the reward under a "quest complete" banner.

A quest is a data asset: a title, some objectives, a reward, and optional conditions for when it may be offered. You make one by duplicating a sample quest and filling in its Details panel. The party's progress is remembered per quest asset, so the quest asset is the quest's identity: a quest keeps working when its giver is unloaded, the leader changes, or the game is saved and loaded.

docs.title: What you can change
docs.text:
• A "bring me N of something" quest: Make a collection quest.
  • A defeat-enemies, talk-to-someone or go-somewhere quest: Give a quest to defeat enemies, talk to someone, or go somewhere.
  • Which NPC gives it and what they say: the NPC's Quest and quest dialogue fields; see Interaction, NPCs and dialogue.
  • When it may be offered: its Gates (below).
  • How the quest screens look: their Blueprints' class defaults under XenoCore › Quest.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Piece Kind Job Quests/DA_XenoCore_Quest_Collection01, DA_XenoCore_Quest_Monster01 Quest definitions (data assets) The two Gym sample quests Quests/GaurPlain/DA_XenoCore_Quest_GP_* Quest definitions The seven quests of the Gaur Plain slice, given by NPCs placed in Maps/L_XenoCore_GaurPlain Quest ledger Built in (on the player controller) Status, objective counts, who asked, which quest is tracked. Reach it in a Blueprint with Get Party Quests Offer Quest Blueprint node with Accepted and Declined outputs Opens the offer screen, continues on Accepted or Declined UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_QuestOffer Screen Title, requester, summary, objectives, rewards, Accept/Decline UserInterface/W_XenoCore_QuestLog Screen Every accepted and finished quest, from the menu UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_QuestTracker HUD plate The tracked quest and its outstanding objectives UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_QuestReward HUD plate The "quest complete" banner with what was paid Quest UI nodes Blueprint nodes (XenoCore › Quest) Row info for the log, requester name, Open Quest Log

Every XenoCore Experience has the quest ledger; there is nothing to add to a map.

The sample NPCs are in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym: NPC_QuestGiver gives DA_XenoCore_Quest_Collection01 and NPC_MonsterQuestGiver gives DA_XenoCore_Quest_Monster01. Characters/NPC/B_XenoCore_Npc_Sample also carries Collection01, as a ready-made example; the plain B_XenoCore_Npc gives no quest.

docs.title: What the two sample quests do
docs.text:
• Collection01 is a collect quest: one Collect Item objective for 2 ID_XenoCore_EtherCrystal, taken from the bag on turn-in, rewarding ID_XenoCore_BlueChain, 500 gold and 200 experience.
  • Monster01 is a kill quest: one Defeat Enemy objective for 2 B_XenoCore_Minion_Melee, rewarding ID_XenoCore_ScrapPlating, 300 gold and 400 experience. Every minion killed while the quest is active counts, including any child Blueprint of the minion. Its Party Level At Least gate is set to 1, so it never blocks: it is there as a worked example. Raise the level to see a gate work.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
A quest's status, shown on screen as the log's status column:

Status Meaning Offerable? Unknown Never answered Yes Declined Turned down once Yes, the player can come back Active Accepted, objectives outstanding No Ready To Turn In Every objective met No Complete Turned in and paid. Final No
  1. Offer. The NPC's graph calls Offer Quest. If the quest is not offerable (already taken, or a gate does not hold) nothing opens. The screen pauses the conversation, which resumes on the answer. Exactly one of Accepted or Declined always fires, even if the screen is torn down.
  2. Accept. The status becomes Active and the counts are filled straight away from the bag. A collect quest for something you already carry can be Ready To Turn In the moment you accept it. The giver's name is recorded. If nothing is tracked yet, this quest becomes the tracked one.
  3. Progress.
    • Collect Item counts are recomputed from the bag every time the bag changes. They are never added up from pickups, so spending or selling the item lowers the count again.
    • Defeat Enemy counts go up by one per kill, only while the quest is Active. Kills before you accepted do not count. They cannot be recomputed, so they are what the save file keeps.
    • Talk To NPC counts when the party talks to the placed NPC whose Quest Id matches, before that NPC's own graph runs, so a last-step talk to the giver can hand in within the same conversation. Reach Location counts when the leader walks into the matching Quest Location (companions never count), once per visit for each quest.
    • When every objective is met the status moves to Ready To Turn In, and back to Active if a collected item leaves the bag.
  4. Turn in. The NPC's graph calls Turn In. It re-checks the bag first. If the quest is not really ready it returns false and stays Active. Otherwise it:
    • removes the collected items whose objective has Consume On Turn In ticked,
    • pays the gold, and experience to the whole roster (reserve members at the Reserve Experience Rate, 0 in the sample, see Progression),
    • adds the reward items to the party bag,
    • marks the quest Complete, moves tracking to another running quest, and shows the reward banner.

Gates are checked when a quest is offered, never again. A quest you already have is not taken away because the leader changed to a lower-level character.

The quest marker ("!" bubble) over a giver shows while the quest is offerable or ready to turn in, and hides while it is Active. A gated quest shows no marker at all.

Who asked. The offer screen and the tracker name the requester in this order: the quest's own Requester Name; otherwise the NPC offering it; otherwise the name recorded at Accept. The tracker has no NPC to ask, which is why the name is recorded. It reads "Return to name" when the quest is ready.

The minimap marks what the tracked quest still wants in blue: the enemies a Defeat Enemy objective needs, the NPC of a Talk To NPC step, the Quest Location of a Reach Location step, and the giver once the quest is ready. See Minimap.

The tracker follows exactly one quest. Pick it in the Quest Log. Show or hide it with the quest tracker button (see Controls).

Saving. Every quest's status (by name), its counts, its recorded requester and the tracked quest are saved. On load, collect counts are recomputed from the restored bag; kill counts come from the file. See Save and front end.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
On a quest definition:

Setting Where it lives What it does Title XenoCore › Quest The quest's name on every screen Kind XenoCore › Quest Collection, Material, Monster, Challenge, Search, Normal, Story. A label only: it titles the offer screen and sorts the log, and changes no behaviour Area XenoCore › Quest Free text shown beside the quest in the log Requester Name XenoCore › Quest Who is asking. Leave empty to use the NPC's Display Name Requester Portrait XenoCore › Quest The face on the offer screen. Empty hides the frame Summary XenoCore › Quest The paragraph under the requester Objectives XenoCore › Quest What must be done (below) Gates XenoCore › Quest Conditions before it is offered. All must hold. Empty means always offerable Reward XenoCore › Quest Gold, Experience, and Items (one entry per item, so ten of a thing is ten entries) Can Decline XenoCore › Quest Untick to show only Accept, and ignore Back

Each objective:

Setting What it does Description The prose line on the offer screen and in the log Counter Label The noun in "Name 0/2". Empty uses the item's own name Kind Collect Item, Defeat Enemy, Talk To NPC or Reach Location Item Target The item to hold (Collect Item) Enemy Target The enemy class to defeat (Defeat Enemy). A parent class counts every child. A soft reference: the quest does not load the enemy Blueprint Target Id Talk To NPC: the placed NPC's Quest Id. Reach Location: a placed XenoCore Quest Location's Location Id. Matched by name Required Count How many Consume On Turn In Take the items away on turn-in (Collect Item) Icon Source, Icon Category, Icon Texture The icon beside this objective on the offer screen, log and tracker

Each gate is Party Level At Least (the leader's level) or Quest Completed (another quest must be turned in, not just accepted).

Talk and location steps match by name

A quest asset cannot point at an actor placed in a level, so Talk To NPC and Reach Location match the objective's Target Id against an NPC's Quest Id or a Quest Location's Location Id. Saving an objective with an empty Target Id reports an error. See Create a kill, talk or location quest.

Fails silently: a gate that can never pass

A quest whose gate never holds is simply never offered. There is no marker to notice missing, and nothing is logged. To check, run XenoQuestStatus in the console, or call Get Gate Requirement Text on Get Party Quests from a Blueprint: it returns the reason as player text. No shipped screen shows it yet.

Reordering objectives breaks existing saves

Saved counts are stored in objective order. Reorder a shipped quest's Objectives and a player's saved kill counts land on the wrong objective.

The screens' styling and spacing live on their Blueprints' class defaults under XenoCore › Quest: colours for the tracker and reward banner, the banner's duration, and so on.

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
• A new quest is a new data asset, not code: duplicate DA_XenoCore_Quest_Collection01 into Content/MyGame/Quests/, edit it, and set it as the Quest of a placed NPC. See Make a collection quest.
  • Custom quest flow (extra lines, a cutscene between accept and the first objective) goes in the NPC's On Interact graph around Offer Quest and Turn In. Use Get Lines For with Greeting, Accepted, Declined, In Progress or Turn In to pick the NPC's authored lines.
  • Accepting from script (a story quest with no screen): call Accept on Get Party Quests. Leave Giver empty; the tracker then says "Return to the quest giver".
  • A custom step with no objective kind of its own (pull a lever, win a minigame): use a Talk To NPC or Reach Location objective and advance it from any Blueprint with Notify Objective on Get Party Quests, passing its Kind and the objective's Target Id.
  • A new objective kind needs a programmer: the list of kinds is fixed in C++.
  • Reacting to quests from your own Blueprints: listen for XenoCore.Quest.Message.Changed and re-read the component, or XenoCore.Quest.Message.TurnedIn for the payout. See Events you can listen to.

Console command for checking the ledger: XenoQuestStatus prints every quest the party has touched.

For programmers: classes

Definition UXenoCoreQuestDefinition; ledger UXenoCoreQuestComponent (a controller component added by the plugin's GameFeatureData, XenoCore.uasset); Offer Quest is the latent node UXenoCoreOfferQuest; screens derive from UXenoCoreQuestOfferBase, UXenoCoreQuestLogBase, UXenoCoreQuestTrackerBase and UXenoCoreQuestRewardBase; UI helpers are UXenoCoreQuestUIStatics. A new objective kind is a value appended to EXenoCoreObjectiveKind (never reorder it) plus a listener in UXenoCoreQuestComponent for whatever advances it.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
For programmers
  • On the controller, not a world subsystem. Quest state must outlive a map and be saved. The controller is also where Lyra and XenoCore keep other party-wide state, such as the bag.
  • Keyed by the definition. Same reason the progression component keys characters by their member definition: the NPC may be gone, and the asset outlives everything.
  • No "Offered" status. A state that exists only while a screen is up can be stranded by a crash or a level change. The screen's being open is the screen's business.
  • Counts recomputed from the bag. A running total drifts the first time anything changes the bag without the message it expects. Re-reading the bag is correct by construction.
  • Changed carries no detail; TurnedIn does. Every screen re-reads the component on Changed, so no copy can go stale. The turn-in payout is the exception: once paid, the gold is part of a running total and cannot be reconstructed by re-reading.
  • Kind is only a label. If code branched on it, adding a new kind would stop being data.

Next: Shops and trade · Interaction, NPCs and dialogue

docs.title: Reactions and statuses
docs.text:
All · 15 min read · No code

A reaction is one step of the Break → Topple → Daze chain. A status is a timed buff or debuff such as Slow or Strength Up. Both are plain Gameplay Effects applied to the target's Ability System Component (ASC), and both are represented on that ASC by a gameplay tag. Nothing tracks "this enemy is Toppled" anywhere else: every system that cares, from the damage formula to the popups to the player's knock-down animation, asks the target's ASC whether it holds the tag. The chain rule (Topple only works on a Broken target, Daze only on a Toppled one) is enforced by the effects themselves, not by the Arts that apply them.

At a glance

In play: BREAK, TOPPLE and DAZE pop up over an enemy as the chain lands; a Toppled or Dazed character falls and cannot act. Buffs and debuffs pop up by name and show as icons on the party rows.

What you can change, no code:

  • Which Arts Break, Topple or Daze: Make an art inflict reactions
  • A new buff or debuff: Add a status effect
  • The knock-down and flinch clips for one character: Give a character its own combat animations
  • How long each reaction lasts: the Duration of Battle/Reactions/GE_XenoCore_Reaction_*
  • Every setting: What you can change

See the Glossary for Break, Topple, Daze and Status effect.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Piece Asset / class Job Reaction effects Battle/Reactions/GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Break, _Topple, _Daze Grant Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Break / .Topple / .Daze for their own duration Status effects Battle/Status/GE_XenoCore_Status_* (19 shipped: Slow, Haste, Poison, Bleed, Blaze, Chill, Bind, Regenerate, Max HP Up, and Up/Down for Strength, Ether, Agility, Physical Def and Ether Def) Modify an attribute or grant a tag, for a duration Status base class UXenoCoreStatusEffect A Gameplay Effect that also knows its name, colour, abbreviation and icon Status icons UserInterface/Status/Icons/T_XenoCore_Status_* Optional icon textures Who applies them An Art definition's Effects list; the minion's Arts DA_XenoCore_Minion_Rend (Break) and DA_XenoCore_Minion_Sweep (Topple) Apply the effect to the target Popups UXenoCoreBattleNotifySubsystem · UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_BattleNotify BREAK / TOPPLE / DAZE and status names over the affected character HUD icons UXenoCorePartyMemberPlateBase · W_XenoCore_PartyMemberPlate One icon per active status on a party member's plate Player reactions Battle/GA_XenoCore_Player_Topple, GA_XenoCore_Player_Daze (UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_ToppleReact, _DazeReact) Knock-down animation and movement lock when the player's side is Toppled or Dazed Enemy reactions Characters/Enemies/Minion/GA_XenoCore_Minion_Topple, GA_XenoCore_Minion_Daze (same classes), granted by AbilitySet_XenoCore_Minion_Melee The minion's knock-down (AM_XenoCore_Minion_Topple, AM_XenoCore_Minion_Daze), held for as long as the reaction lasts Incapacitation UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_AutoAttack › Incapacitated Tags A Toppled or Dazed attacker does not swing or use its Arts Flinch UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_HitReact · GA_XenoCore_Player_HitReact, GA_XenoCore_Minion_HitReact Directional hit reaction

How the chain is enforced, as read from the effects' components:

Effect Requires the target to have Grants GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Break nothing Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Break GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Topple Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Break Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Topple GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Daze Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Topple Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Daze

The requirement is the effect's Require Tags to Apply/Continue This Effect component (Application Tag Requirements › Must Have Tags), so a Topple on a target that is not Broken is refused and nothing is logged. Break lasts 10 s (a number of ours; XC1's is not documented), Topple 3.5 s and Daze 2.0 s.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Applying. An Art's Effects entry picks the effect, rolls its Chance, and applies it to each recipient. For a status, the entry's Duration and Magnitude are sent into the effect as SetByCaller values on XenoCore.Status.Duration and XenoCore.Status.Magnitude, so one status asset serves every Art that applies it, each with its own numbers. Reactions carry their own timings, so their entries leave Duration at 0.

A Topple or Daze applied to a target that is not in the right state is refused by the effect. The Art still plays, still deals damage and still goes on cooldown; the reaction simply does not land.

While active. The tag is on the target's ASC for the effect's duration. What reads it:

  • The damage formula: a Dazed target cannot be missed, Ether Arts always crit a Dazed target, and a critical hit on a Toppled or Dazed target uses the larger critical multiplier.
  • Art Effects conditions (Target is Broken / Toppled / Dazed).
  • The enemy AI, which chooses its next Art by the target's reaction state (see Enemies and AI).
  • The popup subsystem, which shows BREAK (pink), TOPPLE (green) or DAZE (yellow) the moment the tag first appears.
  • A VRoid character's face, which changes expression on each reaction.
  • On the player's side: GA_XenoCore_Player_Topple and GA_XenoCore_Player_Daze trigger when the tag is added to their own ASC (trigger source: owned tag added). They play the knock-down montage (Topple follows it with a get-up), hold the ability open until the montage ends, and carry Gameplay.MovementStopped so the character cannot move meanwhile. The trigger, the hold and the movement lock come from the C++ classes, so a Blueprint copy only chooses clips.
  • A knock-down does not start while the character holds Status.XenoCore.ArtExecuting or Status.XenoCore.Arming. So a player Toppled in the middle of an Art or a weapon draw carries the Topple (TOPPLE shows, and the auto-attack pauses) but does not fall. Enemies are never affected: their Arts and draws hold neither tag.
  • On the enemy side: GA_XenoCore_Minion_Topple and GA_XenoCore_Minion_Daze trigger the same way and play the minion's knock-down. They have Hold While Trigger Tag Present on, so the minion stays down for exactly as long as the reaction tag lasts: a clip shorter than the reaction holds its last pose, a longer one is cut when the tag goes. The minion has no get-up clip, so it simply blends back to its idle.
  • Any attacker built on the auto-attack base (the auto-attack itself and the minion's Arts) checks Incapacitated Tags (Topple and Daze by default). While the attacker carries one, its auto-attack loop pauses, its Arts refuse to start (so the enemy AI sees them as not ready and no cooldown is spent), and a swing already in flight does not connect. The enemy's chase also stops, so a toppled minion does not turn to follow you.

Ending. When the effect expires GAS removes the tag. Nothing else has to clean up.

Statuses. When a UXenoCoreStatusEffect is newly applied, its Display Name pops up over the character in its Colour, in upper case, smaller than a reaction. Refreshing a status that is already on does not pop up again. Party member plates re-read their character's active statuses every Status Refresh Interval (default 0.2 s) and draw one icon per status: the Icon texture if set, otherwise the Colour with the Abbreviation written on it. Debuffs sort before buffs.

Hit reactions. Each landed hit sends XenoCore.Event.HitReact to the victim. The victim's hit-react ability decides whether to flinch and picks front, back, left or right from its own facing. It does not activate while the victim holds Status.XenoCore.ArtExecuting (mid-Art) or Status.XenoCore.Arming (drawing a weapon). A flinch also does not play while the victim holds one of its Flinch Suppressed By Tags (Topple and Daze by default), so a knock-down is never replaced by a flinch. Damage still lands in every case; only the animation is suppressed.

A hit never interrupts. As in XC1, a landed hit does not stop a swing or an Art; only a reaction (Topple, Daze) does. The shipped flinches are additive clips on their own AdditiveHitReact slot, so the jolt layers over whatever the body is doing. The hit-react ability's Flinch On Hit plays it; both shipped hit reacts turn it on (the C++ default is off).

Knockback. A flinch also knocks the victim back, straight away from the attacker: its hit-react ability's Push Distance (60 cm) x the hit's Force Multiplier, over Push Time (0.12 s), and then it stops dead. Auto-attacks ship at Force Multiplier 1 and the shipped damage Arts at 2. Whatever stops the flinch stops the push too, so a guard, an Art in progress, a weapon draw or a knock-down is never shoved. The flinch itself plays additively, so the body leans with the hit while it moves.

docs.text:
