Add Event On Focused and Event On Unfocused. For example, set Render Custom Depth on the lever mesh to true and false. They fire once per change: when the prompt starts offering this actor, and when it stops (out of range, disabled, or a menu covers the world).

No focus event on destruction

An actor destroyed while it is focused does not receive On Unfocused. Clean up in Event End Play if a highlight lives on something else.

docs.title: 6. Place it
docs.text: Drag BP_MyGame_Lever into your level. You need nothing else: no ability, no input, no widget.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Place the lever in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play.
  2. Walk up to it. At about 2 m the prompt beside the player shows A Pull and X Inspect.
  3. Press X (keyboard F): the message prints; the prompt stays.
  4. Press A (keyboard E): the lever acts, and the prompt disappears straight away.
  5. Walk away and back: no prompt, because it is disabled.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
No prompt at all

Check, in order: Interact Enabled is ticked on the placed instance; Can Interact returns true; the player is within Interact Range of the actor's origin; a menu, banner or conversation is not covering the world (the prompt hides then).

Another interactable wins

The prompt offers only the nearest available interactable. An NPC or chest closer to the player takes the prompt. Move them apart or shorten the other's range.

The Blueprint child of an NPC or chest shows a third action that does nothing

NPCs have an Extra Interact Verbs list. The interaction subsystem keeps only the first two verbs (A and X), drops the rest from the prompt, and logs a warning once per actor (LogXenoInteract: "offers N verbs but only 2 interact inputs exist"). See World and maps troubleshooting.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Remember that it was pulled: add a XenoCore Save Participant component and tick SaveGame on the variable that holds the state. See Make a system save.
  • Interaction, NPCs and dialogue
  • A third button is a programmer job.
For programmers

A third button needs a new input action, a new interact-press ability, and a raise of UXenoCoreInteractionSubsystem::MaxPressableVerbs (a constexpr 2). The prompt widget can draw four.

docs.title: Add a menu screen
docs.text:
Designer · 45 min · No code

Result: a new entry in the in-game menu, Bestiary, that opens your own screen. The gamepad and keyboard navigate it, B / Escape returns to the menu, and the character cannot move or jump while it is open.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• UI shell and HUD: layers, activatable widgets and input modes.
  • Restyle the menus lists the shared button and text styles to reuse.

docs.title: How a menu screen works
docs.text:
XenoCore's menus use Epic's CommonUI through Lyra:

  • A screen is an activatable widget: a widget that knows when it is on top, where focus goes, and whether it handles Back. Blueprint screens derive from Lyra's LyraActivatableWidget.
  • Screens are pushed onto a layer, a stack of screens. Menus go on the layer tagged UI.Layer.Menu (a gameplay tag). Only the top screen of a layer is shown, and Back pops it off to reveal the one underneath.
  • The menu (UserInterface/W_XenoCore_MenuShell) is itself a screen on that layer. Input/Abilities/GA_XenoCore_ToggleMenu pushes it when the player presses the menu button.
  • The shell has no hand-placed buttons. Each time it opens it builds one button per menu entry, from Project Settings › Game › XenoCore UI › Menu Entries. An entry is data: a label, and either a screen to push or an action to run. So adding a screen to the menu is a settings change, not an edit to the shell.
  • A screen's Input Config decides the input mode. Menu mode switches off the gameplay input contexts, so the character stops responding while the screen is up.

The Party, Equipment and Items screens are all built this way, as Blueprints. Use UserInterface/W_XenoCore_PartyManager as your reference when something is unclear.

docs.title: 1. Create the screen
docs.text:
1. In MyGame/UI, right-click and choose User Interface › Widget Blueprint. Pick LyraActivatableWidget as the parent class. Name it W_Bestiary.
  2. Open it. In the Designer, build the layout: a background, a title, and a vertical box of buttons or a list. Use W_XenoCore_MenuButton or W_XenoCore_TabButton from UserInterface/Foundation so it matches the rest of the menus.
  3. Any text or image you lay over a button must have Visibility set to Hit Test Invisible (or Self Hit Test Invisible for a panel).

Fails silently: a label drawn over a button steals the pad's A press

With the default input settings, pad A on a focused button is delivered as a click at the button's centre, routed by what is under that point. A visible text block sitting over the button receives the click instead, and the button never fires. The mouse works if you click beside the text, so it looks intermittent. Make every overlay Hit Test Invisible.

docs.title: 2. Set its class defaults
docs.text:
Click Class Defaults and set (the categories are Lyra's and CommonUI's):

Setting Value Why Input › Input Config Menu Switches gameplay input off while the screen is up Back › Is Back Handler ticked Without it, B / Escape does nothing on this screen Back › Is Back Action Displayed In Action Bar ticked Shows the Back glyph in the footer

Then override Get Desired Focus Target (under Functions › Override) and return the widget that should have the cursor when the screen opens, such as the first button.

Fails silently: no focus target

Without Get Desired Focus Target a gamepad player opens the screen with nothing selected, and the stick does nothing. The mouse still works, so you may not notice at your desk.

docs.title: 3. Bind your buttons in Construct
docs.text:
In the Graph, bind each button's click once:

  1. Select the button in the Designer and click + next to On Clicked in its Details › Events, or
  2. In Event Construct, drag the button's variable and use Assign On Clicked.

Bind clicks in Construct, never in On Activated

Assign adds a handler every time it runs. On Activated runs every time the screen is reopened, so the third visit fires your click three times.

CommonUI reuses closed screens

A closed screen is pooled and handed back the next time it is pushed. Anything that must start fresh on each visit (a selection, a flag, a "done" bool) must be reset in On Activated, not in Construct or as a variable default.

docs.title: 4. Add the entry to the menu
docs.text:
1. Open Edit › Project Settings, and under Game choose XenoCore UI.

  2. Under Menu › Menu Entries, click +. Fill in the new entry:

    Field Value What it does Id Bestiary A stable name. Another list can replace this entry by using the same Id Label Bestiary The button's text Description Monsters you have met. The line along the bottom of the menu while the entry is highlighted Screen W_Bestiary The screen pushed when the button is pressed Layer leave empty Empty means UI.Layer.Menu Sort Order 650 Lower sorts higher. The shipped entries are 100 apart Visible If leave empty A condition class; empty means always shown Starts Group unticked Leaves a gap above the entry (Menu Group Gap), as above Save Hidden unticked Leaves the entry out without deleting it

  3. Close Project Settings. The change is saved to Config/DefaultGame.ini.

The shipped entries, and their Sort Order:

Sort Id Label Opens 100 Equipment Equipment Screen W_XenoCore_EquipmentScreen 200 Arts Arts Action Open Arts Screen 300 Skills Skills Action Open Skills Screen 400 Collectables Collectables Screen W_XenoCore_ItemMenu 500 Party Party Screen W_XenoCore_PartyManager 600 QuestLog Quest Log Action Open Quest Log 700 ChangeTime Change Time Screen XenoCoreChangeTimeScreen 800 Save Save Action Open Save Screen (Starts Group: the system entries follow a gap) 900 Load Load Action Open Load Screen 1000 Tutorials Tutorials Screen XenoCoreTutorialLogBase 1100 Settings Settings Screen Lyra's W_LyraSettingScreen 1200 ReturnToTitle Quit to Title Action Return To Title (asks first if there is unsaved progress) 1300 QuitGame Quit Game Action Quit Game (asks first if there is unsaved progress)

So 650 puts Bestiary between Quest Log and Change Time. Two entries with the same Sort Order keep the order they are listed in.

When the entry is pressed, the screen is pushed onto its layer and focus goes to the screen's Get Desired Focus Target, the same as the shipped screens. Pushing on the menu layer stacks your screen on top of the menu, so Back returns to the menu without any extra wiring.

Don't push onto UI.Layer.Modal or the Game layer

UI.Layer.Modal is for Lyra's full-screen dialogs and does not stack under the menu. The game layer holds the HUD, and a screen there never takes Menu input mode.

Fails silently: an Id that is already taken

Entries are merged by Id. An entry whose Id matches a shipped one (for example Save) replaces that entry rather than adding a new button. Give each of your entries its own Id.

Thirteen entries fill the menu at 1080p

The shipped thirteen entries, with their padding and the group gap, just fit a 1080-pixel-high screen without scrolling. Before adding a fourteenth, lower Menu Button Padding or Menu Group Gap, or hide an entry you do not need, and check the bottom entry is still on screen.

docs.title: 5. Optional: keep your entries in your own asset
docs.text:
Editing Menu Entries changes the project's DefaultGame.ini. To keep your entries in your own content instead (for example inside your own Game Feature plugin):

  1. In Content/MyGame/UI, create a Data Asset of class XenoCoreMenuEntrySet. Name it MES_MyGame_Menu.
  2. Add your entries under Entries, filled in as in step 4.
  3. In XenoCore UI, add the asset to Menu › Additional Menu Entry Sets.

Sets are merged after Menu Entries, in list order. An entry with a matching Id replaces the earlier one where it stands, so a set can also reword a shipped entry, or tick Hidden on it to remove it. An entry with no Id is always added.

docs.title: 6. Optional: do something other than open a screen
docs.text:
• Run something: create a Blueprint child of XenoCoreMenuAction, override Run (you are given the Player and the Menu widget), and set it as the entry's Action. Action wins over Screen when both are set. The action runs on its class default object, so keep no state on it.
  • Show it only sometimes: create a Blueprint child of XenoCoreMenuCondition, override Is Visible (given the Player), and set it as Visible If. It is asked each time the menu opens.

  • A different button: set Menu › Menu Button Class to your own CommonUI button. Implement the XenoCoreMenuButton interface on it to receive the whole entry (label and Icon) through Set Menu Entry; otherwise the shell calls its Set Button Text function. The default is XenoCoreMenuEntryButton, a Party Tactics-style row; Lyra's W_LyraMenuButton also works. Menu Button Padding sets the space around each button (default 4 px below).

  • A menu of your own layout: call Build Menu In Panel (or Build Menu with a panel reference) from your widget's Construct to fill a panel with the same buttons, or read Get Menu Entries and call Activate Menu Entry yourself.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym, press Play, open the menu (pad Y, keyboard I).
  2. Bestiary is in the list between Quest Log and Change Time. Select it with the pad; its description shows along the bottom of the menu.
  3. The screen opens with your first button selected. Move with the stick or arrow keys.
  4. Press A on a button and its click runs once.
  5. Press Jump: the character does not jump.
  6. Press B (keyboard Escape). You are back on the menu. Close the menu and move normally.
  7. Open Bestiary again and click once: it still fires once.

Keyboard

Keyboard Enter or Space presses the focused button too. See Controls.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Back does nothing

Is Back Handler is not ticked on W_Bestiary.

The character jumps or moves while the screen is open

Input Config is left at Default. Set it to Menu.

The screen opens but nothing is selected on a gamepad

Override Get Desired Focus Target.

A click fires twice after reopening

You bound it in On Activated. Move the binding to Event Construct.

Bestiary is not in the menu

Check Hidden is unticked, Visible If is empty or returns true, and no other entry (in Menu Entries or an entry set) has the same Id. If the button is there but does nothing, the Output Log names the entry (LogXenoMenu): "has neither an Action nor a Screen", or "did not load".

Fails silently in a packaged build: the entry does nothing

A screen or action named only in settings is not found by the cooker. Put your UI under a folder that is always cooked, or add its folder to Additional Asset Directories to Cook. See Restyle the menus.

More in UI and input troubleshooting.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Add a confirmation popup to ask Yes/No inside your screen.
  • Add an input action with a prompt to show a footer glyph for a screen action.
  • Add a mechanic by subclassing: the C++ screen bases, for a programmer, if your screen needs logic a Blueprint graph struggles with.

docs.title: Add a party member
docs.text:
Designer · 30 min · No code

Result: a new character with their own name, portrait, look, stats, starting gear and Arts joins the roster. You field them from the Party screen, lead with them, and they fight beside the others.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Your first change. It explains the two assets every member is made of: the member definition and the pawn Blueprint.
  • To use a VRoid Studio model instead of the Mannequin body, see Add a VRoid party member instead. The shipped party is the seven VRoid members (Kael, Mira, Nia, Dorran, Isolde, Sabine, Tamsin); the game starts with Kael and Mira and the rest are recruited. The Mannequin colour members in Characters/Party, including the Quinn assets this page copies, are kept on disk as samples and are not in the starting roster.

docs.title: What you will make
docs.text:
Asset How you make it What it decides Member definition Duplicate Characters/Party/PartyMember_Quinn Name, role, portraits, which pawn to spawn, which AI drives it, its EXP curve Pawn Blueprint Child Blueprint of Characters/Party/B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base Body, materials, animation style, stats, starting level, starting gear, Arts Pawn data Characters/Party/PawnData_XenoCore_Party_Quinn Which abilities the body is granted, its input config and tag rules Stats effect Battle/Attributes/GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_Party_Quinn HP, Strength, Ether, Agility and Talent charge at each level Anim profile Duplicate one of Characters/Party/AnimProfiles/DA_XenoCore_AnimProfile_* Victory emote, idle breaks, and any per-character reaction or death clips

The pawn is a child of the party base, not a copy of a sample: a copy brings the sample's gear, learnset and look with it, silently. The other four are duplicated: they hold only numbers and links, which step 2 repoints. Use the _Manny pawn data and stats effect for a masculine body.

Never create a member definition or pawn from scratch

A blank member definition has no Member Class, and a blank pawn has no pawn data. Both fail without an error at runtime: the character never spawns, or spawns with no abilities and cannot die. Duplicating the member definition and setting the pawn's Combatant Pawn Data in step 2 avoids every one of these.

docs.title: 1. Make the five assets
docs.text:
1. Create a folder Content/MyGame/Party.
  2. In Plugins › XenoCore Content › Characters › Party, right-click B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base and choose Create Child Blueprint Class.
  3. In the same folder, right-click and Duplicate PartyMember_Quinn and PawnData_XenoCore_Party_Quinn.
  4. In Battle › Attributes, duplicate GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_Party_Quinn.
  5. In Characters › Party › AnimProfiles, duplicate a profile whose clips suit the body (see step 2).
  6. Rename them B_Party_Rook, PartyMember_Rook, PawnData_Party_Rook, GE_BaseStats_Rook and DA_AnimProfile_Rook, and move all five into MyGame/Party.

docs.title: 2. Point the assets at each other
docs.text:
The duplicates still point at the sample they came from, and the new pawn points at nothing yet. Set every link:

  1. Open PawnData_Party_Rook. Set Pawn Class to B_Party_Rook. Leave Ability Sets, Tag Relationship Mapping and Input Config as they are. Save.

  2. Open B_Party_Rook and click Class Defaults. Under XenoCore › Combatant:

    • Combatant Pawn Data: PawnData_Party_Rook
    • Stats Effect: GE_BaseStats_Rook
    • Combatant Level: the level they start at. The shipped party starts at 1; a member recruited later is raised to the party's level when they join.

    Under XenoCore › Animation:

    • Anim Profile: DA_AnimProfile_Rook. Leave it empty and the character still fights, but never celebrates a win - the victory emote has no default. Pick a profile whose clips suit the body: the shipped feminine members (Maroon, Pink, Yellow, Cyan, Purple) use feminine idle breaks and emotes.
    • Compile and Save.
    • Open PartyMember_Rook. Under XenoCore › Party:
    • Member Class: B_Party_Rook
    • Display Name: Rook
    • Role: Attacker, Defender or Healer. It is shown on the Party screen and stored; no system changes behaviour on it yet.
    • Portrait: any texture from Characters/Party/Portraits for now. Making your own is Bake a portrait.
    • Menu Portrait: the full-body card on the main menu. Leave it empty and the card uses Portrait.
    • Experience Curve (XenoCore › Progression): a row of Game/DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves, the EXP needed for each level. Pick XC1 or one of the shipped characters' rows, or add a row of your own. Empty uses the progression default.
    • Controller Class: leave BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember. Empty also works: the party component's default is used.
    • Save. The Content Browser runs the member check on save: an empty Member Class, or a pawn with no Combatant Pawn Data, is reported as an error.

Pawn Class on the pawn data is never read for a party member: the party spawns the definition's Member Class, and only the experience's own pawn data uses Pawn Class. Setting it keeps the asset honest. Members whose ability sets, input and tag mapping are the same can share one pawn data asset.

docs.title: 3. Give them a look
docs.text:
In B_Party_Rook:

  1. Select the Mesh component. Under Materials, pick new material instances for element 0 and element 1. The coloured samples use pairs from Characters/Party/Materials, such as MI_XenoCore_Quinn_01_Pink and MI_XenoCore_Quinn_02_Pink. Duplicate a pair into MyGame/Party and change their colour parameters.
  2. In Class Defaults, under Default, find Cosmetic Part and set it to Characters/Core/Cosmetics/B_XenoCore_Cosmetic_Feminine or B_XenoCore_Cosmetic_Masculine. This picks both the body mesh and the animation set. See Change a character's animation style.

docs.title: 4. Give them their own stats
docs.text: Open GE_BaseStats_Rook. It has one modifier per stat, each reading a curve table row at the character's level and multiplying it by a value. Change the multipliers to make Rook sturdier or stronger than the sample. The whole model, and how to add rows of your own, is in Author a character's statline.

docs.title: 5. Set their starting gear
docs.text:
1. In B_Party_Rook, select the Equipment Component in the Components panel.
  2. Under XenoCore › Equipment › Starting Equipment, each entry is a Slot (Weapon, Head, Chest, Arms, Legs, Feet) and an Item Definition. The Quinn sample wears Weapons/RedSword/ID_XenoCore_RedSword and five Inventory/Armour/ID_XenoCore_Battle* pieces. Change them as you like, but always keep a Weapon.

  3. Starting Inventory adds items to the party bag without equipping them. Do not list an item there that Starting Equipment already equips, or it is added twice.

  4. On the same component, set Allowed Weapon Types to the kinds of weapon Rook may wield, such as DA_XenoCore_WeaponType_Greatsword. The starting weapon must be one of them: saving the pawn reports an error if it is not. Empty allows any weapon, and saving warns.

The weapon decides more than damage

A weapon's ability set grants the character's Talent Art and the draw and sheathe behaviour. A member with no weapon has no Talent Art and cannot draw.

docs.title: 6. Give them Arts
docs.text: Arts come from the Art Learn Table inherited from B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base: Characters/Party/Learnsets/DT_XenoCore_ArtLearnset_Default, which teaches Back Slash, Light Heal and Air Slash. To give Rook a different set, duplicate that table (or create a Data Table with row structure XenoCoreArtUnlock), edit its rows, and set it as Art Learn Table in Rook's own Class Defaults (XenoCore › Arts). Each row is an Art, the Unlock Level at which it is learned, and a Default Slot (0 to 7 in unlock order, or -1 for learned but not placed). Set palette slots and unlocks covers this in full.

docs.title: 7. Put them in the roster
docs.text:
1. Open Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party and click Class Defaults.
  2. Under XenoCore › Party, add PartyMember_Rook to Starting Roster.
  3. Compile and Save.

Members are fielded in roster order until Max Active Members is reached; the rest wait in reserve (active and reserve members). To recruit Rook later in the story instead, leave the roster alone and see Choose the starting party.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play. Do not use Continue from the title screen: a save remembers the old roster.
  2. Open the menu (pad Y, keyboard I) and go to the Party screen. Rook is in the roster with the portrait and role you set.
  3. Swap Rook into an active slot, close the menu, and walk. Rook follows you with the new materials.
  4. Back on the Party screen, make Rook the leader. You now control Rook, with Rook's Arts on the palette and Rook's weapon drawn in battle.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: Rook is not in the roster

The roster in a save file wins over Starting Roster. Start with Play in the editor or New Game, not Continue.

Fails silently: Rook appears, but with Quinn's name, stats or materials

One of the duplicated assets still points at the Quinn sample. Check the four links in step 2: Member Class, Combatant Pawn Data, Stats Effect, and Pawn Class on the pawn data.

Rook has the Manny body whatever you set

Cosmetic Part points at a class with no animation-style tag, so no body-mesh rule matches and the pawn takes the base's Default Mesh, SKM_Manny. Set it to one of the two B_XenoCore_Cosmetic_* actors, or clear it completely. Saving the pawn shows a warning naming the part.

Rook has default stats and an error names the pawn on every Play

Stats Effect is empty. Set it.

Rook cannot be hurt and cannot die

Combatant Pawn Data is empty or points at pawn data with no ability sets. Death is an ability, so a pawn without its abilities cannot die. The member definition shows this as an error in the Content Browser.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Party and Characters: who owns what, and why a reserve member has no body.
  • Author a character's statline
  • Choose the starting party
  • Bake a portrait

docs.title: Add a skill or a skill tree
docs.text:
Designer · 45 min · No code

Result: your character has their own skill tree. Its first branch, Guardian, raises Physical Defence as its trait and holds five skills: one that raises max HP, one that strengthens their healing, and one that gives a Strength buff when they land a killing blow. In Play, SP from kills (or the XenoGiveSP cheat) fills the branch, "Skill Learnt" floats over the character, and the stats change.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Add a party member: you need your own character Blueprint to point at the tree. The shipped characters already have trees.
  • Read Skills for how branches, SP, traits and the three kinds of skill effect fit together. The glossary defines skill, skill tree, branch, SP and trait.
  • Know which skill fields exist: the tables on the concept page list every field of a branch and of a skill.

New table, not a copy

Build your own tree from a blank table rather than duplicating a shipped one. The shipped trees carry sample names and 63 stand-in skills, and a duplicate inherits all of them.

docs.title: 1. Create the tree
docs.text:
1. In the Content Browser, create the folder Content/MyGame/Skills.
  2. Right-click in it and choose Data › Data Table. For the row structure pick XenoCoreSkillBranchRow. Name it DT_MyGame_SkillTree_Guardian.
  3. Open it and click Add to add a row. Rename the row Guardian.

Choose the row name now and keep it

The row name is what every save stores for this branch. Renaming it after players have saves silently resets their progress on that branch. Change Display Name instead.

docs.title: 2. Fill in the branch
docs.text:
With the Guardian row selected, set:

  1. Display Name to Guardian.
  2. Trait Description to Prioritising this trait will improve physical defence.
  3. Trait Stat to XenoCore.Stat.PhysicalDefence, and Trait Operation to Add.
  4. Trait Ladder: Data Table DT_XenoCore_SkillTraitLadders, Row Name StatMedium (5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 as the branch fills).
  5. Cost Curve: Data Table DT_XenoCore_SkillCostCurves, Row Name Starting (300, 700, 1,000, 2,000, 3,500 SP).
  6. Tick Unlocked At Start. Leave First Skill Prelearned off, so you can watch skill 1 being learnt.

Your own ladder or cost curve

Ladders and cost curves are shared tables, so several branches can point at one row. To make your own, open Battle/Skills/DT_XenoCore_SkillTraitLadders (or DT_XenoCore_SkillCostCurves), click Add, name the row (for example GuardianDefence), and fill its array: - A ladder row's Values needs exactly six numbers: the trait at 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 skills learnt. - A cost row's Costs needs exactly five numbers: the SP for skills 1 to 5.

Then pick that row name in the branch. Validation flags a row with the wrong count. Adding a row edits a shipped table, so note it for template updates; the six shipped ladder rows and two cost rows are XC1's numbers, so add rows rather than changing theirs.

docs.title: 3. Add a stat skill
docs.text:
1. Add five entries to Skills. Every branch must have exactly five; the order is the order they are learnt.
  2. Expand entry 0 and set Display Name Sturdy Frame and Description Max HP +{Value} %. ({Value} is filled in from Value).
  3. Set Shape Circle, Timing Always, Scope Self.
  4. Set Value to 5.
  5. Add one entry to Stats: Stat XenoCore.Stat.MaxHealth, Operation Scale.

Scale adds a percentage of the stat; Add adds points. The stats a skill can raise are the channels of GE_XenoCore_SkillStats: Strength, Ether, Agility, Physical Defence, Ether Defence, Critical Rate, Block Rate, Weight, Weapon Attack Min and Max, Max Health and Move Speed.

docs.title: 4. Add a bonus skill
docs.text:
1. Expand entry 1: Display Name Mender, Description Healing arts restore {Value} more.
  2. Shape Hexagon, Timing In Battle Party, Scope Self.
  3. Value 15.
  4. Bonus XenoCore.SkillBonus.HealingPower. Leave Stats empty.

A bonus skill changes nothing by itself: the healing art asks for the caster's total HealingPower bonus when it heals. The concept page lists every bonus tag and who asks for it.

docs.title: 5. Make the behaviour for a reacting skill
docs.text:
A skill that reacts to something needs a small ability Blueprint. This one gives a Strength buff on a kill.

  1. In Content/MyGame/Skills, right-click and choose Blueprint Class. Under All Classes, pick XenoCoreSkillAbility_TimedBuff. Name it GA_MyGame_Skill_OnKill_StrengthUp.
  2. Open it, click Class Defaults, and under XenoCore › Skills set:
    • Trigger to On Kill.
    • Buff to GE_XenoCore_Status_StrengthUp (in Battle/Status).
  3. Compile and Save. There is no graph to write.

The shipped examples are in Battle/Skills/Abilities; GA_XenoCore_Skill_OnKill_Haste is the same shape with a different buff.

docs.title: 6. Add the reacting skill
docs.text:
1. Back in the tree, expand entry 2: Display Name Rallying Blow, Description Strength Up for {Value} % on a kill.
  2. Shape Square, Timing In Battle Party, Scope Self.
  3. Value 20 (the buff's strength), Duration 20 (seconds), Chance 50 (percent).
  4. Ability to GA_MyGame_Skill_OnKill_StrengthUp.

docs.title: 7. Fill the last two skills
docs.text:
Give entries 3 and 4 a name and an effect of your choice, using the patterns above. Two quick ones:

  • Weight −5: Stats XenoCore.Stat.Weight, Operation Add, Value -5.
  • Last Stand: Stats XenoCore.Stat.Agility, Operation Scale, Value 15, Condition Health At Or Below, Condition Threshold 50. It holds only while HP is at or below half.

Scale needs something to scale

A party member's defences come only from equipment, so a Scale defence skill on a character wearing no armour adds nothing. Scale Strength, Ether, Agility or Max HP, or use Add for defence.

A skill with no effect is still sold to the player

A skill with no Stats, Bonus or Ability can be learnt and does nothing. The table only warns about it in the Data Validation log. Never ship one.

docs.title: 8. Validate and save
docs.text:
1. Save the table.
  2. Right-click it in the Content Browser and choose Asset Actions › Validate Assets. Fix every error; read every warning.

Add more branches the same way. XC1 gives every character five, and five is what the Skills screen is laid out for; nothing stops a sixth, but each extra column makes the card wider. Row order is the order the columns are drawn and the first unlocked row is the branch selected at the start.

docs.title: 9. Give the tree to your character
docs.text:
1. Open your character Blueprint (for example MyGame/Characters/B_MyGame_Party_Guardian) and click Class Defaults.
  2. Under XenoCore › Skills, set Skill Tree to DT_MyGame_SkillTree_Guardian.
  3. Compile and Save.

docs.title: 10. Optional: a branch a quest unlocks
docs.text:
1. Add a second row, untick Unlocked At Start, and set its Cost Curve row to Quest (the cheaper curve).
  2. Open your quest definition. Under Reward, add an entry to Skill Branches: Member is your character's member definition, Branch is the row name, exactly.

When the quest is turned in, the branch opens, a notice floats over the character, and the offer screen and turn-in banner name the branch as a reward.

Branch is typed by hand, so it is checked for you: validating or saving the quest reports an error if the member has no Skill Tree, or if their tree has no row with that exact name. It must be the row name, not the Display Name.

docs.title: 11. Optional: unlock a branch or give SP from a Blueprint
docs.text:
For anything that is not a quest (a cutscene, a landmark, a story beat), use the party's progression component. In any Blueprint graph:

  1. Place Get Party Progression.
  2. From its output, call:
    • Unlock Skill Branch with Member (your member definition) and Branch (the row name). Safe to call twice.
    • Award Skill Points with Member and Amount. The SP goes into that character's selected branch, exactly like kill SP. Tick Apply Reserve Rate if a benched character should get the reserve share.
    • Select Skill Branch to change a character's selected branch from script. It returns false for a locked or unknown branch.

A wrong row name passed to these at runtime is not checked in advance; it is refused with a warning in LogXenoSkills.

docs.title: 12. Optional: a skill with its own logic
docs.text:
XenoCoreSkillAbility_TimedBuff (step 5) covers the triggers it lists. For anything else, make a Blueprint child of XenoCoreGameplayAbility_Skill instead, and point a skill's Ability at it. The ability is granted while the skill reaches the body and removed when it stops. This example grants Strength Up whenever the character is below a third of their HP, checked twice a second.

  1. Right-click in Content/MyGame/Skills, Blueprint Class, All Classes, XenoCoreGameplayAbility_Skill. Name it GA_MyGame_Skill_LowHealthStrength.
  2. Class Defaults › XenoCore › Skills: set Evaluate Interval to 0.5. With 0 the ability never polls; use 0 when your logic waits for events instead.
  3. In the Event Graph, override On Evaluate. Get the avatar (Get Avatar Actor From Actor Info), call Find Health Component on it, then Get Health Normalized; when that is below 0.33, call Apply Buff To Self with GE_XenoCore_Status_StrengthUp. Get Skill Value and Get Skill Duration read the skill entry's Value and Duration, so one ability can serve several skills with different numbers.
  4. For event-driven logic, override Activate Ability (call the parent first) and wait on gameplay events there instead of polling.
  5. Compile and Save, then set it as a skill's Ability.

Keep the ability self-contained: no tags or effects on it that it does not need, and never give the base class anything.

docs.title: Changing a shipped tree instead
docs.text: To replace a stand-in skill with the original effect, or with your own, edit that skill's entry in their Battle/Skills/DT_XenoCore_SkillTree_* table exactly as in steps 3 to 6. This edits a shipped asset: note the change so you can reapply it after a template update. Keep each branch at five skills, and do not rename rows (see the warning above).

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Make your character the leader (Party menu), or add them to the starting party. Start a new game so their record is seeded from the new table.
  2. Open the console (the key left of 1) and run XenoSkills. The Output Log lists Guardian as open, 0/5 learnt, and selected.
  3. Run XenoGiveSP 300. LogXenoSkills reports learnt 'Sturdy Frame', and "Skill Learnt" floats over the character. Their max HP is 5 % higher: the second HP figure on their Party screen row.
  4. Run XenoGiveSP 1700. Skills 2 and 3 are learnt (700 + 1,000 SP).
  5. Open the main menu and choose Skills. The Guardian column shows three lit icons and the fourth dark. Focus the header: the trait reads Physical Defence Up 30 (the StatMedium ladder at three skills), Selected, and SP 0 / 2,000.
  6. Fight an enemy in L_XenoCore_Gym and land the killing blow with your character. About half the time a Strength Up status appears over them, and LogXenoSkillAbility logs a line naming the OnKill trigger and GE_XenoCore_Status_StrengthUp.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently

The Skills screen says "No skill tree". Skill Tree is empty on the Blueprint the character actually spawns as. Check the member definition's Member Class, and set the tree on that class. If the table has the wrong row structure, LogXenoSkills logs an error naming it.

Fails silently

A skill is learnt but nothing changes. Check, in order: it has an effect at all (a skill with no Stats, Bonus or Ability does nothing); its Timing is In Battle Party and the character is benched; its Condition is not met; its Scope is Self and you are looking at another character. A stat the skill effect has no channel for is logged, as a warning naming the skill. See Troubleshooting.

Fails silently

XenoGiveSP or kills stop filling anything. The selected branch is complete, and SP beyond that is thrown away. Select another branch on the Skills screen. XenoGiveSP always pays the leader, into the leader's selected branch.

Fails silently

You changed Unlocked At Start or First Skill Prelearned and nothing moved. A character's record is seeded once. Branches already in a save keep their saved state; only branches new to the table are seeded. Start a new game to see the change.

Fails silently

The on-kill buff never appears. The trigger fires on the body that dealt the last damage; if another party member finished the enemy, it is theirs. With Chance below 100 it is also a roll; set it to 100 while testing. On-miss and on-critical triggers only fire for attacks that go through XenoCore's damage formula.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Skills: reach rules, bonuses, the stat carrier, saves.
  • Create a collection quest: the quest that unlocks a branch.
  • Add a status effect: a new buff for a reacting skill to apply.
  • Tune progression: experience and Art Points beside SP.

docs.title: Add a VRoid party member
docs.text:
Designer · 2 h · No code

Result: a character made in VRoid Studio is a playable party member. It runs, fights, blinks and changes expression in battle, using the same animations, abilities and weapon sockets as every other member.

Read this first: this route depends on the VRM4U plugin

Importing a .vrm file, and the sample VRoid members' spring bones and facial expressions, use the third-party VRM4U plugin. It ships with the project (Plugins/VRM4U) and builds with it, and XenoCore.uplugin depends on it. The scripted pipeline used to build the samples is not part of the product, so this page describes the editor-only route: every step can be done by hand in the editor. If you have removed VRM4U from your copy, you cannot import .vrm files; use a mesh on the Mannequin skeleton instead (Add a party member).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Add a party member. A VRoid member is the same assets plus a cosmetic part that carries the VRoid body.
  • VRoid Studio (Stable), and the VRM4U plugin enabled in Edit › Plugins.

Licence: never ship an unedited VRoid sample model

VRoid Studio output may be used in paid games. pixiv's sample models may be used commercially but may not be redistributed for a fee unedited. Edit a sample's textures and parameters in VRoid Studio into an original, or build your own, before you sell anything. Do not build a character creator from VRoid data.

The seven sample characters ship edited: each has its own tint on hair and clothing (Base Color Tint on its MI_Lit_* hair and cloth instances) and the XenoCore emblem painted into its outfit texture at the left chest. Give your own sample-based character an edit of its own: change Base Color Tint on its hair and cloth material instances, and paint your own mark into its outfit texture in an image editor, then re-import the texture (or make the edit in VRoid Studio before export). The samples' VL_/VM_ objects in each VRM/ folder carry no licence terms (the licence fields are empty; the meta holds bone mapping only). Your own import's VL_ object carries whatever the VRoid export dialog was set to.

docs.title: How a VRoid member works
docs.text:
The pawn still uses an invisible Mannequin body (SKM_Manny_Invis or SKM_Quinn_Invis, Lyra's own, under Content › Characters › Heroes › Mannequin › Meshes). That body runs XenoCore's animation, plays every montage and ragdolls on death. The VRoid mesh is a cosmetic part attached to it that copies its pose through an IK retargeter. Nothing in the abilities, AI or party code knows the difference.

The retargeter copies joint rotations, not hand positions, so a VRoid hand is never exactly where the Mannequin's is. The weapon is therefore held by the VRoid body: its skeleton carries the two weapon sockets, XC_WeaponGrip_R and XC_WeaponStow_Back, and a weapon attaches to whichever body has them. You place them per character in step 7.

Each character has one folder, named for them, laid out the same way. Dorran, the sample used below, is Characters/VRoid/Dorran:

Folder Holds Dorran/ What you edit: pawn, cosmetic part, member definition, anim profile, portrait Dorran/Mesh/ The meshes (SK_ and its _Lit copy), the skeleton with the weapon sockets, physics, pose assets Dorran/Materials/Lit/ The lit material instances the game draws Dorran/Materials/Toon/ VRM4U's own toon materials, kept as a fallback Dorran/Textures/ Every texture Dorran/Animation/ The post-process and retarget anim Blueprints, face animation, IK rig, retargeter Dorran/VRM/ The importer's licence and metadata objects

The two bases, the face-expression table and the lit master material sit directly in Characters/VRoid/. Asset names keep the AvatarSample_C suffix the importer gave them.

SK_ is the mesh here, and SKEL_ is the skeleton

The importer's prefixes are the reverse of Lyra's (where SK_ is a skeleton and SKM_ a skeletal mesh). In a VRoid Mesh/ folder, SK_AvatarSample_C is the mesh and SKEL_AvatarSample_C is the skeleton that carries the weapon sockets. See Asset naming.

Piece Sample (Dorran) Role VRoid mesh Mesh/SK_AvatarSample_C_Lit What you see Retarget anim Blueprint Animation/ABP_XenoCore_VRoidRetarget_C Copies the invisible body's pose, and drives the face Cosmetic part B_XenoCore_Cosmetic_VRoid_C Actor carrying the mesh and its animation-style tag Pawn Blueprint B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_C Invisible body, cosmetic part, stats, gear Member definition PartyMember_VRoid_C Name, portrait, pawn class IK rig and retargeter Animation/IK_AvatarSample_C, Animation/RTG_Manny_To_AvatarSample_C Map the Mannequin skeleton onto the VRoid one Weapon sockets Mesh/SKEL_AvatarSample_C: XC_WeaponGrip_R on J_Bip_R_Hand, XC_WeaponStow_Back on J_Bip_C_Chest Where this character holds the drawn weapon and carries the sheathed one Post-process anim Blueprint Animation/ABP_Post_AvatarSample_C (made by VRM4U on import) Spring bones for hair and cloth, and turns face curves into the model's own morph targets

The last row is why the face needs VRM4U at runtime as well as at import: the mesh's Post Process Anim Blueprint uses VRM4U nodes.

docs.title: 1. Export from VRoid Studio
docs.text:
1. Open your character. Do not change the Expression Editor: its expressions are the facial rig.
  2. Export VRM with every reduction option off. Bone reduction removes hair and skirt bones.
  3. VRM 1.0 or 0.0 both import.

docs.title: 2. Import
docs.text:
1. Create Content/MyGame/VRoid/Rook.
  2. Drag the .vrm file into it. In the VRM4U import dialog keep the defaults; in its advanced options, No MorphTarget and No physics asset must stay off.
  3. Check the import: open the skeletal mesh and look at Morph Targets. A VRoid Studio export has about 56. Zero means the face will never move: delete the import and try again.
  4. Open the imported skeletal mesh and set its Physics Asset to the imported PHYS_ asset. The importer creates it but does not assign it, and ragdoll death needs it.

Toon or lit materials

The import brings VRM4U's toon materials. The samples instead draw a _Lit copy of each mesh whose materials are instances of Characters/VRoid/M_XenoCore_VRoidLit, which lights like the rest of the world and does not depend on VRM4U. To match them, duplicate your mesh and swap its materials for instances of that material.

docs.title: 3. Build the IK rig and retargeter
docs.text:
1. Duplicate Characters/VRoid/Dorran/Animation/IK_AvatarSample_C into your character's Animation/ folder and set its Preview Mesh to your VRoid mesh. VRoid Studio exports all use the same J_Bip_* bone names, so the chains carry over. If a chain shows red, reassign its bones by hand. Automatic characterisation does not recognise VRoid rigs, so do not rely on it.
  2. Duplicate RTG_Manny_To_AvatarSample_C (masculine) or RTG_Quinn_To_AvatarSample_K (feminine) and set its target IK rig to your new rig.
  3. In the retargeter, keep Run IK Rig off. With IK on, the ankles are pulled to the Mannequin's ankle height and the whole body sinks into the floor.

docs.title: 4. Make the retarget anim Blueprint
docs.text:
1. Create an Animation Blueprint for your VRoid skeleton. Parent class: XenoCoreFaceAnimInstance.
  2. In its AnimGraph, add Retarget Pose From Mesh. Set Retarget From to the parent skeletal mesh component, and IK Retargeter Asset to your retargeter.
  3. Add Modify Curve after it, expose its Curve Map pin, and connect the Face Curves variable to it. That one wire drives blinking and expressions.
  4. Connect to Output Pose, compile and save. Compare against ABP_XenoCore_VRoidRetarget_C.

docs.title: 5. Make the member
docs.text:
The pawn uses a member definition and pawn data like any other member.

  1. Right-click Characters/VRoid/B_XenoCore_Cosmetic_VRoid_Base and choose Create Child Blueprint Class. On its inherited MeshComponent, set the mesh to yours and Anim Class to your new anim Blueprint. In Class Defaults, set Static Gameplay Tags to one tag, Cosmetic.AnimationStyle.Masculine or .Feminine, to match the body. The base has no tag, so skipping it leaves the body on the base's default mesh and the unarmed masculine clips.
  2. Right-click Characters/VRoid/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_Base and choose Create Child Blueprint Class. Do not duplicate a sample member: a copy brings that character's gear, learnset, skill tree and anim profile with it, silently. The base holds only the invisible Mannequin body and the body-mesh rules that pick it, so leave those alone. In the child's Class Defaults set:
    • Cosmetic Part: your cosmetic part.
    • Combatant Pawn Data: Characters/VRoid/PawnData_XenoCore_Party_VRoid, for any body. Its Pawn Class is the VRoid base, so a member does not also load the Mannequin colour samples (B_XenoCore_Party_Manny / _Quinn) and their materials, as the Characters/Party/PawnData_XenoCore_Party_* assets would. Empty means the character cannot be hurt or die.
    • Stats Effect and Combatant Level, exactly as in Add a party member.
    • On the Mesh component, Skeletal Mesh Asset: SKM_Quinn_Invis for a feminine body. The base uses SKM_Manny_Invis, and the body-mesh rules switch it by tag either way.
  3. Duplicate PartyMember_VRoid_C, set Member Class to your pawn, Display Name, Portrait, Menu Portrait (the full-body main-menu card) and Experience Curve (a row of Game/DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves; each sample has its own). Then either add it to Starting Roster on BP_XenoCore_Party, which starts with Kael and Mira, or have an NPC recruit it as the other five samples are (Recruit a party member from an NPC).
  4. Duplicate DA_XenoCore_AnimProfile_VRoid_C (a data asset; data assets cannot have a base) beside your pawn and set the pawn's XenoCore › Animation › Anim Profile to the copy. It is empty, so nothing changes until you give the character its own clips; see Give a character its own combat animations.

Fails silently: two members share one anim profile

Point every member at its own profile. Two pawns on one profile share it: giving either its own Topple changes both.

docs.title: 6. Give them their own kit
docs.text:
A child of the base starts with the party base's defaults: the default learnset, no skill tree, the Junk Sword and its Talent Art (Turn Strike), and no victory emote. The duplicated member definition still carries the sample's role and AI profile. Set each one:

Piece Where How Arts Pawn Class Defaults › XenoCore › Arts › Art Learn Table Duplicate a learnset into your folder and edit its rows. Three palette slots are open at level 1. See Set palette slots and unlocks. Talent Art The weapon's ability set A Talent Art belongs to the sword, not the character. For a character-specific Talent Art, give them their own sword: a child of B_XenoCore_Sword_Base and of ED_XenoCore_Sword_Base, whose ED grants AbilitySet_XenoCore_SwordCommon plus a set holding only the Talent (a child of GA_XenoCore_TalentArt_Base). See Make a Talent Art and Add a weapon. The samples are Isolde, Sabine and Tamsin's Violet, Amber and Ivory Swords. Skills Pawn Class Defaults › XenoCore › Skills › Skill Tree Point it at a tree, or make one. See Add a skill or a skill tree. Starting gear Pawn's equipment component, Starting Equipment The sword above in Weapon, plus armour. Weapon type Pawn's equipment component, Allowed Weapon Types The kinds of weapon the character may wield. Every sample is DA_XenoCore_WeaponType_Greatsword. Saving the pawn reports an error if the starting weapon is not allowed. Role and AI Member definition: Role, and XenoCore › AI › AI Profile A healer wants a higher Heal Threshold. See Tune companion AI. Victory emote Your anim profile's Victory Montages Empty means the character does not celebrate. See Give a character its own combat animations. Portraits Member definition Portrait and Menu Portrait Bake a portrait

Fails silently: the new character has Turn Strike

The base's Junk Sword grants Turn Strike. Until your character's Starting Equipment names a sword of their own, their centre palette slot is Turn Strike, and equipping any other character's sword gives them that character's Talent Art instead.

Fails silently: a blue Mannequin draws inside the VRoid body

The pawn's body mesh rules still select the visible SKM_Manny or SKM_Quinn. In the pawn's character parts component, every Body Meshes rule, and Default Mesh, must point at an _Invis mesh.

docs.title: 7. Place the weapon sockets
docs.text:
Without these the weapon falls back to the invisible Mannequin's hand and floats beside the hand you can see.

  1. Open your VRoid skeleton (SKEL_...). In the skeleton tree, right-click J_Bip_R_Hand and choose Add Socket. Name it exactly XC_WeaponGrip_R.
  2. Right-click J_Bip_C_Chest, add a socket, and name it exactly XC_WeaponStow_Back.
  3. Right-click each socket › Add Preview Asset and pick a sword mesh, for example Weapons/GreatSword/SM_GreatSword.
  4. To see them in a pose: right-click a clip such as Characters/Player/Animations/Kwang/AS_Kwang_Idle › Retarget Animations, pick your retargeter, and save the copy in a folder of your own that you will delete before shipping (for example Content/MyGame/Scratch). In the skeleton editor's Preview Scene Settings › Animation, pick that copy. An idle, a swing, and the draw and sheathe clips cover every pose worth checking.
  5. Move and rotate each socket until the grip sits in the palm and the sheathed sword lies flat on the back. Leave each socket's Scale at 1.0: a socket's scale multiplies every weapon the character holds. To change how big weapons are, see Size in Add a weapon. A good start is to copy the values from a sample of the same body style (SKEL_AvatarSample_L for masculine, SKEL_AvatarSample_K for feminine).
  6. Save the skeleton.

Fails silently: one character's weapons are smaller or larger than everyone else's

A weapon socket has a Scale other than 1.0. It is easy to change by accident while dragging the gizmo in scale mode. Set both sockets' Scale back to 1.0.

Fails silently: a misspelled socket name

The names are the contract and must match exactly. A socket named anything else is ignored, and the weapon goes back to floating, with nothing logged.

Every weapon follows the same two sockets

Tune them once per character, not per weapon. If one weapon sits differently from the others, fix that weapon's mesh or its actor instead (see Add a weapon).

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym, press Play (not Continue), and field your member from the Party screen (menu: pad Y, keyboard I).
  2. It follows you and runs with the same animation as the Mannequin members.
  3. Watch its face for ten seconds: it blinks at random intervals.
  4. Engage an enemy. The expression hardens when the battle starts and changes again when the character is Toppled or Dazed.
  5. The sword sits on its back while exploring (sheathed), and in its hand once drawn.
  6. Open the console (the key left of 1) and run XenoCore.Weapon.Describe <name> to see what it may wield and is holding.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: the face never moves

The import has no morph targets (re-import with Optimize Vertex off), the Curve Map pin is not wired to Face Curves, or the mesh lost its Post Process Anim Blueprint (the ABP_Post_ asset from the import). If you duplicated the mesh for lit materials, check the duplicate still has it.

The character floats or sinks, or its arms stay out in a T-pose

The retargeter has Run IK Rig on, or a chain in your IK rig has no bones. Open the retargeter and check its preview against the Mannequin.

Fails silently: the character stands in place when it dies

The mesh has no Physics Asset. Assign the imported PHYS_ asset.

The sword floats off the hand, or sits inside the body

The skeleton has no XC_WeaponGrip_R / XC_WeaponStow_Back, or they are misspelled, so the weapon is on the invisible Mannequin. Check step 7.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Change a character's animation style
  • Bake a portrait
  • Animation

docs.title: Add a weapon
docs.text:
Designer · 45 min · No code

Result: a new sword, Stone Blade, with its own look and stats. It sits in the party's bag, you equip it from the Equipment screen, the character draws it in battle, and its numbers show on the stat block.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Your first change. You should know class defaults and the party pawns.
  • Equipment: slots, and why a weapon is four assets.

docs.title: How a weapon is put together
docs.text:
A weapon is a chain of assets. Each points at the next:

Piece Sample (Blue Sword) What it decides Item definition Weapons/BlueSword/ID_XenoCore_BlueSword Name, description, icon, slot, stats, sell value. This is what sits in the bag. Equipment definition Weapons/ED_XenoCore_Sword_Base › Weapons/BlueSword/ED_XenoCore_BlueSword What equipping it spawns, where it attaches, and which abilities it grants Weapon actor Weapons/B_XenoCore_Sword_Base › Weapons/BlueSword/B_BlueSword The mesh you see Weapon instance Weapons/GreatSword/B_WeaponInstance_GreatSword Which animation layer the character uses with it drawn and sheathed Ability set Weapons/GreatSword/AbilitySet_XenoCore_JunkSword Abilities the weapon grants while worn

Every shipped sword's actor is a child of B_XenoCore_Sword_Base (the greatsword mesh) and its equipment definition a child of ED_XenoCore_Sword_Base (the instance type, the back socket, and AbilitySet_XenoCore_SwordCommon, which draws and sheathes the sword and applies its stats). A sword differs only in its item, its material, and the Talent Art its ability set (a list of abilities granted while the weapon is worn) grants. Junk, Blue, Green and Red share AbilitySet_XenoCore_JunkSword (Turn Strike); the Violet, Amber and Ivory Swords each grant their own Talent Art. Weapons/IronBlade holds only a mesh and material.

A sword whose Talent Art you want to change is covered in step 3. A new sword is the short route below. A new kind of weapon that animates differently needs the extra section at the end.

docs.title: 1. Make the chain
docs.text:
1. Create MyGame/Weapons/StoneBlade under Content.
  2. In Plugins › XenoCore Content › Weapons, right-click each base, choose Create Child Blueprint Class, and save the child in your folder:
    • B_XenoCore_Sword_Base → B_MyGame_StoneBlade
    • ED_XenoCore_Sword_Base → ED_MyGame_StoneBlade
  3. From Weapons › BlueSword, duplicate these two:
    • ID_XenoCore_BlueSword → ID_MyGame_StoneBlade
    • MI_XenoCore_BlueSword → MI_MyGame_StoneBlade

Why the item definition is copied, not inherited

An item definition's fragments are instanced objects, and a Blueprint child of an item definition cannot be saved once it overrides them ("Illegal reference to private object"). Lyra's own items are all copies for the same reason. Treat an item definition as data.

Fails silently: never create an item definition from blank

Always duplicate an existing weapon. A new, empty item definition has no Equipment Definition, so the item shows in the list, you select it, and nothing happens. Nothing is logged.

docs.title: 2. Give it its own look
docs.text:
1. Open MI_MyGame_StoneBlade and change BaseColor. Save.
  2. Open B_MyGame_StoneBlade. Select the inherited SwordMesh component and set every material slot to MI_MyGame_StoneBlade (the greatsword mesh has three). To use a different mesh, set it here too. Compile and Save.

Fails silently: part of the sword keeps the default material

A slot left empty draws the mesh's own material. Set all of them.

docs.title: 3. Point the chain at itself
docs.text:
Duplicates still point at the originals. Repoint them:

  1. Open ED_MyGame_StoneBlade (Class Defaults). Under Actors To Spawn, set Actor To Spawn to B_MyGame_StoneBlade. Leave Attach Socket as it is: the weapon spawns on the back and moves to the hand when drawn.
  2. Leave Instance Type as the base set it. Ability Sets To Grant inherits AbilitySet_XenoCore_SwordCommon, which gives no Talent Art. To give the sword one, set the list to AbilitySet_XenoCore_SwordCommon plus a set granting only the Talent Art (see Make a Talent Art), or replace it with Weapons/GreatSword/AbilitySet_XenoCore_JunkSword alone for Turn Strike. Never list SwordCommon and JunkSword together: both grant the draw and stats abilities, so the weapon would get them twice.
  3. Compile and Save.
  4. Open ID_MyGame_StoneBlade (Class Defaults). Set Display Name to Stone Blade.
  5. In Fragments, expand each fragment and set:
    • Inventory Fragment Equippable Item › Equipment Definition: ED_MyGame_StoneBlade
    • Xeno Core Fragment Item Display › XenoCore › Display › Description and Icon
    • Xeno Core Fragment Item Category › XenoCore › Item › Sell Value and Sort Order (and Rarity, see Item rarity)
    • Xeno Core Fragment Equip Slots › XenoCore › Equipment › Allowed Slots: keep Weapon
  6. Compile and Save.

docs.title: 4. Set its stats
docs.text:
1. In ID_MyGame_StoneBlade, open the Inventory Fragment Set Stats fragment.
  2. Edit Initial Item Stats. Each entry is a XenoCore.Stat.* tag and a whole number:
Tag Stone Blade Note XenoCore.Stat.WeaponAttackMin 55 Low end of the damage roll XenoCore.Stat.WeaponAttackMax 80 High end. The game caps the spread at Min + 99 XenoCore.Stat.CriticalRate 10 Whole percent: 10 means 10% XenoCore.Stat.PhysicalDefence 0 Remove the row rather than leaving 0
  1. Compile and Save.

Add a stat to equipment lists every tag and what it does.

docs.title: 4b. Set its weapon type
docs.text:
Every character may only wield certain kinds of weapon (its weapon type), as in Xenoblade Chronicles: the swap list for a character never shows a weapon they cannot use.

  1. In ID_MyGame_StoneBlade, open the Xeno Core Fragment Equip Slots fragment.
  2. Under XenoCore › Equipment, set Weapon Type to Weapons/Types/DA_XenoCore_WeaponType_Greatsword.
  3. Compile and Save.

Leaving Weapon Type empty lets anyone wield it. The pawn's save-time check warns when a typed character starts with an untyped weapon.

The type also gives the weapon its gem sockets: the Greatsword's Default Gem Slots is 2. For one weapon with a different count, tick Override Gem Slots on the same fragment and set Gem Slots. See Add a gem.

docs.title: 5. Put it in the bag
docs.text:
For testing, give the party one at the start:

  1. Open the leader's pawn Blueprint, for example Kael's, Characters/VRoid/Kael/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_L.
  2. In the Components panel, select its equipment component (the XenoCoreEquipmentComponent) and find XenoCore › Equipment › Starting Inventory.
  3. Add an entry: Item Definition ID_MyGame_StoneBlade, Count 1.
  4. Compile and Save.

Use Starting Equipment instead to have a character wear it from the start. Never list the same weapon in both, or the party gets two.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play.
  2. Open the menu and go to Equipment. Choose the character and the Weapon slot.
  3. Stone Blade is in the list. Its comparison block shows your numbers against the current weapon.
  4. Equip it. Close the menu and walk into a minion's range: the character draws Stone Blade from the back, in your material.
  5. Fight. Damage rises and falls with the attack range you set.

If the weapon is missing from the list, open the console (`) and run XenoCore.Weapon.Describe: it prints each character's allowed weapon types, held weapon and how many bag weapons their swap list shows.

docs.title: A new kind of weapon
docs.text:
Make the type first. Right-click in the Content Browser › Data › Data Asset › XenoCoreWeaponTypeDefinition, name it DA_MyGame_WeaponType_Spear, and set its Display Name. Point your weapon's Weapon Type at it (step 4b), then give every character who may use spears the type: open their pawn Blueprint, select the equipment component, and add it to XenoCore › Equipment › Allowed Weapon Types.

Fails at save: a starting weapon the character cannot wield

If a pawn's Starting Equipment weapon is a type missing from its Allowed Weapon Types, saving the pawn reports an error naming both. It would never equip.

Run XenoCore.Weapon.Describe in the console during Play to see each character's allowed types, held weapon and how many bag weapons their swap list shows.

Then give the type its own look and swings. Everything below is on the type asset, and every field is optional: left empty, a weapon of this type uses the Greatsword's stance, draw, sheathe and swings, exactly like the shipped swords.

All of these are on the type asset's Details panel, under Animation, Attack and Gems.

Field (on the type) What it changes Empty means Armed Layers The stance while drawn: a linked anim layer, chosen by the character's cosmetic tags (one rule for Masculine, one for Feminine, or just a Default Layer) The weapon instance's Equipped Anim Set (the greatsword stance) Sheathed Layers The stance while sheathed The weapon instance's Unequipped Anim Set (unarmed) Draw Montage, Sheathe Montage The draw and sheathe animations The greatsword draw and sheathe Attack Montages The auto-attack combo, in order The greatsword swings Attack Montages Stationary Full-body versions for standing still; only read when Attack Montages is set Use Attack Montages Attack Range How far the auto-attack reaches, cm 420

The type also carries Default Gem Slots (2), the gem sockets every weapon of the type gets.

  1. The stance: duplicate Characters/Player/AnimLayers/ABP_XenoCore_GreatSwordAnimLayers into your folder. It is an override-only child of ABP_XenoCore_ItemLayersBase: open it and replace its asset overrides (idle, combat locomotion blend space) with your weapon's clips, and set Idle Break Anim in its class defaults, or leave it empty for no fidget. Put it in the type's Armed Layers › Default Layer.
  2. The swings: duplicate the greatsword attack montages (Characters/Player/Animations/Kwang/AM_XenoCore_Attack_A and friends) and swap in your clips, then list them in Attack Montages.
  3. Draw and sheathe: duplicate AM_GreatSword_Unsheathe / AM_GreatSword_Sheathe the same way.

No weapon instance, equipment definition or ability needs to change.

Fails silently: a swing montage with no hit notify

Every attack montage needs the XenoCore Gameplay Event notify with XenoCore.Event.MeleeHit at the moment the blow lands, copied from the greatsword montage you duplicated. Without it the swing plays and never deals damage, and nothing is logged.

Fails silently: an art using an attack montage

Never point an art at one of these montages: the auto-attack stops its own montages by asset, and would cut the art off on its first frame. Give the art its own copy.

If the new kind of weapon needs its own ability set, duplicate AbilitySet_XenoCore_JunkSword and keep all three of its entries:

  • GA_XenoCore_WeaponDrawSync moves the weapon between back and hand.
  • GA_XenoCore_EquipmentStats applies the weapon's stats.
  • GA_XenoCore_TurnStrike is the character's Talent Art.

Fails silently: an ability set missing an entry

Without GA_XenoCore_EquipmentStats the weapon equips, draws and shows its name, and adds no stats. Without GA_XenoCore_WeaponDrawSync it never leaves the back. Without GA_XenoCore_TurnStrike the character has no Talent Art while wearing it. None of these log anything.

docs.title: Size, position and materials
docs.text:
• Size has two knobs, both on the weapon:

    • A whole family of weapons: the Attach Transform › Scale on the family's base equipment definition. Every sword inherits 0.75 from Weapons/ED_XenoCore_Sword_Base, so all swords are drawn at 75% of their mesh. Change it there to resize every sword at once.
    • One weapon: its actor Blueprint's StaticMesh component Scale (1.0 on every shipped sword). Scale the component, never the actor: drawing and sheathing rewrite the actor's transform every time.

    The two multiply. Never size a weapon with a character's socket: see below. - Pivot: export the mesh with its pivot at the grip, where the palm closes, and the blade along +X. Then it sits in every character's hand without an offset, and scaling shrinks it toward the hand. - Where it sits on a character is that character's two weapon sockets, not the weapon. See step 7 of Add a VRoid party member. A socket places a weapon, and its Scale must stay 1.0: socket scale multiplies every weapon that character ever holds, so one character's swords quietly come out a different size from everyone else's. - Materials from a pack (Paragon, Megascans) must be moved into XenoCore with the weapon. The packs are not part of the project, so on any other machine the material slot is empty and the weapon renders grey. Use the editor's Move on the material, its textures and functions, never Copy, so the mesh is repointed; then cap the textures at 1K (right-click › Texture Source Actions › Reduce Size). The Gold Sword's Materials/ folder is the worked example.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text: Symptom Fix The weapon is in the bag but not in a character's swap list Its Weapon Type is not in that character's Allowed Weapon Types. This is the weapon lock working. XenoCore.Weapon.Describe shows both. The item is in the list but will not equip Equipment Definition is empty on the item, or Allowed Slots does not include Weapon. The Output Log names the reason (NotEquippable or WrongSlot). The weapon renders as a grey checker on someone else's machine Its material still lives in a pack folder that is not part of the project. Move it in, as described under Size, position and materials. The stat block shows the name but zeros Initial Item Stats is empty or on the wrong fragment. See Troubleshooting: items and equipment. The sword stays on the back when drawn The equipment definition's ability set has no GA_XenoCore_WeaponDrawSync. Keep AbilitySet_XenoCore_SwordCommon in Ability Sets To Grant.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Equipment and Animation.
  • Add armour, Add a stat to equipment.
  • Build a drop table to make it drop from enemies.

docs.title: Change a character's animation style
docs.text:
Designer · 1 h · No code

Result: a character switches between the masculine and feminine body and movement set, or uses a third animation style you create, with its own idle, locomotion and idle break.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • Add a party member

docs.title: How the style is chosen
docs.text:
One gameplay tag decides both the body and the movement clips:

  1. The pawn Blueprint's Cosmetic Part names a small actor, Characters/Core/Cosmetics/B_XenoCore_Cosmetic_Masculine or B_XenoCore_Cosmetic_Feminine. It has no mesh; it only carries a tag, Cosmetic.AnimationStyle.Masculine or .Feminine.
  2. On Begin Play the pawn adds that part. The pawn's Body Meshes rules read the tag and pick the body: Masculine gives SKM_Manny, Feminine gives SKM_Quinn.
  3. When the weapon is drawn or sheathed, the weapon instance reads the same tag and picks an animation layer: a small anim Blueprint holding the idle and locomotion clips.
Weapon state Layer rules on Weapons/GreatSword/B_WeaponInstance_GreatSword Sheathed (Uneuipped Anim Set, Lyra's spelling) Feminine → ABP_XenoCore_UnarmedAnimLayers_Feminine; otherwise ABP_XenoCore_UnarmedAnimLayers Drawn (Equipped Anim Set) ABP_XenoCore_GreatSwordAnimLayers for everyone

The layers live in Characters/Player/AnimLayers. The feminine layer is a child of the masculine one that swaps two assets: the idle and the locomotion blend space. Nothing else differs.

docs.title: Switch a character's style
docs.text:
1. Open the character's pawn Blueprint, for example the Mannequin sample Characters/Party/B_XenoCore_Party_Quinn, and click Class Defaults.
  2. Under Default, set Cosmetic Part to B_XenoCore_Cosmetic_Masculine or B_XenoCore_Cosmetic_Feminine. A VRoid member's Cosmetic Part is its own VRoid part (for Mira, Characters/VRoid/Mira/B_XenoCore_Cosmetic_VRoid_K): change the tag in that part's Static Gameplay Tags instead, and its pawn's Body Meshes pick the matching invisible body.
  3. The body swaps with it. If you want a feminine movement set on the Manny body, you cannot do it with this field alone: see Make a new style below.
  4. Compile and Save.

The character takes the wrong body

Cosmetic Part points at an actor with no Cosmetic.AnimationStyle tag, so the body-mesh rules match nothing and the pawn takes Body Meshes › Default Mesh (SKM_Manny on the shipped party pawns) with the default layers. Use one of the two shipped parts, or clear the field entirely (the pawn then keeps its own mesh). Saving the pawn Blueprint shows a warning naming the part and its tags.

docs.title: Change a style's idle break
docs.text:
A character standing still plays an occasional fidget. Its default is set on each layer.

Fails silently: the character's anim profile wins

If the character's anim profile lists Idle Breaks (sheathed) or Armed Idle Breaks (drawn), those clips play instead of the layer's Idle Break Anim, and editing the layer changes nothing. Every VRoid party member's profile ships with its own idle breaks. To change a VRoid member's fidgets, edit its profile: see Give a character its own combat animations. The layer's Idle Break Delay and Idle Break Jitter still set the timing.

  1. Open ABP_XenoCore_UnarmedAnimLayers (or the feminine or greatsword layer) and click Class Defaults.
  2. Under XenoCore › Idle Break:
    • Idle Break Anim: the fidget clip. Empty means this style never fidgets.
    • Idle Break Delay: seconds of standing still before a fidget, 8 by default.
    • Idle Break Jitter: random extra seconds on top, 6 by default, so party members do not fidget in unison.
  3. Compile and Save.

docs.title: Make a new style
docs.text: This example adds a Heavy style with its own idle and walk.

docs.title: 1. The tag
docs.text:
1. Open Project Settings › Project › Gameplay Tags.
  2. Click Add New Gameplay Tag, enter Cosmetic.AnimationStyle.Heavy, and pick a tag source (ini file) of your own, not one of XenoCore's.

docs.title: 2. The cosmetic part
docs.text:
1. In Characters/Core/Cosmetics, duplicate B_XenoCore_Cosmetic_Masculine into MyGame/Characters as B_Cosmetic_Heavy.
  2. Open it, click Class Defaults, and in Static Gameplay Tags replace Cosmetic.AnimationStyle.Masculine with Cosmetic.AnimationStyle.Heavy. It must carry only that one tag (it is under Actor). Compile and Save.

docs.title: 3. The layer
docs.text:
1. In Characters/Player/AnimLayers, find ABP_XenoCore_UnarmedAnimLayers_Feminine. Duplicate it into MyGame/Characters as ABP_HeavyAnimLayers. It is already a child of ABP_XenoCore_UnarmedAnimLayers, holding only asset overrides.
  2. Open it. In the Asset Override Editor (it opens by itself for a child anim Blueprint; else Window › Asset Override Editor), replace the idle sequence and the locomotion blend space with your own. To make a blend space, duplicate Characters/Player/BlendSpaces/BS_XenoCore_Unarmed_Locomotion_Feminine and swap its samples.
  3. Set its Idle Break Anim as above. Compile and Save.

Duplicate the feminine layer, never re-create the masculine one

ABP_XenoCore_UnarmedAnimLayers is the fallback the character's main anim Blueprint links when nothing else is linked. Replacing or renaming it breaks every character silently.

Set each override once

An asset override added twice on the same node keeps both entries, and which one wins cannot be seen in the asset. If you make a mistake, delete the layer and duplicate it again.

docs.title: 4. Teach the weapons and the body
docs.text:
1. Open Weapons/GreatSword/B_WeaponInstance_GreatSword (and any other weapon instance you use).
  2. In Uneuipped Anim Set › Layer Rules, add an entry: Required Tags Cosmetic.AnimationStyle.Heavy, Layer ABP_HeavyAnimLayers.
  3. In Equipped Anim Set, add a Heavy rule only if you made a drawn-weapon layer too. Otherwise the default greatsword layer is used.
  4. Open the pawn Blueprint you want to use the style. In the Components panel select its character parts component, and under Body Meshes › Mesh Rules add an entry: Required Tags Cosmetic.AnimationStyle.Heavy, Mesh the body you want. Compile.

  5. In the same Blueprint's Class Defaults, set Cosmetic Part to B_Cosmetic_Heavy. Compile and Save.

  6. If a weapon's type (Weapons/Types/DA_XenoCore_WeaponType_*) sets Armed Layers or Sheathed Layers, those win over the weapon instance's anim sets: add the Heavy rule there too. The shipped Greatsword type leaves both empty.

Fails silently: the style never appears

A weapon instance with no rule for your tag falls back to its default layer, with no warning. Every weapon instance the character can hold needs the rule.

The character takes the default body

A tag with no Body Meshes rule selects Default Mesh: SKM_Manny on the shipped party and player bases, or the invisible Mannequin on a VRoid pawn. Every style tag a pawn can carry needs its own Body Meshes rule on that pawn. Saving the pawn reports a Cosmetic Part whose tags match no rule.

Keep a Default Mesh on your own pawns

With no Default Mesh, an unmatched tag selects no body at all. XenoCore's party and player characters guard against it at Begin Play: they use the mesh they spawned with and log a LogXenoCosmetics warning once per class. A pawn that is not a XenoCore combatant has no such guard and turns invisible. Saving a pawn with no Default Mesh shows a warning.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym with the character active and leading.
  2. Walk and stand still. The movement and idle are your style's; after about eight to fourteen seconds still, the fidget plays.
  3. Engage an enemy. The drawn-weapon layer takes over, and blends back when you sheathe.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Symptom Fix The fidget you set never plays The character's anim profile has its own Idle Breaks, which win. See the warning under Change a style's idle break. The style's walk never appears A weapon instance (or weapon type) has no layer rule for the tag. See step 4. The character turns invisible or takes the wrong body The tag has no Body Meshes rule on that pawn, or Default Mesh is empty.

The layer swaps with a visible pop

The swap is blended by an inertialization request on the DefaultGroup slot group. A layer you built by hand with its own slot nodes in another group blends wrong. Duplicate a shipped layer instead of building one.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Animation: the host anim Blueprint, linked layers and why locomotion stays snappy.
  • Add a weapon: a weapon instance's anim sets.

docs.title: Give a map its music
docs.text:
Level designer · 20 min · No code

Result: your map plays a field track while the party explores, crossfades to a battle track the moment a fight starts, fades the battle track out under the victory fanfare when you win, and picks the field track up again from where it was cut.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Two looping tracks imported as Sound Waves (or Sound Cues or MetaSounds): one for exploring and one for battle. Either may be left out.
  • A map that runs the XenoCore Experience. See Build a world-partition map.

docs.title: How area music works
docs.text:
One actor per map, XenoCore Area Music (AXenoCoreAreaMusic), holds both tracks. The class names no track of its own: you choose them on the placed actor, and an empty slot is silence. Each map's music lives and dies with that map, so it never carries into the next one.

When What you hear The map starts Field Music fades in over Field Start Fade Seconds The party enters battle The field track fades out and Battle Music fades in, from the top, over Enter Battle Fade Seconds The battle is won The battle track fades out over Victory Fade Seconds, so the victory fanfare plays alone The battle ends without a win (you fled, or the enemy gave up) The battle track fades out over Leave Battle Fade Seconds The battle is over The field track fades back in over Field Return Fade Seconds, from where it was cut Night falls (19:00) or ends (05:00) Field Music Night, if set, crossfades with the day track over Day Night Fade Seconds; never mid-battle Rain or a storm starts The music lowers by the weather type's Music Volume Scale, over Weather Duck Seconds. See Tune a map's weather

"In battle" is the same rule the rest of the template uses: the leader has drawn, or an enemy nearby is fighting the party. See Party. The actor checks it every Poll Seconds (0.2), so a transition can start up to a fifth of a second late.

Both tracks play as UI sounds: the music carries on under the pause and party menus, which pause the world.

docs.title: 1. Put the tracks on Lyra's Music sound class
docs.text:
1. Open each Sound Wave in the Content Browser.
  2. Under Sound, set Class to Lyra's Audio/Classes/Music.
  3. Tick Looping if the track is not already set to loop.
  4. Save.

Fails silently: a track on the wrong sound class ignores the Music slider

A track left on the default sound class plays at full volume whatever the player sets Music to in the options. Nothing warns. Put every music track on Audio/Classes/Music.

docs.title: 2. Place the actor
docs.text:
1. In Place Actors, search for XenoCore Area Music and drag it into your map. Where you put it does not matter: the music is not positional.
  2. In the Outliner, name it AreaMusic so it is easy to find.

World Partition: keep it loaded everywhere

In a partitioned map, the actor must not be spatially loaded, or it streams out with its cell and the music stops when the player walks away from wherever you dropped it. A newly placed Area Music actor already has Is Spatially Loaded off. Leave it off.

docs.title: 3. Choose the tracks
docs.text:
Select the actor and, in its Details panel:

Setting Category Value Field Music Music › Field Your exploring track. Empty = Fallback Field Music from Project Settings › Game › XenoCore Content › Startup, or silence if that is empty too Field Volume Music › Field Start at 1.0; set it in step 4 Battle Music Music › Battle Your battle track. Empty = Fallback Battle Music from the same settings; if that is empty too, the field track plays straight through fights Battle Volume Music › Battle Start at 1.0; set it in step 4 Resume Field Music Music › Field On (default): after a battle the field track continues from where it was cut. Off: from the top Field Music Night Music › Field Optional. Played while exploring at night. Empty = the field track plays at night too Field Night Volume Music › Field Volume of the night track

The battle track always starts from the top.

Resume needs a Sound Wave

The field track resumes from where it was cut only if it is a Sound Wave. A Sound Cue or MetaSound restarts from the top after each battle.

docs.title: 4. Match the two volumes
docs.text:
Two tracks bought from different places are rarely mastered to the same loudness. Left at equal volumes, every fight jumps up or down in level.

  1. Measure each file's average loudness (RMS, in dB) in any audio tool. In the free editor Audacity, open the file, select all, and choose Analyze › Measure RMS.
  2. Pick a target loudness and set each volume to bring its track there. Every 6 dB louder than the target is roughly half the volume. For example, a battle track 7 dB louder than the field track needs a Battle Volume a little under half its Field Volume.
  3. Play, and adjust both volumes together by ear. Scaling both by the same amount keeps the match.
