The sample map Maps/L_XenoCore_GaurPlain has an AreaMusic actor with both track slots empty: the template ships no licensed music. Set your own tracks on it, or set Fallback Field Music and Fallback Battle Music in Project Settings › Game › XenoCore Content › Startup to give every map with empty slots the same music.

docs.title: 5. Tune the fades (optional)
docs.text:
All under Music › Transitions, in seconds:

Setting Default Fades Enter Battle Fade Seconds 1.0 Field out and battle in when a fight starts Leave Battle Fade Seconds 2.5 Battle out when a fight ends without a win Victory Fade Seconds 0.75 Battle out on a win, under the fanfare Field Return Fade Seconds 3.0 Field back in after the battle Day Night Fade Seconds 5.0 Day and night field tracks into each other Weather Duck Seconds 4.0 The music following a weather change in volume Poll Seconds (advanced) 0.2 How often the battle state is read

Field Start Fade Seconds (3.0, Music › Field) is the fade-in when the map starts.

Save the level.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play in your map. The field track fades in over about three seconds.
  2. Open the pause menu. The music keeps playing.
  3. Hit an enemy. Within a second the field track gives way to the battle track.
  4. Win the fight. The battle track fades away quickly and the victory fanfare plays on its own; the field track then returns from the point where it was cut, not from the start.
  5. Start another fight and run until the enemy gives up. The battle track fades out more slowly and the field track returns.
  6. In the options menu, lower Music. Both tracks get quieter.

The Output Log prints one line when the map starts, naming each track and its volume: AreaMusic <name>: field=... (x1.00), night=... (x1.00), battle=... (x1.00). <name> is the actor's internal object name, not its Outliner label, so the two can differ.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: no music at all

There is no Area Music actor in the map, or Field Music is empty and so is Fallback Field Music in Project Settings (as in the shipped Gaur Plain). Check the log line above: no line means no actor; field=None means an empty slot.

The music stops when you walk away

The actor is spatially loaded in a World Partition map. Select it and untick Is Spatially Loaded.

Music from another map keeps playing, or two tracks play at once

Two Area Music actors are in the same map, or one is in a sublevel that loads alongside it. Keep exactly one per map.

Fights get much louder (or quieter) than exploring

The two volumes are not loudness-matched. Redo step 4.

The battle track never starts

Battle Music is empty, which by design keeps the field track playing through fights. If it is set, check that the party really enters battle: lock on and draw, or let an enemy hit you.

The Music slider does nothing

The tracks are not on Audio/Classes/Music. See step 1.

More in World and maps troubleshooting.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Build a world-partition map
  • Party: when the party counts as in battle.
  • The victory fanfare itself is Project Settings › Game › XenoCore Content › Battle › Victory Fanfare.

docs.title: Give a map its time of day and weather
docs.text:
Level designer · 20 min · No code

Result: your map's sun crosses the sky with the clock, night falls with a moon and stars, and the area rolls its own weather: here, rain one time in ten and a thunderstorm now and then. The minimap shows the time and the weather icon.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Read Time of day and weather.
  • A map that runs the XenoCore Experience, with a XenoCore Map Area actor and an Area Definition (the minimap needs the same two). See Give a map its minimap.

docs.title: 1. Check the map's lights
docs.text:
The director drives the lights already in your map; it does not bring its own.

  1. Select the map's Directional Light and set Mobility to Movable.
  2. Make sure the map also has a Sky Light, an Exponential Height Fog and a Sky Atmosphere. A Volumetric Cloud using the engine's m_SimpleVolumetricCloud material is what rain and storms close up; without one the weather still dims and greys the scene, but the sky stays open.

Fails silently: a sun that is not Movable

The clock runs and the minimap shows the right time, but the sun never moves. One warning is logged at Begin Play. Set the directional light to Movable.

docs.title: 2. Place the director
docs.text:
1. In Place Actors, search for XenoCore Environment Director and drag one into the map. Its position does not matter. Place one per map.
  2. In its Details panel, under Environment, set Profile to World/DA_XenoCore_SkyProfile_Default, or to a copy of it in your own folder if you want a different day.
  3. Leave the light slots under Environment › Lights empty to use the map's first of each, or pick the actors if your map has more than one.
  4. If your grass sways with a wind material parameter collection, set Environment › Wind › Wind Collection to it, and the parameter names below it to the ones your foliage reads. Rain and storms then blow it harder.

docs.title: 3. Make the area's weather table
docs.text:
1. In your folder, right-click › Data › Data Table, and pick the row structure XenoCoreWeatherChanceRow. Name it DT_MyGame_Weather_MyArea.
  2. Add a row: Weather XenoCore.Weather.Rain, Percent 10.
  3. Add a row: Weather XenoCore.Weather.Storm, Percent 3.
  4. Leave Phases empty on both, so they can roll at any time of day.
  5. Save.

Whatever the rows leave under 100 (here 87%) is clear weather. Gaur Plain's table, Maps/Areas/DT_XenoCore_Weather_GaurPlain, is a working example.

docs.title: 4. Point the area at it
docs.text:
1. Open your Area Definition (the asset your XenoCore Map Area actor's Area points at).
  2. Under Weather, set Weather Table to DT_MyGame_Weather_MyArea.
  3. Save.

An area whose Weather Table is empty is always clear.

docs.title: 5. (Optional) A night track
docs.text: On the map's XenoCore Area Music actor, set Field Music Night. It crossfades in at nightfall and back out at dawn, never mid-battle. See Give a map its music.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play in your map. The minimap shows the area name, a weather icon (none when clear) and the time.
  2. Open the console (`) and run XenoCore.Time.Scale 60: an hour passes every second. Watch the sun set, the moon rise and the stars come out. Run XenoCore.Time.Scale 1 to go back.
  3. Run XenoCore.Weather.Set Rain lock snap. Rain falls round the camera, the sky greys and the music drops. Stand under an arch or roof: no rain falls there.
  4. Run XenoCore.Weather.Set Storm lock snap, then XenoCore.Weather.Lightning. The sky flashes and thunder follows.
  5. Run XenoCore.Weather.Reroll to hand the weather back to your table.
  6. Open the menu, choose Change Time, pick an hour and confirm. The screen fades and the clock jumps.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: the weather never changes from clear

The area's Weather Table is empty, the map has no XenoCore Map Area actor, or the Map Area points at a different Area Definition. Run XenoCore.Time.Describe to see what the clock and weather think.

The weather icon shows, but nothing on screen changes

The map has no XenoCore Environment Director, or XenoCore.Environment.Freeze is 1.

Rain falls but shows no icon, or never lowers the music

That weather has no row in World/DT_XenoCore_WeatherTypes (or in the table set in Project Settings › Plugins › XenoCore Environment › Weather Types). Add one with the same Tag.

Night is as bright as day

Auto exposure is lifting the night. Lower Night Exposure Floor EV100 on your sky profile; try values live with XenoCore.Environment.NightFloor.

Rain falls indoors

The overhead capture that stops rain is off: tick Rain Height Map (Environment › Weather › Height Map) on the director. Or the roof is translucent, which the capture leaves out.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Add a new kind of weather: a gameplay tag under XenoCore.Weather, a row in the weather types table, and a row in an area's weather table.
  • Change how fast time passes, or the phase hours: Project Settings › Plugins › XenoCore Environment › Clock.
  • Time of day and weather.

docs.title: Chain Arts into Break, Topple and Daze
docs.text:
Designer · 30 min · No code

Result: three Arts that work as a combo. The first Breaks the enemy, the second Topples a Broken enemy, the third Dazes a Toppled one, and the third also deals bonus damage only against a Toppled target.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Make an attack Art
  • Break, Topple, Daze in the glossary.

docs.title: How the chain works
docs.text:
Each reaction is a gameplay effect in Battle/Reactions. An Art inflicts one by listing it in its Effects.

Reaction effect Grants gameplay tag Lands only if the target has GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Break Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Break nothing: always lands GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Topple Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Topple Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Break GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Daze Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Daze Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Topple

The effects enforce the order, not the Arts. A Topple entry on an Art used against an enemy that is not Broken is simply refused: no error, no Topple. That is how the chain is meant to work, so you never need to check the order yourself.

Each reaction lasts its own time, authored on the effect (Break lasts 10 seconds, Topple 3.5, Daze 2). While Toppled or Dazed, a target is knocked down, cannot auto-attack or use Arts, and takes bigger critical hits (×1.5 instead of ×1.25).

docs.title: 1. The Break Art
docs.text:
1. Create a blank Art: in MyGame/Arts, right-click › Data › Data Asset › XenoCoreArtDefinition, named DA_Sunder. Fill in its name, Power, Cooldown Duration, its own Cooldown Tag, Montage and Palette Glyph as in Your first art. Do not duplicate DA_XenoCore_AirSlash or another finished Art: the copy brings its effects along.
  2. Under Art, set Category to Break, so the Arts menu colours it as a Break Art.
  3. Under Art › Effects, click + on Effects and set the new entry: Effect GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Break, Chance 1.0, Condition Always, Recipient Each target. Leave Duration and Magnitude at 0: reactions carry their own timing and never read them.

docs.title: 2. The Topple Art
docs.text:
1. Create another blank Art, DA_Upend, the same way, with its own name and Cooldown Tag.
  2. Category: Topple.
  3. Add one effect: GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Topple, set as for Sunder.

docs.title: 3. The Daze Art with a bonus
docs.text:
1. Create a third blank Art, DA_Stun, own name and tag, Category Daze, effect GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Daze.
  2. For bonus damage against a Toppled target, you need an entry whose condition is Target is Toppled. Add a second Effects entry:
    • Effect: Battle/Status/GE_XenoCore_Status_StrengthDown
    • Duration: 10
    • Condition: Target is Toppled

The Daze lands, and a Toppled target is also weakened for ten seconds.

Conditions see the target before the hit

Every condition is judged on the target as it was before this Art landed. So an Art that both Breaks and has a Target is Broken entry only triggers that entry on an enemy that was already Broken; it cannot chain off its own Break in one press.

The conditions you can use:

Condition True when Always Always In the art's position Any of the Art's Positional Bonuses is met From the front, From the side, From behind The user stands there relative to the target Target is Broken, Toppled, Dazed The target has that reaction

docs.title: 4. Put them on one character
docs.text:
1. Open the character's pawn Blueprint (for Kael, Characters/VRoid/Kael/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_L), click Class Defaults, and note the Data Table in XenoCore › Arts › Art Learn Table. This is the character's learnset.
  2. Open that Data Table and click Add three times. On each row set Art to one of DA_Sunder, DA_Upend, DA_Stun, Unlock Level 1, and Default Slot a slot number no other row in the table uses (-1 leaves the Art unslotted, for the player to place from the Arts menu).
  3. Save the table.

Slots fill from the centre out, so slots 0 and 1 sit either side of the Talent Art. More in Set palette slots and unlocks.

docs.title: Chain across the party
docs.text:
A reaction is on the target, not the attacker. So one party member can Break and another Topple: the chain works across characters with no extra setup. Give the Break Art to one member and the Topple Art to another.

AI-controlled companions read the chain from the same effects. Because Upend's Topple effect needs a Broken target, a companion holds Upend until the enemy is Broken (AI Wait For Reaction, on by default) and then favours it (AI Chain Bonus). See Tune companion AI.

Enemies use exactly the same effects: the sample minion's Arts are Art definitions too - DA_XenoCore_Minion_Rend Breaks and DA_XenoCore_Minion_Sweep Topples. See Give an enemy Arts and AI.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym with the three Arts on the leader's palette.
  2. Use Upend (Topple) on a fresh minion. Nothing happens: it is not Broken.
  3. Use Sunder. "Break" pops over the minion.
  4. Within ten seconds, use Upend. The minion falls: "Topple".
  5. While it is down, use Stun. "Daze", and the Strength Down icon if it applies.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
The new Arts are not on the palette

Default Slot is read only when a character's palette is first built, so a loaded save keeps its old palette. Slot the Arts from the Arts menu, or test from a fresh start.

Fails silently: Topple never happens

The Topple Art is used after Break has worn off (10 seconds), or on an enemy never Broken. The effect refuses itself without a message. Shorten the gap, or lengthen Break's duration on a copy of the reaction effect.

The reaction pops up but the enemy doesn't fall

The target has no ability that plays the knockdown when the tag arrives. It still cannot act, so it just stands there. Party members have them (Battle/GA_XenoCore_Player_Topple, _Daze) and so does the minion (Characters/Enemies/Minion/GA_XenoCore_Minion_Topple, _Daze, granted by AbilitySet_XenoCore_Minion_Melee). A new enemy with its own skeleton needs its own copies with its own montages; see Add an enemy.

The popup never appears

The effect is a status or reaction you made yourself, without a display name. Reactions are named from their class; statuses need a Display Name (Make a status effect).

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Reactions and statuses: the reaction state machine, immunity and timings.
  • Make a status effect

docs.title: Make an attack Art
docs.text:
Designer · 40 min · No code

Result: an Ether cone attack called Frost Fan. It hits every enemy in front of you, reads Ether instead of Strength, deals double damage from the side, Slows anyone it hits from behind, and grows stronger and faster to recharge as the player trains it.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Your first art. This recipe assumes you have made Stone Cleave, and goes further: area, attribute, positional bonuses, conditional effects and levels.
  • In the glossary: Art, Break, Status effect.

docs.title: 1. Start from a blank Art
docs.text:
1. In MyGame/Arts, right-click › Data › Data Asset, pick XenoCoreArtDefinition and name it DA_FrostFan. Do not duplicate DA_XenoCore_AirSlash: the copy would bring Air Slash's Break and side-Slow effects with it.
  2. Open it. Under Art, set Display Name Frost Fan and Description Ether damage in a cone. Slows from behind.
  3. Give it its own Cooldown Tag, Cooldown.MyGame.Art.FrostFan: add the tag in Project Settings › Project › Gameplay Tags (in a tag source of your own), then pick it here. Until you do, saving reports an error, and Arts sharing a tag share one cooldown.
  4. Set Target Type to Enemy. Under Art › Animation, set Montage to an existing Art montage such as Characters/Player/Animations/Kwang/AM_XenoCore_BackSlash. Under Art › Palette, set Palette Glyph to the one Battle/Arts/DA_XenoCore_AirSlash uses.
  5. Leave Ability Class empty. The Art then runs as the shared GA_XenoCore_Art_Base.

DA_XenoCore_SlitEdge (from the side, lowers Physical Defence) and DA_XenoCore_StreamEdge (a cone) in Battle/Arts were built this way and are worth comparing against.

docs.title: 2. Make it an Ether art
docs.text:
All under Art:

  1. Attribute: Ether. Damage now uses the attacker's Ether against the target's Ether Defence, instead of Strength against Physical Defence.
  2. Category: Ether. This is the colour category the Arts menu shows; it changes no numbers.
  3. Effect Type: Damage.
  4. Under Art › Palette, set Glyph Colour to a blue, to match.

docs.title: 3. Make it hit an area
docs.text:
Under Art › Area:

  1. Area: Cone in front of the user.
  2. Area Radius: 600 (cm).
  3. Cone Angle: 100 (degrees, full width).

An area Art aimed at a cone or at a circle around the user needs no target in reach, so Distance is ignored for it. For Single target or Circle around the target, Distance is the reach, and confirming the Art from further away makes the character run in and strike on arrival.

To see the shape in play, run XenoCore.Arts.DrawArea 1 in the console: every Art draws its area, and who it hit, at impact. Tune the radius and angle by eye. (Not in Shipping builds.)

docs.title: 4. Reward position
docs.text:
1. Under Art › Positional, add one entry to Positional Bonuses:
    • Position: Beside the target
    • Power Multiplier: 2.0
    • Announce Chance: ticked. The palette lights "Chance!" while you stand there.
  2. You can add a second entry for another position. The best multiplier that applies is used.

The front, side and back are judged from the target's facing: within 60° of its front is front, beyond 120° is behind, between is the side.

docs.title: 5. Add a conditional status
docs.text:
Under Art › Effects, add one entry:

Field Value Meaning Effect Battle/Status/GE_XenoCore_Status_Slow What to apply Chance 0.5 50% per target hit Duration 8 Seconds. Required for statuses Magnitude 0 Slow's strength is fixed in its own asset Condition From behind Only when the user is behind that target Recipient Each target Announce Chance ticked Lights the palette's Chance while behind

Conditions are checked against each target as it was before this hit, so an Art that Breaks cannot also count its own Break for a "Target is Broken" entry. The full list of conditions, and reactions, is in Chain Arts into Break, Topple and Daze. Making your own status is Make a status effect.

docs.title: 6. Make it grow with training
docs.text:
Arts level from I to XII with Art Points. Power, Cooldown Duration, and each effect's Duration and Magnitude are scalable floats: a Value times a curve row keyed by the Art's level.

  1. Create a curve table CT_MyGame_ArtLevels (right-click › Data › Curve Table, pick Linear) with two rows:
    • FrostFan.Power: keys 1 = 1.0, 12 = 2.0
    • FrostFan.Cooldown: keys 1 = 1.0, 12 = 0.6
  2. Under Art, expand Power and set Value 150, Curve Table CT_MyGame_ArtLevels, Row Name FrostFan.Power. At level I it is 150; at XII, 300.
  3. On Cooldown Duration: Value 14, row FrostFan.Cooldown. 14 seconds untrained, 8.4 fully trained.
  4. Under Art › Level, Base Level Up Cost is the AP to reach level II; later levels multiply it (see Tune levelling).

With no curve, a scalable float is just its Value at every level.

The shipped Arts do not scale with level yet

The sample Arts' Power and Cooldown Duration have no curve, so training them on the Level Up tab does not change their numbers. Give them curves as above if you use them.

docs.title: 7. Animation
docs.text:
Keep the borrowed Montage to start. To use your own:

  1. The montage's slot must be in the DefaultGroup slot group: FullBody is the one the shipped Arts use.
  2. Set Impact Fraction: where in the montage the hit lands, as a fraction of its length (0.45 = a little before halfway). An Art applies itself on this timer, not from a notify.
  3. Montage Play Rate speeds the whole Art up, impact included.

Fails silently: a montage on another slot group

A montage whose slot is outside DefaultGroup blends wrong against the character's animation layers, and nothing reports it.

docs.title: 8. Optional: slow time
docs.text: Under Art › Time Dilation, set Time Dilation below 1.0 (for example 0.35) to slow the world while the Art plays, as Turn Strike does. Time Dilation Start and Time Dilation End are fractions of the montage; Time Dilation Keeps User Speed keeps the user moving at full speed inside the slow motion. 1.0 is off.

docs.title: 9. Optional: how companions use it
docs.text: Under Art › Companion AI, Usable By AI and AI Priority decide whether and how much an AI-controlled member picks this Art; AI Conditions limit it to targets that meet them, for example Target lacks tag with a status tag so it is not used twice on the same enemy. See Tune companion AI.

docs.title: 10. Teach it
docs.text: Add a row for DA_FrostFan to a character's learnset (the Data Table in their pawn's Class Defaults › XenoCore › Arts › Art Learn Table) as in Your first art, or see Set palette slots and unlocks.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym, slot Frost Fan on a member's palette from the Arts menu, and lead with them.
  2. Engage a group of minions and stand to one side of the one you are locked on. "Chance!" lights.
  3. Use Frost Fan. Every minion in the cone takes damage; the side one takes more.
  4. Walk behind one and use it again: about half the time it is Slowed, and its auto-attacks come round visibly slower.
  5. Open the console (`), type XenoGiveAP 5000, level Frost Fan up on the Arts menu's Level Up tab, and check that it hits harder and recharges faster.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Validation error on save: 'takes its duration from the art, and Duration is 0'

Every shipped status takes its duration from the Art. With Duration 0 it would last no time at all. Set a duration.

Validation error on save: 'Cooldown Tag ... is also used by ...'

Another Art definition uses the same Cooldown Tag, usually one you picked from an existing Art. Give this Art its own tag.

Save warning: 'No Montage'

The definition has no Montage. The Art still works, but plays no animation: its effect lands the moment it is used. A blank Art starts with none; set one as in step 1.

It hits only the locked target

Area is still Single target.

Fails silently: damage is 0

Power's Value is 0, or its Row Name is misspelled and the curve reads 0.

It does physical damage

Attribute is still Physical. Category only changes the colour.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Arts: the definition, the shared ability, dispatch by spec.
  • Chain Arts into Break, Topple and Daze
  • Make a support Art
  • Add a stat to the damage formula (needs a programmer)

docs.title: Bake a portrait
docs.text:
Designer · 30 min · No code

Result: a party member has a portrait of their own, cut out on a transparent background. It shows on their HUD plate, on the Party screen and in the equipment screen's character strip. A second, full-body menu portrait fills their card on the main menu.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Add a party member: you need a member definition to set the portrait on.
  • An image editor that can crop and save PNG with transparency.

Any image in the right shape works. This page shows how to render one with the editor's built-in tools.

docs.title: What a portrait must be
docs.text: Property Value Why Size 320 × 384 pixels (5:6), as the samples Larger than any box it is drawn in; mipmaps scale it down cleanly Background Transparent (alpha) The plate draws the portrait over its own frame and shadow Framing Head and neck, facing the camera The HUD box is small; the samples are framed close on the face, and a waist-up bust is hard to read Texture Group UI Loads at full resolution and never streams down

docs.title: 1. Render the character in the editor
docs.text:
Skip to step 2 if you already have artwork.

  1. Create an empty level (File › New Level › Empty Level) with one directional light and a Sky Light. Save it in a scratch folder of your own, such as MyGame/WorkLevels: it is a work level, not game content.
  2. Drag your pawn Blueprint into the level, or for a VRoid member drag its skeletal mesh.
  3. Select its mesh component. Set Animation Mode to Use Animation Asset and pick an idle, for example MM_Unarmed_Idle_Ready from Lyra's Mannequin animations (or the MF_ version for a feminine character), so it is not in a T-pose.
  4. Under Rendering, tick Render CustomDepth Pass. This is what lets the screenshot tool cut the character out.
  5. Place a Camera Actor facing the character at head height and pilot it (right-click › Pilot). Frame head and shoulders.
  6. Open High Resolution Screenshot... from the viewport's camera menu (the one labelled Perspective). Tick Use custom depth as mask, set Screenshot Size Multiplier to 2 or more, and click Capture.

The image lands in your project's Saved/Screenshots folder with the background transparent.

docs.title: 2. Crop it
docs.text:
1. Open the PNG in your image editor.
  2. Crop to a 5:6 rectangle around the head, and scale to 320 × 384.
  3. Check the edge of the silhouette on a light background. If it has a dark fringe, feather or defringe the edge by one pixel.
  4. Save as T_Portrait_Rook.png.

docs.title: 3. Import it
docs.text:
1. Drag the PNG from your file browser into the Content Browser folder MyGame/Party/Portraits.
  2. Open the texture and set:
    • Texture Group: UI
    • Compression Settings: EditorIcon, as the samples (uncompressed, keeps a clean alpha edge)
    • Mip Gen Settings: SimpleAverage, so the portrait scales down without aliasing
    • Filter: Trilinear
  3. Save.

docs.title: 4. Set it on the character
docs.text:
1. Open the character's member definition, for example PartyMember_Rook.
  2. Under XenoCore › Party, set Portrait to T_Portrait_Rook. Save.

docs.title: 5. Optional: a menu portrait
docs.text:
The main menu shows each active member as a full-height card. It uses Menu Portrait (on the same member definition); left empty, the card falls back to Portrait.

  1. Render the whole body as in step 1, standing in an idle, facing the camera.
  2. Crop to 600 × 1720 pixels with the crown of the head near the top and the body centred on the head. The card shows only the top part of the image (Portrait Crop 0.55 on the card, roughly crown to hips) and fills its height, so a head placed lower is cut off at the waist. Portrait Crop is a setting of the card itself, not of your texture; you never need to change it.
  3. Import it with Texture Group UI, Compression Settings BC7 (it is much larger than a HUD portrait), Mip Gen Settings SimpleAverage and Filter Trilinear.
  4. On the member definition, under XenoCore › Party, set Menu Portrait to it. Save. The samples are Characters/VRoid/<Name>/T_XenoCore_MenuPortrait_VRoid_*, for example Characters/VRoid/Kael/T_XenoCore_MenuPortrait_VRoid_L.

The HUD samples are in Characters/Party/Portraits, for example T_XenoCore_Portrait_Blue: open one to compare your import settings.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play with the character in the active party.
  2. Their HUD plate shows the new portrait, cut out cleanly against the plate.
  3. Open the menu: the character's card shows the menu portrait. Check the Party screen and the equipment screen's character strip too.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
The portrait shows a black or grey box around the character

The PNG has no transparency, or the texture's alpha was stripped on import. Check the texture editor's alpha channel view. Re-export with transparency.

The portrait is blurry

The texture is streaming a lower mip. Set Texture Group to UI and tick Never Stream.

The leader's HUD plate still shows the old face

The plate for the character you control reads the same Portrait field. If it does not change, you are testing from a save or the definition was not saved.

Re-make the portrait when the character changes

A portrait is a picture, not a live render. Change a character's materials and the old portrait still shows the old colours.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Add a party member
  • Restyle the menus: the HUD plate's frame and shadow around the portrait.
  • UI shell and HUD

docs.title: Branch a conversation
docs.text:
Designer · 40 min · No code

Result: an NPC who says different things depending on the state of the game: whether a quest has been done, how strong the party is, and what the party carries. The conversation is a chain of nodes you can put anything between.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Give an NPC a conversation.
  • Basic Blueprint graph editing.

Conditions, not player choices

XenoCore dialogue branches on game state. It has no node for the player picking a reply from a list. A yes/no answer is available only through a quest offer (Accept or Decline), or through your own widget between two lines.

docs.title: The nodes
docs.text:
Right-click in the graph and search by name. They live under XenoCore › Dialogue, XenoCore › Quest and XenoCore › NPC in the node menu.

Node What it does Pins Show Dialogue Shows one line and waits for the player to press A Speaker, Line, Source in; Advanced fires on the press. Does not close the box. Play Dialogue Plays a whole list of lines, then closes the box Lines in; Completed fires after the box closes Close Dialogue Takes the box down and gives the player back movement and camera No target pin. Does nothing if no conversation is open, so it is safe at the end of every branch. Offer Quest Shows the quest panel and waits for an answer Quest, Giver in; Accepted or Declined fires, never both Get Party Quests The party's quest record Use it to ask about quests Get Lines For (XenoCore › NPC) One of this NPC's authored line lists Which: Greeting, Accepted, Declined, In Progress, Turn In

Show Dialogue, Play Dialogue and Offer Quest are latent: the graph pauses on them and carries on from an output pin later. Chain the next node from that output pin, never from the plain exec pin beside it.

docs.title: 1. Make an NPC Blueprint of your own
docs.text:
Branching needs a graph, so this NPC gets its own Blueprint.

  1. Right-click Characters/NPC/B_XenoCore_Npc and choose Create Child Blueprint Class. Name it B_MyGame_Npc_Elder and move it to MyGame/NPCs.
  2. Open it. In Class Defaults, set Display Name. Quest is empty and Has Quest is off already: the base Blueprint starts blank.
  3. In the Event Graph, right-click, search for On Interact (XenoCore › NPC) and add it.

Adding the event in the child replaces the parent's default graph for this NPC. To keep the parent's behaviour for some cases, right-click the event and choose Add call to parent function.

The parent's graph is also where a shop opens and where Member To Recruit joins the party. If your elder should recruit someone, call Try Recruit (XenoCore › NPC › Recruit) at the end of the branch that should do it; it does nothing on an NPC with no member set. Talk-to objectives still count without it: they are counted before the graph runs.

docs.title: 2. Branch on a quest
docs.text:
This elder thanks the party once a quest is done. Use any quest asset, for example Quests/DA_XenoCore_Quest_Monster01.

  1. From On Interact, add Get Party Quests, then from its result Get Status, with Quest set to the quest asset.
  2. Add Switch on EXenoCoreQuestStatus on the result.
  3. From Complete: Show Dialogue (You cleared the storehouse. Thank you.), then from its Advanced pin, Close Dialogue.
  4. From every other output: Show Dialogue (The storehouse is still overrun...), then from its Advanced pin, Close Dialogue.

The quest status is saved with the game, so this branch survives a save and reload.

Status Meaning Unknown Never offered or never answered Declined Turned down; can still be offered Active Accepted, objectives outstanding Ready To Turn In Every objective met Complete Handed in and paid

docs.title: 3. Branch on the party
docs.text:
Other things worth asking, all pure nodes:

Question Node Category Does the party carry an item? Get Party Item Count (Item Def) > 0 XenoCore › Inventory Is a quest offerable right now (gates met, never answered)? Is Offerable XenoCore › Quest Is a quest ready to hand in? Is Ready To Turn In XenoCore › Quest

Each drives a Branch into different Show Dialogue chains.

docs.title: 4. Do something between two lines
docs.text:
Because the conversation is an ordinary graph, you can put any node between two Show Dialogue nodes: give an item (Add Item To Party), take one (Remove Item From Party), offer a quest, open a shop, play a sound. For example:

  1. Show Dialogue (Take this. It was my father's.)
  2. From Advanced: Add Item To Party, Item Def your item.
  3. Show Dialogue (Look after it.) → Close Dialogue.

To stop the NPC handing it over twice, branch on Get Party Item Count first.

A pause longer than 2 seconds closes the box

Between two lines nothing is waiting for the player, so a conversation left open for more than 2 seconds with no line on screen is treated as abandoned and closed (see If it doesn't work below). A Delay of 3 seconds between two Show Dialogue nodes therefore closes the box, and the next line opens it again: a visible blink, with a warning in the log. Keep pauses under 2 seconds. A quest, trade or shop panel open between two lines does not count; the timer waits for it.

Fails silently: variables on the NPC are not saved

A boolean you add to the NPC Blueprint ("already gave the gift") resets when the map reloads or a save is loaded. Branch on something the game saves: quest status, or what the party carries.

docs.title: 5. Place it
docs.text:
1. Compile and Save the Blueprint.
  2. Drag B_MyGame_Npc_Elder from the Content Browser into your map.
  3. Save the level.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play, walk up to the elder and press A (keyboard E) to talk. You get the "still overrun" branch.
  2. Complete the quest your Switch reads (or, for a quick test, use a quest you can finish fast).
  3. Talk to the elder again. You get the thank-you branch.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
The box closes by itself after 2 seconds, with a warning

Show Dialogue leaves the box up by design, so every branch must end in Close Dialogue (or be a Play Dialogue, which closes itself). A branch that simply stops is caught: after 2 seconds the box closes and the Output Log shows a LogXenoDialogue warning naming the NPC, "...was left open with no line waiting - closing it. End every chain of Show Dialogue nodes in its On Interact with Close Dialogue." Find the branch that ends without it and add the node.

Fails silently: the conversation stops after the first line

The next node is wired to the plain exec output of Show Dialogue instead of Advanced. The plain output fires immediately, before the player presses anything.

The parent's quest behaviour still runs

You called the parent function, or the child has no On Interact of its own. Check the graph.

Fails silently: the gift is handed over every time

A variable on the NPC is not saved (see step 4). Branch on Get Party Item Count or a quest's status instead.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Offer a collection quest: the default graph already handles a whole quest.
  • Give a quest to defeat enemies or talk to someone.
  • Interaction, NPCs and dialogue, Quests.

docs.title: Swap the camera feel
docs.text:
Designer · 30 min · No code

Result: the exploration camera sits where you want it: further back or closer, higher or lower, wider or narrower, and smoother or snappier as it follows the party leader. You can switch back to the shipped camera in one field.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Input and camera
  • XenoCore uses Epic's Gameplay Cameras plugin. If you haven't used it, open one of the assets below first and look around the node graph.

docs.title: How the camera is put together
docs.text:
Asset What it is Cameras/CA_XenoCore_Player The camera asset each character carries. Its director always runs one rig. Cameras/CameraRig_XenoCore_Explore The rig: a chain of camera nodes that turns "where the character is and where the stick points" into a camera position.

Every character carries a Gameplay Camera component pointing at CA_XenoCore_Player: the player pawn (Game/B_XenoCore_Player) and every party member (Characters/Party/B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base, which the VRoid base Characters/VRoid/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_Base and all seven sample members inherit from). When you switch leader, the new leader's camera takes over, so both must point at the same camera asset.

The explore rig's nodes, and what each one changes on screen:

Node Settings You see Boom Arm Boom Offset How far behind, above and to the side of the character the camera sits Offset Translation Offset, Rotation Offset A fixed nudge after the boom, for example framing the character left of centre Field Of View Field Of View Wider or narrower view Dampen Position Forward Damping Factor, Lateral Damping Factor How loosely the camera trails the character when they move. Higher trails more. Dampen Rotation Yaw Damping Factor, Pitch Damping Factor How loosely it follows turns Collision Push Collision Sphere Radius, Pull Interpolator How the camera slides in front of walls instead of clipping through

docs.title: 1. Make your own copies
docs.text:
1. Create MyGame/Cameras.
  2. In Plugins › XenoCore Content › Cameras, right-click CameraRig_XenoCore_Explore › Duplicate, name it CameraRig_MyGame_Explore and move it to MyGame/Cameras.
  3. Duplicate Cameras/CA_XenoCore_Player the same way, as CA_MyGame_Player.
  4. Open CA_MyGame_Player. In its Camera Director (a single-rig director), set the rig to CameraRig_MyGame_Explore. Save.

Working on copies keeps the shipped camera intact, so switching back is one field.

docs.title: 2. Point the characters at your camera
docs.text:
1. Open Game/B_XenoCore_Player. In the Components panel, select the GameplayCamera component. Set its Camera Asset to CA_MyGame_Player. Compile and Save.
  2. Do the same in Characters/Party/B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base. Every party member, the VRoid ones included, inherits its camera from this base, so this one change covers them all.

Fails silently: only one of the two

If only the player pawn uses your camera, it looks right until you switch leader in the Party menu, and then the old camera comes back.

docs.title: 3. Tune the rig
docs.text:
Open CameraRig_MyGame_Explore and adjust, one node at a time:

  1. Distance and height: on Boom Arm, change Boom Offset. X is along the boom (negative is further back), Z is height.
  2. Framing: on Offset, a small Translation Offset sideways puts the character off centre, which helps when the HUD sits on one side.
  3. Field of view: on Field Of View. Wider feels faster and shows more of the field; narrower frames characters larger.
  4. Follow softness: on Dampen Position and Dampen Rotation. Lower damping gives a tight, responsive camera; higher gives a drifting, cinematic one. Change forward and lateral separately: a little forward lag reads as speed, lateral lag reads as floatiness.
  5. Save after each change and check it in Play; rig edits apply the next time you press Play.

Keep the collision node last in its chain

Collision Push must run after the nodes that place the camera, or it tests the wrong position and the camera clips into walls. Leave the node order as it is and change values.

docs.title: 4. (Optional) The recentre sweep
docs.text:
Right stick click runs Input/Abilities/GA_XenoCore_CameraReset, which swings the view back behind whoever you are driving. Under XenoCore › Camera on its Class Defaults:

Setting Default You see Recentre Duration 0.35 How long the sweep runs. 0 snaps at once Recentre Interp Speed 8 How quickly it closes on the target angle Recentre Pitch -10 The pitch it settles at. Negative looks down onto the character

To recentre on something else (the locked target, say):

  1. Right-click GA_XenoCore_CameraReset › Create Child Blueprint Class, save it in MyGame/Cameras.
  2. In the child, under Functions › Override, choose Get Recentre Rotation and return the rotation you want.
  3. Open Game/AbilitySet_XenoCore_Input, find the Granted Gameplay Abilities entry whose Ability is GA_XenoCore_CameraReset, and set it to your child. Keep its Input Tag. Save.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play.
  2. Run in a circle and then stop. The camera trails and settles the way you tuned it.
  3. Back into a wall. The camera slides in rather than clipping through.
  4. Open the menu, make another member leader on the Party screen, close the menu. The camera feels the same.
  5. Click the right stick on a gamepad (it has no keyboard key) to recentre behind the character.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Nothing changed

The characters still point at CA_XenoCore_Player, or your camera asset's director still runs the shipped rig.

The camera sits inside the character's head

The camera component has no Camera Asset, or the asset has no rig. The engine then falls back to the character's eye position.

The camera changes after switching leader

Only one of the two pawn Blueprints was updated.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Input and camera
  • Tune targeting: the lock-on camera behaviour.
  • Conversations frame themselves with a separate rig, Cameras/CameraRig_XenoCore_Dialogue, set in Project Settings › XenoCore Content › Dialogue Camera Rig (cleared = off) and per NPC with Use Dialogue Camera / Dialogue Camera Rig. Your explore rig does not affect it.

docs.title: Give a character its own combat animations
docs.text:
Designer · 20 min · No code · Last tested: 2026-09-30 (automated play test)

Result: one character topples, flinches, blocks, dodges, dies or celebrates a win with its own clips, while every other character keeps the shared ones. You edit one asset per character.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Add a party member or Add an enemy type
  • Reactions and statuses: what Flinch, Topple and Daze are.
  • Montages for your clips, on the same skeleton as the character's body. Party members animate on the UE5 Mannequin (SK_Mannequin), the minion on SK_Minion_Core.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Every reaction gameplay ability ships with its own clips: GA_XenoCore_Player_Topple plays AM_XenoCore_Player_Topple, for everyone who has it. A character's anim profile can override those clips for that character only.

Empty means "use the default", at every level. No profile, no row for a reaction, or an empty slot inside a row: each falls back to the ability's own clip for that slot. So you only fill in what is different. A profile with a Topple Front clip and nothing else still uses the shared clip when the character is hit from behind, and still plays the shared get-up.

Each row in a profile is keyed by a gameplay tag:

Reaction Key in the profile Abilities that read it Flinch (hit react) Anim.XenoCore.Reaction.Flinch GA_XenoCore_Player_HitReact, GA_XenoCore_Minion_HitReact Topple Anim.XenoCore.Reaction.Topple GA_XenoCore_Player_Topple, GA_XenoCore_Minion_Topple Daze Anim.XenoCore.Reaction.Daze GA_XenoCore_Player_Daze, GA_XenoCore_Minion_Daze Block Anim.XenoCore.Reaction.Guard GA_XenoCore_Guard, GA_XenoCore_Minion_Guard Dodge Anim.XenoCore.Reaction.Evade GA_XenoCore_Evade, GA_XenoCore_Minion_Evade Attack bounced off a block Anim.XenoCore.Reaction.Recoil GA_XenoCore_Recoil, GA_XenoCore_Minion_Recoil

The profile holds clips only. How long a Topple lasts, whether it holds until the reaction ends, and what blocks it all stay on the ability, so they are the same for every character.

The party's dodge is the one reaction that does not choose by side. GA_XenoCore_Evade lists a duck and a sidestep under Random Montages and plays one of them at random on every miss, whichever side the attacker is on. A profile Evade row still wins: a filled Front, Back, Left or Right slot replaces the random pick when the attacker is on that side.

docs.title: 1. Find or make the character's profile
docs.text:
• VRoid party members already have one each, beside their pawn: Characters/VRoid/Dorran/DA_XenoCore_AnimProfile_VRoid_C, and the same for _L (Kael), _K (Mira), _S (Nia), _M (Isolde), _Q (Sabine) and _Y (Tamsin). Each holds that character's victory emote and idle breaks; its Reactions list is empty, so every reaction uses the shared clips until you add a row. The Mannequin colour samples have theirs in Characters/Party/AnimProfiles.
  • Anyone else: in your folder, right-click › Data › Data Asset, pick Xeno Core Character Anim Profile, and name it DA_MyGame_AnimProfile_<Name>. Then open the character's pawn Blueprint, Class Defaults, and set XenoCore › Animation › Anim Profile to it. Enemies have the same field on their Blueprint (for example B_XenoCore_Minion_Melee).

docs.title: 2. Override a reaction
docs.text:
1. Open the profile.
  2. Under Reactions, click +. Set the key to the reaction you want, for example Anim.XenoCore.Reaction.Topple.
  3. Fill in only the slots you have clips for:
    • Front, Back, Left, Right: the clip when the attacker stands on that side of the character. A knock-down usually needs only Front; the shipped Topple uses one clip for every side.
    • Follow Up: the get-up, crossfaded in after the main clip. Its blend time is the follow-up montage's own Blend In.
  4. Save.

For a party member's Evade (and Guard or Recoil) clip, put the montage on the Defence slot if the character should keep both hands on its weapon while dodging armed: on that slot the body comes from your clip and the arms from the weapon stance. On FullBody your clip's arms play too, which suits a sheathed character but lets the hands drift off a two-handed grip.

docs.title: 3. Override the death (optional)
docs.text:
Add clips to Death Montages. One is picked at random when the character dies. Any clip here replaces the pawn's own Death Montages list entirely, so a character with its own deaths never rolls a generic one.

This is for enemies. A party member at 0 HP is downed, not killed: it kneels and waits for a revive, using one shared set of kneeling clips that is not part of the profile. See Party gauge and revive.

docs.title: 4. Give the character a victory emote (optional)
docs.text:
When a battle is won, every living party member sheathes their weapon and then plays a celebration from Victory Montages. One clip is picked at random. This slot has no default: a character with an empty list does not celebrate.

  • Use a montage on the FullBody slot. The weapon is already on the character's back, so unarmed clips are fine.
  • Masculine or feminine is the clip you choose. The shipped party's emotes are in Characters/Core/Animations/Victory: Kael AM_XenoCore_Victory_FistRaise, Mira AM_XenoCore_Victory_WhoopWhoop, Nia AM_XenoCore_Victory_Celebration, Dorran AM_XenoCore_Victory_RaisedFist, Isolde AM_XenoCore_Victory_Curtsy, Sabine AM_XenoCore_Victory_Salute and Tamsin AM_XenoCore_Victory_SmallClap.
  • Moving or jumping cancels the emote, and so does a new fight starting.
  • Keep it short; 2 to 4 seconds reads well.

The fanfare that plays at the same moment is a project setting, not part of the profile: Project Settings › Game › XenoCore Content › Battle › Victory Fanfare. The shipped sound, Audio/Battle/SW_XenoCore_VictoryFanfare, is a short, soft chime of about three seconds, mixed to sit just under the area music, with its asset Volume at 1.0. Point the setting at your own sound to replace it, or clear it to win in silence. If you swap in a louder sound, lower that sound's Volume rather than the music.

Party members controlled by the AI sheathe on their own after the win. One that was in the middle of drawing its weapon at that moment finishes the draw and is then asked to sheathe again, so it still celebrates a moment later. The character you control is asked once: if you draw again yourself, you stay armed and skip the emote.

docs.title: 5. Idle breaks and faces (optional)
docs.text:
The same profile gives the character its personality out of battle:

  • Idle Breaks and Armed Idle Breaks: the fidgets played while standing still, sheathed and drawn. One is picked at random, never the same twice running. Empty uses the stance's own break.
  • Social Expressions and Solo Expressions (VRoid faces): the expressions a resting companion pulls when it chats with another member, or on its own. Empty means a neutral face.

docs.title: 6. Share a profile
docs.text: Several characters that should move the same way can point Anim Profile at one asset. This is also how enemy types on the same skeleton share their clips: make one profile for the skeleton and point every enemy Blueprint on it there.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play with the character in the party.
  2. Open the console (`) and type XenoCore.Anim.Describe (the leader), or XenoCore.Anim.Describe enemy, or part of a pawn's name such as XenoCore.Anim.Describe VRoid_C. The Output Log lists every reaction slot and where it comes from: PROFILE for yours, default for the shared clip.
  3. XenoCore.Anim.Play Topple front plays the clip a front Topple would use, on the leader, without a fight. Add enemy or a name to preview someone else. This plays the clip only: no movement lock, no get-up.
  4. XenoCore.Reaction 2 topples the leader for real (XenoCore.Reaction 2 enemy for an enemy); XenoCore.Reaction 0 clears it. The character falls with your clip and gets up.
  5. XenoCore.Battle.Victory plays the whole battle-won sequence without a fight: the fanfare, then each party member's own victory emote.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: the shared clip plays anyway

XenoCore.Anim.Describe tells you which case you are in:

  • "profile: None": the pawn's Anim Profile is empty. Set it on the Blueprint the character actually spawns as, not on a parent you do not use.
  • "profile row ... matches NO reaction this body is granted": the row's key is a reaction this character does not have. Check the key against the table above.
  • The ability shows "no ProfileKey - always its own montages": a reaction ability you made yourself has no Profile Key. Set it under XenoCore › Reaction on that ability.

The character T-poses or freezes during the reaction

The clip is on a different skeleton from the body. Saving the character's pawn Blueprint reports each clip in its profile that does not fit the body, and saving the profile reports clips from two different skeletons in one profile. Give each skeleton its own profile.

Nobody celebrates after a win

The Output Log says why, on lines starting victory:. "has no VictoryMontages" means that character's profile slot is empty. "refused ... wrong skeleton, or no FullBody slot?" means the montage cannot play on that body. "never finished sheathing" means the character was still armed six seconds after the win; for the character you control, this usually means you drew the weapon again. "still armed - asking it to sheathe again" is normal for an AI party member that was mid-draw at the win; it repeats every half second until the weapon is away, and stops if a new fight starts. No victory: line at all means the game did not count it as a win: the last enemy died while nobody in the party was armed, or another enemy was still fighting.

A duplicated VRoid pawn shares the original's profile

Duplicating B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_C, or making a child of it, keeps its Anim Profile, so the new member and Dorran share one asset and editing one changes both. Duplicate the profile as well and point the new pawn at the copy.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Choose an animation style: walking, running and the base idle, which come from the character's style and its weapon rather than from the profile.
  • Reactions and statuses
  • Animation

docs.title: Author a character's statline
docs.text:
Designer · 30 min · No code

Result: a party member has their own HP, Strength, Ether and Agility curve from level 1 to 99, read from rows you wrote. Levelling them up moves every number along your curve.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Add a party member: you need a character with their own Stats Effect.
  • Glossary: Curve table, Gameplay effect.

docs.title: How a statline works
docs.text:
A character's base stats are one gameplay effect, set as Stats Effect on their pawn Blueprint (open it, click Class Defaults, then XenoCore › Combatant). It is applied at the character's level when their body spawns, and again on every level-up.

Each stat is one modifier on that effect:

Field on the modifier Value in the samples Why Attribute XenoCoreStatSet.Strength, .Ether, .Agility, LyraHealthSet.MaxHealth, LyraHealthSet.Health, XenoCoreStatSet.TalentChargePerHit, XenoCoreStatSet.CharacterLevel One modifier per stat Modifier Op Override Re-applying at a new level replaces the old number Magnitude Calculation Type Scalable Float A value times a curve Scalable Float Magnitude A Value, a curve table and a Row Name The stat at level N is Value × row(N)

The seven VRoid characters each have rows of their own in Battle/Attributes/CT_XenoCore_PartyStatlines (Kael.MaxHealth, Mira.Strength and so on, levels 1 to 99), read by their own effect (GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_Kael, ...) with every Value at 1.0, so the number in the table is the number the game uses. The curves are XC1's own: each character follows the XC1 party member their skill tree comes from (Kael Shulk, Mira Reyn, Nia Dunban, Dorran Fiora, Isolde Melia, Sabine Riki, Tamsin Sharla). The older stock members read CT_XenoCore_BaseStats's shared rows with a different Value multiplier each. Give your character rows of their own, which is what this recipe does.

How much EXP each level costs is separate from the statline: it is the member definition's Experience Curve, a row of Game/DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves. Each VRoid character has a row of its own. See Tune levelling.

CharacterLevel is the exception: it uses the custom calculation XenoCoreMMC_EffectLevel, which simply reports the level the effect was applied at. Leave it alone.

Defence, block and critical rate are not on the statline

A party member's Physical Defence, Ether Defence, block and critical rate start at zero and come entirely from equipment. That is intended. See Equipment.

docs.title: 1. Write the rows
docs.text:
The simplest route is a spreadsheet.

  1. In the Content Browser, right-click Battle/Attributes/CT_XenoCore_PartyStatlines and choose Export as CSV. Save it into your own project folder.
  2. Open the CSV. The first row is ---,1,2,3,...,99: the levels. Each further row is a name then 99 values.
  3. Add four rows for your character, named with your own prefix: Rook.MaxHealth, Rook.Strength, Rook.Ether, Rook.Agility. Fill in a value for every level. A good start is to copy one character's rows (say Kael.*) and scale them.
  4. Duplicate CT_XenoCore_PartyStatlines into MyGame/Party as CT_MyGame_BaseStats, right-click the duplicate and choose Reimport With New File, and pick your CSV.

Reimport points at a file on the template author's machine

The shipped curve tables remember the CSV they were imported from, on a path that does not exist on your machine. A plain Reimport of a shipped table fails. Always use Reimport With New File, on your own duplicate.

You can also edit rows directly: open the table, switch to the table view, and edit a cell. The editor can add a row too (the + Curve button) and rename one (double-click its name), but for 99 levels the CSV is quicker.

docs.title: 2. Point the stats effect at your rows
docs.text:
If your character does not yet have a stats effect of their own, duplicate Battle/Attributes/GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_Kael into MyGame/Party (for example as GE_BaseStats_Rook) and set it as Stats Effect on your pawn Blueprint.

  1. Open your character's stats effect, for example GE_BaseStats_Rook.
  2. Expand Modifiers. For the Strength modifier, under Scalable Float Magnitude, set Value 1.0, Curve Table CT_MyGame_BaseStats and Row Name Rook.Strength.
  3. Do the same for Ether, Agility and MaxHealth.
  4. Point the Health modifier at the MaxHealth row too. That is what makes a level-up heal the character to full. (The sample table has no Kael.Health row, so the samples do the same.)
  5. Leave TalentChargePerHit and CharacterLevel as they are. Talent charge is a flat percentage of the gauge per landed auto-attack; 0 means this character charges some other way. See Make a Talent Art.
  6. Check that every Modifier Op reads Override.
  7. Click Save.

Fails silently: keep Health on the statline, as Override

Every level-up full-heals the character only because the statline overrides Health as well as MaxHealth. Removing that modifier, or switching it to Add, silently removes the level-up heal.

docs.title: 3. Raise the level cap (optional)
docs.text:
The cap is 99. It is a config value, not an asset field, so there is nothing to set in the Details panel. To raise it, open your project's Config/DefaultGame.ini in a text editor and add:

[/Script/XenoCoreRuntime.XenoCoreStatSet]
MaxCharacterLevel=120

Then extend your curve rows, and the rows of DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves, to the new cap. A curve past its last key repeats its last value, so without new keys levels 100 to 120 would all have level 99's stats.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play with the character in the active party.
  2. Open the menu and go to the Party screen. Check the character's HP and stats against your rows at their level.
  3. Close the menu, open the console (~) and type XenoAwardExp 5000. The party levels up.
  4. Open the Party screen again. The numbers match your rows at the new level, and the character is at full HP.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: a stat reads 0

The modifier's Value is 0. A scalable float is Value × curve, so a zero Value gives zero whatever the table says. Set it to 1.0.

Fails silently: stats double on every level-up

A modifier uses Add instead of Override. Every re-application then stacks on the last.

Symptom Fix A stat reads the modifier's bare Value (1), and the Output Log has UCurveTable::FindCurve : Row '<name>' not found in CurveTable '<table>' The Row Name does not match a row in the table. Check spelling and prefix. The level changes but the stats do not The pawn's Stats Effect is empty, so the character runs on default attributes. An error naming the pawn is logged on every Play. Set Stats Effect. Continue shows old numbers Stats are recomputed from the curve at load, but the level comes from the save. Test with Play in the editor or New Game. Levels past 99 all have level 99's stats You raised the cap but not the curve rows. Add keys up to the new cap.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Stats and damage: what each stat does in the damage formula.
  • Tune levelling: experience curve and level cap.
  • Curve tables reference

docs.title: Offer a collection quest
docs.text:
Designer · 30 min · No code

Result: an NPC with a marker over their head offers a quest to bring them three of an item. The quest appears on the HUD tracker and in the Quest Log, counts as the party picks the items up, and pays gold, EXP and an item when handed in.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Give an NPC a conversation.
  • Quests.

docs.title: How a quest is put together
docs.text:
A quest is one data asset of class XenoCoreQuestDefinition. The sample is Quests/DA_XenoCore_Quest_Collection01, which asks for two Inventory/Items/ID_XenoCore_EtherCrystal. In Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym it is given by the placed NPC NPC_QuestGiver; Characters/NPC/B_XenoCore_Npc_Sample carries it too, as a ready-made example.

B_XenoCore_Npc's default On Interact graph already runs the whole quest, so a collection quest needs no graph: you set the NPC's Quest and fill in its line lists. What the default graph does:

When the player talks and the quest is… The NPC plays Then Not yet taken (or declined before) Dialogue (the greeting) Shows the offer panel …and the player accepts Accepted Dialogue The quest is active …and the player declines Declined Dialogue The quest can be offered again later Taken, not finished In Progress Dialogue Nothing Taken, every objective met Turn In Dialogue Takes the items and pays the reward

Any empty list falls back to Dialogue.

Counting is automatic. The party's bag is re-read whenever it changes, and the count is set from it. Items the party already holds when it accepts count straight away, so a quest can be ready to hand in the moment it is accepted.

docs.title: 1. Create the quest
docs.text:
1. In the Content Browser, open Plugins › XenoCore Content › Quests, right-click DA_XenoCore_Quest_Collection01 and choose Duplicate.
  2. Move the copy into your own folder, for example MyGame/Quests, and name it DA_MyGame_Quest_LampOil.
  3. Double-click it and set, under XenoCore › Quest:
Setting Value What it does Title Lamp Oil The offer panel's title, the log and the tracker Kind Collection A label for the panel and the log. It changes no behaviour. Area Riverside Where the log groups it Requester Name (empty) Empty uses the giver's Display Name Requester Portrait optional The face beside "Requested By" Summary The lamplighter has run dry... The paragraph on the offer panel Can Decline Ticked Unticked shows only Accept

docs.title: 2. Set the objective
docs.text:
In Objectives, expand entry 0 (the duplicate already has one) and set:

Setting Value Description Bring 3 Scrap Plating to the lamplighter. Kind Collect Item Item Target ID_XenoCore_ScrapPlating (in Inventory/Items) Required Count 3 Counter Label (empty): the counter row uses the item's name, "Scrap Plating 0/3" Consume On Turn In Ticked: the three are taken when the quest is handed in Icon Source From Item

A quest can have several objectives (click + beside Objectives to add one); all must be met.

docs.title: 3. Set the reward and gates
docs.text:
1. Expand Reward and set Gold 300 and Experience 150.
  2. Under Reward › Items, click + and pick ID_XenoCore_BlueSword (in Weapons/BlueSword). Each entry is one item; add the same item twice to give two.
  3. (Optional) Reward › Skill Branches opens a character's skill branch when the quest is handed in, the way XC1's later branches arrive.
  4. (Optional) Under Gates, click + and set the gate's Kind: Party Level At Least shows Required Level; Quest Completed shows Required Quest. A gated quest shows no marker and cannot be offered until every gate holds. Gates are checked only when offering.
  5. Click Save. If the editor reports a validation error, read it: a missing Item Target or a Required Count of 0 means the quest can never finish.

EXP goes to the party, and gold to the party's purse. Reserve (benched) members earn none by default: Reserve Experience Rate is 0 on Game/BP_XenoCore_Progression.

docs.title: 4. Give it to an NPC
docs.text:
1. Drag Characters/NPC/B_XenoCore_Npc into your level, or select one you placed.
  2. In the Details panel, under XenoCore › NPC, set Display Name.
  3. In the same category, set Quest to DA_MyGame_Quest_LampOil. Leave Has Quest off: with Quest set it is ignored, and the quest decides the marker.
  4. Under XenoCore › NPC › Dialogue, fill in Dialogue (the greeting before the offer).
  5. In the same category, fill in Accepted Dialogue, Declined Dialogue, In Progress Dialogue and Turn In Dialogue. See Give an NPC a conversation for how to write a line.
  6. Save the level.

With Quest set, the marker over the NPC follows the quest by itself: it shows while the quest can be offered or is ready to hand in, and disappears while the quest is in progress.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play and walk up to the NPC. The marker is over their head.
  2. Talk. The greeting plays and the offer panel opens. Accept.
  3. The tracker shows "Scrap Plating 0/3".
  4. Pick up or loot three Scrap Plating (every minion family's chests can hold it). The count rises each time.
  5. Return. The marker is back. Talk: the turn-in lines play, the reward banner shows 300 G, 150 EXP and the sword, and the three Scrap Plating leave the bag.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: the count sticks at 0

Item Target is a different item from the one being picked up. Check that it is the exact item definition (not a duplicate with the same display name). Every change to the party's bag refreshes the count, including changes made with Lyra's own inventory nodes.

Symptom Fix The marker never appears A gate is not met (the party level is too low, or the required quest is not handed in), or the quest was already completed in this save. Quest progress is saved, so test with New Game or Play in the editor. The quest was ready, then went back to in progress The items were sold or traded away. The count is read from the bag each time; only Consume On Turn In takes them. Talking plays only the greeting, never the offer Quest is empty on the placed NPC. Check the instance in the level, not the Blueprint.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Give a quest to defeat enemies or talk to someone.
  • Branch a conversation to offer the quest from your own graph with Offer Quest.
  • Quests.

docs.title: Give a character its own idle breaks and faces
docs.text:
Designer · 20 min · No code

Result: one companion (an active member the AI drives) fidgets with its own clips and has its own temperament at rest: a cheerful brawler laughs when it turns to a friend, a deadpan lookout looks bored. Every other character keeps its own. You edit one asset per character, and the face table if you want a new expression.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Companion AI and aggro: when a resting companion strolls, turns to a friend or pulls a face. This recipe only changes which clip and which face.
  • The character needs an anim profile: the data asset set as Anim Profile in its pawn Blueprint's Class Defaults (XenoCore › Animation). Every shipped VRoid member has one beside its pawn, for example Characters/VRoid/Kael/DA_XenoCore_AnimProfile_VRoid_L. For anyone else, make one as in Give a character its own combat animations, step 1.
  • Faces work only on a character with a face: a VRoid member. A Mannequin-bodied member still gets its idle breaks, still turns to its friends and looks at them, but shows no expression.
  • Idle-break clips are animation sequences (not montages) on the UE5 Mannequin skeleton (SK_Mannequin). Characters/Core/Animations/IdleBreaks ships nine you can use: AS_XenoCore_IdleBreak_Browse, _GimmeBreak, _Greeting, _Impatient, _Poise, _Relaxed, _Sneeze, _Stretch and _Waiting. Lyra's own MM_Unarmed_IdleBreak_Fidget, MM_Unarmed_IdleBreak_Scan and MF_Unarmed_Idle_Break work too.

docs.title: 1. Give the character its own idle breaks
docs.text:
1. In the Content Browser, double-click the character's anim profile (for Kael, Characters/VRoid/Kael/DA_XenoCore_AnimProfile_VRoid_L).
  2. Under Idle, click + beside Idle Breaks and pick a clip. Repeat for each clip. These play while the weapon is sheathed. Four is a good number: one is picked at random each time and never the same one twice running.
  3. Leave Armed Idle Breaks empty unless you have clips made for holding the weapon. Empty means the stance's own break plays with the weapon out (for the greatsword, Kwang's laugh).
  4. Click Save.

Fails silently: an unarmed fidget with the sword out

A clip in Armed Idle Breaks plays with the weapon in hand. An unarmed fidget there swings its arms straight through the sword, and nothing complains. Leave the list empty rather than borrow an unarmed clip.

How often the character fidgets is not in the profile: it is Idle Break Delay and Idle Break Jitter (XenoCore › Idle Break) in the Class Defaults of the stance's layer Blueprint in Characters/Player/AnimLayers (for example ABP_XenoCore_UnarmedAnimLayers). That setting is shared by everyone using the stance. See Animation.

docs.title: 2. Give the character a temperament
docs.text:
1. In the same profile, under Face, click + beside Social Expressions to add an entry. These are the faces it pulls when it turns to a companion at rest, and when a companion turns to it.
  2. For each entry set:
    • Expression: a row name from Characters/Core/Face/DT_XenoCore_FaceExpressions, for example Smile, Laugh, Smug or Bored.
    • Chance: how likely, against the other entries in this list.
    • Intensity: 0 to 1, how strongly it is worn.
    • Duration: seconds.
  3. Add entries to Solo Expressions the same way. These are pulled now and then while the character stands alone.
  4. Click Save.

Both lists empty means a neutral face at rest. The faces for battle, a Topple, being downed or a victory come from the face's own rules and are not affected. (See the glossary for Topple and downed.)

The shipped members show the range: Kael is warm (Smile, Happy, Laugh, Thinking), Mira playful (Laugh, Happy, Wink, Giggle), Nia dry (Smug, Smile, Annoyed, Bored).

docs.title: 3. (Optional) Add an expression of your own
docs.text:
1. Open Characters/Core/Face/DT_XenoCore_FaceExpressions and click Add in the Data Table editor's toolbar. Rename the new row (right-click it > Rename). Its name is what profiles, face rules and Blueprints ask for.
  2. In the row's Curves, click + once per face curve, type the curve name as the key and its weight at full intensity as the value. Use the VRM presets: happy, angry, sad, relaxed, surprised, aa, ih, ou, ee, oh, blink, blinkLeft, blinkRight. Most expressions are a mix: the shipped Annoyed is angry 0.45 with blink 0.3, for narrowed eyes under a half frown.
  3. Tick Suppress Blink for an expression whose eyes are already shut or squeezed.
  4. For movement on top of the mix, such as a laugh's mouth, set Pulse Curve (for example aa), Pulse Weight and Pulse Rate (cycles per second).
  5. Click Save, then use the row name in a profile.

Fails silently: a curve the face does not have

A curve name the VRoid model's face does not have shows nothing and logs nothing, exactly like a typo. The VRM presets above are known to reach the face. Check any row that uses a raw Fcl_* morph curve in Play before you rely on it.

docs.title: 4. (Optional) Play a face from a Blueprint
docs.text:
Call Play Expression On Actor with the character (its pawn or its cosmetic part), a row name, a weight and a duration: for a cutscene beat, a dialogue line or a quest reward. It returns false and does nothing on a character without a face, so it is safe to call on anyone.

To make a companion look at something at the same time, take the companion's controller (Get Controller), Cast To XenoCorePartyMemberController, and call Request Attention on it with the actor and a number of seconds. A player-controlled character has no such controller, so the cast fails and nothing happens.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_GaurPlain with the character in the active party, and press Play.
  2. Walk a few steps and stop. Stand still for half a minute.
  3. The character takes its own fidgets from your Idle Breaks, not in step with the others, and no clip twice running.
  4. Now and then it walks up to a companion, the two look at each other, and it wears one of its Social Expressions; the companion may answer with one of its own a moment later.
  5. Draw your weapon. With Armed Idle Breaks empty, its armed fidget is the stance's own.

Idle Breaks and Armed Idle Breaks are copied once, when the body first animates: if you change them while playing, stop and press Play again. Social Expressions and Solo Expressions are read each time a face is chosen, so edits to those show without a restart.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text: Symptom Cause The character never fidgets The idle break waits Idle Break Delay (8 s) plus up to Idle Break Jitter (6 s) of standing completely still. Out of battle a companion may stroll off before then It still plays the old stance fidget The Anim Profile is set on a Blueprint the character does not spawn as, or the clips went into the other list (Idle Breaks is weapon away, Armed Idle Breaks weapon drawn) Saving the pawn reports a clip on the wrong skeleton An idle-break clip is not on SK_Mannequin. Retarget it, or use one of the shipped clips No face ever shows The character has no face (a Mannequin body), or both expression lists are empty, or Chance is 0 on every entry One expression never shows The row name is misspelt, or the row uses a curve the face does not have. Both fail silently Companions never turn to each other They never rest: the leader keeps moving. No activity starts while the leader moves faster than Leader Moving Speed (60 cm/s), a parameter of the XenoCore Party Hold task in Characters/Party/AI/ST_XenoCore_PartyMember

docs.title: Add a confirmation popup
docs.text:
Designer · 20 min · No code

Result: a Yes/No question drawn over your own menu screen, with the screen still visible behind a dimmed scrim. Yes runs your work once. No or Back closes only the popup, and the cursor returns to the button you were on.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • Add a menu screen. You need a screen to ask from; this recipe uses its W_Bestiary.

docs.title: How popups work in XenoCore
docs.text:
A XenoCore popup is not Lyra's full-screen dialog. It is a small activatable widget pushed into a stack inside the screen that asks, named OverlayStack. The screen stays drawn underneath, and the popup's scrim dims it.

The shipped popup is UserInterface/W_XenoCore_ConfirmPopup (its parent class is XenoCoreConfirmPopupBase). It already does the parts that are easy to get wrong:

  • It handles Back, and Back means No, so Back never falls through and closes your screen.
  • It sets its own input mode and starts the cursor on Yes, or on No when you ask it to.
  • It has a title, a question, and an optional red warning line that collapses when empty.

The Ask Confirm node shows it and continues on exactly one of two pins, On Yes or On No, once, after the popup has closed.

docs.title: 1. Give your screen an overlay stack
docs.text:
1. Open W_Bestiary and switch to the Designer tab.
  2. If your root content is not already an Overlay, right-click it in the Hierarchy and choose Wrap With… › Overlay.
  3. From the Palette, drag a Common Activatable Widget Stack onto that overlay as its last child, so it draws on top.
  4. Rename it OverlayStack and tick Is Variable at the top of the Details panel.
  5. In its Slot settings, set Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment to Fill.
  6. Set its Visibility to Self Hit Test Invisible, so it never blocks clicks when it is empty.

docs.title: 2. Ask
docs.text:
In W_Bestiary's Graph, where you want to ask (for example the click of a "Forget entry" button):

  1. Store the widget the cursor is on, such as the clicked button, in a variable ReturnFocus (a Widget object reference).
  2. Add Ask Confirm (category XenoCore › Confirm) and set:
    • Stack: drag in Get OverlayStack.
    • Popup Class: W_XenoCore_ConfirmPopup.
    • Title: Forget entry.
    • Question: Remove this creature from the bestiary?
    • Expand the node's advanced pins for Warning (This cannot be undone.) and Focus Cancel (tick it for a question whose Yes cannot be undone, so a stray press answers No).
  3. From On Yes, do the work.
  4. From both On Yes and On No, call Set Focus on ReturnFocus.
  5. Compile and Save.

Nothing needs binding or unbinding: each Ask Confirm is its own node instance and fires once.

No also covers the unexpected

On No fires for No, for Back, when the popup is closed from outside while still asking (the screen under it closed), and when the popup cannot be shown at all (no stack, or no class; the Output Log says "Ask Confirm: no popup to ask with"). So a graph waiting on the answer is never left hanging.

docs.title: 3. Optional: your own popup look
docs.text:
Duplicate W_XenoCore_ConfirmPopup into MyGame/UI and restyle it. Keep its parent class and these widget names, which the parent class looks for:

Widget Type Required ConfirmButton, CancelButton CommonUI buttons Yes: the popup will not compile without them TitleText, MessageText, WarningText Text blocks Optional

Make the text blocks Hit Test Invisible, then set Popup Class on the node to your copy.

Asking twice with one popup

Ask Confirm (Existing Popup) asks with a popup that is already on screen instead of pushing a new one. A new question replaces an open one, and the old one answers No.

For programmers: asking from a C++ screen

A C++ screen uses the same popup:

  • Give the screen a UCommonActivatableWidgetStack bound as OverlayStack and a TSubclassOf<UXenoCoreConfirmPopupBase> property set to W_XenoCore_ConfirmPopup on the Blueprint. Don't name the path in C++.
  • Push it with OverlayStack->AddWidget<UXenoCoreConfirmPopupBase>(PopupClass), bind the popup's OnDeactivated() to restore focus (call RemoveAll(this) first, because the popup is pooled), then call one of:
    • AskWithAnswer(Title, Question, Warning, bFocusCancel, [this](bool bConfirmed){ ... }), which reports both answers, once, after the popup has closed;
    • Ask(Title, Question, Warning, bFocusCancel, [this]{ ... }), which calls back on Yes only.
  • Is Asking (also Blueprint-callable) is true while a question is open; the save screen uses it to ignore its own keys meanwhile.
  • UXenoCoreSaveScreenBase is the worked example. See Add a mechanic by subclassing for setting up a C++ module.

docs.title: Other screen helpers you can call from Blueprint
docs.text:
A Blueprint screen or HUD widget built on the XenoCore bases can also call these nodes:

Node On What it does Set Shown Immediate Any HUD plate (XenoCoreHudPlateBase) Show or hide at once, with no fade. Changes opacity only, so the plate keeps ticking Set Show Delay Any HUD plate Hold the fade-in back this many seconds, to stagger a column of plates. Fade-out is never delayed Collapse All Except Any HUD plate Collapse every widget in the plate except one and the panels above it Begin Hidden, Skip Intro A HUD plate's own graph Start hidden (cancel the entrance, then hide), or just cancel the entrance. Call from Construct on a plate that decides its own visibility Set Target Target plate (XenoCoreTargetPlateBase) Show an actor's name and level on the badge, or None to hide it Focus Row, Get Focus Target Trade row (XenoCoreTradeRowBase) Put the cursor on the row's button; the button itself, which is what can hold focus Get Focus Target Art row (XenoCoreArtRowBase) The same, for an Arts list row Get Slot Index, Is Selectable Save row (XenoCoreSaveRowBase) Which slot the row stands for; false for the autosave row while saving, and for a file from a newer build while loading

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Play, open the menu, open Bestiary, and click the button that asks.
  2. The popup appears over the screen; the screen is dimmed but visible. With Focus Cancel ticked, the cursor is on No.
  3. Press B (keyboard Escape). Only the popup closes, and the cursor is back on the button.
  4. Ask again and choose Yes. The work runs once.
  5. Ask a third time and choose No. Nothing runs.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: the cursor is lost after the popup closes

Nothing hands focus back automatically, and nothing is logged. Call Set Focus on the stored widget from both pins.
