Symptom Fix The popup covers the whole screen and the screen behind vanishes You pushed it onto UI.Layer.Menu instead of OverlayStack. A layer shows only its top widget, so the popup replaced your screen. Give Ask Confirm the screen's own stack. On No fires immediately and no popup appears Stack or Popup Class is empty. The Output Log says "Ask Confirm: no popup to ask with". Back closes my screen as well You are using a popup of your own that is not a child of XenoCoreConfirmPopupBase. Such a popup must tick Is Back Handler in its Class Defaults, or Back falls through to the screen under it, which closes and takes the popup with it. The popup asset will not compile It is missing ConfirmButton or CancelButton, or they are not CommonUI buttons. See step 3.

docs.text:

  • Add a HUD element
  • UI shell and HUD

docs.title: Make a consumable item
docs.text:
Designer · 45 min · No code

Result: an item, Mend Salve, that the party carries in the bag. Using it spends one and restores the leader's HP.

Read this first: what the template does and does not do

XenoCore has no "use item" command in the menu today. The Items menu lists, sorts and describes items, and nothing in it spends one. Items are spent by quests (turn-in), by shops and trades, and by your own abilities.

This recipe therefore builds the item and a gameplay ability that uses it. You trigger the ability with an input or from another graph. A menu entry that calls it is a UI job; see Add a menu screen.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Add a weapon: item definitions and fragments.
  • Items and inventory: one bag entry is one item.

docs.title: How it is put together
docs.text:
Piece You make Based on The item ID_MyGame_MendSalve A shipped item from Inventory/Items The heal GE_MyGame_Mend Lyra's /Game/Environments/Gameplay/GE_GameplayEffectPad_Heal The use GA_MyGame_UseMendSalve A new Lyra Gameplay Ability

The ability carries a Party Item (XenoCore) cost: it cannot activate unless the party holds a Mend Salve nobody is wearing, and committing the ability spends one. The cost does the bag work through XenoCore's inventory functions, which find the party's bag for you and tell every open screen that the bag changed.

docs.title: 1. Make the item
docs.text:
1. Create a MyGame/Items folder under Content.
  2. In Plugins › XenoCore Content › Inventory › Items, right-click ID_XenoCore_CoolPotato, choose Duplicate, move the copy into MyGame/Items and name it ID_MyGame_MendSalve. Never create an item definition from blank.
  3. Open it. In Class Defaults, set Display Name to Mend Salve.
  4. Expand Fragments. In the Xeno Core Fragment Item Category entry, under XenoCore › Item, leave Category on Collectables (the potato's), and set Max Carried to 20 and Sell Value. Max Carried is the most the party may hold; 0 means no limit. Do not pick Items: no Items-menu tab lists that category, so the salve would be carried but never shown.
  5. In the Xeno Core Fragment Item Display entry, set Description and Icon.
  6. Make sure there is no Xeno Core Fragment Equip Slots entry, or the item becomes equipment.
  7. Click Compile, then Save.

docs.title: 2. Make the heal
docs.text:
1. In the Content Browser, open Content/Environments/Gameplay (Lyra's own content), right-click GE_GameplayEffectPad_Heal, choose Duplicate, move the copy into MyGame/Items and name it GE_MyGame_Mend.
  2. Open it. The heal amount is on its execution, not a modifier: under Executions, in the Lyra Heal Execution entry's Calculation Modifiers, set the BaseHeal modifier's scalable float. Keep its Gameplay Cues entry (GameplayCue.Character.Heal): that is the heal effect you see.
  3. Click Save.

docs.title: 3. Make the ability
docs.text:
1. In MyGame/Items, right-click and choose Blueprint Class. Under All Classes, pick LyraGameplayAbility. Name it GA_MyGame_UseMendSalve.
  2. Open it. In Class Defaults, set Instancing Policy to Instanced Per Actor and leave Activation Policy on On Input Triggered.
  3. Under Costs, click + beside Additional Costs and choose Party Item (XenoCore) from the entry's class dropdown.
  4. In that entry, under XenoCore › Cost, set Item Definition to ID_MyGame_MendSalve and Quantity to 1.
  5. In the event graph, build this chain from Event ActivateAbility:
    1. Commit Ability. This spends the Mend Salve. Branch on its return value; on False, End Ability and stop.
    2. On True: Apply Gameplay Effect to Owner, Gameplay Effect Class GE_MyGame_Mend.
    3. End Ability.
  6. Click Compile, then Save.

With an empty bag the ability does not activate at all, because the cost is checked before activation.

Without a cost

To spend items from a graph instead, use Consume Items From Party (XenoCore › Inventory) with Item Def and Count. It spends exactly that many or nothing, returns false when there are not enough, and never takes an item someone is wearing. Get Free Party Item Count tells you beforehand how many can be spent.

Fails silently: do not use Lyra's Inventory Item cost

The cost list also offers Lyra's own Inventory Item cost, and it looks like the same thing. In stock Lyra 5.8 its code is compiled out: its check always fails, so an ability carrying it can never activate, with nothing logged. Use Party Item (XenoCore).

Fails silently: spend items with the XenoCore nodes

Lyra's own inventory functions also remove items. XenoCore notices and still updates open screens and quest counters, but Lyra's removal functions can take an item a character is wearing, which then vanishes from the save. Use Consume Items From Party or Remove Item Instance From Party (both under XenoCore › Inventory).

docs.title: 4. Give the party some to use
docs.text:
1. Open a pawn in the starting party, for example Kael, Characters/VRoid/Kael/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_L.
  2. In the Components panel, select its equipment component.
  3. In the Details panel, under XenoCore › Equipment, click + beside Starting Inventory.
  4. In the new entry, set Item Definition to ID_MyGame_MendSalve and Count to 3.
  5. Click Compile, then Save.

Fails silently: a pawn that never spawns

Starting Inventory reaches the bag only when that pawn is spawned. A member who is not in the party's Starting Roster (on Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party), such as the colour mannequins in Characters/Party, or B_XenoCore_Player, never spawns at New Game, so their list is ignored with nothing logged. The shipped roster starts with Kael and Mira.

docs.title: 5. Grant the ability
docs.text:
For a first test, grant it from the console (step 3 of Test it). To keep it:

  1. Open Characters/Party/AbilitySet_XenoCore_PartyMember. Every VRoid member is granted it, through Characters/VRoid/PawnData_XenoCore_Party_VRoid.
  2. Click + beside Granted Gameplay Abilities.
  3. In the new entry, set Ability to GA_MyGame_UseMendSalve.
  4. Set Input Tag to a gameplay tag your input config maps to a key. See Input and camera and Add an input action prompt.
  5. Click Save.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play.
  2. Let a minion hit you so you are below full HP.
  3. Open the console and enter AbilitySystem.Ability.Grant GA_MyGame_UseMendSalve, then AbilitySystem.Ability.Activate GA_MyGame_UseMendSalve.
  4. The leader heals. Open the menu's Collectables tab: the party now holds two Mend Salves.
  5. Activate it three more times. The fourth use does nothing: with the bag empty the cost check fails and the ability does not activate.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text: Symptom Fix The ability activates but nothing heals The heal effect has no amount, or its cue was removed. Test the effect alone with AbilitySystem.Effect.Apply GE_MyGame_Mend. The ability never activates The cost's Item Definition is a different item from the one in Starting Inventory; both must be ID_MyGame_MendSalve. Also check that the cost is Party Item (XenoCore), not Lyra's Inventory Item (see the warning above). The count never goes down The graph does not call Commit Ability. The cost is only paid on commit. The bag has no Mend Salves at New Game The pawn you gave Starting Inventory to never spawns (see the warning in step 4).

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Items and inventory.
  • Build a drop table to have enemies drop it.
  • Open a shop to sell it.

docs.title: Add a stat to the damage formula
docs.text:
Programmer · 60 min · C++

Result: a new character stat, Critical Damage, that adds to the critical-hit multiplier. A character with 0.5 Critical Damage lands crits at ×1.75 instead of ×1.25.

Designers: try a skill first

Adding a new stat to the formula needs C++; there is no editor-only route. But crit damage itself needs none: a skill whose Bonus is XenoCore.SkillBonus.CriticalDamage already adds that many percent to the crit multiplier. See Add a skill. Hand this page to a programmer only when equipment or effects must carry a stat that does not exist yet.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A working C++ build of the project. See Troubleshooting: build and editor.
  • Stats and damage: the formula and what each stat means.
  • Set a character's statline: how stats reach a character.

docs.title: How the formula is put together
docs.text:
Two C++ classes own the maths, both in Plugins/GameFeatures/XenoCore/Source/XenoCoreRuntime:

Class File Job UXenoCoreStatSet Public/AbilitySystem/Attributes/XenoCoreStatSet.h Holds every stat as a gameplay attribute (set by gameplay effects): Strength, Ether, Agility, the defences, Critical Rate, Block Rate, Weight, weapon attack, level, Talent Gauge UXenoCoreDamageExecution Public/AbilitySystem/Executions/XenoCoreDamageExecution.h Reads those stats and computes the damage

The execution runs inside Battle/Attributes/GE_XenoCore_Damage, through the Blueprint child BP_XenoCoreDamageExecution (which only sets the level-difference curve). Two formulas are used:

  • Party attacker: floor((stat + weapon) × art × (1 − def) × mods × lvl × block), with the target's defence as a fraction capped at Max Defence Fraction (0.9).
  • Enemy attacker: floor(max(stat − def, 0) × art × mods × lvl × block), with the target's defence as flat points.

UXenoCoreDamageExecution::GetCombatSide decides the side by what the attacker is (an AXenoCoreEnemyCharacter, a character with a member definition, then its team), never by whether a player is driving it. AI companions and the leader use the same formula.

block is Block Multiplier on a blocked hit, 0 by default, so a block negates the hit (0.5 restores XC1's halving), and 1 otherwise.

mods holds the crit multiplier (and any first-strike bonus), floored at Minimum Modifiers (0.1). That is where the new stat goes.

docs.title: Two routes
docs.text:
Both classes are exported, so a C++ class in your module can derive from either. What the formula lacks is a hook: Execute_Implementation computes the whole result in one function, and no term can be overridden on its own.

Route What you do Cost Edit the formula in place (the steps below) Add the attribute to UXenoCoreStatSet and a few lines to UXenoCoreDamageExecution Small, but it edits plugin source. Keep it as a patch and reapply it after template updates Keep it in your module Put the attribute on your own attribute set (a child of UXenoCoreStatSet or of ULyraAttributeSet) granted in your ability sets, and derive your own execution from UXenoCoreDamageExecution, overriding Execute_Implementation Nothing of XenoCore's is edited, but your override must reproduce the whole formula, and GE_XenoCore_Damage must use your execution (a copy of the effect, or BP_XenoCoreDamageExecution reparented)

For one small term such as this one, the in-place edit is less to maintain. Choose the second route when you are replacing the formula outright.

docs.title: 1. Add the attribute
docs.text:
In XenoCoreStatSet.h, add an accessor beside the others:

ATTRIBUTE_ACCESSORS(UXenoCoreStatSet, CriticalDamage);

and the attribute itself in the private: block, following the existing pattern:

// Added to the crit multiplier. 0 = no bonus.
UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, Category = "XenoCore|Stats", Meta = (AllowPrivateAccess = true))
FGameplayAttributeData CriticalDamage;

In XenoCoreStatSet.cpp, initialise it in the constructor list with CriticalDamage(0.0f).

You do not need to add a clamp. ClampAttribute sends every attribute it does not name to its last branch, which keeps the value at zero or above.

docs.title: 2. Capture it in the execution
docs.text:
In XenoCoreDamageExecution.cpp, inside the FStatics struct, add a capture definition. Build it from the public accessor, as the others are; the capture macro does not compile against the set's private members:

FGameplayEffectAttributeCaptureDefinition CriticalDamageDef;
// in FStatics():
CriticalDamageDef = { UXenoCoreStatSet::GetCriticalDamageAttribute(), ESrc::Source, true };

ESrc::Source with true snapshots the attacker's value when the attack starts, which is how every other attacker stat is captured. Then register it in the constructor:

RelevantAttributesToCapture.Add(XenoCoreDamage::Statics().CriticalDamageDef);

docs.title: 3. Use it
docs.text:
Find the critical-hit block in Execute_Implementation (it sets Modifiers to CriticalMultiplierVsReacting or CriticalMultiplier, then adds the Critical Hit Plus skill bonus). Read the new stat and add it after those lines, still inside the block:

float CritBonus = 0.0f;
ExecutionParams.AttemptCalculateCapturedAttributeMagnitude(
    XenoCoreDamage::Statics().CriticalDamageDef, Params, CritBonus);
Modifiers += CritBonus;

Add it to the UE_LOG(LogXenoDamage, Verbose, ...) line as well, so you can see it.

docs.title: 4. Build
docs.text:
1. Close the editor completely. A new UPROPERTY cannot go through Live Coding.
  2. Build the LyraEditor target, then check the end of the build log, not only the exit code.
  3. Open the editor.

docs.title: 5. Give a character some
docs.text:
A stat that nothing sets is always 0. Give the player some with a test effect first:

  1. In MyGame/Battle, right-click and choose Blueprint Class, pick GameplayEffect, and name it GE_MyGame_CritDamageTest.
  2. Open it and set Duration Policy to Infinite.
  3. Click + beside Modifiers. Set Attribute to XenoCoreStatSet.CriticalDamage, Modifier Op to Add, and the Scalable Float Magnitude Value to 0.5.
  4. Click Compile, then Save.

Then give it a permanent home:

  • Per character: add a modifier to that character's statline effect. See Set a character's statline.
  • From equipment: see Add a stat to equipment, section "A brand-new stat". Equipment needs no code for it: one row on the stats effect.

docs.title: 6. Show it on the character sheet (optional)
docs.text: The character sheet and equipment screen read one table, UXenoCoreInventoryStatics::GetStatDefinitions() in Private/Inventory/XenoCoreInventoryStatics.cpp. Add a Row(...) for your attribute. Rows need a XenoCore.Stat.* tag only if an item can grant the stat; pass FGameplayTag() otherwise. Set the last flag (character sheet) to true. The table is built once per process, so this needs a full rebuild and a fresh editor.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym.
  2. In the console, enter Log LogXenoDamage Verbose.
  3. Enter AbilitySystem.Effect.Apply GE_MyGame_CritDamageTest.
  4. Fight a minion until CRITICAL HIT! appears and the damage number turns gold.
  5. In the Output Log, the damage line for that hit reads mods=1.75.

A character without critical rate never crits. If none appear, give the test effect a Critical Rate modifier too (Add 1.0 for a crit every hit).

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: the stat reads 0 on the attacker

The character has no UXenoCoreStatSet at all, or nothing sets the new attribute. Stats arrive only through gameplay effects. Check the attribute with showdebug abilitysystem.

Symptom Fix The editor compiles but the stat is missing from the attribute list Live Coding patched the code but not the reflection data. Close the editor, confirm UnrealEditor.exe is no longer running, and do a full build. Crits read mods=1.25 with the test effect applied The capture was added to FStatics but not registered in RelevantAttributesToCapture, or the read sits outside the critical-hit block. No crits at all The character has no Critical Rate. Add a Critical Rate modifier to the test effect. The stat does not show on the character sheet Step 6 needs a full rebuild and a fresh editor; the table is built once per process.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Stats and damage.
  • Add a stat to equipment.
  • Subclass a mechanic: setting up your own C++ module for the second route.

docs.title: Build a drop table
docs.text:
Designer · 20 min · No code

Result: your enemy leaves chests whose tier odds and contents you chose, and a hand-placed chest in the map uses the same table.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Your first enemy. You should have your own enemy Blueprint.
  • Loot: chest tiers, and why contents are rolled on opening.

docs.title: How loot works
docs.text:
When an enemy dies:

  1. Its Drop Table decides the chest tier at once: Wooden, Silver or Gold. The tier is what the player sees on the ground.
  2. A chest appears where it fell, after Chest Drop Delay seconds (2 by default).
  3. When the player opens the chest, the table rolls its contents from that tier's pool.
  4. The player takes all of it or none of it.

Because the roll happens on opening, the same chest can hold different items after a reload. An unopened chest survives the reload itself, and leaving the map; see Loot.

A drop table is a data asset of class XenoCoreDropTable. The samples are one per enemy family in Inventory/Loot: DA_XenoCore_Drops_Grunt, _Skirmisher, _Bulwark and _Brute (each with its own material and silver chance), plus DA_XenoCore_Drops_Minion for the base minion and the dummy. Each family also has a Rare form of its material in its silver and gold pools, so the Rare guarantee does not land on one item.

Setting Default What it does Gold Chance 0.02 Chance of a gold chest, checked first Silver Chance 0.25 Chance of silver if gold did not land Pools One pool per tier. Each pool has Min Items, Max Items and Entries Pool › Entries › Item Def An item that can drop. Loaded only if it is rolled, when a chest is opened Pool › Entries › Weight 1.0 How likely, relative to the pool's other entries. Not a percentage Pool › Entries › Min Level / Max Level 0 The entry only drops from an enemy of this level range. 0 = no limit on that side. The level is the enemy's, kept on the chest Pool › Guarantee One Of Rarity empty Every chest from this pool holds at least one item of this rarity. See Set and style item rarity Pool › No Duplicate Equipment off A weapon or armour piece comes out of one chest at most once. Materials can still repeat

A warning on save is not an error

Saving the table warns when an item sits below its rarity's Lowest Chest Tier, for example a Legendary in the Wooden pool. It still saves, in case you meant it.

So with the defaults: 2% gold, then 25% of the remaining 98% silver (24.5% overall), and wooden the rest of the time.

docs.title: 1. Create the table
docs.text:
1. In MyGame/Enemies, right-click and choose Data › Data Asset. Pick Xeno Core Drop Table. Name it DA_MyGame_Drops_Stonejaw. Or duplicate the family table closest to your enemy (Inventory/Loot/DA_XenoCore_Drops_Grunt for a melee type) and change it.
  2. Double-click it to open it. Every setting below is under XenoCore › Loot.

docs.title: 2. Set the tier odds
docs.text:
1. Gold Chance: 0.05.
  2. Silver Chance: 0.30.

Both are 0 to 1.

docs.title: 3. Fill a pool for every tier
docs.text:
1. Click + beside Pools three times. Set the key dropdown of the three entries to Wooden, Silver and Gold.
  2. In each pool, set Min Items and Max Items from the table below.
  3. In each pool, click + beside Entries once per item, and set each entry's Item Def and Weight.
  4. Click Save.

The items are in Inventory/Items, Inventory/Armour and Weapons/<Name>.

Tier Min Items Max Items Entries (Item Def, Weight) Wooden 1 2 ID_XenoCore_ScrapPlating 3, ID_XenoCore_EtherCrystal 1 Silver 1 3 ID_XenoCore_EtherCrystal 2, ID_XenoCore_BlueSword 1 Gold 1 2 ID_XenoCore_RedSword 1, ID_XenoCore_BattleArmour 1

Each item in a chest is rolled on its own, so the same entry can come up twice - unless it is equipment and No Duplicate Equipment is on.

Level bands

Give gear an enemy-level range so early enemies cannot drop late gear. The samples' gold pools stop the Battle set at level 8, start Veteran Gauntlets at 4, the Prototype pieces at 5 and the Legendary Vanguard Plate at 10. If no entry fits the enemy's level, the chest opens empty and LogXenoDrop says so.

Fails silently: the chest opens empty

Every tier the enemy can roll needs a pool with at least one entry whose Weight is above 0. A missing pool gives an empty chest, not a fallback to another tier. A warning is logged under LogXenoDrop, and nothing shows in game.

Weight 0 parks an entry

Set an entry's Weight to 0 to stop it dropping without deleting it.

docs.title: 4. Give it to your enemy
docs.text:
1. Open your enemy Blueprint (here B_MyEnemy) and click Class Defaults.
  2. Under XenoCore › Loot, set Drop Table to DA_MyGame_Drops_Stonejaw.
  3. Click Compile, then Save.

Other loot settings on the enemy:

Setting Where What it does Always Gold Chest XenoCore › Loot, also per placed enemy Ignore the odds and always drop gold. For unique monsters. Chest Drop Delay XenoCore › Enemy › Loot, also per placed enemy Seconds before the chest appears Chest Class XenoCore › Loot The chest Blueprint. Keep Inventory/Loot/BP_XenoCore_TreasureChest

An empty Drop Table means the enemy drops no chest. That is allowed and is not logged; use it for bosses that should not drop anything.

docs.title: 5. Place a chest by hand (optional)
docs.text:
1. Drag Inventory/Loot/BP_XenoCore_TreasureChest into the level.
  2. With the placed chest selected, under XenoCore › Loot, set Drop Table.
  3. In the same category, set Tier and Source Level (the level its level bands roll against).
  4. To have it start closed and swing open on interact, untick Lid Open On Spawn (under XenoCore › Loot › Presentation).

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Temporarily set Gold Chance to 1.0.
  2. Press Play in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and defeat your enemy.
  3. A gold chest appears. Open it: it holds one or two of your gold items. Take All puts them in the bag.
  4. Set Gold Chance back.

docs.title: Check the numbers without opening chests
docs.text: In the console (` key): XenoCore.Loot.Simulate Stonejaw 6 5000 rolls the table whose name contains Stonejaw 5,000 times as a level-6 enemy, and prints the tier odds and how often each item lands per chest, tier by tier. Not in Shipping builds.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: no chest at all

Drop Table is empty on the enemy (allowed, so not logged), or Chest Class is empty.

Symptom Fix The chest opens empty A tier has no pool, or no entry fits the enemy's level band. The Output Log says so under LogXenoDrop. Add a pool for every tier, or widen Min Level / Max Level. Some rows say (no room) The party already holds as many as the item's Max Carried allows. Take All takes what fits; the rest stays in the chest, which can be opened again once there is room. The player cannot pick single items Not a fault: the chest panel offers Take All or Take None. Choosing individual items is not built yet. See Troubleshooting: items and equipment. Gear I expected never drops Its Weight is 0, or the enemy's level is outside the entry's band. Check with XenoCore.Loot.Simulate.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Loot.
  • Place enemies: unique monsters with Always Gold Chest.
  • Add a weapon, Add armour.

docs.title: Give an enemy Arts
docs.text:
Designer · 40 min · No code

Result: your enemy uses its own Arts, with its own animations and cooldowns, and chains them on the party the way the minion does: a Break, then a Topple once its target is Broken.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Add an enemy type. You should have your own enemy Blueprint.
  • Create an attack art. Enemy Arts are ordinary Art definitions.
  • Reactions and statuses: Break, Topple, Daze.

docs.title: How enemies choose Arts
docs.text:
An enemy fights with the same AI as a companion. Every enemy runs the shared StateTree Characters/Enemies/Core/AI/ST_XenoCore_EnemyFreeroam through the AI controller Characters/Enemies/Core/BP_AIC_XenoCore_Enemy. While it has someone to fight, the tree's Fight state runs three tasks:

Task Job XenoCore Chase Aggro Target Moves into reach of whoever holds the most aggro on it XenoCore Fight Target Keeps its auto-attack swinging at that target XenoCore Use Best Art Every Decision Interval, scores the Arts on its Arts list and uses the best one that is ready

So an enemy's Arts are data on the enemy, not states in the tree. The tree never names an Art, and one tree serves an enemy with no Arts and an enemy with ten.

Scoring is exactly the companions': an Art must be off cooldown and its target in reach, then it scores its AI Priority plus any condition bonuses. See How a companion chooses an art.

The sample minion, Characters/Enemies/Minion/B_XenoCore_Minion_Melee, has two Arts in Characters/Enemies/Minion/Arts:

Art Does AI DA_XenoCore_Minion_Rend Break +2 priority while the target is not Broken DA_XenoCore_Minion_Sweep Topple Held until the target is Broken, then jumps the queue

So a minion that Breaks a party member follows up with a Topple: the same chain the party runs on it.

docs.title: 1. Make the Art
docs.text:
1. In Plugins › XenoCore Content › Characters › Enemies › Minion › Arts, right-click DA_XenoCore_Minion_Rend, choose Duplicate, move the copy into MyGame/Enemies/Golem and name it DA_MyGame_Golem_Crush. Or start blank, as in Create an attack art.
  2. Open it. Under Art, set Display Name, Power, Distance (its reach) and Cooldown Duration.
  3. Under Art › Effects, set the Effects entry. For a Break, use Battle/Reactions/GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Break.
  4. Create a gameplay tag for its cooldown in Project Settings › Gameplay Tags (click Add New Gameplay Tag), for example Cooldown.MyGame.Art.GolemCrush.
  5. Under Art, set Cooldown Tag to that tag.
  6. Under Art › Animation, set Montage to a montage on your enemy's skeleton, made for this Art.
  7. Click Save.

Fails silently: an Art that borrows the auto-attack's montage

Using an Art stops the enemy's auto-attack, and the auto-attack stops its swing by montage. If the Art plays the same montage asset as the auto-attack, it is stopped on its first frame: no hit, no damage, nothing logged. Duplicate the clip's montage under the Art's own name, as the minion's AM_XenoCore_Minion_Art_Rend and _Sweep are.

Fails silently: two Arts sharing a cooldown tag

A duplicated Art keeps the original's Cooldown Tag. Two Arts with one tag go on cooldown together: using either one makes both unavailable. Give every Art its own tag.

docs.title: 2. Teach it when to fire
docs.text:
In the same Art, under Art › Companion AI:

Setting Value Usable By AI On. Off, the enemy never picks it AI Priority Higher wins. 1 is the default AI Conditions Optional. For a Break opener, click +, set Check to Target lacks tag, Tag to Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Break, untick Required and set Bonus 2 AI Wait For Reaction On for a Topple or Daze Art: it is held until its reaction can land AI Chain Bonus Extra score while its reaction can land. Default 3

A Topple or Daze Art needs no conditions: the enemy reads the Art's own Effects and holds it until the target is Broken (or Toppled). See The reaction chain.

Art › Aggro › Threat sets how much aggro the Art builds when an enemy uses it. It matters only for party Arts; you can leave it.

docs.title: 3. Give it to the enemy
docs.text:
1. Open your enemy Blueprint (here B_MyGame_Golem) and click Class Defaults.
  2. Under XenoCore › Enemy › Arts, click + beside Arts and pick your Art.
  3. If your enemy was duplicated from the minion, remove the minion's Arts from the same list (the dropdown beside each entry › Delete).
  4. Click Compile, then Save.

Arts on this list are granted at level 1 when the enemy spawns. Enemy Arts do not level: the enemy's own Enemy Level already scales its damage through its stats.

Nothing goes in the ability set: the list is the whole job.

docs.title: 4. Pace it
docs.text:
In the same Class Defaults, expand AI Profile under XenoCore › Enemy › Arts:

Setting Default What it does Decision Interval 1.5 s Time between Art decisions. The auto-attack keeps swinging in between Decision Jitter 0.3 Random spread on each interval, so a group of enemies does not act in unison Post Art Cooldown 3 s After any Art, choose no other for this long, on top of the Art's own cooldown Reliability 100 % Chance to act at all on a decision. Lower makes a lazier enemy Seek Positional Bonus Off for enemies Leave off: enemies fight from where they stand

A boss with a long Post Art Cooldown and high-power Arts feels very different from a swarm enemy with short cooldowns and weak ones, with no AI changes at all.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Place your enemy in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play.
  2. Hit it once, then stand still and let it fight.
  3. It auto-attacks, then uses its Break: the struck character shows BREAK. If it has a Topple Art, it follows up within Break's window.
  4. Open the console (~) and type log LogXenoAI Verbose. Every decision the enemy makes prints as <enemy>: decision - <Art>=<score> ..., listing each usable Art and its score.
  5. To try the follow-up alone, Break yourself with XenoCore.Reaction 1; the enemy should use its Topple Art next.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Symptom Fix It only ever auto-attacks The Art is not on the enemy's Arts list, Usable By AI is off, its Distance is shorter than the distance the enemy fights from, or the Art's montage is the auto-attack's (see step 1). The decision log shows whether the Art is ever considered. It uses Break but never Topple Topple needs the target Broken when Topple lands. If Break's window is shorter than the time Topple takes to connect, the chain breaks. Use a faster Topple montage, or lengthen the Break on GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Break. That effect is shared, so check what else uses it first. It uses the same Art back to back The Art has no Cooldown Duration, or no Cooldown Tag. Raise Post Art Cooldown on the enemy too. Two Arts go on cooldown together They share a Cooldown Tag (see the warning in step 1).

More in Enemies and AI troubleshooting.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Enemies and AI, Companion AI and aggro.
  • Make an art inflict reactions for the party's side of the chain.
  • Tune companion AI: the same Companion AI settings, from the party's side.

docs.title: Set an enemy's statline
docs.text:
Designer · 30 min · No code

Result: your enemy type has its own HP, Strength, Ether, Agility and defences at every level, from your own curve table, so one number on a placed enemy (its level) sets all of them.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Add an enemy type.
  • Stats and damage and Curve tables.

docs.title: How an enemy gets its stats
docs.text:
1. The enemy Blueprint's Stats Effect (Class Defaults, under XenoCore › Enemy) names a gameplay effect.
  2. When the enemy spawns, that effect is applied at the enemy's Enemy Level.
  3. Each modifier in the effect reads one row of a curve table at that level, and overrides one attribute with the result.
  4. The enemy's level attribute itself is set straight from Enemy Level.

The sample is Battle/Attributes/GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_Minion_Melee, reading rows Minion_Melee.* from Battle/Attributes/CT_XenoCore_EnemyStats. Enemy stats rise in a straight line with level. The melee minion's HP and Strength follow an XC1 Colony 9 field enemy (HP 900 + 100 per level, Strength 69 + 10 per level); its other rows are placeholders to be tuned for your game.

The other minion types (Brute, Bulwark, Skirmisher) have their own effects that read the same Minion_Melee.* rows and multiply them: each modifier's coefficient Value is that type's multiplier (Strength: Melee 1.0, Brute 1.45, Bulwark 1.15, Skirmisher 0.9). That is how one table row serves several enemy types.

docs.title: What each stat means on an enemy
docs.text:
Enemy stats are read differently from party stats. This is intended.

Row Attribute On an enemy MaxHealth Health and Max Health HP. The effect sets both from this one row, so it spawns at full health. Strength Strength Damage of its physical attacks: Strength − the target's Physical Defence Ether Ether Damage of ether attacks. The shipped enemies have none. Agility Agility Hit and evade chance. Each point of difference from the party is 1%. PhysicalDefence Physical Defence A fraction, 0 to 0.9. 0.2 takes 20% off the party's physical hits. EtherDefence Ether Defence A fraction, like Physical Defence

On party members the two defences are flat points; on enemies they are fractions. Never copy a party defence value onto an enemy.

docs.title: 1. Make your curve table
docs.text:
The easiest route is a spreadsheet saved as CSV. The first column is the row name, and the header row holds the levels:

Name,1,99
Golem.MaxHealth,300,30000
Golem.Strength,40,900
Golem.Ether,0,0
Golem.Agility,8,120
Golem.PhysicalDefence,0.1,0.4
Golem.EtherDefence,0.05,0.3

Two columns are enough: with linear interpolation, level 50 falls on the straight line between them.

  1. Save it as CT_MyGame_EnemyStats.csv.
  2. Drag it into MyGame/Enemies in the Content Browser.
  3. In the import dialog, set Import As to CurveTable (it opens on DataTable) and Choose Curve Interpolation Type to Linear, then click Apply.
  4. Double-click the new asset and check the rows.

You can also duplicate Battle/Attributes/CT_XenoCore_EnemyStats and edit its cells in the curve table editor. It already has rows for Minion_Melee, Minion_Ranged, Minion_Siege and Minion_Super, plus Minion.ExperienceScale (see EXP for a kill).

Change the numbers by re-importing the CSV

Re-import an edited CSV over your own curve table (right-click › Reimport) rather than deleting and re-creating it. It stays the same asset, so every stats effect pointing at it keeps working. On a duplicate of a shipped table, use Reimport With New File instead: the shipped tables remember a source file that is not on your machine.

docs.title: 2. Point your stats effect at it
docs.text:
1. In Plugins › XenoCore Content › Battle › Attributes, right-click GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_Minion_Melee, choose Duplicate, move the copy into MyGame/Enemies and name it GE_MyGame_BaseStats_Golem.
  2. Open it and expand Modifiers.
  3. For every modifier, keep Modifier Op as Override.
  4. For every modifier, under Scalable Float Magnitude, set Curve Table to CT_MyGame_EnemyStats and Row Name to the matching Golem.* row.
  5. For every modifier, set the coefficient Value to 1.0, unless you want this type to scale another type's rows.
  6. Click Compile, then Save.

Fails silently: a coefficient you did not mean

The coefficient Value multiplies the curve row, and nothing on the table shows it. If you duplicated the Brute, Bulwark or Skirmisher effect, your copy carries that type's multiplier (for example Strength ×1.45). Set Value to 1.0 on every modifier unless you meant it.

Fails silently: Add instead of Override

Every modifier must be Override. With Add, applying the effect again stacks the numbers on top of the old ones.

docs.title: 3. Use it
docs.text:
1. Open your enemy Blueprint and click Class Defaults.
  2. Under XenoCore › Enemy, set Stats Effect to GE_MyGame_BaseStats_Golem.
  3. Click Compile, then Save.

docs.title: 4. EXP for a kill
docs.text:
Two settings on the enemy Blueprint's Class Defaults, under XenoCore › Enemy (both can also be changed on a placed enemy):

Setting What it does Experience Reward The type's base EXP. A Brute is worth more than a Grunt at the same level. Shipped minions pay 15 to 50. Experience Level Scale A curve row that multiplies Experience Reward at the enemy's level: pick a Curve Table and a Row Name. The minions use CT_XenoCore_EnemyStats › Minion.ExperienceScale. Empty = the same EXP at every level.

The party's level difference from the enemy then scales the result again.

docs.title: 5. Balance against the party
docs.text:
Three numbers decide how a fight feels:

  • Enemy Strength against party defence. Party defence is flat points summed from armour. If a full set of armour approaches an enemy's Strength, that enemy barely scratches the party.
  • Agility difference. Hit chance is 100% plus the attacker's Agility minus the defender's, one percent per point, never below 5% (Agility Hit Per Point and Hit Chance Floor on Battle/Attributes/BP_XenoCoreDamageExecution). Armour Weight comes off the wearer's Agility for this roll.
  • Level difference. Damage in both directions is scaled by the gap between the two levels, from Battle/Attributes/CT_XenoCore_DamageLevelDiff. A few levels matter a lot.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Place the enemy in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym at Enemy Level 1, and a second one at 99.
  2. Press Play. Open the console (~) and enter Log LogXenoDamage Verbose.
  3. Let each hit you. The Output Log's damage line shows stat= for each, matching your curve at those levels.
  4. Lock on (target mode): the level-99 enemy's health bar drains far slower.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: a row name typo

A modifier whose Row Name does not exist in the table evaluates to 0. The enemy spawns with 0 in that stat and no error shows in game. Open the effect and check each row is found.

Symptom Fix All stats are 0 and it dies in one hit Stats Effect is empty. The Output Log says the enemy "has no StatsEffect". One type's stats are a multiple of what the table says The modifier's coefficient Value is not 1.0 (see the warning in step 2). Stats stack up higher every time A modifier is Add instead of Override. Changing Enemy Level during play does nothing The level is read once, when the enemy spawns. A spawner sets it before then; a Blueprint can re-level a live enemy with Set Enemy Level (XenoCore › Enemy), which also heals it to full.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Stats and damage, Curve tables.
  • Add armour: the other half of the balance.
  • Set a character's statline for party members.

docs.title: Add a stat to equipment
docs.text:
Designer · 15 min · No code (a brand-new attribute needs C++)

Result: a weapon or armour piece that grants a stat it did not before, for example a ring of Agility on a pair of boots. The last section covers a stat that is not in the list yet: one row on an effect, plus C++ only if the attribute itself is new.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Add a weapon or Add armour.
  • Stats and damage: what each stat does in a fight.

docs.title: How item stats reach a character
docs.text:
1. An item definition lists its stats in Inventory Fragment Set Stats › Initial Item Stats: a XenoCore.Stat.* gameplay tag and a whole number per row.
  2. When the item enters the bag, Lyra copies those numbers onto the item.
  3. When the item is equipped, its ability set grants the gameplay ability Inventory/GA_XenoCore_EquipmentStats. That ability applies one shared gameplay effect, Inventory/GE_XenoCore_EquipmentStats. The effect's modifiers are the list of stats: each one names an attribute and a Set By Caller tag, and the ability fills every such tag from the item's number for it (0 if the item has none).
  4. When the item is unequipped, the ability ends and the effect is removed.

So an item never has its own effect asset, and the ability names no stat at all. The effect's modifier rows are the one list of what equipment can grant.

docs.title: The stats an item can carry
docs.text:
Tag Attribute it adds to Unit on the item Shown on the equipment comparison? XenoCore.Stat.WeaponAttackMin Weapon Attack Min points Yes XenoCore.Stat.WeaponAttackMax Weapon Attack Max points Yes XenoCore.Stat.PhysicalDefence Physical Defence points Yes XenoCore.Stat.EtherDefence Ether Defence points Yes XenoCore.Stat.CriticalRate Critical Rate whole percent (10 = 10%) Yes XenoCore.Stat.BlockRate Block Rate whole percent Yes XenoCore.Stat.Weight Weight points; more is worse Yes XenoCore.Stat.Strength Strength points No, character sheet only XenoCore.Stat.Ether Ether points No, character sheet only XenoCore.Stat.Agility Agility points No, character sheet only

Every equipped item adds to the character's base value. Critical and Block Rate are divided by 100 on the way in, because the attributes hold a 0 to 1 fraction.

docs.title: Steps (existing stat)
docs.text:
1. Open the item definition, for example your ID_MyGame_HideVest, and click Class Defaults.
  2. In Display › Fragments, expand the Inventory Fragment Set Stats entry. If the item has none, click + on Fragments and pick Inventory Fragment Set Stats for the new entry.
  3. Under Equipment › Initial Item Stats, click +. Set the key to XenoCore.Stat.Agility and the value to 5.
  4. Compile and Save.

That is all. No effect, ability or table needs to change.

Strength, Ether and Agility do not appear on the comparison block

The item comparison block shows seven rows: attack min and max, both defences, crit, block and weight. A Strength, Ether or Agility bonus still works and shows on the character sheet, but the comparison does not list it.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Kael's pawn, Characters/VRoid/Kael/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_L. In the Components panel select the equipment component, then add your item to XenoCore › Equipment › Starting Inventory. Compile and Save.
  2. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play. Open the main menu and look at Kael's stats.
  3. Equip the item on the equipment screen. Agility on the character sheet rises by 5. Unequip it: it falls back.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
The item's number shows but the character doesn't get it

The effect has no modifier row for that tag. The item card still shows the number. On equip, the Output Log warns (LogXenoCoreEquipmentStats): "carries XenoCore.Stat.… but GE_XenoCore_EquipmentStats has no SetByCaller modifier for it". Add the row (see the last section).

Fails silently: a stat tag outside XenoCore.Stat

The warning above only checks tags under XenoCore.Stat. A row with any other tag on Initial Item Stats is ignored with no message. Keep equipment stat tags under XenoCore.Stat.

Critical Rate of 10 did nothing, or 0.1 did nothing

Values are whole numbers. 10 is 10%. A fraction such as 0.1 cannot be entered, and 1 is 1%.

A screen of your own shows the old numbers

The stats are applied inside the equip call, so they are right the moment it returns. A widget that reads them only when it opens will not see a later change. Refresh it from the XenoCore.Equipment.Message.SlotChanged message. See Events.

docs.title: A stat that is not in the list
docs.text: A stat that is not in the table, such as Max HP on a piece of armour, needs one row on the effect. XenoCore.Stat.MaxHealth already exists as a tag.

docs.title: If the attribute already exists
docs.text:
1. Open Inventory/GE_XenoCore_EquipmentStats. Under Modifiers, add an entry. Copy the shape of an existing row:
    • Attribute: LyraHealthSet.MaxHealth
    • Modifier Op: Add
    • Magnitude Calculation Type: Set By Caller
    • Data Tag: XenoCore.Stat.MaxHealth
  2. On the item, add XenoCore.Stat.MaxHealth to Initial Item Stats with a value.
  3. If the value is authored as a whole percent (15 meaning 15 %), open Inventory/GA_XenoCore_EquipmentStats and add the tag to Percent Stat Tags (XenoCore › Equipment). Critical Rate and Block Rate are already treated as percent, so they need no entry.

No graph and no code. Equip the item and the attribute moves.

Key the modifier by tag, not by name

A Set By Caller modifier keyed by a Data Name instead of a Data Tag can never be filled from an item, and always reads 0. The ability logs a warning naming the effect and the attribute.

docs.title: If the attribute is new
docs.text:
Needs a programmer

Attribute sets are C++, so step 1 is a programmer's job. Steps 2 and 3 are editor work.

  1. The attribute (C++). Attribute sets are C++. Add it to UXenoCoreStatSet, or to your own set granted in your ability sets, and give the damage formula a use for it if it affects combat. Add a stat to the damage formula walks through both.
  2. The tag. Add XenoCore.Stat.CriticalDamage in your own tag source (Project Settings › Gameplay Tags), not in XenoCore's. Keep it under XenoCore.Stat so the missing-row warning covers it.
  3. Then the three steps above.

docs.title: Showing it on the menus
docs.text:
Needs a programmer

The equipment screen, item card and character sheet list their stat rows from a table written in C++, not from an asset. A stat without a row there applies but does not appear on those screens, and only a programmer can add the row.

For programmers

The table is UXenoCoreInventoryStatics::GetStatDefinitions() (label, order, lower-is-better, percent, which screens). Add a row with the tag and label, and choose whether it shows on the comparison block and the character sheet. It is built once per process, so this needs a full rebuild and a fresh editor.

GE_XenoCore_EquipmentStats is a shipped asset. Note the rows you add for when you take a template update.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Equipment, Items and inventory.
  • Gameplay tags reference.

docs.title: Footsteps by surface
docs.text:
Level designer · 30 min · No code

Result: characters walking on your new ground type, here snow, play a snow step sound and a puff of snow, and the old grass and stone surfaces keep theirs.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A step sound (Sound Wave, Sound Cue or MetaSound) and optionally a small Niagara effect for the new surface.
  • Build a world-partition map if you are making a new map.

docs.title: How a footstep picks its sound
docs.text:
Five links, each set in a different place. A footstep plays only when all five agree.

# Link Where Sample 1 The animation marks each step Anim notifies on the walk and run clips send AnimEffect.Footstep.Walk (and AnimEffect.Footstep.Land on landing) already set up 2 The ground says what it is A physical material with a Surface Type Environment/PM_XenoCore_Grass = Grass 3 The surface type has a name Project Settings › Physics › Physical Surface SurfaceType4 = Grass 4 The name becomes a gameplay tag Project Settings › LyraContextEffects › Surface Type To Context Map SurfaceType4 → SurfaceType.Grass 5 The tag picks the effect A context effects library row: effect tag + context tag → sounds and Niagara ContextEffects/CFX_XenoCore

The character's Lyra Context Effect component traces the ground under the foot, reads its physical material, turns the surface into a tag, and plays whatever the library lists for that step tag + that surface tag. The party pawns use CFX_XenoCore.

Ground with no physical material resolves to SurfaceType.Default, which plays the concrete step.

docs.title: 1. Add the surface type
docs.text:
1. Project Settings › Engine › Physics, section Physical Surface.
  2. Fill the next free slot (the shipped project uses 1 to 4; the XenoCore project setup (Install) adds slot 4, Grass, to a buyer's project) with the name Snow. Note the slot number, for example SurfaceType5.

docs.title: 2. Add the tag
docs.text:
1. Project Settings › Project › Gameplay Tags. Click Add New Gameplay Tag.
  2. Name it SurfaceType.Snow and set Source to DefaultGameplayTags.ini (the project's own tag list), not a plugin's tag file. Click Add New Tag.

Keep surface tags in the project's own tag list

The surface-to-tag map is read very early, when the game's settings load. A tag defined in a plugin's tag file may not exist yet at that moment, so the mapping silently points at nothing and the surface falls back to the default step.

docs.title: 3. Map the surface type to the tag
docs.text:
1. Project Settings › Game › LyraContextEffects.
  2. In Surface Type To Context Map, add SurfaceType5 (it shows as Snow) → SurfaceType.Snow.

docs.title: 4. Make the physical material
docs.text:
1. In the Content Browser, open MyGame/Environment, right-click, and choose Physics › Physical Material (class PhysicalMaterial). Name it PM_Snow.
  2. Set its Surface Type to Snow.

docs.title: 5. Put it on the ground
docs.text:
Choose the one that matches your ground:

  • A landscape: select the Landscape actor and set Default Phys Material to PM_Snow. That covers the whole landscape unless its material outputs a physical material per paint layer.
  • A material used by meshes: open the material and set Phys Material in its Details.
  • One static mesh: open it in the Static Mesh editor and set Collision › Simple Collision Physical Material.

Fails silently: a landscape with no physical material sounds like concrete

A landscape without Default Phys Material resolves every step to the default surface, which is mapped to the concrete sound. Nothing warns. Any new map's landscape needs this field.

docs.title: 6. Add the effect rows
docs.text:
Rather than editing XenoCore's library, give the characters a library of your own:

  1. In the Content Browser, open MyGame/Audio, right-click, and choose Data › Data Asset. Pick the class Lyra Context Effects Library and name it CFX_MyGame.

  2. Add two entries to Context Effects:

    Effect Tag Context Effects AnimEffect.Footstep.Walk SurfaceType.Snow your step sound, your Niagara puff AnimEffect.Footstep.Land SurfaceType.Snow your landing sound

  3. Add CFX_MyGame to the characters. Open Game/B_XenoCore_PlayableCharacter_Base and Characters/Party/B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base. On each, select the LyraContextEffect component and add CFX_MyGame to Default Context Effects Libraries. Compile and Save both.

Both pawn bases need it: the player's pawn and the party members are built on different bases. The VRoid party members (Characters/VRoid/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_Base and its children) are children of B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base, so they inherit it. (On the party base the LyraContextEffect component comes from its C++ parent, so it shows as inherited; the library list you set on the Blueprint is still what the members use.) Libraries add up rather than one winning: a step plays every matching row from every library in the list.

Or add rows to CFX_XenoCore

Adding the two rows to ContextEffects/CFX_XenoCore also works and touches one asset instead of three. It is a shipped asset, so a template update may overwrite it.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Place a flat mesh or paint an area that uses PM_Snow in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym or your map.
  2. Play and walk from the normal floor onto it. The step sound changes to yours, and your puff appears under each foot.
  3. Jump and land on it. The landing sound is yours.
  4. Walk back onto grass or stone. Their sounds are unchanged.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Still the concrete step

The ground has no physical material, or the physical material's Surface Type is still Default. Check the landscape's Default Phys Material first.

Silence on the new surface

The surface resolved to SurfaceType.Snow, but no library row matches. Check the row's Effect Tag is exactly AnimEffect.Footstep.Walk and its Context is exactly SurfaceType.Snow, and that CFX_MyGame is on the pawn you are playing.

Works for the leader, not for party members

The library is on only one of the two pawn bases.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Build a world-partition map
  • Animation: where the footstep notifies sit in the clips.

docs.title: Tune hit feedback
docs.text:
Designer · 20 min · No code

Result: a landed hit shakes the camera and rumbles the pad the way you want, for the player's hits and for hits the player takes, and a critical hit announces itself the way you want.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Your first art. You should know where the XenoCore content is.
  • A gameplay cue is a cosmetic (sound, particles, camera shake, rumble) played by a tag, here GameplayCue.XenoCore.*. The asset that plays it is a cue notify in a cue folder. See also gameplay effect.

docs.title: How hit feedback is put together
docs.text:
A landed hit produces feedback from three places. Knowing which one owns what saves a lot of guessing:

What you see or feel Where it comes from Asset Camera shake and pad rumble The hit cue GameplayCue.XenoCore.Hit GameplayCues/GCN_XenoCore_Hit The swing whoosh The swing cue GameplayCue.XenoCore.Swing GameplayCues/GCN_XenoCore_Swing Sparks, hit sound, the damage number over the enemy Lyra's damage cue, carried by the damage effect Battle/Attributes/GE_XenoCore_Damage → Lyra's GCNL_Character_DamageTaken Particles on the target for a critical, a block or an evade Cues the damage calculation fires on the character that was hit GameplayCues/GCN_XenoCore_Hit_Critical, GCN_XenoCore_Hit_Blocked, GCN_XenoCore_Hit_Evaded CRITICAL HIT! over the target, the gold critical number and the critical hit sound The damage calculation, plus Lyra's damage cue Project Settings › Game › XenoCore Content › Critical Hit

The auto-attack and every damaging Art fire the hit cue themselves, after the hit has landed. A missed swing fires nothing. Heals never fire the hit cue.

Lyra's damage cue draws the number and plays the hit-confirm and kill sounds for every party member's hits, not only the leader's: an AI-controlled ally's hit on an enemy sounds and reads the same as yours. An enemy's hit on a party member plays the damage-taken sound instead, and draws a number over whoever was hit. For an AI-controlled ally that number and sound come from XenoCore, not Lyra: the sound is Ally Damage Taken Sound (and Ally Damage Taken Critical Sound) under Project Settings › Game › XenoCore Content › Battle. Clear it and allies take hits silently.

On a critical hit the same cue switches to Lyra's critical style: the number draws gold and the hit-confirm sound is the heavier critical one. At the same moment CRITICAL HIT! pops over the target, arriving larger and snapping down to its resting size.

The cue runs on whichever side has a local player controller. When the player hits an enemy, the player's camera shakes. When an enemy hits the player, the player's camera shakes too. When an enemy hits an AI-controlled party member, nothing shakes, because nobody is looking through that character.

GCN_XenoCore_Hit is a Burst cue: it plays once and is never spawned into the world. Its settings live in one struct, Burst Effects.

docs.title: 1. Make your own camera shake
docs.text:
1. Create a folder MyGame/Feedback under Content.
  2. Find Lyra's Feedback/CameraShakes/CS_Character_DamageTaken (in the project's own Content folder, not under Plugins). This is the shake the hit cue uses today.
  3. Duplicate it into MyGame/Feedback and name it CS_MyGame_Hit.
  4. Open CS_MyGame_Hit and adjust it. It is a legacy (oscillation) camera shake: under Oscillation, start with Oscillation Duration and Rot Oscillation (each axis's Amplitude and Frequency). A short, sharp shake reads as impact, a long one reads as an explosion.
  5. Save.

docs.title: 2. Make your own rumble (optional)
docs.text:
1. Duplicate Lyra's Feedback/Haptics/FFE_Character_Damage (project Content folder) into MyGame/Feedback. Name it FFE_MyGame_Hit.
  2. Open it and edit the curves. Keep it short: a rumble that outlasts the hit feels like lag.
  3. Save.

docs.title: 3. Point the hit cue at your assets
docs.text:
The cue's tag is fixed in C++, so there is exactly one hit cue in the project. Change what it plays, not which cue plays.

  1. Open GameplayCues/GCN_XenoCore_Hit and click Class Defaults.
  2. Expand Burst Effects.
  3. Under Burst Camera Shake, set Camera Shake to CS_MyGame_Hit. Use Shake Scale to make the whole shake stronger or weaker without editing the shake asset.
  4. Under Burst Force Feedback, set Force Feedback Effect to FFE_MyGame_Hit.
  5. Compile and Save.

This is an edit to a shipped asset

It is one reference change. Write it down, because a template update that replaces GCN_XenoCore_Hit will point it back at Lyra's shake.

Fails silently: a second notify with the same tag

Do not duplicate GCN_XenoCore_Hit and leave both with the tag GameplayCue.XenoCore.Hit. Only one of them will play, and which one is not something you choose.

docs.title: 4. Change the swing whoosh (optional)
docs.text:
1. Open GameplayCues/GCN_XenoCore_Swing, Class Defaults, Burst Effects.
  2. Under Burst Sounds, replace the sound (Lyra's Lyra_MeleeWhoosh_01) with your own.
  3. Compile and Save.

docs.title: 5. Tune the critical hit (optional)
docs.text:
1. Open Edit › Project Settings › Game › XenoCore Content and find the Critical Hit category.

  2. Set what you want:

    Setting Default What it does Critical Hit Text CRITICAL HIT! The line raised over the target. Keep the word HIT in it: a bare "CRITICAL" reads as a low-health warning. Critical Hit Scale 1.15 Resting size of the line. BREAK, TOPPLE and DAZE are 1. Critical Hit Punch 1.7 The line arrives this many times its resting size and snaps down to it in about 0.14 s. 1 = no punch. Critical Hit Stop Seconds 0 (off) A brief freeze of the whole world on a critical hit, in real seconds. XC1 has none. Try 0.06. Critical Hit Stop Dilation 0.05 World speed during that freeze. Only used when Critical Hit Stop Seconds is above 0.

  3. The settings save to the project's config as you change them. The line's colour is Critical Colour on BP_XenoCoreDamageExecution (see Stats and damage).

The hit-stop never fights other slow motion. It starts only when the world is running at normal speed, so it is skipped during an Art's slow motion, and it hands time back only if nothing else has changed the world speed in the meantime.

Anything else can raise a line with the same punch: the Notify node has a Punch input (1 = none).

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Plug in a gamepad, open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play.
  2. Use the pad, not the keyboard, for the whole test.
  3. Attack a minion. Each landed hit shakes the camera and rumbles the pad. A miss does neither.
  4. Let a minion hit you. The camera shakes on its hits too.
  5. Watch a critical hit (your Critical Rate comes from equipment, so equip something with Critical Rate, or wait for one). CRITICAL HIT! slams in over the target, the number beside it is gold and the hit sound is heavier than a normal hit's.
  6. Watch an ally's hits on an enemy. Each one draws a number and plays the hit-confirm sound.

To test rumble while using a keyboard, open the console (`) and enter LyraPC.ShouldAlwaysPlayForceFeedback 1. Set it back to 0 when you are done.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
No rumble at all

Rumble plays only while the last input you used was the gamepad, and only while Vibration is on in the game's settings (Gamepad › Hardware). Touching the mouse or keyboard switches it off until you press a pad button again. Nothing is logged. Use LyraPC.ShouldAlwaysPlayForceFeedback 1 to rule this out.

Fails silently: a cue added to an effect never shakes the camera

If you give an Art's own effect a Gameplay Cue in its Gameplay Cues list, the cue's sparks and sounds play but its camera shake and rumble never do. Cues fired by a gameplay effect carry no player controller, so there is nothing to shake. This is true in stock Lyra as well. Put shake and rumble only in GCN_XenoCore_Hit, which is fired directly with the controller filled in.

Fails silently: a new cue that never plays

A cue notify is only found if it sits under a registered cue folder. The registered folders are XenoCore/Content/GameplayCues (registered by the XenoCore Game Feature) and the project's Content/GameplayCues and Content/GameplayCueNotifies (from Config/DefaultGame.ini). Put your own cues under Content/GameplayCues/MyGame/. A notify anywhere else loads fine, shows no error, and never plays.

Numbers or hit sounds on hit are gone

Those come from XenoCore's own damage cue, GameplayCues/GCNL_XenoCore_DamageTaken, fired by the cue tag GameplayCue.XenoCore.DamageTaken on GE_XenoCore_Damage. A damage effect that fires Lyra's GameplayCue.Character.DamageTaken instead shows sparks but no number and no hit sound, and nothing is logged. Duplicate GE_XenoCore_Damage for new damage effects. See Troubleshooting: combat and arts.

Fails silently: CRITICAL HIT! shows but the number is the normal colour

The battle line and the gold number both come from XenoCore. If you see the line and a normal number, the damage effect is firing Lyra's cue rather than GameplayCue.XenoCore.DamageTaken. See Troubleshooting: combat and arts.

The game seems to stutter on critical hits

That is the hit-stop. Set Critical Hit Stop Seconds back to 0.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Combat loop: when hits land and who fires what.
  • Stats and damage: what decides a hit or a miss.
  • Tune the auto-attack.

docs.title: Add an input action with a prompt
docs.text:
Designer · 40 min · No code

Result: a new button, Whistle, that runs a gameplay ability once per press, plus a glyph on the HUD that shows the right key for keyboard or gamepad.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Input and camera: how a key reaches an ability.
  • Controls: which keys are already taken.

docs.title: How a key reaches an ability
docs.text:
XenoCore uses Lyra's input chain. Five pieces, each in its own asset:

# Piece Sample Decides 1 Input Action Input/InputActions/IA_XenoCore_QuestTracker That the action exists, and when it fires (its triggers) 2 Mapping context Input/Mappings/IMC_XenoCore Which keys and pad buttons fire it 3 Input tag (gameplay tag) InputTag.XenoCore.QuestTracker The name that links the action to an ability 4 Input config Input/InputData_XenoCore Action ↔ input tag 5 Ability set entry Game/AbilitySet_XenoCore_Input Which ability to run for that input tag

The on-screen glyph is a sixth, separate piece: a row in a CommonUI action table (UserInterface/Foundation/DT_XenoCore_Actions) that says which key to draw. It does not read the mapping context. You keep the two in agreement yourself.

IMC_XenoCore is added by the XenoCore plugin at priority 2, above Lyra's IMC_Default at 1. Both are added by the plugin's own Game Feature Data. Don't lower it: other contexts that share keys would start winning. When two contexts map the same key, the higher priority wins only if its action consumes the key; otherwise both fire. Its contexts only apply in Game input mode, so a menu switches them all off.

docs.title: 1. Create the tag
docs.text:
1. Open Project Settings › Project › Gameplay Tags and click Add New Gameplay Tag.
  2. Name it InputTag.MyGame.Whistle. Set Source to your own tag source (for example MyGameTags.ini; create it with Add New Tag Source if you have none), not XenoCore's.
  3. Click Add New Tag.

docs.title: 2. Create the Input Action
docs.text:
1. In the Content Browser, open MyGame/Input, right-click, and choose Input › Input Action. Name it IA_MyGame_Whistle.
  2. Open it. Set Value Type to Digital (bool).
  3. Under Triggers, click + and choose Pressed. Save.

Fails silently: a one-shot action with no trigger fires every frame

With no trigger, a held key fires the action on every frame. An ability that ends straight away then starts again on the next frame, so one tap runs it five or six times. Every one-shot action needs the Pressed trigger. Abilities that stay active for a montage are protected, which is why some Lyra actions get away without one.

docs.title: 3. Map the keys
docs.text:
1. Open Input/Mappings/IMC_XenoCore. Click + beside Mappings and pick IA_MyGame_Whistle.
  2. Add a keyboard key (for example G) and a gamepad button. Check Controls first; pick keys nothing else uses.
  3. Save. This edits a shipped asset; note it for template updates.

A shared key is decided by priority, silently

If Lyra's IMC_Default or another context maps the same key, only the higher-priority context gets it. The other action simply stops working. Nothing warns.

docs.title: 4. Link the action to the tag
docs.text:
Open Input/InputData_XenoCore. Under Ability Input Actions, add an entry: Input Action IA_MyGame_Whistle, Input Tag InputTag.MyGame.Whistle. Save.

Every party pawn data points at this one input config, so this covers all characters.

docs.title: 5. Create the ability
docs.text:
1. In MyGame/Abilities, right-click and choose Blueprint Class. Under All Classes, pick LyraGameplayAbility. Name it GA_MyGame_Whistle.
  2. Open it and click Class Defaults:
    • Lyra › Ability Activation › Activation Policy: On Input Triggered.
    • Tags › AssetTags (Default AbilityTags): add a tag such as Ability.MyGame.Whistle. Tag relationship rows (for example "no whistling during dialogue") can only reach an ability that has an ability tag.
  3. In the graph: Event ActivateAbility → your effect (play a sound, print a string to start) → End Ability.

End the ability

An ability that never calls End Ability stays active, and the next press is ignored.

docs.title: 6. Grant it with the input tag
docs.text:
Every playable body, the player's and each party member's, gets its input abilities from one shared set, Game/AbilitySet_XenoCore_Input. Its pawn data lists it beside that body's own set.

  1. Open Game/AbilitySet_XenoCore_Input. Under Granted Gameplay Abilities, add an entry: Ability GA_MyGame_Whistle, Input Tag InputTag.MyGame.Whistle.
  2. Save.

That is the only grant. Do not also add it to AbilitySet_XenoCore_Hero or AbilitySet_XenoCore_PartyMember: those hold each body's non-input abilities, and a second grant gives that body the ability twice.

Leader-only actions

Interact and its X action are granted only to whoever is leader, from AbilitySet_XenoCore_Interact (the party's Leader Only Ability Set). Put an action there instead if a companion's body must not have it at all.

AbilitySet_XenoCore_Input is a shipped asset; note your row for template updates. To keep it in your own content, make your own ability set and add it to the Ability Sets of each pawn data you use: Characters/VRoid/PawnData_XenoCore_Party_VRoid (shared by all seven VRoid members), Game/PawnData_XenoCore_Player and each Characters/Party/PawnData_XenoCore_Party_*.

docs.title: 7. Add the glyph row
docs.text:
1. Open UserInterface/Foundation/DT_XenoCore_Actions and add a row named Whistle.
  2. Display Name: Whistle.
  3. Keyboard Input Type Info › Key: the same keyboard key as step 3.
  4. Default Gamepad Input Type Info › Key: the same pad button as step 3.
  5. Save.

The glyph can lie

The row's keys are typed in, not read from IMC_XenoCore. If you change the mapping later and forget the row, the HUD shows a key that does nothing. Change both together.

Keyboard key icons

Lyra's keyboard data has icons only for mouse buttons. XenoCore adds a keycap icon for 81 keyboard keys (letters, digits, F-keys, arrows, modifiers, punctuation) in UserInterface/Input/CommonInput_XenoCore_Keyboard, named by Project Settings › Game › XenoCore UI › HUD › Keyboard Key Icons. A key outside that set draws its prompt text with no key, and nothing is logged. To add one, add a texture and a row to that data asset.

docs.title: 8. Put the glyph on the HUD
docs.text:
1. In MyGame/UI, right-click and choose User Interface › Widget Blueprint (parent User Widget). Name it W_MyGame_WhistlePrompt.
  2. In the Palette, find Lyra's InputActionWidget (it lives in the project's Content/UI/Foundation/Widgets) and drag it into a Horizontal Box, with a Text label beside it.
  3. In its Details, set Input Actions to one entry: table DT_XenoCore_Actions, row Whistle.
  4. Compile and Save.
  5. Add it to the HUD through one of the HUD's slots, for example HUD.Slot.XenoCore.BottomCenter, with an Add Widgets action. See Add a HUD element. This leaves W_XenoCore_HUDLayout untouched.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play.
  2. The HUD shows the keyboard glyph. Press G: the ability runs once, even if you hold it.
  3. Pick up a gamepad and touch a stick. The glyph switches to the pad button. Press it: it runs once.
  4. Open the Party screen, switch leader, close the menu, and press it again. It still works.
  5. Open the menu and press it: nothing happens while the menu is up.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Nothing happens

Check the chain in order: the tag in the input config and the ability set entry are the same tag; Activation Policy is On Input Triggered; no higher-priority context takes the key.

It fires several times per press

The action has no Pressed trigger.

It works until I switch leader

The ability was granted in a set only some bodies receive (AbilitySet_XenoCore_Hero, or one party member's pawn data). Grant it in AbilitySet_XenoCore_Input.

It fires twice per press

The ability is granted twice to the same body: in AbilitySet_XenoCore_Input and in AbilitySet_XenoCore_Hero or AbilitySet_XenoCore_PartyMember. Keep only the AbilitySet_XenoCore_Input row.

The glyph shows the wrong key, or nothing on keyboard

The row's keys don't match the mapping, or the row has no keyboard key.

docs.title: Menu prompts
docs.text: To show an action in a menu's footer instead, use a CommonUI button: set its Triggering Input Action to your table row, and tick Display In Action Bar on the button. Without that tick, the key works but no glyph is drawn. A button that must not take space can sit in a 0×0 Size Box with Render Opacity 0; don't collapse it, because a collapsed button still draws its glyph but refuses the press.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Input and camera
  • Add a menu screen
  • UI and input troubleshooting

docs.title: Set and style item rarity
docs.text:
Designer · 10 min · No code · Last tested: 2026-10-04

Result: an item draws its name in its rarity's colour, with one to three diamonds, in every menu that shows it. You can also change what each rarity looks like, or add a new rarity.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Items and inventory: an item is one Blueprint with fragments.
  • Loot: chest tiers. A chest tier is not the same thing as an item's rarity.

docs.title: How rarity works
docs.text:
XenoCore uses Xenoblade 3's three rarities: Common, Rare and Legendary.

  • Rarity belongs to the item. Every copy of an item has the same rarity, and nothing is rolled when an item drops. To have a Common and a Rare version of the same thing, make two items.
  • Every shipped item states its rarity. If an item's rarity is left empty, it falls back to the lowest-ranked row of the table below (Common), but don't rely on that: set Rarity on every item you add, Common included.
  • What each rarity looks like is one row of the data table UserInterface/Items/DT_XenoCore_ItemRarities: its name colour, diamond count, chest beam colour and optional pickup sound.
  • Rarity never changes a price. Prices still come from Sell Value, as in Xenoblade 3.
Rarity Name colour Diamonds Lowest chest Common white 1 Wooden Rare gold 2 Silver Legendary purple 3 Gold

docs.title: Make an item rare
docs.text:
1. Open the item's Blueprint, for example Inventory/Armour/ID_XenoCore_BattleArmour, and click Class Defaults.
  2. Under Display › Fragments, expand the XenoCore Fragment Item Category entry.
  3. Set XenoCore › Item › Rarity to XenoCore.Item.Rarity.Rare or XenoCore.Item.Rarity.Legendary.
  4. Compile and Save.

docs.title: The samples
docs.text:
New Game starts with one of each tier in the bag, so every look is on screen at once. They come from Kael's (Characters/VRoid/Kael/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_L) Starting Inventory:

Item Rarity Tab Vanguard Plate Legendary Torso. It is also in every minion family's Gold chest pool, for enemies of level 10 and up Veteran Gauntlets Rare Arms Prism Chain Legendary Collectables Silver Moon Flower Rare Collectables Fine Scrap Plating Rare Materials

They are sample content. Take them out of that list before you ship: open Kael's pawn, select its equipment component, and remove the rows from XenoCore › Equipment › Starting Inventory.

docs.title: Make a rarer copy of an item
docs.text:
1. Right-click the item and choose Duplicate. Never create an item definition from scratch: a blank one cannot be equipped.
  2. Rename the copy, change its Display Name and its numbers, and set its Rarity.
  3. Point quests, shops and drop tables at whichever copy they should hand out.

docs.title: Change how a rarity looks
docs.text:
Open DT_XenoCore_ItemRarities and edit a row:

Column What it does Rarity The tag this row describes. Rows are found by this tag, never by row name. Display Name The word shown in details panes ("Rare · Heavy") and used by the Rarity sort. Rank Higher is rarer. It orders the Rarity sort and decides which row is the default. Name Colour / Tint Name The colour of item names. Turn Tint Name off to leave names in each screen's own colour. On a Lyra menu button the colour is written into the label's font material for its normal, hovered and pressed states, so a focused row keeps its rarity colour. Name Outline / Name Outline Colour / Name Outline Size A thin dark outline round the tinted name: 1 unit, black at 85%. On by default. It frames every edge of every letter, so gold and purple stay readable on the pale menu rows. Size 2 starts to fill in small letters. Name Shadow / Name Shadow Colour / Name Shadow Offset A soft drop shadow under the outline: 1 unit, black at 50%. On by default. Keep it subtle: a strong 2-unit shadow makes small text look smeared. Pips / Pip Colour / Pip Texture The diamond count (0 for none), their colour, and their art. The shipped art is T_XenoCore_RarityPip, a white diamond with a dark rim, tinted by Pip Colour. Don't leave Pip Texture empty: the fallback, a turned square, reads as broken triangles at the menu's scale. Lowest Chest Tier Drop tables warn when an item sits in a lower chest's pool than this. Chest Beam Colour The beam of a chest whose tier stands for this rarity. By default a gold chest glows purple, which says Legendary. Pickup Sound Optional. Plays when an item of this rarity is picked up, or offered by a chest.

docs.title: Add a rarity
docs.text:
1. Project Settings › Project › Gameplay Tags: add the gameplay tag XenoCore.Item.Rarity.Mythic, or whatever name you want, in your own tag source.
  2. Add a row to DT_XenoCore_ItemRarities with that tag and a Rank above Legendary.
  3. Set items to the new tag.

docs.title: Turn rarity off
docs.text:
• Project Settings › Game › XenoCore UI › Items › Item Rarity Table: clear it. Names then draw in each screen's own colour, with no diamonds and no rarity word.
  • To keep the data but hide the look, turn off Tint Name and set Pips to 0 on every row.

docs.title: Change the diamond size
docs.text:
• Project Settings › Game › XenoCore UI › Items › Rarity Pip Size (12) sizes the diamonds on every screen.
  • A widget's own Pip Size pin on Apply Item Rarity, or the loot popup's Row Pip Size, overrides it when above 0. Leave them at 0 so one setting keeps every screen matching.

Set a name's font before Apply Item Rarity

The outline is part of the font. A Set Font after Apply Item Rarity removes the outline again. Three screens had this bug: the loot popup, the quest offer and the reward banner.

docs.title: Make a chest guarantee a rare item
docs.text:
Xenoblade 1's silver and gold chests always hold one rare material. Open your drop table (for example Inventory/Loot/DA_XenoCore_Drops_Grunt), expand XenoCore › Loot › Pools, open the Silver or Gold entry, and set its Guarantee One Of Rarity to XenoCore.Item.Rarity.Rare.

When the roll finds nothing that rare, its last pick is redrawn from that pool's qualifying entries, so the item count stays inside Min Items to Max Items.

docs.title: Where rarity shows
docs.text:
Every details pane has a Rarity row (label and tier name, in the tier's colour):

  • the Items menu, on every tab;
  • the equipment screen's item pane and its swap list;
  • the shop and trade screens, under Type.
For programmers: the widgets behind the Rarity row

On the Items menu and the shop and trade screens it's a DetailsRarityHB row: a DetailsRarityLabel and a DetailsRarityValue. Shop and trade fill it from C++, and the Items menu fills it with Apply Item Instance Rarity Label. On the equipment screen the stat block adds it as its own first row.

  • Items menu: row name and diamonds, the details name, the labelled Rarity row, and a Rarity mode in its Y sort. The Type line is plain text (for example "Heavy"), with no rarity in it.
  • Equipment screen: the loadout buttons, the item pane's Rarity row (the stat block's first row; the pane's header shows the name in the rarity colour with no rarity word in front), and the swap list header.
  • Shop and trade:
  • Row names and diamonds. An unaffordable row keeps its colour, dimmed.
  • The details name and the Rarity row. The Type row stays plain; for a weapon it names the weapon's type ("Greatsword") rather than "Equipment".
  • The buy/sell confirm and the trade header.
  • A Rarity option in the sort cycle.
  • Loot panel: names and diamonds, rarest first. A "(no room)" line stays red.
  • Pickup badge, quest offer rewards and quest reward banner.
  • Chest beams, coloured by the rarity each chest tier stands for. Turn this off with Use Rarity Beam Colour on the chest Blueprint.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play. New Game's bag holds the samples above.
  2. Open the main menu, then Items. On the Materials tab, Fine Scrap Plating's name is gold with two diamonds; on Collectables, Prism Chain is purple with three.
  3. Select a row: the details pane shows a Rarity row in the same colour.
  4. Press the sort button (Y on a pad) until the prompt reads Sort: Rarity: the rarest items rise to the top.
  5. If you made your own item rare, add it to Kael's Starting Inventory and check it the same way.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Symptom Fix A Rare or Legendary item is drawn white, with one diamond Its Rarity is empty, which means Common. Set it on the item's XenoCore Fragment Item Category. Every item is drawn plain, with no diamonds XenoCore UI › Items › Item Rarity Table is cleared. Point it back at UserInterface/Items/DT_XenoCore_ItemRarities. Your new rarity draws like Common The table has no row for its tag. The Output Log warns once: Rarity '...' has no row in .... Add the row. A name in your own widget lost its dark outline A Set Font runs after Apply Item Rarity. Set the font first. Diamonds look like triangles The row's Pip Texture is empty. Set it to UserInterface/Items/T_XenoCore_RarityPip.

More checks: Items and equipment troubleshooting.

docs.title: Give a quest to defeat enemies, talk to someone, or go somewhere
docs.text:
Designer · 30 min · No code · Last tested: 2026-10-08

Result: quests whose steps are "defeat five golems", "speak to the ferryman" and "reach the old gate", with no code. The HUD tracker counts each one, and the minimap marks the next talk or place for the quest you are tracking.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • Offer a collection quest. This recipe uses the same quest asset and NPC set-up.

docs.title: What objectives are supported
docs.text:
An objective's Kind offers four choices. All four work:
