ButtonStyle_XenoCore_TitleEntry The title screen's entries W_XenoCore_TabButton Every tab strip (Items, Equipment, Shop, Trade) MI_XenoCore_FontColor_TabButton The tab labels' text colour, as a material MI_XenoCore_FontColor_MenuButton, MI_XenoCore_FontColor_TitleEntry Text colour materials for menu buttons and title entries W_XenoCore_MenuButton The larger menu button, used by the shop and trade screens TextStyle_XenoCore_TitleEntry, TextStyle_XenoCore_TitleEntrySelected Title screen text

docs.title: The main menu and its entries
docs.text:
The in-game main menu (UserInterface/W_XenoCore_MenuShell, built on XenoCoreMainMenuBase) and the party tactics panel share one house palette: a navy panel with a blue rim, Orbitron text, steel-grey secondary text and a blue accent. Its pieces are drawn in C++, so their look is a set of class defaults rather than a style asset:

  • The menu entries are XenoCoreMenuEntryButton, the default Project Settings › Game › XenoCore UI › Menu › Menu Button Class. Make a Blueprint child of it, set Label Font, Text Colour, Dim Colour, Highlight Colour and Accent Colour under XenoCore › Look, and point Menu Button Class at your child. Any CommonButtonBase child works there, including W_XenoCore_MenuButton.

  • The party cards are XenoCorePartyCardBase. Make a Blueprint child, change its XenoCore › Look settings, and set it as Card Class in W_XenoCore_MenuShell's Class Defaults (XenoCore › Menu).

  • The main menu's own panel is not a class default. Open W_XenoCore_MenuShell in the Designer: the entry panel is the Border EntriesPanel (change its Brush › Tint and the outline colour), and the darkening over the world is the Border ScreenDim (Brush Color).

docs.title: 1. Back up what you are about to change
docs.text: Style assets are shared, so this recipe edits shipped XenoCore assets in place. Write down each asset you change (or commit before and after), so you can reapply your changes after a template update.

docs.title: 2. Change the row colours
docs.text:
1. Open UserInterface/Foundation/ButtonStyle_XenoCore_Menu. It is a small Blueprint: open Class Defaults.
  2. Under Normal, Selected and Disabled, each state has a brush: Normal Base, Normal Hovered, Normal Pressed, Selected Base, Selected Hovered, Selected Pressed, and Disabled. Each brush is a rounded box. (They are greyed out while Single Material is ticked; leave it off.)
  3. Change each brush's Tint to your colours. Keep Normal Base close to your panel colour so rows read as a list, and make Selected Base clearly different; that is where the cursor is.
  4. Compile and Save.

Every row that uses this style changes at once: the Items list, Equipment rows, Arts rows, the Party screen's member buttons and the trade rows.

docs.title: 3. Change the tab strip
docs.text:
1. Open UserInterface/Foundation/MI_XenoCore_FontColor_TabButton and change its colour parameters for the unselected and selected states. Save.
  2. Open UserInterface/Foundation/W_XenoCore_TabButton if you want to change its size, padding or background. Keep Min Width at 0.

Don't swap in Lyra's tab button

Lyra's W_LyraButtonTab has a minimum width of 320. A twelve-tab strip of them is 3840 pixels wide and pushes headers, tables and titles off screen, which looks like three unrelated bugs. Keep using W_XenoCore_TabButton.

docs.title: 4. Change the font
docs.text:
1. Import your font file (.ttf or .otf) into MyGame/UI/Fonts. Unreal creates a Font Face and asks whether to create a Font asset from it too: click Yes. The Font is named after the face with _Font on the end.
  2. Open each style that names a font and set its Font Family to your new Font:
    • TextStyle_XenoCore_TitleEntry, TextStyle_XenoCore_TitleEntrySelected
    • W_XenoCore_TabButton and W_XenoCore_MenuButton, which set their font directly
  3. Text blocks placed directly in screens also carry a font. In a screen, select a text block and set Font › Font Family in Details.
  4. Two screens are drawn in C++ and take their font from a Font Family class default instead: the party tactics panel (XenoCoreTacticsPanelBase, Tactics › Text) and the Change Time screen (XenoCoreChangeTimeScreen, Change Time › Text). Set it on a Blueprint child; the tactics panel's child goes in Tactics Panel Class (see Party tactics).

The shipped menus use Lyra's Orbitron font from Content/UI/Foundation/Fonts. Search the Content Browser for widgets referencing it (right-click the font, Reference Viewer) to find every place to change.

Fails silently: a text block with a Style ignores its Font

A Common Text Block that has a Style set draws with the style's font and colour, and ignores the Font and Color and Opacity you type in its own Details. Nothing marks this. If a label refuses to change, clear its Style (set it to None) or change the style asset instead.

docs.title: 5. Replace a whole screen
docs.text:
Restyling changes how shared pieces look. To swap an entire screen or HUD widget for your own, use the two XenoCore pages in Edit › Project Settings › Game. Each setting starts at the shipped asset.

XenoCore UI: the widgets XenoCore opens from code, plus the in-game menu.

Group Settings Must derive from Screens Save Screen, Quest Log Screen, Quest Offer Screen, Shop Screen, Trade Screen, Arts Screen, Skills Screen, Gem Popup The matching XenoCore base, for example XenoCoreShopScreenBase HUD Interact Prompt, Loot Popup, Battle Notify, Dialogue Box XenoCoreInteractPromptBase, XenoCoreLootPopupBase, XenoCoreBattleNotifyBase; the dialogue box should derive from XenoCoreDialogueBoxBase HUD Damage Taken Numbers, Damage Dealt Numbers, Heal Numbers Niagara systems. Each number's colour is set inside its system Items Item Rarity Table, Rarity Pip Size, the Gem Socket icons See Set and style item rarity Tutorials Tutorial Table, Tutorial Card See Add a tutorial card Menu Menu Entries, Additional Menu Entry Sets, Menu Button Class, Menu Button Padding, Menu Group Gap See Add a menu screen

XenoCore Content: non-UI assets C++ spawns or applies.

Group Setting What it is Dialogue Dialogue Anchor The actor that carries the speech box. Must derive from XenoCoreDialogueAnchor; its Blueprint holds the box height Feedback Beam Material The light shaft over a healed or buffed character Debug Reaction Break Effect, Reaction Topple Effect, Reaction Daze Effect What the XenoCore.Reaction debug command applies

To replace one:

  1. Duplicate the shipped widget into Content/MyGame/UI (for example W_XenoCore_ShopScreen to W_MyGame_ShopScreen) and change it. Keep its parent class.
  2. Set the matching setting to your copy. Settings are saved to Config/DefaultGame.ini.
  3. Add your folder to Project Settings › Packaging › Additional Asset Directories to Cook (an advanced setting; it is DirectoriesToAlwaysCook in DefaultGame.ini). See below.

If a setting is cleared, fails to load, or names a widget with the wrong parent, XenoCore logs a warning (XenoCore UI setting '...' did not load) and uses the shipped asset, so a mistake costs your change, never the feature.

Fails silently in a packaged build: your replacement is not cooked

A setting holds a soft reference, and the cooker does not follow soft references in settings. The shipped widgets are cooked only because Config/DefaultGame.ini always cooks /XenoCore/UserInterface and /XenoCore/Characters/NPC, or because other cooked assets reference them. A replacement stored anywhere else works in the editor and is missing from a packaged build, which then quietly falls back to the shipped screen. Add your folder (for example /Game/MyGame/UI) to Additional Asset Directories to Cook (DirectoriesToAlwaysCook), or make sure something that is cooked references it.

docs.title: 6. Author your own styles, not references to Lyra's
docs.text:
When you create new widgets, create your own style assets in MyGame/UI/Styles: right-click, Blueprint Class, and pick CommonButtonStyle or CommonTextStyle as the parent. Point your widgets at those.

Referencing Lyra's style assets from /Game/UI/... works today, but it ties your look to host content you don't own, and any change there changes you.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play.
  2. Open the menu (pad Y, keyboard I) and open the Items screen. Rows and tabs use your colours; move the cursor and the selected state uses yours too.
  3. Open Equipment and the Party screen; their rows changed as well.
  4. Talk to the gym's shopkeeper and check the shop's buttons.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
One label won't take the new font or colour

It is a Common Text Block with a Style set. Clear the style or edit that style.

The main menu's entries didn't change

They are XenoCoreMenuEntryButton, drawn in C++, not a style asset. Set XenoCore UI › Menu Button Class to your own child of it. See The main menu and its entries.

My replacement screen shows in the editor but the packaged game uses the old one

Your folder is not cooked. See step 5.

Tab strip runs off the screen

A tab list is using a tab button with a large Min Width. Use W_XenoCore_TabButton.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Add a menu screen
  • UI shell and HUD
  • UI and input troubleshooting

docs.title: Make a system save
docs.text:
Designer · 30 min · No code

Result: your own state is written into XenoCore's save file and comes back on Continue or Load, with old save files still loading. The worked example is a lever that stays pulled; the same steps save a bestiary, a crafting bench or anything else, without editing XenoCore.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Save and front end: slots, the autosave, what XenoCore itself saves.
  • Add an interactable object builds the lever used below. Any actor works.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
XenoCore saves its own systems (party, levels, bag, quests, chests) itself. Anything else takes part as a save participant: an actor, component or object that stores its own record in the file under its own key. XenoCore never needs to know what the record holds.

Piece What it is SaveGame flag on a variable Marks what to save. Only flagged variables are written XenoCore Save Participant component (UXenoCoreSaveParticipantComponent) Add it to an actor and that actor's flagged variables are saved. No graph needed XenoCore Save Participant interface (IXenoCoreSaveParticipant) Optional. Gives an object a key, a data version and two hooks Register Save Participant / Unregister Save Participant On the save subsystem, for anything the component does not cover

What is found without any registration: the player controller, the player state, the game state, and every component on those three, if it implements the interface. So a party-wide system on a controller component only needs the interface.

Order. On load, participants are restored after all of XenoCore's own systems, so a participant that reads the party or the bag while restoring sees the loaded state.

Records that nobody claims are kept. If a participant is missing this session (a streamed-out actor, a system removed for one build), its record is carried into the next save instead of being lost.

docs.title: 1. Flag what to save
docs.text:
1. Open your Blueprint (here BP_MyGame_Lever). Select the variable that holds the state, such as a boolean bPulled.
  2. In its Details, open the advanced section under Variable and tick SaveGame.
  3. Repeat for every variable that must survive a load.

Fails silently: a struct saves empty

Only flagged properties are written, and that includes the fields inside a struct variable. Flag a struct variable but not the struct's own fields, and it saves as all defaults. For a Blueprint struct, open the struct asset, expand each field with its arrow and tick Save Game there too.

docs.title: 2. Add the component
docs.text:
1. In Components, add XenoCore Save Participant.
  2. Leave Save Key empty for an actor placed in a level. Its key is then made from the map and the actor's name, which is unique.
  3. For an actor spawned at runtime, set Save Key to a unique name, such as MyGame.Forge.

That is all the lever needs. The component registers the actor at Begin Play and unregisters it at End Play. Unregistering records the actor's current state first, so an actor that streams out and back in, or a level left and re-entered, gets its state back.

Fails silently: two actors with one key

A spawned actor with an empty Save Key is keyed by its class, so a second copy has the same key. Only the first one registered is saved; the other logs an error (XenoCoreSave: ... registered with save key '...', already used by ... and, at save time, duplicate save participant key). Give every copy of a spawned actor its own key.

A key is forever

Records are found by key. Renaming a key, or renaming a placed actor whose key is derived from its name, leaves every existing save holding a record nobody claims, so the actor loads with its defaults. Settle keys and placed-actor names before release.

docs.title: 3. React to a load (optional)
docs.text:
The component restores the variables and nothing else. If the lever must also look pulled, use the interface's hooks:

  1. Class Settings › Interfaces › Add: XenoCore Save Participant.
  2. Implement On Save Data Restored. It runs after this actor's record has been applied, and is given Saved Version. Here, snap the lever mesh to the pulled pose if bPulled is true, and call Set Interact Enabled with the opposite.
  3. Implement On Pre Save Capture only if some state lives outside flagged variables: copy it into them there. It runs just before this actor is written.

On Save Data Restored runs only when there was a record

An actor the save has never heard of keeps its defaults and hears nothing. To react to every load, bind the save subsystem's On Save Loaded instead; it fires once the whole load is applied, participants included, and passes the slot index.

docs.title: 4. Version your data (optional)
docs.text:
Implement Get Save Data Version and return 1. When you later change what you save (rename a variable, change what a number means), return 2, and in On Save Data Restored convert data that arrived with Saved Version 1.

Adding a new flagged variable does not need a new version: an older record simply has no value for it, and the variable keeps its default.

Your version is your own. XenoCore's save file has its own version, which you never change. A save made with a XenoCore release older than save participants loads as "no participant has saved anything yet".

docs.title: 5. Other kinds of participant
docs.text:
You have Do this A component on the player controller, player state or game state (a party-wide system) Implement the interface on the component. It is found automatically; no save participant component, no registration An actor that is not placed and not spawned by you, or a plain object Call Register Save Participant on the save subsystem with it (and a Save Key if it can exist twice), and Unregister Save Participant from its End Play A record you want gone (a quest line reset) Forget Save Record with its key; Has Save Record checks for one

A registered object does not have to implement the interface; its flagged variables are saved either way. The interface only adds the key, the version and the hooks.

If a record already exists when something registers (it was loaded, or it streamed out earlier), it is applied at once, unless a load is still being applied, in which case it waits and is applied with everything else.

For programmers: C++ participants

A C++ class implementing IXenoCoreSaveParticipant may override CaptureSaveData(FArchive&) and RestoreSaveData(FArchive&, int32 SavedVersion) to write whatever it likes instead of its UPROPERTY(SaveGame) fields. The archive stores object pointers as paths. The defaults (GetSaveParticipantKey, GetSaveDataVersion, OnPreSaveCapture, OnSaveDataRestored) are BlueprintNativeEvents: override the _Implementation versions. All of it is exported, so this works from your own module; see Add a mechanic by subclassing. XenoCore's own file version is EXenoCoreSaveVersion (currently Gems = 5; participant records arrived in ParticipantData = 3).

docs.title: Rules that keep old saves loading
docs.text:
These are the rules XenoCore's own saved data follows. Follow them in your records too.

  • Keep state on something that outlives the world for anything party-wide: a controller component, not a pawn. A benched party member has no pawn.
  • Store asset references as soft references or paths, never as object pointers to live actors. An asset that has since been deleted is then skipped instead of breaking the load.
  • Store enums and table rows by name, never by number, if the list may grow.
  • Recompute what you can. Save only what nothing else remembers.
  • Guard starting grants. If your system gives something at the start of a game (a first entry, a free item), check Was World Loaded From Save on the save subsystem first, or every load gives it again.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Place the lever in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym, press Play, and pull it.
  2. Open the console and enter XenoSave 1. The Output Log reports XenoCoreSave: captured 1 save participant(s).
  3. XenoSaveDump prints each slot; slot 1 now lists 1 participant records.
  4. Stop, press Play again, and enter XenoLoad 1. After the map reloads the lever is still pulled and offers no prompt. The log line restored ... 1/1 participant record(s) confirms it.
  5. Load a save made before you added the component: it loads, and the lever starts unpulled.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Loaded, but the value is back to its default

The variable is not flagged SaveGame, or it is a struct whose fields are not flagged. Or the actor was renamed since the save was written, which changed its key.

Only one of several spawned copies keeps its state

They share a key. Set Save Key per copy. The Output Log names the clash.

The value loads, but the actor does not look right

The component restores variables only. Apply them in On Save Data Restored.

docs.title: Add Y-to-sort to an item list
docs.text:
Designer · 10 min · No code (a small Blueprint edit) · Last tested: 2026-10-04

Result: pressing Y on your screen cycles how its item list is ordered, and the action bar shows Sort: Rarity (or whichever mode is current). The cursor stays on the same item when the order changes.

The Items menu (UserInterface/W_XenoCore_ItemMenu) and the equipment swap list (UserInterface/W_XenoCore_ItemSwapList) already have this. Use this recipe for a new screen of your own, or to change which modes those two offer. Open either of them to see a finished example.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • A menu screen of your own with a List View showing items. See Add a menu screen.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
UserInterface/Foundation/W_XenoCore_ItemSortControl is a widget you place inside your screen. It draws nothing on its own. While your screen is open it puts the Y prompt on the action bar, and when Y is pressed it re-sorts the list you name.

Mode Order Default The order the bag holds them in, oldest first. Lists drew this before sorting existed Most Recent Newest first Name A to Z Rarity Rarest first, then A to Z Value Highest sell value first Stat The slot's own number, highest first: max Attack for a weapon, Physical Def for armour. Other items sort by value

Ties always keep bag order, so equal items never swap places when you re-sort.

docs.title: 1. Place the control
docs.text:
1. Open your screen's Widget Blueprint and switch to the Designer tab.
  2. In the Palette, search for W XenoCore Item Sort Control and drag it into the screen's root panel. Its size and position don't matter.
  3. In the Hierarchy, rename it SortControl.

docs.title: 2. Set it up
docs.text:
Select SortControl. In Details › XenoCore › Sort:

Setting Value Target List Name The name of your List View in the Hierarchy, for example ItemList (the default). It must match exactly Modes Which modes Y cycles through, in order. The first is the order the screen opens in. Two or more entries Sort Action Already set to DT_XenoCore_Actions › MerchantSort (Y), the same button as the shop's sort. Leave it Prompt Format Optional. Empty gives Sort: {0}, where {0} is the mode's name

docs.title: 3. Make the list open sorted
docs.text:
1. Switch to the Graph tab.
  2. Find each Set List Items node that takes its items from Get Items For Slot or Get Items For Category. There may be more than one; check every function and event.
  3. Drag SortControl from Variables into the graph and, from it, place a Sort Items node.
  4. Put it on the wire: Get Items For … → Sort Items → Set List Items.
  5. Compile and Save.

Without this step Y still works, but the list opens in bag order each time.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play and open your screen. The action bar shows Sort: Default (or your first mode).
  2. Press Y (pad) or the keyboard key shown in the prompt. The prompt names the next mode and the list re-orders. The highlighted item stays highlighted.
  3. Press Y through every mode. On Rarity, Legendary items are at the top.
  4. Close the screen and reopen it. It opens in your first mode again.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: no prompt on the action bar

Sort Action is empty, or Modes has fewer than two entries. Nothing is logged. Check both on SortControl.

Fails silently: the prompt changes but the list doesn't

Target List Name doesn't match your List View's name in the Hierarchy. Copy the name across exactly.

The list reopens in an unsorted order. One Set List Items still reads straight from Get Items For … without going through Sort Items. Find it and route it through.

docs.text:

  • Add a menu screen.

docs.title: Choose the starting party
docs.text:
Designer · 15 min · No code

Result: a new game starts with the characters you choose, the ones you choose fighting and the rest in reserve, with the leader you choose. A further character joins later when the player walks into a trigger.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Your first change
  • Any member you want to add must already exist: Add a party member.
  • Glossary: Party, roster, Active member, reserve member, Leader, Member definition.

docs.title: Where the party is set
docs.text:
Everything is on one asset, Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party, the party component the XenoCore Experience adds to the player controller. Open it and click Class Defaults; the settings are under XenoCore › Party.

Setting What it does Starting Roster Every character the party has at the start, in order Max Active Members How many fight at once, the leader included. The rest of the roster starts in reserve. Leader Slot Which active slot the player controls. 0 is the first. Default Controller Class The AI used for any member whose definition names none Leader Only Ability Set Abilities only the body the player drives gets (the sample: interaction) Spawn Inner Radius, Spawn Arc Degrees and the other XenoCore › Party › Spawn settings How companions are scattered behind the leader at spawn; see Where they appear

docs.title: 1. Pick who is in the party
docs.text:
1. In Starting Roster, arrange the entries so the characters you want fighting come first. The party fills active slots in this order and puts everyone after that in reserve.
  2. Remove any character you want to recruit later instead of having from the start.

docs.title: 2. Pick how many fight
docs.text:
1. Set Max Active Members. The C++ default is 3; the sample sets 7, so every character who joins fights and nobody waits in reserve. The sample starts with two (Kael and Mira) and recruits the other five on Gaur Plain. Lower it to bench the end of the roster.
  2. The HUD has seven party plates, so any value from 1 to 7 draws a plate for every active member.

Reserve members earn nothing in the sample

Benched characters earn a share of every experience award, set by Reserve Experience Rate on the progression component Game/BP_XenoCore_Progression. The C++ default is XC1's 90%; the sample sets 0, and recruits catch up by joining at the party's level instead. See Tune levelling.

docs.title: 3. Pick the leader
docs.text:
1. Set Leader Slot to the active slot you want to control. With the roster order above, 0 is the first character in the list.
  2. Compile and Save.

The player can change the active members out of combat from the Party screen. The leader can also change in combat: tap a trigger to switch to the next or previous member, or pick a new leader on the Party screen.

docs.title: 4. Recruit someone later
docs.text:
The sample recruits its five other characters by talking to them; see Recruit a party member by talking to them. For a character who joins when the player walks into a spot instead:

  1. Open a map and, from the Place Actors panel, drag XenoCore Party Recruit Trigger into the level where the character should join.
  2. In its Details panel, under XenoCore › Party:
    • Member To Recruit: the character's member definition.
    • Activate Immediately: on to put them straight into the fight if there is a free active slot; off to send them to reserve.
    • Join At Party Level: on (the default) to bring them up to the party's level when they join, so a mid-story recruit is not left behind.
    • Recruit On Overlap: on to recruit when the player walks into the box. Turn it off if a cutscene or dialogue will call Recruit on the trigger instead.
    • Destroy After Recruiting: on for a one-time story beat.
  3. Scale the Recruit Volume box to cover the spot.

The trigger's On Recruited event fires after the character has joined, for a banner or a line of dialogue. From any Blueprint you can also call Add To Roster on the party component (Get Party Component returns it).

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play.
  2. The HUD shows one plate per active member, and you control the character in Leader Slot.
  3. Open the menu (pad Y, keyboard I) and go to the Party screen. The reserve lists everyone else from Starting Roster.
  4. Walk into your recruit trigger. The character joins, into the fight if there was room.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: the change does nothing when I press Continue

A save stores the roster, the active party, the party size and the leader. Continue loads that and ignores Starting Roster. Test with Play in the editor, or New Game.

Fails silently: Starting Roster is ignored on New Game

Project Settings › XenoCore Content › Startup › Starting Roster Override, when it is not empty, replaces Starting Roster for a New Game. It is empty in the shipped plugin; clear it if your project set it.

The Party screen refuses to swap anyone

Bench swaps, reorders and removals are refused while the party is in combat, and a message says so. Picking a new leader from the active members still works. Disengage first. Recruiting through a trigger or Add To Roster is never refused.

A character in the roster never appears

Their member definition has no Member Class, or its pawn has no Combatant Pawn Data. Open the definition; the Content Browser marks it with an error.

With an empty Starting Roster, the player spawns alone

That is supported: the player gets the Experience's default pawn and no companions. Add at least one member to get a party.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:

  • Add a party member
  • Tune levelling

docs.title: Make a status effect
docs.text:
Designer · 30 min · No code

Result: a new debuff, Frostbite, that lowers Agility and deals damage every second. It announces itself over whoever it lands on, shows its icon on their HUD plate, and any Art can apply it with its own duration and strength.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Make an attack Art: how an Art's Effects list works.
  • Glossary: Status effect, Gameplay effect.

docs.title: How a status works
docs.text:
A status is a gameplay effect whose class is XenoCoreStatusEffect. The gameplay-effect part does the work: modifiers, duration, periodic ticks and the tags it grants. The XenoCoreStatusEffect part adds only what the UI needs:

Field (Status category) What it does Display Name The popup over the character, and the line in the Arts menu Abbreviation Two or three letters drawn on the HUD icon when there is no Icon Colour The popup's colour and the icon's fill Icon Optional artwork for the HUD icon Is Buff Buffs sort after debuffs on the plate

There is no list to register it in: any XenoCoreStatusEffect that lands is announced and drawn.

The numbers belong to the Art, not the status. Every shipped status reads its duration, and where it has one its strength, from SetByCaller values the Art sends:

SetByCaller tag Sent from the Art's entry Used by XenoCore.Status.Duration Duration Every shipped status XenoCore.Status.Magnitude Magnitude Bleed, Poison, Blaze, Chill (damage per second), Regenerate (healing per second), and every stat up, stat down, Slow and Haste (strength as a percentage)

The shipped statuses are in Battle/Status:

Kind Assets What they do Stat down GE_XenoCore_Status_StrengthDown, EtherDown, AgilityDown, PhysicalDefDown, EtherDefDown Stat lowered by Magnitude percent (15 gives ×0.85) Stat up ..._StrengthUp, EtherUp, AgilityUp, PhysicalDefUp, EtherDefUp, MaxHealthUp Stat raised by Magnitude percent (15 gives ×1.15) Speed ..._Slow, ..._Haste Auto-attack speed lowered / raised by Magnitude percent Damage over time ..._Bleed, ..._Poison, ..._Blaze, ..._Chill Magnitude damage every second Healing over time ..._Regenerate Magnitude healing every second Bind ..._Bind Cannot move

Their icons are in UserInterface/Status/Icons.

The percentage statuses (stat up, stat down, Slow, Haste) compute their modifier with XenoCoreStatusPercentCalc: the percentage the Art or skill sends, or its Default Percent (30, so ×1.3 / ×0.7) when the entry sends no Magnitude. A skill whose Ability applies one sends the skill's Value as the percentage (Skills).

docs.title: 1. Duplicate the closest status
docs.text:
1. Duplicate Battle/Status/GE_XenoCore_Status_Poison into MyGame/Status as GE_Status_Frostbite. Poison already has a periodic damage modifier reading XenoCore.Status.Magnitude.
  2. Open it.

docs.title: 2. Present it
docs.text:
Under Status:

  1. Display Name: Frostbite. Abbreviation: FRB.
  2. Colour: an icy blue. Is Buff: off.
  3. Icon: optional. Import a square texture with alpha, Texture Group UI, or leave it empty and the icon is drawn as the colour with the abbreviation on it.

docs.title: 3. Give it its own tag
docs.text:
1. Find the component that grants tags (Grant Tags to Target Actor, in the effect's Components list). Replace Status.XenoCore.Debuff.Poison with a new tag, Status.MyGame.Debuff.Frostbite. Add the tag first in Project Settings › Project › GameplayTags (Add New Gameplay Tag), or pick it from the tag picker's Add New row.
  2. Keep your tag under a Debuff or Buff parent. Anything that asks "does this character have any debuff?" can then match the parent.

Fails silently: two statuses sharing a tag

A status that keeps Poison's tag is Poison to anything that checks tags. Always give a new status its own tag.

docs.title: 4. Add the Agility modifier
docs.text:
1. In Modifiers, keep the periodic damage modifier.
  2. Add one: Attribute XenoCoreStatSet.Agility, Modifier Op Multiply Additive, Magnitude a scalable float of -0.3 (Agility ×0.7).
  3. Leave the Duration Policy as Has Duration with its magnitude set to Set By Caller, tag XenoCore.Status.Duration, exactly as Poison had it.
  4. Check Duration › Period › Period is 1.0: one second between damage ticks. Leave Stacking as Poison had it (Stack Per Target, Stack Limit Count 1), so a second hit refreshes the status rather than adding a stack.
  5. Save.

Fails silently: copying Agility Down's modifier

GE_XenoCore_Status_AgilityDown's modifier reads its strength from XenoCore.Status.Magnitude through XenoCoreStatusPercentCalc. Frostbite already uses Magnitude for its damage per tick, so a copied modifier would take the same number: a Magnitude of 25 would also lower Agility by 25 %. One status has one Magnitude; keep the second modifier a fixed scalable float.

docs.title: 5. Apply it from an Art
docs.text:
On any Art definition, under Art › Effects, add:

Field Value Effect GE_Status_Frostbite Chance 1.0 Duration 12 Magnitude 25 (damage per tick) Condition Always Recipient Each target

Both Duration and Magnitude are scalable floats, so they can grow with the Art's level (Make an attack Art, step 6).

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym with the Art slotted.
  2. Use it on a minion. "Frostbite" pops over it in your colour, and it takes damage every second for twelve seconds.
  3. Have a minion apply it to the party instead (give the status to a minion Art's effect list), or use an Art with Recipient User on yourself: your HUD plate shows the icon.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Save error: 'takes its duration from the art, and Duration is 0'

The Art's entry has Duration 0. The status would last no time at all. The Art definition reports this as an error; set a duration.

Save error: 'takes its strength from the art, and Magnitude is 0'

The status reads XenoCore.Status.Magnitude and the entry sends nothing, so it would tick for 0. Set Magnitude.

Fails silently: no popup and no icon

The effect's class is a plain gameplay effect, not XenoCoreStatusEffect. Always duplicate a shipped status rather than creating a new gameplay effect.

The Agility change is permanent

The effect's Duration Policy was changed to Instant. An instant effect changes the base value for good. Keep Has Duration.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Reactions and statuses
  • Chain Arts into Break, Topple and Daze
  • Gameplay tags reference

docs.title: Add a mechanic by subclassing
docs.text:
Programmer · 1–2 h · C++

This page is for programmers

It needs Visual Studio and C++. If you are a designer wanting a variation on an existing mechanic, you almost never need it: right-click the XenoCore Blueprint closest to what you want (for example Battle/Arts/GA_XenoCore_TalentArt_Base) and choose Create Child Blueprint Class, then change its Class Defaults. The recipes show this for Arts, enemies, NPCs and screens. If a recipe cannot do what you need without C++, hand this page to a programmer.

Result: your own C++ module, in its own plugin, that builds on XenoCore's classes (here, a new kind of Art ability) without a single edit to XenoCore's source. A template update then replaces XenoCore and leaves your code alone.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Architecture overview: what lives in the plugin and why.
  • A working C++ toolchain: Requirements.
  • C++ classes lists every class with its header.

docs.title: The rule
docs.text: Don't edit XenoCore's source, and don't edit Lyra's. Add behaviour by subclassing, in a module you own. If a base class is missing a hook you need, that is a gap in the template: report it (Reporting bugs) rather than patching around it, and keep any unavoidable patch small and written down.

docs.title: Two ways to subclass
docs.text:
Blueprint child C++ child Needs Nothing Your own C++ module Good for Content-shaped variation: different numbers, a different montage, a few extra graph nodes New logic: overriding virtual functions, per-frame work, new properties with validation Works on Any class marked Blueprintable or Abstract-but-Blueprintable Every public XenoCore class (they are all exported)

Try a Blueprint child first. Most extension in the samples is Blueprint children of C++ bases: GA_XenoCore_BackSlash is a Blueprint child of the C++ Art ability.

docs.title: Which bases are built for extension
docs.text:
Base For C++ child? UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_Art Arts. Data-driven by UXenoCoreArtDefinition; override ActivateAbility, CanActivateAbility, EndAbility, ApplyCooldown. BeginStrike and ApplyArtEffect are callable helpers. Yes UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_TalentArt, UXenoCoreTalentArtDefinition Talent Arts Yes UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_AutoAttack, UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_TargetMode Auto-attack, target mode Yes UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_Reaction and its children …_HitReact (flinch), …_DefenceReact (guard, evade, recoil) and …_KnockdownReact (…_ToppleReact, …_DazeReact) Reactions. Derive from the child closest to yours: Reaction itself holds only the shared machinery (direction, hold, follow-up), each child adds its own trigger and refusals Yes UXenoCoreStatusEffect Status effects (a Gameplay Effect with display data) Yes UXenoCoreArtDefinition, the item fragments (UXenoCoreFragment_*) New data on arts and items Yes UXenoCoreHudPlateBase Any HUD element that fades in and out; the player plate, party plates, target plate, quest tracker and banners derive from it Yes UXenoCoreMerchantScreenBase A buy/sell/exchange screen; shop and trade derive from it Yes UXenoCoreBootScreenBase (…LogoBootScreenBase, …MovieBootScreenBase, …ShaderBootScreenBase) Cards in the boot sequence; override ShouldShow, OnBootScreenShown, OnBootScreenLeaving Yes UXenoCoreConfirmPopupBase, UXenoCoreSaveScreenBase, UXenoCoreTitleScreenBase, quest log/offer/reward bases, UXenoCoreLootPopupBase, UXenoCoreStatBlockBase, UXenoCoreTutorialCardBase Menu screens and popups Yes UXenoCoreMainMenuBase, UXenoCorePartyCardBase, UXenoCoreMenuEntryButton The main menu, its party cards and its entries Yes AXenoCoreCombatantCharacter, AXenoCorePartyCharacter, AXenoCoreEnemyCharacter Characters. Enemies do not derive from the combatant base; see Enemies and AI Yes AXenoCoreInteractableActor Doors, levers, signs: anything the player presses A on. See Add an interactable object Yes UXenoCoreEquipmentComponent, UXenoCoreAnimInstance Equipment, animation Blueprints Yes UXenoCoreStatSet, UXenoCoreDamageExecution, UXenoCoreMMC_EffectLevel Stats and the damage formula. The execution has no per-term hooks; see Add a stat to the damage formula Yes UXenoCorePartyMemberDefinition, AXenoCorePartyMemberController, AXenoCoreEnemyController Party data, party AI, enemy AI Yes AXenoCoreEnemySpawner A squad of field enemies; see Place enemies Yes UXenoCoreMenuAction, UXenoCoreMenuCondition What a menu entry does, and when it shows. Normally Blueprint; see Add a menu screen Yes IXenoCoreSaveParticipant, UXenoCoreSaveParticipantComponent Your own saved data. See Make a system save Yes The StateTree tasks and conditions (FXenoCore*Task, FXenoCore*Condition) Enemy and party AI building blocks Yes, and callable

Every public class and struct in XenoCoreRuntime is exported with XENOCORERUNTIME_API, so a C++ class in your own module can derive from it and call its functions. The only exceptions are the module object and the two console-command cheat extensions (UXenoCoreSystemCheats, UXenoCoreProgressionCheats), which are not meant to be extended. The three interfaces (IXenoCoreAnimProfileProvider, IXenoCoreMapMarkerSource, IXenoCoreMenuButton) are exported too; only their U halves are minimally exported, which is all implementing one needs.

Link error: \"unresolved external symbol\" on a Lyra class

Some of Lyra's own classes are not exported from LyraGame (for example ULyraAnimInstance, ULyraButtonBase, ULyraGameplayAbility_FromEquipment, ULyraGameplayAbility_Interact). A C++ class of yours that derives from one compiles and then fails to link. XenoCore's bases never require one: each derives only from exported Lyra classes. Derive a Blueprint from the Lyra class instead.

docs.title: 1. Create your plugin
docs.text:
1. Edit › Plugins › Add, choose Game Feature (with C++). Name it MyGameCore. It is created under Plugins/GameFeatures/MyGameCore.

  2. Open MyGameCore.uplugin and add XenoCore to its Plugins list:

    "Plugins": [
    { "Name": "XenoCore", "Enabled": true }
]

  3. Open Source/MyGameCoreRuntime/MyGameCoreRuntime.Build.cs and add the modules you build on:

    PublicDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new string[]
{
    "Core", "CoreUObject", "Engine",
    "XenoCoreRuntime", "LyraGame",
    "GameplayAbilities", "GameplayTags", "GameplayTasks",
});

    Add CommonUI, UMG, SlateCore if you subclass a screen or HUD base.

  4. Never add XenoCore's editor module (XenoCoreEditor) to a runtime module's dependencies.

docs.title: 2. Switch your feature on
docs.text: A Game Feature does nothing until an experience enables it. Open Experiences/B_XenoCore_Experience and add MyGameCore to Game Features to Enable, beside XenoCore. Note this change for template updates, or use a copy of the experience as your own.

docs.title: 3. Write the subclass
docs.text:
An art that can only be used while the user is below half health:

// MyGameArt_Desperation.h
#pragma once
#include "Arts/XenoCoreGameplayAbility_Art.h"
#include "MyGameArt_Desperation.generated.h"

UCLASS(Blueprintable)
class MYGAMECORERUNTIME_API UMyGameArt_Desperation : public UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_Art
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    UPROPERTY(EditDefaultsOnly, Category = "MyGame|Art", meta = (ClampMin = "0", ClampMax = "1"))
    float MaxHealthFraction = 0.5f;

protected:
    virtual bool CanActivateAbility(const FGameplayAbilitySpecHandle Handle,
        const FGameplayAbilityActorInfo* ActorInfo, const FGameplayTagContainer* SourceTags,
        const FGameplayTagContainer* TargetTags, FGameplayTagContainer* OptionalRelevantTags) const override;
};

In the .cpp, call Super::CanActivateAbility(...) first and return false if it does; only then add your test. Build with the editor closed.

Then, in the editor, create a Blueprint child of UMyGameArt_Desperation if you want one, and set it as the Ability Class on an Art definition. See Create an attack art.

docs.title: 4. Follow the base-class rules
docs.text:
Always call Super

The Art base does range checks, cooldowns, movement locking and montage bookkeeping in its overrides. Skipping Super skips all of it, often with no visible error until an art never ends or never goes on cooldown.

Fails silently: a Blueprint array override replaces the C++ defaults

The bases fill tag lists in their constructors. For example, the Art base adds Gameplay.MovementStopped and Status.XenoCore.ArtExecuting to Activation Owned Tags, which is what roots the character and keeps flinches from interrupting. If a Blueprint child edits that list at all, its list replaces the whole C++ one. Nothing warns. In a Blueprint child, leave these lists alone or re-add every entry the base had. In a C++ child, append in your constructor rather than assigning.

Don't change behaviour for other children

If you add a subclass between a XenoCore base and existing children, defer to Super for anything that has not opted in to your new behaviour.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Build (editor closed). The Output Log on startup shows no errors from MyGameCore.
  2. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym, Play, and give a character the new art.
  3. At full health the art is refused; below half health it fires, goes on cooldown and ends normally.
  4. Replace the XenoCore plugin folder with a fresh copy of the same version. Your plugin still builds and the art still works.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Unresolved external symbol at link

The base is one of Lyra's unexported classes (see the warning above), or your Build.cs is missing a module the base's header needs, such as GameplayAbilities or StateTreeModule.

My class doesn't appear in the class picker

Your Game Feature isn't enabled by the experience, or the class isn't Blueprintable.

The art freezes the character

An override returned without calling Super::EndAbility, so the movement-stop tag was never removed.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• C++ classes
  • Make a system save
  • Add a stat to the damage formula

docs.title: Make a support Art
docs.text:
Designer · 30 min · No code

Result: two support Arts. Mend heals one ally the player picks from the party HUD. Rally raises the whole party's Strength and gives them Regenerate, with no healing of its own.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Your first art and Make an attack Art.
  • Glossary: Status effect.

docs.title: How a support Art differs from an attack
docs.text:
The same Art definition does both. Three fields change what it is:

Field Attack Heal one ally Party buff Effect Type Damage Heal No damage or healing Target Type Enemy One ally Whole party Effects Reactions, debuffs on each target Optional The buffs, Recipient set to suit

With Effect Type set to Heal, the shared Art ability applies the heal effect Battle/Arts/GE_XenoCore_Heal instead of the damage effect, plays the heal cue, and shows the amount restored as a number over the character, including 0 on a character already at full health. You add no cue and no effect yourself. One ally makes confirming the Art open an ally selector on the party HUD and a small white ring under the highlighted member; the Art is only spent when you confirm a character, and cancelling costs nothing.

Support Arts are for battle

Like every Art, a heal is used from the battle palette. An ally-targeted Art never checks the distance to an enemy, but out of battle there is no palette: the party recovers HP on its own instead (Tune revive and defeat).

Never make a heal by duplicating an attack

An attack's montage carries hit notifies and a weapon trail, and an attack's ability applies the damage effect. Duplicate either into a heal and the heal fires melee hits, trails a blade, and damages. Start a support Art blank, use DA_XenoCore_LightHeal, the shipped heal, as the reference for its settings, and give it a gesture montage with no notifies.

docs.title: 1. Mend: heal one ally
docs.text:
1. In MyGame/Arts, right-click › Data › Data Asset, pick XenoCoreArtDefinition and name it DA_Mend. Create it blank rather than duplicating DA_XenoCore_LightHeal: a copy carries whatever the original holds.
  2. Open it. Set Display Name Mend, Description Restores HP to one party member., and its own Cooldown Tag Cooldown.MyGame.Art.Mend.
  3. Leave Ability Class empty. (Light Heal points at its own older ability Blueprint, GA_XenoCore_LightHeal, which is not needed: the shared Art ability picks the heal effect for any Art with Effect Type Heal.)
  4. Set the three fields: Effect Type Heal, Target Type One ally, Attribute Ether. Category: Heal.
  5. Power is the amount healed, before the art-level curve. Try 300.
  6. Cooldown Duration: 10.
  7. Set Montage to Characters/Player/Animations/Kwang/AM_XenoCore_LightHeal: a casting gesture with no notifies. Set a Palette Glyph and Glyph Colour.

Ether does not change a heal

A heal restores Power, scaled by the art's level and by any healing skill bonus (such as Healing Wisdom). The caster's Ether stat plays no part: unlike damage, a heal does not run through the damage formula. Attribute Ether marks it as an ether art, which wakes ether-sensing enemies nearby.

docs.title: 2. Rally: buff the whole party
docs.text:
1. Create another blank Art the same way, DA_Rally. Set Display Name, Description, its own Cooldown Tag, Montage (AM_XenoCore_LightHeal again) and Palette Glyph.
  2. Effect Type: No damage or healing. Target Type: Whole party.
  3. Power: leave it; nothing reads it for this effect type.

  4. Under Art › Effects, add two entries:

    Effect Duration Magnitude Recipient Battle/Status/GE_XenoCore_Status_StrengthUp 20 0 Whole party Battle/Status/GE_XenoCore_Status_Regenerate 15 40 Whole party

    Strength Up raises Strength by Magnitude percent; a Magnitude of 0 sends nothing and it falls back to its default of 30 % (×1.3). Regenerate heals Magnitude HP every second, so it needs one. Both need a Duration.

  5. Cooldown Duration: 30. Save.

Recipient and Target Type are different things

Target Type decides who the Art is aimed at. Each effect's Recipient decides who that one entry lands on: Each target, the User, or the Whole party. An attack can carry a User entry to buff its caster as it hits.

docs.title: 3. Your own gesture montage (optional)
docs.text:
If you replace AM_XenoCore_LightHeal:

  1. Make a montage from a casting or gesture sequence on the Mannequin skeleton. Lyra's own heal uses AM_MM_Generic_Unequip, an upper-body gesture, as reference.
  2. Put it on the FullBody slot (the DefaultGroup slot group), like the shipped Arts. Every Art roots the character while it plays, so an upper-body slot gains nothing here.
  3. Add no notifies. No hit events, no weapon trail.
  4. Set Impact Fraction to where the spell lands in the gesture.

docs.title: 4. Teach them
docs.text: Add a row for each to a character's learnset, the Data Table set as their Art Learn Table (Set palette slots and unlocks).

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym with two or more party members active. Slot Mend and Rally on the leader's palette.
  2. Engage a minion and take some damage. Select Mend and confirm: a selector appears on the party HUD. Move it to a wounded member and confirm. The heal plays and a number shows the HP restored.
  3. Select Mend again and press back instead: the selector closes and Mend is not on cooldown.
  4. Use Rally. Every active member's HUD plate shows the Strength Up and Regenerate icons, and their HP ticks up every second.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Content Browser warning: 'A Heal art aimed at an Enemy heals the enemy'

Target Type is still Enemy. Set One ally, User or Whole party.

The selector opens and nothing happens

The Art is on cooldown or the party has one member. Check the palette ring.

Fails silently: the buff never appears

The entry's Duration is 0. The Art definition reports this as an error on save; fix it.

Heal shows sparks, a trail or a hit reaction

The montage was duplicated from an attack. Use a notify-free gesture montage.

docs.text:
