  • Make a status effect
  • Reactions and statuses

docs.title: Make a Talent Art
docs.text:
Designer · 40 min · No code

Result: a new weapon-granted Talent Art, Shatter, paid for with the Talent Gauge instead of a cooldown. Whoever holds the weapon fills the gauge with landed auto-attacks and spends it on Shatter from the palette's centre slot.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Make an attack Art
  • Glossary: Talent Art, Talent gauge.
  • A weapon of your own is easiest: Add a weapon. This recipe edits a copy of the sample greatsword's ability set.

docs.title: How a Talent Art works
docs.text:
Piece Sample Notes Talent Art definition Battle/Arts/DA_XenoCore_TurnStrike A XenoCoreTalentArtDefinition: every Art field, plus Gauge Cost Talent Art ability Battle/Arts/GA_XenoCore_TurnStrike Child of the Talent Art class; points at the definition Grant Weapons/GreatSword/AbilitySet_XenoCore_JunkSword The weapon's ability set grants it Weapon Weapons/GreatSword/ED_XenoCore_JunkSword Ability Sets To Grant names that set Fill rate the character's stats effect TalentChargePerHit: gauge % per landed auto-attack

The weapon owns the Art; the character owns the fill rate. Equip a different weapon and the same character has a different Talent Art, filling at the same speed.

A Talent Art has no cooldown: the gauge is the cooldown. The gauge (0 to 100) persists out of combat, and a Talent Art that misses or is interrupted still spends it. While it plays, the world can slow down around the attacker.

Talent Arts are not in a learnset

A Talent Art never appears on the Arts palette row, is never learned through a character's Art Learn Table, and cannot be levelled with Art Points. It lives only in the palette's centre slot during battle.

docs.title: 1. The definition
docs.text:
1. In MyGame/Arts, right-click › Data › Data Asset, pick XenoCoreTalentArtDefinition and name it DA_Shatter. Create it blank rather than duplicating DA_XenoCore_TurnStrike, so it inherits none of Turn Strike's effects.
  2. Set Display Name, Description, Power, Effects, Montage and Palette Glyph as for any Art.
  3. Leave Cooldown Duration at 0 and Cooldown Tag empty.
  4. Under Talent Art, set Gauge Cost: 100 spends a full gauge; 50 spends half.

  5. Optional slow motion, under Art › Time Dilation:

    • Time Dilation: how slow the world runs while Shatter plays. 1.0 is off; Turn Strike uses 0.35.
    • Time Dilation Keeps User Speed: on keeps the attacker at normal speed while the world slows. Off slows everyone, attacker included.
    • Time Dilation Start / End: the window, as fractions of the montage. 0 to 1 is the whole Art.

    These are on every Art definition, not only Talent Arts.

docs.title: 2. The ability
docs.text:
1. Right-click Battle/Arts/GA_XenoCore_TalentArt_Base and choose Create Child Blueprint Class. Name it GA_Shatter. Do not duplicate GA_XenoCore_TurnStrike: the base carries both the damage effect and the heal effect, so a healing Talent Art works with no extra setting.
  2. Open it, click Class Defaults, and set Art Data (XenoCore › Art) to DA_Shatter.
  3. Leave Talent Gauge Effect as GE_XenoCore_TalentCharge: the same effect that fills the gauge also empties it.
  4. Keep Ability Tags as Ability.XenoCore.Art.Talent, so tag rules that name Arts still cover it. The palette does not need the tag: it finds the Talent Art by its class.
  5. Compile and Save.

The palette's centre slot looks up the Talent Art the character was actually granted (any ability built on the Talent Art class) and shows that Art's name, description and icon, and lights when the gauge covers its Gauge Cost. Nothing on the palette widget needs to change.

docs.title: 3. Grant it through the weapon
docs.text:
1. Create a Data Asset of class LyraAbilitySet named AbilitySet_MyWeapon, and add one entry to Granted Gameplay Abilities: GA_Shatter. Nothing else.
  2. Open your weapon's equipment definition (a child of Weapons/ED_XenoCore_Sword_Base; see Add a weapon) and set Ability Sets To Grant to AbilitySet_XenoCore_SwordCommon and AbilitySet_MyWeapon. SwordCommon grants GA_XenoCore_WeaponDrawSync and GA_XenoCore_EquipmentStats: without it the weapon never draws and never applies its stats. Setting the list replaces the base's, so list both.

A character with two Talent Arts

Grant only one Talent Art per character at a time. With two, the centre slot uses the first it finds and logs a warning naming the one it ignored.

docs.title: 4. The fill rate
docs.text: The gauge fills from landed auto-attacks by the character's TalentChargePerHit, a percentage of the gauge per hit, set by a modifier on their stats effect (Author a character's statline). 20 fills in five hits; 0 means that character never charges from auto-attacks.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Equip the weapon on the leader and press Play in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym.
  2. Engage a minion. The centre slot shows Shatter with an empty ring around it.
  3. Let auto-attacks land. The ring fills, and the disc lights once the gauge reaches Shatter's Gauge Cost (half-way for a cost of 50).
  4. Confirm the centre slot. Shatter plays, the world slows if you set dilation, and the gauge empties by Gauge Cost.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
The centre slot shows the palette's own Talent entry, not Shatter

The palette found no Talent Art on the character, so it fell back to the entry authored on UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_ArtSlot. Check that the weapon's ability set grants GA_Shatter and that GA_Shatter has Art Data set; a Talent Art without it logs a warning ("is granted but has no ArtData") and is skipped.

A new weapon's Talent Art appears only at the next fight

The palette re-reads the Talent Art when it binds to a character and each time a battle starts, not when you equip. Swapping weapons out of battle shows the new Talent Art as soon as the next fight begins.

Fails silently: the gauge never fills

The character's TalentChargePerHit is 0, or auto-attacks are missing (misses do not charge). See Tune auto-attacks.

The weapon no longer draws

GA_XenoCore_WeaponDrawSync was removed from the ability set.

The whole game stays in slow motion

Should not happen: the dilation is restored on every way the Art can end. If it does, report it; slomo 1 in the console restores normal speed.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Arts
  • Equipment: weapons, ability sets, and what equipping grants.
  • Add a weapon

docs.title: Set up a trade
docs.text:
Designer · 20 min · No code

Result: an NPC whose prompt shows a second button, Trade. You offer them collectables from your bag in exchange for an item they want to part with, and a generous offer earns a bonus item on top.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Write an NPC conversation
  • Shops and trade: trade values and the bonus rule.

docs.title: How trading works
docs.text:
Trading is barter, not gold. The NPC offers a short list of items. The player picks one and puts up items from their bag. If what the player offers is worth at least the item's price, the trade goes through.

What the player may offer: only Materials and Collectables. Equipment, key items, gems, crystals and arts manuals are never shown on the player's side.

What things are worth on the trade table, from each item's Sell Value:

Item category Trade value Materials Sell Value × 1 Everything else (collectables, weapons, armour…) Sell Value × 10

So collectables picked up in the world are worth ten times their shop sell price in a trade. That is the point of trading: it turns exploration into gear.

The bonus ("overtrade"). Each NPC can hold one bonus item. If the player offers at least the item's price + the bonus item's value, they get the bonus too.

Setting a trade table is all it takes. An NPC with a trade table automatically shows Trade as their second prompt, on pad X (keyboard F). You never type "Trade" anywhere.

Piece Sample Trade table Trade/DA_XenoCore_Trade_Colony9 NPC Characters/NPC/B_XenoCore_Npc, placed Trade screen UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_TradeScreen

docs.title: 1. Check the items
docs.text:
Each item on either side of a trade needs a XenoCoreFragment_ItemCategory fragment with a Sell Value above 0. An item without one is worth nothing and can't be traded.

For testing, make sure you know one or two Collectables the player can pick up in your level. The gym has collectable orbs placed.

docs.title: 2. Create the trade table
docs.text:
1. In MyGame/Trades, create a Data Asset of class XenoCoreTradeTable. Name it DA_Trade_Fisher.
  2. Open it. Under XenoCore › Trade › Offers, add one or two entries to Offers:
    • Item: what the NPC hands over.
    • Price Override: 0 to ask the item's own trade value, or a number to ask that.
  3. Read the greyed-out columns on each row:
    • Resolved Price: what the player must offer for this item.
    • Overtrade At: what the player must offer to get the bonus too. 0 when there is no bonus.

On a table you have just opened these may take a moment to fill in while the items load. In game the items load when the trade screen opens, not with the map. 4. Under XenoCore › Trade › Overtrade Bonus, optionally set: - Item: the bonus item. Leave empty for an NPC who never gives a bonus. - Value Override: how much extra the player must offer on top of a row's price. 0 uses the bonus item's own trade value. Resolved Value shows the result. 5. Save, then right-click the asset and choose Asset Actions › Validate Assets. Fix any error (no offers, an offer with no item, a row priced at 0).

Keep the list short. A trader offers one or two things, not a shop's stock.

Price Override 0 means \"use the item's value\", not \"free\"

Nothing is ever traded for free. A gift belongs in a quest reward.

The bonus is one per NPC, not one per row

Overtrade Bonus belongs to the trader. The threshold moves with whichever row the player is trading for (row price + bonus value), but the bonus item is always the same one.

docs.title: 3. Give the table to an NPC
docs.text:
1. Place Characters/NPC/B_XenoCore_Npc in your level, or select one already there.
  2. In Details › XenoCore › NPC, set Display Name and set Trade Offers to DA_Trade_Fisher.
  3. Optionally set Portrait. The trade screen shows it beside the NPC's half of the exchange.
  4. Save the level.

Set it on the placed NPC, never in Class Defaults

Trade Offers is per instance. In the Blueprint's Class Defaults it makes every NPC a trader.

docs.title: 4. (Optional) Change what they say afterwards
docs.text:
The NPC Blueprint's On Interact graph already handles trading. When the press was the Trade button, it calls Open Trade, which has two exits:

  • Traded: at least one exchange happened.
  • Cancelled: the player backed out, or the screen could not open.

The stock graph does nothing on either exit: the trade screen closes and the NPC says no more. To give the NPC a closing line, make a child Blueprint of B_XenoCore_Npc in MyGame/NPCs, override its On Interact, and after Open Trade add a Play Dialogue on Traded (for example "Pleasure doing business.") and another on Cancelled ("Come back any time."). Working in a child means a template update does not overwrite your lines.

Branch on Is Trade Verb, never on the verb number

On Interact receives a Verb Index. Trade is index 1 today, but adding an entry to Extra Interact Verbs shifts it. Use the Is Trade Verb node to ask. A graph comparing Verb Index to 1 opens the wrong thing silently.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play. Pick up a few collectables.
  2. Walk up to your NPC. The prompt shows Talk and Trade.
  3. Press X (keyboard F). The trade screen opens with the NPC's offers.
  4. Pick an offer. Your side lists only materials and collectables.
  5. Offer items worth at least the Resolved Price. The trade goes through, the item is in your bag and your offered items are gone.
  6. If you set a bonus, offer at least the Overtrade At value on another trade. You receive the bonus item as well.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
No Trade prompt appears, and X changes the party's orders instead

Trade Offers is empty on this placed NPC. X opens a trade only while the prompt offers Trade; anywhere else a tap of X switches the party's Attack tactic (see Party tactics).

My items aren't listed on my side

Only Materials and Collectables can be offered. Check the item's category fragment.

An offer can never be afforded

The item has no category fragment or a Sell Value of 0, so it has no value to derive a price from. The table's validation reports it.

The Output Log says Open Trade could not load W_XenoCore_TradeScreen

The trade screen asset was moved or renamed. See UI and input.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Open a shop: the gold version, on the Talk button.
  • Shops and trade
  • Branch a conversation: place Open Trade (category XenoCore › Trade) anywhere in a conversation of your own.

docs.title: Tune auto-attacks
docs.text:
Designer · 20 min · No code

Result: the free auto-attack that runs while you are engaged swings at the speed, reach and rhythm you want, uses your own swing animations, and fills the Talent Gauge at your chosen rate.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Play the sample: how engaging starts auto-attacks.
  • Glossary: Auto-attack, Talent gauge.

docs.title: What decides an auto-attack
docs.text:
What Where Reach, rhythm, animations, root motion The auto-attack ability, Battle/GA_XenoCore_AutoAttack (party). Enemies have their own, for example Characters/Enemies/Minion/GA_XenoCore_Minion_Attack Per-weapon-type swings and reach The equipped weapon's type, Weapons/Types/DA_XenoCore_WeaponType_*, Attack category. Filled in, it replaces the ability's Attack Montages, Attack Montages Stationary and Attack Range for that type; empty uses the ability's. The shipped Greatsword type leaves them empty Damage The attacker's Strength and weapon attack range against the target's Physical Defence (Stats and damage) Speed The AutoAttackSpeed attribute: 1.0 normal; Slow and Haste change it Talent charge per hit TalentChargePerHit on the character's stats effect

The cadence is swing length + Swing Recovery, divided by AutoAttackSpeed. Swing length comes from the animation itself, so a longer clip spaces itself out rather than overlapping the next.

docs.title: The ability's settings
docs.text:
Open Battle/GA_XenoCore_AutoAttack and click Class Defaults. Everything is under XenoCore › AutoAttack unless noted.

Setting Default What it does Attack Range 300 (the C++ default is 420; the shipped ability overrides it) How far the swing reaches, centre to centre, in cm. A swing only starts inside it Contact Reach Tolerance (XenoCore › Attack) 60 Extra reach at the moment of contact only, so a target drifting a little during the windup is still hit Swing Recovery 0.35 Idle seconds between one swing ending and the next starting Montage Play Rate 1.0 Speeds every swing up (and its hit) without new animations Attack Montages A, B, C upper-body swings Played in order and looped while moving Attack Montages Stationary The same swings, full body Played when standing still. Empty = use Attack Montages always Stationary Speed Threshold 20 Below this ground speed the character counts as standing still Cancel Full Body On Move on Moving mid-swing hands the swing over to the upper-body copy so the legs can run Full Body Cancel Blend Out 0.1 Blend for that hand-over Root Motion When Stationary on Uses the animation's root motion when standing. Shipped clips have none, so this is inert until you add some Face Target On Attack off Snap to face the target as a swing starts. Meant for enemies Face Target Turn Rate (XenoCore › Attack) 0 Turn over the swing instead of snapping. 0 = snap Target Source Target Lock Where the target comes from: the player's lock, or the nearest hostile (enemies) Requires Arming on Draw the weapon before the first swing. Off for enemies, which have no draw Damage Effect GE_XenoCore_Damage The effect that runs the damage formula Additional Effects none Extra effects applied on every landed hit Talent Charge Effect (XenoCore › Talent) GE_XenoCore_TalentCharge Fills the attacker's gauge on a landed hit

docs.title: Make swings faster
docs.text: Raise Montage Play Rate to 1.25 and lower Swing Recovery to 0.2. Both speed up the whole loop; the play rate also speeds the animation itself.

docs.title: Make the reach longer
docs.text: Raise Attack Range. Keep it a little above the target-mode strafe range (400 on GA_XenoCore_TargetMode, see Tune targeting) so the character faces the enemy whenever it is close enough to hit it. Each Art's default Distance is 420 too; change those if you want Arts to match.

docs.title: Use your own swings
docs.text:
To give one weapon type its own swings, put them on its weapon type asset (Attack Montages, Attack Montages Stationary, Attack Range) instead of the ability; the steps below are the same. To change every party member's default swings, edit the ability.

  1. Make one montage per swing. Put the moving set on the UpperBody slot and, if you want whole-body swings when standing still, a copy of each on FullBody.
  2. On every montage, at the contact frame, add the notify XenoCore Gameplay Event with Event Tag XenoCore.Event.MeleeHit. Copy it from AM_XenoCore_Attack_A.
  3. Set Attack Montages and Attack Montages Stationary to your sets, in the same order.

Fails silently: the swing animates and deals no damage

The hit is the notify. A swing montage without the XenoCore.Event.MeleeHit gameplay-event notify plays and never hits, and nothing is logged. Every montage needs one.

Keep the two sets matched

The moving and stationary sets must be the same animations, same length, same notify times. The hand-over when you start moving jumps to the same position in the other set.

docs.title: Change how fast the gauge fills
docs.text: Edit the TalentChargePerHit modifier on the character's stats effect: a percentage of the 0–100 gauge per landed hit. 25 fills in four hits. See Author a character's statline.

docs.title: Change what Slow and Haste do
docs.text: They lower or raise AutoAttackSpeed by the percentage the applying Art or skill sends as its Magnitude, or by 30 % (×0.7 / ×1.3) when it sends none. Change the strength on the Art's effect entry rather than in Battle/Status/GE_XenoCore_Status_Slow or _Haste; to change the fallback, duplicate them as your own statuses (Make a status effect).

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym, lock on to a minion and engage.
  2. Stand still: full-body swings. Walk: the swing carries on in the upper body.
  3. Time five swings before and after your change.
  4. Watch the Talent ring on the palette fill with each hit that lands, not with misses.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
The character never swings

Out of Attack Range, or still drawing the weapon. To see why, type log LogXenoAttack Verbose in the console: the output log then records why the loop is idle, once each time the reason changes.

Enemies stand next to you and never swing

Their auto-attack has Requires Arming on. Enemies have no draw, so the loop waits forever. Turn it off on enemy auto-attacks.

Swings whiff at the edge of range

Raise Contact Reach Tolerance slightly. It widens only whether a started swing connects, not who gets attacked.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Combat loop
  • Stats and damage
  • Tune hit feedback

docs.title: Tune companion AI
docs.text:
Designer · 20 min · No code · Last tested: 2026-10-01

Result: a companion that uses its arts the way you want: a healer who heals early, a damage character who saves an art for the Break, an attacker who acts less often so the player stays the star. And a party that behaves the way you want between fights: chattier, more watchful, or stiller.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Read Companion AI and aggro. It explains what each number below does.
  • Glossary: Aggro, Party tactics, Break, Topple, Daze.
  • Have the Gym map open and a party of at least two.

docs.title: 1. Pace a character
docs.text:
Open the character's party member definition, for example Nia's Characters/VRoid/Nia/PartyMember_VRoid_S, and expand XenoCore › AI › AI Profile.

Field Default Raise it to… Lower it to… Decision Interval 1.5 s think less often react faster Decision Jitter 0.3 vary the rhythm more act more predictably Post-Art Cooldown 3.0 s use fewer arts (weaker companion) chain arts more (stronger companion) Heal Threshold 30 % heal earlier heal only in an emergency Reliability 100 % — sometimes let a decision pass, for a careless character Seek Positional Bonus on — untick: use positional arts from the front, as in XC1 Positional Timeout 2.0 s walk round further before giving up give up sooner

Post-Art Cooldown is the one to reach for if a full party feels too strong.

The same profile's Target Choice fields decide which enemy the companion picks when the party's Attack tactic is At Will: Attacking Me Weight, Attacking Ally Weight (raise it on a defender), Leader Target Weight (raise it to stay with the player), Current Target Weight, Per Ally On Target Weight, Distance Penalty Per Metre and Target Reconsider Interval. Under Focus they are not read: the leader's target is the target.

The player's tactics come first

Everything on this page runs inside the orders the player sets in Party Tactics (hold X, keyboard F): Attack (Focus, At Will, Regroup), Arts (All, No Talent, Auto Only), Stay Back and Prioritise Healing, for the whole party or one member. Under Auto Only a companion uses no arts at all; under Stay Back it holds Stay Back Distance (750 cm, on Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party) from its target. See Party tactics.

docs.title: 2. Teach an art when to fire
docs.text:
Open the art definition, for example Battle/Arts/DA_XenoCore_SlitEdge, and expand Art › Companion AI.

  1. Leave Usable By AI ticked. Untick it to keep the art for the player only.
  2. Set AI Priority. Higher wins. All shipped arts use 1.
  3. Add entries to AI Conditions. For example, to have a companion save an art for a Broken enemy:
    1. Add an element.
    2. Set Check to Target has tag.
    3. Set Tag to Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Break.
    4. Tick Still Active On Impact.
    5. Leave Required ticked.

To make a condition a preference instead of a rule, untick Required and set Bonus.

You do not need conditions for a Topple or Daze art. AI Wait For Reaction (on) holds it until the enemy is Broken (for Topple) or Toppled (for Daze), and AI Chain Bonus (3) makes it the first choice the moment it can land. Lower the bonus if a chain art crowds out everything else, or set it to 0 to switch it off.

Fails silently: an art that never lands

Give every art its own montage. An art that uses the auto-attack's montage (AM_XenoCore_Attack_*) is stopped on its first frame when it cancels the auto-attack. It shows as USED in the companion log and then does nothing: no hit, no reaction, no error. Duplicate the clip under the art's name instead.

docs.title: 3. Set how much aggro an art draws
docs.text: On the same art, Art › Aggro › Threat (default 10). The aggro is Threat × (user's level + 14) and drains at 75 per second. A taunting art wants several hundred. A quiet support art wants 0.

docs.title: 4. Change how companions spread out
docs.text:
The spacing is an ordinary EQS query: Characters/Party/AI/EQ_XenoCore_CompanionCombatSpot. Open it in the EQS editor to change the ring radius, the number of points, or the test weights. The behind/beside variants used for positional arts are EQ_XenoCore_CompanionBackSpot and EQ_XenoCore_CompanionSideSpot.

To use your own copy instead of editing the shipped query, duplicate it into your folder, then on your child of Characters/Party/BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember (Class Defaults › XenoCore › AI) set Combat Spot Query, Back Spot Query or Side Spot Query to it. A template update then leaves your copy alone.

Fails silently: an empty Combat Spot Query

With Combat Spot Query cleared, companions walk straight at the enemy and bunch up. Nothing is logged. An empty Back or Side Spot Query falls back to the combat one.

docs.title: 5. Tune the party between fights
docs.text:
Out of battle each companion looks around, rests and wanders on its own timer. The settings are parameters on tasks in Characters/Party/AI/ST_XenoCore_PartyMember. Duplicate the tree into your folder, edit the copy, and set it as the StateTree on your own child of Characters/Party/BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember (see Party). Then point the party at that controller: Default Controller Class on Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party (Class Defaults › XenoCore › Party) for everyone, or Controller Class on one member definition for that character only.

To make the party… Change On Look around more, or less Glance Interval Min/Max; the … Chance weights XenoCore Party Gaze Look at you more Leader Chance XenoCore Party Gaze Watch the enemy in a fight, with fewer glances away Lower Battle Glance Chance XenoCore Party Gaze Stay put when you take a step Raise Leash Jitter or Follow Start Distance XenoCore Party Hold Set off more promptly Lower Reaction Delay Min/Max XenoCore Party Hold Chat more, wander less Raise Social Chance, lower Stroll Chance XenoCore Party Hold Stand closer or further apart when chatting Social Stand Distance Min/Max XenoCore Party Hold Stand still at rest, as before Set Stroll Chance, Social Chance and Solo Chance to 0 XenoCore Party Hold Keep up with a running leader faster Raise Catch Up Ratio or Catch Up Margin XenoCore Party Follow Leader

What each companion fidgets with and which faces it pulls belong to the character, not the tree: see Give a character its own idle breaks and faces.

Two settings are elsewhere:

  • How heavily a companion turns, starts and stops is XenoCore › Movement › AI Steering on the pawn Blueprint. Lower Rotation Rate Yaw and Max Acceleration for more weight. It applies only while the AI drives the body.
  • Who looks at whom during banter is under Who Is Speaking on Audio/Voice/DA_XenoCore_BattleVoiceConfig, including Exchange Max Distance (5 m), the furthest apart two members can be and still be paired for an exchange.

Crowd avoidance makes a travelling party wobble

Crowd Avoidance While Travelling on BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember (XenoCore › AI › Crowd) is off on purpose. Turned on, companions re-steer round each other every frame and the whole party zig-zags as it follows you, at every Crowd Avoidance Quality; higher qualities wobble more, not less. Nothing is logged. Leave it off: members already keep apart by their trail distances, and avoidance is always on in battle, where they need it.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Play the Gym and lock a minion.
  2. Open the console and type log LogXenoAI Verbose.
  3. Watch the Output Log. Each companion prints a decision line listing every usable art with its score, then USED with the art it chose. Back Slash prints HOLDING while the companion walks behind, then REACHED.
  4. Let a companion take damage. One with Light Heal slotted heals once someone drops below its Heal Threshold.
  5. After the fight, stop walking. Within a few seconds the companions look about on their own timers, and one walks up to another and the two look at each other. Walk off: they set off one by one rather than together, and follow without wobbling.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Symptom Cause A companion never uses an art It is not slotted in that character's Arts menu, Usable By AI is off, or the Arts tactic is Auto Only for that member (or No Talent, for a Talent Art). The decision line shows nothing usable Companions stand by the leader and do not attack The Attack tactic is Regroup. Tap X (keyboard F) to switch between Focus and At Will An art never appears in the decision line It is cooling down, out of reach, or a required condition fails. Back Slash's cooldown is 20 s A heal never fires Nobody is below the Heal Threshold, or no companion has a heal slotted A Topple or Daze art is never used Nothing has Broken (or Toppled) the enemy yet. These arts wait for their reaction; untick AI Wait For Reaction to change that An art is USED but nothing happens It shares the auto-attack's montage, or its hit missed or was blocked. Check with log LogXenoArts Verbose Companions bunch up The controller's Combat Spot Query is empty, or the query it names was deleted. They then walk straight at the enemy. Set it again, or restore EQ_XenoCore_CompanionCombatSpot from your backup A companion stands still in a fight The party is not in battle: the leader has not drawn, and no enemy within 30 m is fighting the party Edits to the party StateTree do nothing You edited a copy that no controller uses. Set it on your controller Blueprint's StateTree component The party zig-zags while following Crowd Avoidance While Travelling is on. Untick it Companions walk, sprint to catch up, then walk again Catch Up Ratio or Catch Up Margin is too high, or Pace Smoothing too high to ease Companions never stroll or chat The leader never stops long enough: no activity starts while the leader moves faster than Leader Moving Speed (60 cm/s) A companion you take over feels sluggish It should not: AI Steering stops applying the moment the player possesses a body. Check the pawn's own Character Movement values, which are what the player gets

Fails silently

A tag condition with an empty Tag is wrong without a word: Target has tag never passes (a required one hides the art for good), and Target lacks tag always passes. Nothing is logged. Check that every tag condition has its tag set.

docs.title: Tune levelling
docs.text:
Designer · 20 min · No code

Result: the party levels at the pace you want. You control how much experience each level costs, how much a kill is worth against enemies above or below the party, how much benched characters earn, the Art Points a kill pays, the starting gold and the level cap.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Your first enemy: an enemy's Experience Reward.
  • Author a character's statline if you change the level cap.

docs.title: Where levelling is set
docs.text:
Progression is one component on the player controller: Game/BP_XenoCore_Progression. Open it and click Class Defaults.

Setting Category Default What it does Default Experience Curve XenoCore › Progression DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves, row XC1 The EXP curve for any character whose member definition names none. XC1 is XC1's own table Experience Curve Member definition › XenoCore › Progression e.g. DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves, row Kael The EXP curve this character levels on. Empty uses the default above Reward Multiplier Curve XenoCore › Progression CT_XenoCore_RewardLevelDiff Row Reward.LevelDiffMultiplier: multiplier on a kill's reward, keyed by party level minus enemy level Reserve Experience Rate XenoCore › Progression 0 (C++ default 0.9, XC1's) Share of every EXP award, and of a kill's AP, a benched character gets. The sample sets 0: everyone who joins fights (up to seven), and a recruit joins at the party's level instead of catching up from the bench Gold XenoCore › Progression 3000 The purse a new game starts with Default Art Level Cap XenoCore › Arts 4 Highest level an Art can be trained to before a manual raises it Art Level Cost Multipliers XenoCore › Arts 11 values, 1 to 65 AP to reach Art levels II to XII, as multiples of each Art's Base Level Up Cost Art Points Base XenoCore › Arts 2.0 The flat part of a kill's AP Art Points Per Enemy Level XenoCore › Arts 2.0 AP per level of the defeated enemy, added to Art Points Base Art Slot Unlock Levels XenoCore › Arts 1,1,1,12,20,28,34,40 Level each slot opens, in unlock order (the bar fills centre-out); keep it ascending. See Set palette slots and unlocks

Both curve tables are in Battle/Attributes. The experience a kill is worth is set on each enemy, as Experience Reward (XenoCore › Enemy), scaled by the enemy's level through its Experience Level Scale curve row (same category; the minions use CT_XenoCore_EnemyStats row Minion.ExperienceScale, so a same-level kill is worth a steady share of a level all the way up). Empty Experience Level Scale pays the flat reward at every level. An enemy's Art Point Reward (same category, default -1) replaces the AP formula for that enemy when it is 0 or more.

Skill Points have their own settings under XenoCore › Skills; see Skills.

docs.title: How a kill is paid
docs.text:
1. The enemy's Experience Reward, scaled by its Experience Level Scale at its level, is multiplied by the Reward Multiplier Curve at party level − enemy level. The party level is the level of the character you control. A positive difference (you out-level the enemy) should pay less; a negative one more.
  2. Every active member receives the result. Every reserve member receives it times Reserve Experience Rate.
  3. Each character banks it towards their own next level. A character can gain several levels from one award.
  4. Each character also banks Art Points: Art Points Base + Art Points Per Enemy Level × the enemy's level, times the same reward multiplier, and times Reserve Experience Rate for reserves. AP is spent on the Arts menu's Level Up tab. Quest rewards and XenoAwardExp pay experience only, never AP.
  5. Each character's selected skill branch fills with Skill Points (Skills).

A level-up re-applies the character's statline at the new level, which also heals them to full.

docs.title: Make levels faster or slower
docs.text:
EXP-to-next-level is a Data Table, Game/DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves, with row structure XenoCoreExperienceCurveRow. Each row is one curve: Experience To Next Level is a list where entry 0 is the cost of level 1 to 2, entry 1 is level 2 to 3, and so on. Past the last entry the character is at the level cap. Note says where the numbers came from.

Row Who uses it Level 1 to 2 XC1 Anyone with no curve of their own (the Default Experience Curve). XC1's own table 40 Kael, Mira, Nia, Dorran, Isolde, Sabine, Tamsin That character, through Experience Curve on its member definition 90 to 120

The character rows are XC1's table × 2.5, each character between ×0.9 and ×1.2 of that, so the party levels at different rates. That is a deliberate change from XC1, which levels everyone on one table. Nothing else holds these numbers: the table is the only copy.

To change the pace:

  1. Open DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves and select a row.
  2. Edit Experience To Next Level. Halving every value halves the grind.
  3. Save. Data Validation runs on save: an empty list, or an entry of 0 or less, is an error, because a character on that curve would stop levelling with nothing logged.

To give a character a curve of its own, add a row (or duplicate one), then open the character's member definition and set Experience Curve to that table and row. To have two characters level together, point both at the same row. For many rows at once, export the table to JSON or CSV, edit, and reimport.

Why a Data Table

It matches the project's other per-level numbers: skill cost curves, trait ladders and SP rewards are Data Tables of the same shape. Earlier versions used a curve table row whose name was written into C++; nothing is named in code any more.

docs.title: Reward fighting up, punish farming down
docs.text:
1. Duplicate CT_XenoCore_RewardLevelDiff and edit Reward.LevelDiffMultiplier. Its keys are the level difference, from negative (the enemy is higher) to positive.
  2. Set Reward Multiplier Curve to your copy.

docs.title: Change how many Art Points a kill pays
docs.text: Set Art Points Per Enemy Level and Art Points Base. To make one enemy (a boss) pay a fixed amount, set its Art Point Reward instead; the reward multiplier still applies.

docs.title: Change what benched characters earn
docs.text:
Set Reserve Experience Rate: 1.0 means no penalty, 0 (the sample) means reserves never level, 0.9 is XC1. The same rate applies to a kill's AP. Skill Points use Reserve Skill Point Rate instead (0 in the sample, C++ default 0.9).

A character recruited mid-game is raised to the party's level when Join At Party Level is on for the NPC or trigger that recruits them (Recruit a party member), so a 0 rate does not leave late joiners behind.

docs.title: Change the level cap
docs.text:
The cap is not on this component, and not in Project Settings. It is MaxCharacterLevel on the stat set, and the only way to change it is to add two lines to your project's Config/DefaultGame.ini with a text editor, with the editor closed:

[/Script/XenoCoreRuntime.XenoCoreStatSet]
MaxCharacterLevel=60

Reopen the editor. A character at the cap stops earning experience. If you raise the cap above 99, lengthen every row of DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves and extend every stat curve to the new level first, or the new levels cannot be reached and add nothing. Data Validation warns about a row shorter than the cap.

docs.title: Change the starting gold
docs.text: Set Gold. It is the starting purse only; after that the saved value is used.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play.
  2. Open the console (~) and type XenoAwardExp 500. The level-up banner shows who levelled.
  3. Open the Party screen. Every member had the same award, but each needs a different amount: with 500 EXP, Tamsin is further along than Sabine.
  4. Kill a minion and compare the award against one of a different level. Enemy levels are set per placement: Your first enemy.

XenoAwardExp pays no AP; kill a minion to see AP arrive. Other console helpers: XenoAwardGold 1000, XenoGiveAP 500, XenoGiveSP 500.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Nobody levels, and an error names BP_XenoCore_Progression

Default Experience Curve is empty or names a row the table does not have, and the character has no curve of its own. The Output Log says "has no DefaultExperienceCurve".

A character levels at the wrong pace, and a warning names its curve

Its member definition's Experience Curve names a row that does not exist. It falls back to the default curve (XC1) and logs "ExperienceCurve row '...' does not resolve". Data Validation marks the member definition with an error for the same reason.

Kills give no experience

The enemy's Experience Reward is 0, or the reward curve returns 0 at that level difference. Check the enemy first.

Continue ignores my changes

Levels, experience and gold are in the save. Test new tuning with Play in the editor or New Game.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Progression: per-character records, and why a benched character keeps its level with no body in the world.
  • Author a character's statline
  • Set palette slots and unlocks

docs.title: Tune revive and defeat
docs.text:
Designer · 15 min · No code · Last tested: 2026-10-01

Result: reviving costs what you want and brings an ally back as healthy as you want. A refused revive says what you want, the party recovers between fights at the rate you want, and losing a battle looks and sounds the way you want.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • Read Party Gauge, downed and revive for what each piece does.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
All of these are on one asset.

  1. Open Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party and select the class defaults.
  2. The price. Under XenoCore › Party › Revive, set Revive Bar Cost. 1 is XC1. 0 makes reviving free, and the prompt then never refuses.
  3. The comeback. Set Revive Health Fraction. 0.3 stands the ally up at 30% of max HP; XC3 uses about 0.15.
  4. The reach. Set Revive Range in cm. Keep it small (around 110) so only the body under the leader's feet is offered in a crowded fight.
  5. The refusal. Set Revive Refused Text to your line, for example Need a full gauge bar. Clear it to show no line. Pick Revive Refused Sound, or clear it for silence.
  6. The end of a fight. Under XenoCore › Party › Battle, set Battle Over Grace: the seconds with no enemy chasing the party before the downed get up at 1 HP.
  7. Recovery between fights. Under XenoCore › Party › Recovery, set Out Of Battle Regen Per Second, the fraction of max HP every member recovers each second once the fight is over (0.1 = 10%; 0 turns it off), and Out Of Battle Regen Delay, the seconds before it starts. Benched members recover too. Fleeing does not count as the fight being over.
  8. The defeat. Under XenoCore › Party › Wipe › Defeat:
    • Defeat Text is the word on screen.
    • Defeat Time Dilation: 0.35 is slow motion; 1.0 turns it off.
    • Defeat Saturation: 0.15 drains nearly all colour; 1.0 turns it off.
    • Defeat Sound is the sting. Clear it for silence.
    • Defeat Banner Class is the banner widget. Clear it for no banner at all.
  9. The downed HUD row. Open UserInterface/HUD/W_XenoCore_HUDLayout. Select each party row. Under XenoCore › Party › Downed, adjust Downed Portrait Tint and Downed Text Colour, or untick Grey When Downed.
  10. Compile and save.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
Press Play in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym, draw your weapon on a minion, then:

  1. Type XenoGaugeAdd -300 in the console to empty the gauge, then XenoDownMember 1. The companion kneels and their row greys out.
  2. Stand on them and press A. Your refusal line appears over them, the gauge shakes and you hear the refusal sound.
  3. Type XenoGaugeAdd 100 and press A again. One bar empties and the ally stands at your Revive Health Fraction.
  4. Type XenoWipeParty. You see your defeat beat, then the party wakes at the respawn point.
  5. Out of battle, type XenoHurtParty 0.3. Every row drops to 30% and then climbs back at your Out Of Battle Regen Per Second.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: no prompt at all over a downed ally

The prompt only appears over a downed party member that the player is not driving, and only within Revive Range. Stand closer. Your own downed body never offers a revive.

Fails silently: the ally got up by themselves

Nothing was chasing the party, so the battle ended and the downed rose at 1 HP. That is the design. To test a revive, keep a minion engaged.

Fails silently: the refusal shows no line

Revive Refused Text is empty, or the press came from AI. Only a player-made refusal is announced.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Party Gauge, downed and revive, including how to change what fills the gauge.
  • Party: where the party respawns after a defeat.

docs.title: Tune targeting
docs.text:
Designer · 30 min · No code

Result: lock-on reaches as far as you want, the character faces its target only when close, out-of-reach Arts make the character run in the way you like, the target marker looks right, and enemies notice the party at the distances you choose.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Controls: how to lock on, cycle targets and leave target mode.
  • Glossary: Target mode, Engage, Aggro.

docs.title: Where targeting is set
docs.text: What Asset Lock-on range Battle/Targeting/GA_XenoCore_TargetMode, Class Defaults Line of sight, on-screen rule Nodes inside GA_XenoCore_TargetMode's graph Facing, camera focus, running in for Arts, marker, arrows, HUD widgets GA_XenoCore_TargetMode, Class Defaults When enemies notice, chase and give up Characters/Enemies/Core/BP_AIC_XenoCore_Enemy, Class Defaults, with per-enemy overrides on the enemy

docs.title: 1. Lock-on range
docs.text:
Open GA_XenoCore_TargetMode, click Class Defaults, and find XenoCore › Targeting › Range:

Setting Default What it does Lock Acquire Range 3000 How far away, in cm, a target can be locked onto or cycled to Lock Keep Range 3000 How far away a locked target can go before the lock drops. Never less than Lock Acquire Range

Set Lock Keep Range a little above Lock Acquire Range (for example 3000 and 3500) so a target picked at the edge is not dropped the moment it steps back.

The two cannot cross: editing either one in Class Defaults pushes the other so keep stays at or above acquire, the data validator reports a saved asset where they differ the wrong way, and the graph reads keep through a getter that never returns less than acquire.

The graph's Step Target From and Is Target Still Valid nodes read these settings through Get Lock Acquire Range and Get Lock Keep Range. Leave those pins wired.

On the same two nodes, Require Line Of Sight drops targets behind walls, and Require On Screen (on Step Target From) ignores enemies you cannot see. These are still node pins: change them in the graph, then Compile and Save.

docs.title: 2. Facing while locked
docs.text:
Under XenoCore › Target Mode in Class Defaults:

Setting Default What it does Strafe While Locked on Face the target while close, side-stepping and backpedalling instead of turning Strafe Max Range 400 "Close" means within this, in cm. Beyond it you run normally even while locked Strafe Range Release Scale 1.2 Hysteresis: facing lets go only at 1.2 × the range, so the boundary does not flicker Retreat Dot Threshold -0.9 Only moving almost straight away counts as backing off; any diagonal turns and runs Strafe Stationary Speed 20 Below this speed you count as standing still, and keep facing Strafe Evaluate Interval 0.05 How often facing is re-checked, in seconds Camera Focus Duration 0.3 When a fight starts, the camera eases onto the target once over this time, then lets go. 0 turns it off

Keep Strafe Max Range a little inside the auto-attack's Attack Range (Tune auto-attacks), so "close" means "trading blows".

docs.title: 3. Running in for an out-of-reach Art
docs.text:
Confirming an Art whose target is beyond its Distance makes the character run in and strike on arrival. Under XenoCore › Targeting › Approach:

Setting Default What it does Approach Timeout 4 Give up after this many seconds. Nothing is spent Approach Arrive Margin 60 Stop this far inside the Art's Distance, so a target stepping back is still in reach Approach Stick Cancel 0.35 Pushing the stick past this cancels the run. Nothing is spent Approach Move Action Lyra's IA_Move The action read to tell the player's stick from the run's own steering

docs.title: 4. The marker and arrows
docs.text:
Under XenoCore › Targeting:

  • Target Indicator Material, Target Indicator Size (250), Target Indicator Height Fraction (0.35 of the target's capsule half-height), Target Indicator Screen Space Size (off: the marker shrinks with distance).
  • Offscreen Arrow Material, Offscreen Arrow Mesh, Arrow Screen Edge Inset (0.88), Arrow Camera Distance (200), Arrow Screen Size Fraction (0.16), Invert Arrow Direction. An empty arrow material means no arrows.
  • Target Acquired Sound: a 2D sound played on lock.
  • Target Plate Class, Player Plate Class, Arts Palette Class: the three HUD widgets that exist only while locked. Swap in your own children of these widgets to restyle them.

docs.title: 5. When enemies notice the party
docs.text:
Open BP_AIC_XenoCore_Enemy, Class Defaults › XenoCore › AI:

Setting Default What it does Engage Radius 1600 An enemy that has noticed the party, or been attacked, fights inside this Disengage Radius Scale 2.5 It stays engaged out to 2.5 × Engage Radius; beyond that you have outrun it Leash Radius 7000 Measured from its home (where it spawned or was placed): beyond this it gives up, heals and walks home Ignore When Levels Below 6 An enemy this many levels below the leader does not notice the party. Attacked, it still fights back Always Aggro off Ignore the level rule: for bosses and unique enemies

How an enemy notices the party is set on the enemy, not the controller: its Detection (XenoCore › AI › Detection: None, Sight, Sound or Ether) and the matching Sight Radius, Sound Radius or Ether Radius. See Place enemies in a map.

These are the defaults for every enemy the controller possesses. To give one enemy different radii, set its own overrides. Open the enemy Blueprint's Class Defaults (for a whole enemy type) or select a placed enemy in the level (for one placement), under XenoCore › AI:

Setting Default What it does Engage Radius Override -1 This enemy's engage radius, in cm Leash Radius Override -1 This enemy's leash radius, measured from where it started Disengage Radius Scale Override -1 This enemy's disengage scale. Values from 0 to 1 count as 1

-1 means "use the controller's value". 0 is a real value, not "off": an Engage Radius Override of 0 means the enemy never gets close enough to engage, even when provoked.

The controller reports the values in force with Get Effective Engage Radius, Get Effective Leash Radius and Get Effective Disengage Radius Scale. An override changed at runtime (a boss phase) applies on the next check.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Press Play in Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym.
  2. Lock on from further away than before, and cycle targets. Nothing beyond the range is offered.
  3. Walk towards the target: within Strafe Max Range you face it and side-step; walk away and you turn and run.
  4. Select an Art from far away and confirm: you run in and strike. Push the stick during the run: it stops and the Art is not on cooldown.
  5. Run up to an unengaged Grunt (it hears by sound): it notices you inside its Sound Radius.
  6. Lock on to one of two engaged minions and defeat it. The lock moves to the other one and you stay in battle with your weapon drawn.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
The character strafes all the way across the field

Strafe Max Range is too large. Facing should only hold at fighting distance.

An enemy ignores the party

Its Detection is None (passive), it hears by Sound and you are walking, or it is Ignore When Levels Below or more levels below the leader. Intended; change its Detection, or tick Always Aggro on its controller if it must notice you.

Defeating the locked enemy mid-fight

When the locked enemy dies and another enemy is still fighting the party, the lock moves to it (one on screen first, then the one with most aggro on the leader, then the nearest) and the battle goes on. Only when no enemy is still fighting does target mode end and the party sheathe. Enemies that are not fighting are never picked.

Enemies chase forever

Leash Radius is measured from the enemy's start point, not from you. A very large leash lets a kited enemy cross the whole map.

One enemy ignores my change to the controller

That enemy, or its placement, has an override that is not -1. Check XenoCore › AI on the placed actor as well as on its Blueprint.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Targeting: why the lock is an ability, not a component.
  • Enemies and AI
  • Tune the camera feel

docs.title: Add a tutorial card
docs.text:
Designer · 15 min · No code · Last tested: 2026-10-10

Result: a tutorial card that pops up, pausing the game, the first time the player meets a mechanic. It shows a title, a few lines of text, an optional picture, and button prompts that show the player's real bindings. A pages through the cards and B skips the rest. Once a card has been seen it never shows again in that save, and it is listed under Main Menu › Tutorials.

XenoCore ships three combat cards: Engaging Enemies (row Targeting), Auto-Attacks and Arts (ArtsBasics) and Break and Topple (BreakTopple).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Know what a gameplay tag is: a card's triggers are tags.
  • To trigger a card on your own event, you need a tag of your own. Add it in Project Settings › Project › GameplayTags (for example MyGame.Tutorial.Crafting).

docs.title: Where the cards live
docs.text: What Where The cards, one row each UserInterface/Tutorials/DT_XenoCore_Tutorials (row structure XenoCoreTutorialRow) The button glyphs the cards draw UserInterface/Foundation/DT_XenoCore_Actions, the rows named Tutorial* Which table, the card widget, and the trigger distances Project Settings › Game › XenoCore UI › Tutorials The Tips on/off switch The Tutorials entry on the main menu

docs.title: 1. Add the card
docs.text:
1. In the Content Browser, open UserInterface/Tutorials/DT_XenoCore_Tutorials.
  2. Click Add in the Data Table editor's toolbar. Rename the new row, for example Crafting. The row name is the card's identity: a save remembers seen cards by row name, so renaming a row later shows that card again to everyone.
  3. In the Row Editor below, fill in Title and Body. Keep the body to two or three short sentences: it wraps, and a long card gets skipped.
  4. Optionally set Image to a texture.

docs.title: 2. Add the button prompts
docs.text:
1. Under Prompts, click + once per line of prompts.
  2. In each entry, set Label (for example Open the crafting menu).
  3. Under Actions, click + and pick a row of DT_XenoCore_Actions. Add more than one action to draw several buttons side by side on one line.

If the button you want has no Tutorial* row yet, see Add a button glyph for a new prompt below.

docs.title: 3. Say when it appears
docs.text:
Under Triggers, add one or more tags. The card shows the first time any of them happens:

Trigger Happens when XenoCore.Tutorial.Trigger.EnemyNear An enemy comes within Tutorial Enemy Near Distance (25 m) of the leader XenoCore.Tutorial.Trigger.BattleStarted The party enters battle Any tag that can be on an enemy, for example Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Topple An enemy within Tutorial Enemy Status Radius (30 m) has that tag Any other tag, for example your MyGame.Tutorial.Crafting A Blueprint calls Trigger Tutorial (category XenoCore › Tutorial) with it

A tag fired by Trigger Tutorial must match the card's trigger exactly: firing MyGame.Tutorial.Crafting.Bench does not show a card that lists MyGame.Tutorial.Crafting. Cards triggered at the same moment show as one sequence, in table order. To change the order, drag rows in the Data Table editor.

docs.title: 4. Fire your own trigger (only for your own tags)
docs.text: In the Blueprint where the moment happens (for example the crafting bench's On Interact), place a Trigger Tutorial node and set its Trigger to your tag. Calling it again after the card has been seen does nothing, so it is safe to call every time.

docs.title: 5. Save
docs.text: Save the Data Table.

docs.title: Add a button glyph for a new prompt
docs.text:
A glyph is drawn from a row of UserInterface/Foundation/DT_XenoCore_Actions. That row only draws a button; the button itself is bound in the game's input mapping. So the row must name the same keys as the input it stands for.

  1. Open Input/Mappings/IMC_XenoCore (or Lyra's IMC_Default for movement, look and jump) and find the input action your card talks about. Note its keyboard key and its gamepad key.
  2. Open DT_XenoCore_Actions. Right-click an existing Tutorial* row and choose Duplicate. Name the copy Tutorial<Something>.
  3. In the copy, set Keyboard Input Type Info › Key and Default Gamepad Input Type Info › Key to the keys you noted. Set Display Name to what the button does.
  4. Save, then pick the row in your card's Actions.

Fails silently: a prompt that names the wrong key

Nothing checks that a glyph row matches the real binding. A row with a typed-in key draws a perfectly good button that does nothing when pressed. Always copy the keys from the input mapping context, and re-check your rows whenever you rebind an input.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and press Play.
  2. Open the console (`) and type XenoCore.Tutorial.Reset to forget every card already seen.
  3. Type XenoCore.Tutorial.Show Crafting (your row name). The card appears and the game pauses. Check the title, body, picture and button glyphs. Press A to close it.
  4. Type XenoCore.Tutorial.Reset again, then cause the trigger for real: walk towards an enemy for EnemyNear, or reach your Trigger Tutorial node. The card appears once.
  5. Cause the trigger again. Nothing shows: the card has been seen.
  6. Open the main menu and choose Tutorials. Your card is listed.

Other console helpers: XenoCore.Tutorial.Trigger <Tag> fires a trigger as the node does, and XenoCore.Tutorial.Tips 0 / 1 turns popups off or on.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
Fails silently: the card never appears

Check in this order. The card was already seen in this save (run XenoCore.Tutorial.Reset). Tips is off on the Tutorials screen (XenoCore.Tutorial.Tips 1). Triggers is empty, or names a tag nothing ever fires. Project Settings › Game › XenoCore UI › Tutorials › Tutorial Table has been cleared or points at a different table.

Fails silently: tips off still marks cards as seen

With Tips off, a card whose trigger happens is recorded as met and never shown. The Tutorials menu fills up either way, and turning tips back on does not replay them.

XenoCore.Tutorial.Show says "no such card". The row name you typed doesn't match the Data Table's row name. Row names are exact.

XenoCore.Tutorial.Trigger says the tag is not registered. Add the tag in Project Settings › Project › GameplayTags first.

The card waits and shows late. A card never covers a menu, a conversation, the loading screen or the Change Time fade; it waits until the screen is free. That is intended.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Tips on/off is a player setting, saved per machine. Seen cards are per save, so a New Game shows them all again.
  • To restyle the card, make a Blueprint child of XenoCore Tutorial Card and set it as Tutorial Card in Project Settings › Game › XenoCore UI › Tutorials. Optional parts your child can name: BodyBox, PageText, NextLabel, SkipGroup. See Restyle the menus.

docs.title: Build a world-partition map
docs.text:
Level designer · 2 h · No code

Result: a large open map of your own that streams in pieces as the party travels, keeps its distant cliffs visible at all times, runs the XenoCore game rules, and is where New Game starts.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Comfortable with Unreal's World Partition and Landscape tools. This recipe covers what XenoCore needs from a map, not the tools themselves.
  • Place enemies and Footsteps by surface are the natural next steps.

The sample maps are not partitioned

Maps/L_XenoCore_GaurPlain and Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym are single, ordinary levels. Use them as a reference for what goes in a XenoCore map, not for how it streams.

docs.title: What a XenoCore map needs
docs.text:
Need Why Default Gameplay Experience = B_XenoCore_Experience Without it the map runs Lyra's default rules: no XenoCore HUD, abilities or teams A LyraPlayerStart Where the party spawns on a new game A navigation mesh over the playable ground Party members follow the leader and enemies chase along it Physical materials on the ground Footstep sounds and effects pick by surface A two-sided landscape material if the terrain ends behind a ridge Otherwise the ridge casts no shadow (see step 4) One XenoCore Area Music actor (optional) The map's field and battle music. See Give a map its music One XenoCore Map Area actor (optional) The minimap image, its bounds and the area's weather table. See Give a map its minimap One XenoCore Environment Director (optional) Time of day and weather on the map's lights. See Give a map its time of day and weather XenoCore Enemy Spawner actors, not individual enemies Each squad streams out with its spawner's cell and refills when it streams back in. See Place enemies

The three one-per-map actors are never spatially loaded: they set that themselves, so they stay loaded wherever the party is.

docs.title: 1. Create the map
docs.text:
1. File › New Level..., choose the Open World template (or Empty Open World). It creates a World Partition level.
  2. Save it as MyGame/Maps/L_MyWorld.

To convert an existing level instead, use Tools › Convert Level. It writes a partitioned copy beside the original and keeps its World Settings.

docs.title: 2. Point it at the XenoCore experience
docs.text:
1. Open World Settings. Under Game Mode, set Default Gameplay Experience to Experiences/B_XenoCore_Experience.
  2. Place a LyraPlayerStart where the party should appear.

Fails silently: no experience set

The map loads, the character walks, and nothing XenoCore works: no HUD, no targeting, no arts. Check Default Gameplay Experience first whenever a new map "does nothing".

docs.title: 3. Set up streaming
docs.text:
In World Settings › World Partition Setup, set the runtime grids. A reasonable start for a map around 1–2 km across:

Grid Cell size Loading range Main streaming grid 128 m (12800) 256 m (25600) HLOD 256 m 512 m

Mark everything that must always exist as not spatially loaded: select it and untick World Partition › Is Spatially Loaded. That means the sun, sky, fog, post-process and reflection captures, the navigation mesh bounds, the player start, and water volumes.

Terrain must be in streamable pieces

One huge mesh or one non-streaming landscape is one cell: it never streams. A Landscape is split into streaming proxies automatically when the level is partitioned; a mesh terrain must be built from tiles.

docs.title: 4. Build the ground
docs.text:
1. Create a Landscape in Landscape mode, or import a heightmap.
  2. Assign your landscape material. In that material, tick Two Sided.
  3. With the Landscape actor selected, set Default Phys Material to your ground physical material (for example Environment/PM_XenoCore_Grass). See Footsteps by surface.
  4. Optionally enable Nanite on the landscape, then build it with Build › Build Landscape, which builds the landscape's Nanite data along with its grass maps and physical material.

Fails silently: a one-sided landscape leaves the valley sunlit

If your terrain rises into a ridge and then stops at the map edge, the sun sees only the back faces of that ridge. Shadow rendering skips back faces, so the whole valley stays lit under a wall that should shade it. The only clue is a small soft shadow from the few faces that point at the sun. Tick Two Sided on the landscape material. Ticking Cast Shadow as Two Sided on the landscape components does not help.

A landscape's footsteps come from Default Phys Material

Unless your landscape material outputs a physical material per paint layer, the whole landscape uses Default Phys Material. Left empty, every footstep on it sounds like concrete.

docs.title: 5. Keep the backdrop visible with HLOD
docs.text:
Distant scenery the player never walks on (a ring of cliffs, far mountains) must stay on screen at any distance. Put it in an HLOD layer, not in the streaming range.

  1. Create an HLOD Layer asset in MyGame/Maps/HLOD, type Mesh Simplify or Instancing.
  2. Select the backdrop actors and set their HLOD Layer to it.
  3. Make sure the runtime partition's HLOD Setups in World Partition Setup lists that layer.
  4. Build › Build HLODs.

Fails silently: \"World contains 0 HLOD actors\"

In 5.8 an actor's HLOD layer does nothing unless the runtime partition's HLOD Setups lists it. The HLOD build then succeeds, logs that it built nothing, and your backdrop vanishes past the loading range. Check the build log for that line.

Also watch the HLOD layer's texture size: each HLOD actor bakes its own textures, and that is download size.

docs.title: 6. Add navigation
docs.text:
1. Place a Nav Mesh Bounds Volume covering the playable ground.
  2. On the RecastNavMesh actor, under Generation, tick IsWorldPartitionedNavMesh so navigation streams with the cells. (It is greyed out on a map that is not World Partition.)
  3. Press P in the viewport to check the green coverage.

docs.title: 7. Make New Game start here
docs.text:
1. Open UserInterface/W_XenoCore_TitleScreen › Class Defaults. Under XenoCore › Title, set New Game Map to L_MyWorld. This edits a shipped asset; note it. Alternatively, set Project Settings › Game › XenoCore Content › Startup › New Game Map Override, which wins over the title screen's setting and leaves the shipped asset untouched.
  2. Add the map to Project Settings › Packaging › List of maps to include in a packaged build.

Fails silently: a map missing from the package

A map reached only through a setting like New Game Map or a save file may not be cooked. The packaged title screen then works and New Game goes nowhere. Always list your maps.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
1. Open L_MyWorld and press Play. The XenoCore HUD appears and the party spawns at the player start.
  2. Walk away from the start. Party members follow (navigation works) and your footsteps sound right for the ground.
  3. Open the console and type wp.Runtime.ToggleDrawRuntimeHash2D. Cells load and unload around you as you move.
  4. Look back at the backdrop from the far side of the map. It is still there.
  5. From the title screen map (L_XenoCore_FrontEnd), press Play, choose New Game, and arrive in L_MyWorld.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
The party spawns but nothing XenoCore works

Default Gameplay Experience is not set.

Party members stand still

No navigation mesh where they are, or it did not stream in.

Distant cliffs pop in

They are spatially loaded without an HLOD, or the HLOD layer is not in HLOD Setups.

More in World and maps troubleshooting.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Megascans at shipping size before you place pack assets.
  • Footsteps by surface
  • Give a map its music: one music actor per map, kept out of spatial loading.
  • Place enemies

Descriptions on generated pages are short on purpose

For programmers: regenerating the generated pages

The generated pages are produced by Docs/Manual/tools/gen_reference.py (Python 3 only) from the plugin's C++ headers, in the repository the manual is built from. If you change XenoCore's C++ in your own copy, the published pages no longer describe your changes; the headers are the source of truth.

docs.title: Asset naming
docs.text:
All · reference · No code

The prefixes XenoCore's content actually uses, so you can tell an asset's type from its name in the Content Browser. Most follow Lyra's own conventions; a few are XenoCore's. XenoCore-authored assets also carry XenoCore after the prefix (GA_XenoCore_TargetMode), which keeps them apart from Lyra's assets of the same kind in search results.

Counts are of the plugin content you receive (Plugins/GameFeatures/XenoCore/Content, including ThirdParty/, excluding Dev/, which is removed before packaging), measured on 2026-10-14. Counts change as content is added.

docs.text:
• BP_ and B_ both mean Blueprint. Lyra uses B_; some XenoCore Blueprints use BP_ (BP_XenoCore_Party, BP_XenoCore_Progression, Inventory/Loot/BP_XenoCore_TreasureChest, Battle/Attributes/BP_XenoCoreDamageExecution). There is no difference in kind.

docs.title: For your own content
docs.text: Use Lyra's prefixes (B_, GA_, GE_, W_, DA_…) and your own project tag in place of XenoCore (GA_MyGame_Fireball), under Content/MyGame/. Then a search for your tag finds only your assets, and a template update never collides with your names.

docs.title: Blueprint nodes
docs.text:
Designer · reference · No code

Generated from source — do not edit by hand.

This page is written by Docs/Manual/tools/gen_reference.py from the plugin's headers. Edit the source comment and re-run the generator instead. See Docs/Manual/tools/README.md.

The Blueprint nodes XenoCore adds that are not member functions of a class: latent nodes (they wait for the player and continue from one of several output pins) and function libraries (nodes you can place in any graph). Search the node's name in the graph's right-click menu. Member functions of components, subsystems and widgets are listed with their class in C++ classes.

docs.title: Latent nodes
docs.text:
Each latent node fires at most one of its output pins, once. A graph waiting on one is suspended until then, so always wire every output pin you care about.

  • Ask Confirm, Offer Quest, Open Shop and Open Trade always fire one: if their screen cannot be shown, or closes without an answer (backed out of, or torn down with the world), they take the No / Declined / Nothing Changed / Cancelled pin.
  • Show Dialogue and Play Dialogue fire nothing if the conversation is closed (by Close Dialogue from another graph, or the world ending) before the line is advanced. The graph waiting on them simply stops there.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Evaluator · reference · No code

What XenoCore runs on, what it depends on, and what it does not support.

docs.title: Engine
docs.text:
Unreal Engine 5.8 (developed against the Epic Games Launcher build 5.8.1) Plugin engine version 5.8.0 in XenoCore.uplugin Host project Your own Lyra Starter Game project for 5.8 (free on Fab). XenoCore is a Lyra Game Feature plugin built against Lyra's C++ (LyraGame); it is tested against unmodified Lyra 5.8. See Install. Binaries None. XenoCore is delivered as C++ source and compiles inside your project the first time it opens, which needs Visual Studio 2022. Both modules are limited to Win64 (PlatformAllowList). Earlier engines Not supported. The content is saved with 5.8, and an older engine cannot load assets saved by a newer one.

See Requirements for the toolchain and hardware.

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text: Platform Status Windows 64-bit Developed and tested here, editor and packaged game. The only platform XenoCore's modules are built for (PlatformAllowList: Win64). macOS, Linux Not supported. Both modules are Win64-only, and the VRoid sample characters rely on the VRM4U plugin, whose assimp library is provided for Windows x64 only. Consoles, mobile Not supported.

docs.title: Game type
docs.text:
Players Single-player only. Party members are AI-controlled characters on one machine. Nothing is replicated or predicted for multiplayer, and some systems depend on that (for example XenoCore sends its own inventory messages because Lyra's only fire through replication). Input Gamepad and keyboard with mouse. See Controls. Saving Local save slots through the engine's save-game system. See Save and front end.

Multiplayer is not a setting you can turn on

Adding multiplayer would mean replicating the party, targeting, arts, inventory messages and save state. Treat it as a new project built on XenoCore's ideas, not an option.

docs.title: Plugin dependencies
docs.text:
XenoCore.uplugin enables these engine and Lyra plugins. They must stay enabled.

Plugin Why XenoCore needs it GameplayAbilities Arts, auto-attack, reactions, statuses and stats DataValidation The save-time checks on XenoCore's data assets ModularGameplay, ModularGameplayActors Components added to Lyra's actors GameplayMessageRouter Gameplay messages AsyncMixin Lyra's asynchronous loading helpers CommonUI, CommonGame, CommonLoadingScreen, UIExtension Menus, HUD layers, loading screen EnhancedInput All input AnimationWarping Stride warping in the locomotion layers GameplayCameras The exploration and art cameras StateTree, GameplayStateTree Enemy and party AI PCG Procedural placement in the sample world Niagara Effects: hit sparks, damage numbers, chest beams, footsteps NiagaraUIRenderer Effects drawn in the UI: the Party Gauge burst, quest-complete, level-up and party-join bursts Water Water in the sample maps DataRegistry Not used directly. Every number a Gameplay Effect or art scales by (FScalableFloat) carries a Data Registry field, so XenoCore's effects and arts reference the plugin; GameplayAbilities depends on it too Metasound Sound assets VRM4U The VRoid sample party: import, toon materials, spring bones and facial expressions, at runtime as well as import. A free third-party plugin (MIT licence) you download and add to Plugins/VRM4U; see Install

docs.title: Your project's plugin list
docs.text: You do not edit Lyra.uproject: XenoCore switches itself on (EnabledByDefault) and enables the plugins above through its own XenoCore.uplugin. Lyra's own sample game features (ShooterCore and the rest) can stay; nothing in XenoCore references them, and XenoCore's maps run their own Experience.

docs.title: VRM4U
docs.text: XenoCore is tested with the public VRM4U_5_8_20260912 release. Use a release built for UE 5.8; its assimp library is included, and a packaged game links it.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: Current version 1.0.0 (VersionName in XenoCore.uplugin, shown on the XenoCore entry in Edit › Plugins) Scheme Semantic Versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. A major release may break your content, your saves or the C++ and Blueprint API, and its changelog says what to re-check. A minor release adds features without breaking them. A patch release only fixes bugs. Changelog Changelog lists every release.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
Your own content. Keep everything you make in your own folder (for example Content/MyGame/) and your own C++ module, never inside Plugins/GameFeatures/XenoCore. An update replaces the plugin folder as a whole, so anything you changed inside it is lost. To change a shipped asset, duplicate it into your folder (or make a child of it) and point your content at the copy; subclass XenoCore's C++ bases instead of editing them. Keep the project in source control, so an update is a diff you can review.

Taking an update. Close the editor, replace the XenoCore folder with the new one, open the project and let it compile, then run Tools › XenoCore › Apply XenoCore Project Settings again (it adds any setting the new release needs and leaves yours alone). Read the changelog first.

Saves. Every save file records a save-data version. A save written by an older XenoCore loads in a newer one: each new version says how older files are brought forward, and so far every step has needed no conversion (the new fields simply start empty). A save written by a newer XenoCore cannot be loaded by an older one: on the Load screen that slot cannot be selected (it can still be deleted), rather than being read with fields the older code does not understand. Version 1.0.0 writes save-data version 5.

Engine versions. XenoCore 1.0.0 supports Unreal Engine 5.8 only. When a new engine version comes out, XenoCore is re-tested against it and a new upload is published for that version; until then, moving your project to the new engine is at your own risk, because Lyra itself changes between engine versions and XenoCore depends on Lyra's C++.

docs.title: Exec functions
docs.text:
An Exec function is typed into the console by its name followed by its arguments. Unreal only routes console input to a fixed set of objects: the player controller, its cheat manager (and cheat-manager extensions), the possessed pawn, the HUD, the game mode and the game instance. An Exec function on a component or a subsystem is not on that list, so typing it is expected to print Command not recognized.

A row marked Yes is declared on a cheat-manager extension, which registers itself on every new cheat manager, so it is typed like any built-in cheat. Exec functions are compiled out of Shipping builds.

docs.title: UXenoCoreContentSettings
docs.text:
Class · derives from UDeveloperSettings · header XenoCoreRuntime/Public/XenoCoreContentSettings.h

Assets XenoCore spawns or applies from code that are not UI. Project Settings > Game > XenoCore Content. Every entry defaults to the shipped asset.

Properties

Property C++ name Type Category Specifiers Default Description Starting Roster Override StartingRosterOverride TArray<TSoftObjectPtr<UXenoCorePartyMemberDefinition>> Startup Config, EditAnywhere Non-empty replaces the party component's authored StartingRoster for a New Game. A load restores from the save. New Game Map Override NewGameMapOverride TSoftObjectPtr<UWorld> Startup Config, EditAnywhere Set = New Game opens this map instead of the title screen's authored NewGameMap. Title Music TitleMusic TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Startup Config, EditAnywhere Played 2D while the title screen is up. Cleared = a silent title. Title Music Volume TitleMusicVolume float Startup Config, EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, ClampMax=2.0 1.0 Volume multiplier for the title music. Fallback Field Music FallbackFieldMusic TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Startup Config, EditAnywhere Played by an Area Music actor whose own Field Music slot is empty. The map's own track always wins; cleared = that area is silent. Fallback Battle Music FallbackBattleMusic TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Startup Config, EditAnywhere As Fallback Field Music, for an Area Music actor whose Battle Music slot is empty. Dialogue Anchor DialogueAnchor TSoftClassPtr<AXenoCoreDialogueAnchor> Dialogue Config, EditAnywhere The actor that carries the dialogue box over whoever is speaking. Must derive from XenoCoreDialogueAnchor. Dialogue Camera Rig DialogueCameraRig TSoftObjectPtr<UCameraRigAsset> Dialogue Config, EditAnywhere The camera that frames a conversation: it blends in when an NPC starts talking and back out when the talk ends. Cleared = the camera stays where it was. Dialogue Turn Seconds DialogueTurnSeconds float Dialogue Config, EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, ClampMax=2.0, Units=s 0.3 How long the player and the NPC take to turn and face each other when a conversation opens (and the NPC to turn back after). 0 snaps. Beam Material BeamMaterial TSoftObjectPtr<UMaterialInterface> Feedback Config, EditAnywhere The material of the light shaft a heal or buff raises over its target. Drives Colour, Intensity and Opacity parameters. Victory Fanfare VictoryFanfare TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Battle Config, EditAnywhere Played once, 2D, the moment a battle is won. Cleared = no fanfare (the party still celebrates). Battle Voice Config BattleVoiceConfig TSoftObjectPtr<UXenoCoreBattleVoiceConfig> Voice Config, EditAnywhere Pacing and playback for every party voice line. Cleared = the party is silent. Gem Registry GemRegistry TSoftObjectPtr<UXenoCoreGemRegistry> Items Config, EditAnywhere Every gem, by id, and the effect gem stats are applied through. Cleared = the shipped registry. Ally Damage Taken Sound AllyDamageTakenSound TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Battle Config, EditAnywhere Played at a companion when it takes damage. Cleared = companions take hits silently. Ally Damage Taken Critical Sound AllyDamageTakenCriticalSound TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Battle Config, EditAnywhere As Ally Damage Taken Sound, on a critical hit. Cleared = the normal sound plays for crits too. Ally Damage Taken Volume AllyDamageTakenVolume float Battle Config, EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, ClampMax=2.0 0.7 Volume of the companion hit sounds. Below 1 so the player's own hits stay the loudest. Critical Hit Text CriticalHitText FText Critical Hit Config, EditAnywhere The line raised over the target on a critical hit. Says hit, so it cannot be read as "critical health". Critical Hit Scale CriticalHitScale float Critical Hit Config, EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.25, ClampMax=4.0 1.15 Resting size of the critical line. Break / topple / daze are 1. Critical Hit Punch CriticalHitPunch float Critical Hit Config, EditAnywhere, ClampMin=1.0, ClampMax=4.0 1.7 The critical line starts this many times its resting size and snaps down to it. 1 = no punch. Critical Hit Stop Seconds CriticalHitStopSeconds float Critical Hit Config, EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, ClampMax=0.5, Units=s 0.0 Hit-stop on a critical hit, in real seconds. 0 = off (XC1 has none). Critical Hit Stop Dilation CriticalHitStopDilation float Critical Hit Config, EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.01, ClampMax=1.0 0.05 World speed during the hit-stop. Reaction Break Effect ReactionBreakEffect TSoftClassPtr<UGameplayEffect> Debug Config, EditAnywhere The Break effect the XenoCore.Reaction debug command reads its duration from. Reaction Topple Effect ReactionToppleEffect TSoftClassPtr<UGameplayEffect> Debug Config, EditAnywhere The Topple effect the XenoCore.Reaction debug command reads its duration from. Reaction Daze Effect ReactionDazeEffect TSoftClassPtr<UGameplayEffect> Debug Config, EditAnywhere The Daze effect the XenoCore.Reaction debug command reads its duration from.
