docs.title: FXenoCoreCombatAIProfile
docs.text:
Struct · header XenoCoreRuntime/Public/AI/XenoCoreCombatAIProfile.h · BlueprintType

How one AI combatant - companion or enemy - behaves in a fight: decision pace, post-art cooldown, heal threshold, positioning.

Properties

Property C++ name Type Category Specifiers Default Description Decision Interval DecisionInterval float AI EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.1, Units=Seconds 1.5 Seconds between art decisions. The auto-attack keeps swinging in between. Decision Jitter DecisionJitter float AI EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, ClampMax=0.9 0.3 Random spread on each interval, as a fraction: 0.3 = 70-130 % (XC3's jitter). Stops companions acting in lockstep. Post Art Cooldown PostArtCooldown float AI EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, Units=Seconds 3.0 After using an art, choose no other for this long - on top of the art's own cooldown. (XC3's IntervalArts.) Heal Threshold HealThreshold float AI EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, ClampMax=100.0, Units=Percent 30.0 An ally below this much health makes heal arts eligible. 30 is XC2's number; XC1's is unsourced. Reliability Reliability float AI EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, ClampMax=100.0, Units=Percent 100.0 Chance to act at all on a decision, 0-100. Below 100 makes a character less dependable, as XC2 does on purpose. Seek Positional Bonus bSeekPositionalBonus bool AI EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly true Move behind or beside the target for an art's positional bonus before using it (XC3). Off = fire from wherever it stands (XC1). Positional Timeout PositionalTimeout float AI EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, EditCondition=bSeekPositionalBonus, Units=Seconds 2.0 Give up on reaching position after this long and use the art anyway. Never circles. Attacking Me Weight AttackingMeWeight float Target Choice EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly 3.0 Engage at Will: score for an enemy that is attacking this character. Attacking Ally Weight AttackingAllyWeight float Target Choice EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly 1.5 Engage at Will: score for an enemy that is attacking another party member. Raise it on a defender. Leader Target Weight LeaderTargetWeight float Target Choice EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly 1.0 Raise it to stay with the player's fight. Current Target Weight CurrentTargetWeight float Target Choice EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly 2.0 Engage at Will: score for the enemy this character is already fighting - stops it flip-flopping. Per Ally On Target Weight PerAllyOnTargetWeight float Target Choice EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly -1.0 Engage at Will: added once per other companion already on an enemy. Negative spreads the party out. Distance Penalty Per Metre DistancePenaltyPerMetre float Target Choice EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0 0.1 Engage at Will: subtracted per metre of distance, so the near enemy wins a tie. Target Reconsider Interval TargetReconsiderInterval float Target Choice EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.1, Units=Seconds 1.0 Engage at Will: how often the choice is reconsidered. A dead target is replaced at once regardless.

docs.text:

docs.title: FXenoCorePartyFollowLeaderTaskInstanceData
docs.text:
Struct · header XenoCoreRuntime/Public/AI/XenoCorePartyTravelTasks.h

Tuning and running state for FXenoCorePartyFollowLeaderTask.

Properties

Property C++ name Type Category Specifiers Default Description Trail Distance TrailDistance float Parameter EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, UIMin=0.0 260.0 The distance a member settles at behind a moving leader. Roughly XC1's trailing distance. Per Slot Spacing PerSlotSpacing float Parameter EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, UIMin=0.0 90.0 Added per party slot, so members string out rather than converging on one distance. Arrive Slack ArriveSlack float Parameter EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, UIMin=0.0 60.0 Once the leader has stopped, arrive within TrailDistance + this and hand over to RecalculatePosition. Leader Stopped Speed LeaderStoppedSpeed float Parameter EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, UIMin=0.0 20.0 The leader counts as stopped below this ground speed. Speed Gain SpeedGain float Parameter EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, UIMin=0.0 1.2 Speed correction per unit of distance error: speed = leader speed + Gain x (distance - trail). Catch Up Ratio CatchUpRatio float Parameter › Pace EditAnywhere, ClampMin=1 1.5 Catch-up never runs faster than leader speed x this, plus CatchUpMargin. Catch Up Margin CatchUpMargin float Parameter › Pace EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0, Units=CentimetersPerSecond 120.0 Flat speed added to the catch-up cap on top of leader speed x CatchUpRatio. Arrive Speed ArriveSpeed float Parameter › Pace EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0, Units=CentimetersPerSecond 380.0 The pace a member comes in at once the leader has stopped. Pace Smoothing PaceSmoothing float Parameter › Pace EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.1 3.0 How fast the chosen pace eases toward its target, per second. Lower is smoother and laggier. Min Speed MinSpeed float Parameter EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, UIMin=0.0 180.0 Never slower than this while following. Max Speed MaxSpeed float Parameter EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, UIMin=0.0 850.0 Never faster than this. Above the player's run, so a member that lost ground regains it. Too Close Fraction TooCloseFraction float Parameter EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, ClampMax=1.0, UIMin=0.0, UIMax=1.0 0.55 Closer than TrailDistance x this is too close - e.g. the leader walked back into the member. Hand over to RecalculatePosition rather than push through the leader's capsule. Repath Interval RepathInterval float Parameter EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, UIMin=0.0 0.5 After a failed or finished path, wait this long before asking the pathfinder again.

docs.title: FXenoCorePartyFollowTask
docs.text:
Struct · derives from FStateTreeTaskCommonBase · header XenoCoreRuntime/Public/AI/XenoCorePartyFollowTask.h

The party member's legs in battle, plus the left-behind teleport at all times.

docs.title: FXenoCorePartyFollowTaskInstanceData
docs.text:
Struct · header XenoCoreRuntime/Public/AI/XenoCorePartyFollowTask.h

Tuning and running state for FXenoCorePartyFollowTask.

Properties

Property C++ name Type Category Specifiers Default Description Trail Distance TrailDistance float Parameter EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, UIMin=0.0 260.0 How close a member is content to get to the leader before it stops. Per Slot Spacing PerSlotSpacing float Parameter EditAnywhere, ClampMin=0.0, UIMin=0.0 90.0 Extra spacing added per party slot, so two members do not aim for an identical stopping distance and grind against each other on arrival. Class · derives from UAnimInstance · header XenoCoreRuntime/Public/Animation/XenoCoreFaceAnimInstance.h · Blueprintable

The parent of every VRoid body's runtime ABP (ABP_XenoCore_VRoidRetarget_*). The AnimGraph retargets the invisible Mannequin body's pose onto the VRoid mesh, then a Modify Curve node writes FaceCurves - one wire, the node's CurveMap pin - into the pose. The mesh's VRM4U post-process ABP (ABP_Post_*) turns those curves into morph targets through the model's own POSE_face asset, so the expressions are the ones authored in VRoid Studio.

Properties

Property C++ name Type Category Specifiers Default Description Face Curves FaceCurves TMap<FName, float> XenoCore › Face Transient, BlueprintReadOnly The curve values this frame. Wired to the Modify Curve node's CurveMap pin. Expression Table ExpressionTable TSoftObjectPtr<UDataTable> XenoCore › Face EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly Named expressions, as mixes of face curves. Rule and PlayExpression names are looked up here first. Blink Curve BlinkCurve FName XenoCore › Face › Blink EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly "blink" The face curve the procedural blink drives. Blink Interval Min BlinkIntervalMin float XenoCore › Face › Blink EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.1 2.5 Shortest time between blinks, in seconds. Each gap is rolled between Min and Max. Blink Interval Max BlinkIntervalMax float XenoCore › Face › Blink EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.1 6.0 Longest time between blinks, in seconds. Blink Duration BlinkDuration float XenoCore › Face › Blink EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.05 0.18 Close-and-open time. Real blinks are 0.1-0.4s; under 0.12 the pose asset barely reaches shut. Expression Blend Speed ExpressionBlendSpeed float XenoCore › Face EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.1 6.0 How fast an expression eases in and out, per second. Talking Tag TalkingTag FGameplayTag XenoCore › Face › Mouth EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly While the character's ASC holds this, the mouth cycles MouthShapes. Empty = never talks. Mouth Shapes MouthShapes TArray<FName> XenoCore › Face › Mouth EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly Mouth curves the generic talking flap cycles through. Mouth Shape Interval MouthShapeInterval float XenoCore › Face › Mouth EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.03 0.11 Seconds each mouth shape is held during the talking flap. Mouth Weight MouthWeight float XenoCore › Face › Mouth EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, ClampMax=1 0.6 How far the mouth opens during the talking flap, 0..1. Lip Sync bLipSync bool XenoCore › Face › Lip Sync EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly true Off = voice lines only flap the mouth, ignoring their lip-sync keys. Raise for a model whose mouth shapes read small. The AI controller enemies are possessed by. It carries the enemy's team; the behaviour itself lives in a StateTree on the pawn's StateTree AI component. Set the team before possession: the pawn reads it once, when it is possessed.

Properties

Property C++ name Type Category Specifiers Default Description Detection Interval DetectionInterval float XenoCore › AI › Detection EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.05 0.2 Seconds between detection checks. Running Speed RunningSpeed float XenoCore › AI › Detection EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, Units=CentimetersPerSecond 280.0 Sound detection only hears a leader moving faster than this. Heal On Give Up bHealOnGiveUp bool XenoCore › AI EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly true Restore full health when this enemy gives up a fight. Provoked Give Up Seconds ProvokedGiveUpSeconds float XenoCore › AI EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0 10.0 Seconds a provoked enemy that never engaged waits with nobody in reach before it gives up (and heals). Engage Radius EngageRadius float XenoCore › AI EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0 1600.0 Enemy notices the player inside this. The default for every enemy this controller possesses; an enemy can override it with its own Engage Radius Override. Leash Radius LeashRadius float XenoCore › AI EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0 7000.0 Beyond this distance from home the enemy gives up and walks back. Measured from home, not from the player, so a kited enemy cannot be led across the whole zone. Disengage Radius Scale DisengageRadiusScale float XenoCore › AI EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=1.0 2.5 An engaged enemy stays engaged out to Engage Radius times this, so one standing on the edge does not flicker in and out of the fight. An enemy can override it with its own Disengage Radius Scale Override. Ignore When Levels Below IgnoreWhenLevelsBelow int32 XenoCore › AI EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=1 6 Enemies ignore the party entirely when the leader is this many levels above them, and only fight if attacked first. bAlwaysAggro is the exception for uniques and bosses. Always Aggro bAlwaysAggro bool XenoCore › AI EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly false Skip the level rule: this enemy detects the party whatever the level gap. For uniques and bosses. Team Id TeamId int32 XenoCore › Teams EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly 2 The team every enemy using this controller belongs to. An int32 rather than FGenericTeamId because that is what ULyraTeamSubsystem speaks and what Lyra's team assets are keyed on.

Keeps a squad of enemies alive here and respawns them after they fall, out of the party's sight. One spawner is one squad: its members wander round it, fight together, and only the last kill drops a chest.

Properties

Property C++ name Type Category Specifiers Default Description Members Members TArray<FXenoCoreSpawnerEntry> XenoCore › Spawner EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly What this spawner keeps alive. Mix entries for a mixed squad. Spawn Radius SpawnRadius float XenoCore › Spawner EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, Units=Centimeters 400.0 Members appear at random reachable spots within this of the spawner. Wander Radius WanderRadius float XenoCore › Spawner EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, Units=Centimeters 1200.0 While unprovoked, members wander to random spots this far from the spawner. 0 = they stand where they spawned. Link Aggro bLinkAggro bool XenoCore › Spawner › Squad EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly true Link aggro: when one member is provoked, the others join. Link Radius LinkRadius float XenoCore › Spawner › Squad EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, EditCondition=bLinkAggro, Units=Centimeters 2500.0 Link aggro reaches members within this of the provoked one. 0 = the whole squad wherever it is. Squad Loot Rule bSquadLootRule bool XenoCore › Spawner › Squad EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly true Only the last member killed drops a chest: gold at Squad Gold Multiplier x the odds, else silver, filled from the leader's (first member's) drop table. Squad Gold Multiplier SquadGoldMultiplier float XenoCore › Spawner › Squad EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, EditCondition=bSquadLootRule 3.0 The squad chest's gold chance is the leader's table's Gold Chance times this. XC1: 3. Unique Monster bUniqueMonster bool XenoCore › Spawner › Unique EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly false Make every member a Unique Monster: gold named label, gold chest, ignores the six-level rule. Unique Name UniqueName FText XenoCore › Spawner › Unique EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, EditCondition=bUniqueMonster The Unique Monster's name. Empty keeps the Blueprint's Display Name. Respawn bRespawn bool XenoCore › Spawner › Respawn EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly true Bring fallen members back. Off = they stay dead until the spawner streams out and in again. Respawn Delay RespawnDelay float XenoCore › Spawner › Respawn EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=1.0, EditCondition=bRespawn, Units=Seconds 90.0 Seconds after a member falls before it may come back. XC1's uniques: 0.3. Behind Camera Min Distance BehindCameraMinDistance float XenoCore › Spawner › Respawn EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, EditCondition=bRespawn, Units=Centimeters 1800.0 Closer than Hidden Distance, a respawn is allowed only behind the camera and beyond this. Poll Interval PollInterval float XenoCore › Spawner › Respawn EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=0.1 1.0 Seconds between respawn checks. Crowd Avoidance Quality CrowdAvoidanceQuality EXenoCoreCrowdQuality XenoCore › AI › Crowd EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite EXenoCoreCrowdQuality::Low Detour Crowd sampling quality while it is on. Measured: higher qualities wobble more, not less. Falls back to the actor's eye height when the actor has no such socket. Native rather than added per Blueprint so it can never be missing. docs.title: UXenoCoreSaveSubsystem
docs.text:
Class · derives from UGameInstanceSubsystem · header XenoCoreRuntime/Public/Save/XenoCoreSaveSubsystem.h

Same rule as GetPartyInventory, GetPartyQuests and GetTargetModeAbility: one resolver, and everything else goes through it. Nothing else names a slot, writes a file, or decides whether a load is in progress.

Events you can bind

Event Type Description OnSaveWritten FXenoCoreSaveWritten Broadcast when a save finishes writing, with the slot and whether it succeeded. OnSaveStarted FXenoCoreSaveStarted Broadcast when a save begins writing. OnSaveRestored FXenoCoreSaveRestored Broadcast once a loaded save has been applied to the world. OnSaveLoaded FXenoCoreSaveLoaded Broadcast once a loaded save has been fully applied, with the slot it came from.

Blueprint functions

Node Kind Signature Description Get Pure UXenoCoreSaveSubsystem* Get() The one resolver. Get Slot Name Pure FString GetSlotName(int32 SlotIndex) "XenoCore_Auto" or "XenoCore_01".."XenoCore_03". Load All Slots Callable TArray<UXenoCoreSaveGame*> LoadAllSlots() Reads every slot's file so the list screen can draw its rows. Load Slot Callable UXenoCoreSaveGame* LoadSlot(int32 SlotIndex) One slot, or null when it is empty. Save To Slot Callable bool SaveToSlot(int32 SlotIndex) Captures the world and writes it to a slot, asynchronously. Request Autosave Callable bool RequestAutosave(const FString& Reason) Writes to the autosave slot. Delete Slot Callable bool DeleteSlot(int32 SlotIndex) Deletes a slot's file. Can Save Now Pure bool CanSaveNow() const True when a save is allowed right now; false in combat or under a menu. Is Save In Progress Pure bool IsSaveInProgress() const True while a write is actually in flight. Is Autosave In Progress Pure bool IsAutosaveInProgress() const Which slot the in-flight write is going to, or NoSlotIndex when nothing is being written. Load From Slot Callable bool LoadFromSlot(int32 SlotIndex) Loads a slot: stashes it, then travels to its map. Is Restoring From Save Pure bool IsRestoringFromSave() const Starting inventory and starting equipment are seeded from the ASC-ready delegate on every pawn's first body, and the roster is seeded from StartingRoster in BeginPlay. Was World Loaded From Save Pure bool WasWorldLoadedFromSave() const True for the whole life of a world that was loaded from a save. Begin New Game Callable void BeginNewGame() Starting a new game: forget that anything was ever loaded, so seeding runs normally again. Restore Pending Save Callable void RestorePendingSave(APlayerController* PlayerController) Applies the pending save to the world, in the one order that works. Get Loaded Slot Index Pure int32 GetLoadedSlotIndex() const The slot this game was last loaded from, or NoSlotIndex (the lowest int32) if none. Register Save Participant Callable void RegisterSaveParticipant(UObject* Participant, FName SaveKey = NAME_None) Adds an actor, component or object to the save. Unregister Save Participant Callable void UnregisterSaveParticipant(UObject* Participant) Removes a participant from the save, keeping what it last held. Forget Save Record Callable bool ForgetSaveRecord(FName SaveKey) No description. Has Save Record Pure bool HasSaveRecord(FName SaveKey) const True when a record is held under this key. Get Play Time Seconds Pure float GetPlayTimeSeconds() const Seconds of play in this save, across sessions. Format Play Time Pure FText FormatPlayTime(float Seconds) Play time as XC1 prints it: "1:55". Has Unsaved Progress Pure bool HasUnsavedProgress() const Has anything been played since the last save, autosave or load? Capture Thumbnail Callable void CaptureThumbnail() Grab the world as it looks right now, for the next save's slot picture. Set Location Text Callable void SetLocationText(const FString& Location) The location and story line the slot row prints. Set Story Text Callable void SetStoryText(const FString& Story) Overrides UXenoCoreSaveSettings::DefaultStoryText. Get Current Location Text Pure FString GetCurrentLocationText() const What a save written now would print for its location: the override, else the map's name, else empty. Get Current Story Text Pure FString GetCurrentStoryText() const What a save written now would print for its story line.

docs.title: FXenoCoreSkillEntry
docs.text:
Struct · header XenoCoreRuntime/Public/Skills/XenoCoreSkillTypes.h · BlueprintType

One skill. It does its work in up to three ways, each optional, all driven by one Value: - Stats - always on while it reaches the body (Equipment Master: Weight -5). - Bonus - a percentage another system asks for (Healing Wisdom: healing +15 %). - Ability - behaviour, a UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_Skill child (Underdog: a buff at battle start). The skill counterpart of an art: data pointing at behaviour, and most skills need no behaviour.

Properties

Property C++ name Type Category Specifiers Default Description Display Name DisplayName FText Skill EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly The skill's name in the Skills menu and the "Skill Learnt" popup. Description Description FText Skill EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly May contain {Value}, filled from Value - "Reduces equipment weight by {Value}." Shape Shape EXenoCoreSkillShape Skill EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly EXenoCoreSkillShape::Circle The frame the skill's icon is drawn in. Timing Timing EXenoCoreSkillTiming Skill EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly EXenoCoreSkillTiming::Always Always applies, or only while the owner is in the battle party (the icon's colour). Scope Scope EXenoCoreSkillScope Skill EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly EXenoCoreSkillScope::Self Who the skill reaches: its owner, the battle party, or the whole party (the icon's glyph). Value Value float Skill › Effect EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly 0.0 XC1's "Effect Value" - what Stats add, what a Bonus is worth, what an Ability reads. Duration Duration float Skill › Effect EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0 0.0 Seconds, for a timed skill (XC1's "time" column) - read by its Ability. 0 for none. Stats Stats TArray<FXenoCoreSkillStatMod> Skill › Effect EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly Stats raised by Value while the skill reaches the body. Resilient Warrior raises two. Condition Condition EXenoCoreSkillCondition Skill › Effect EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly EXenoCoreSkillCondition::Always When the Stats hold. Always for most skills; re-checked as HP and armour change. Condition Threshold ConditionThreshold float Skill › Effect EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, ClampMax=100.0, EditCondition=Condition == EXenoCoreSkillCondition::HealthAtOrBelow || Condition == EXenoCoreSkillCondition::HealthAtOrAbove 50.0 Percent of max HP, for the two health conditions. Chance Chance float Skill › Effect EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, ClampMax=100.0 100.0 Percent chance an Ability's trigger actually fires - XC1's "75% chance" (Hero's Valour). 100 = always. Bonus Bonus FGameplayTag Skill › Effect EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Categories=XenoCore.SkillBonus A percentage another system asks for - UXenoCoreProgressionComponent::GetSkillBonus. Quest EXP and healing ask today; a buyer's system asks with its own tag, and no skill code changes. Ability Ability TSubclassOf<UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_Skill> Skill › Effect EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly Behaviour - granted to the body while the skill reaches it. A UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_Skill child. SP Cost Override SPCostOverride int32 Skill › Advanced EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=-1 -1 SP to learn this one skill. -1 (the default) uses the branch's cost curve; anything else replaces it. Link Cost LinkCost int32 Skill › Advanced EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0 0 Not implemented yet: the Affinity Coins another character pays to link this. Read by nothing.

docs.title: UXenoCoreGameplayAbility_TargetMode
docs.text:
Class · derives from ULyraGameplayAbility · header XenoCoreRuntime/Public/Targeting/XenoCoreTargetModeAbility.h · abstract

The base for GA_XenoCore_TargetMode. It exists to hold the selected target and to be the only thing that writes it - everything else about the mode (input, indicator, the poll) is Blueprint in the child.

Properties

Property C++ name Type Category Specifiers Default Description Current Target CurrentTarget TObjectPtr<AActor> XenoCore › Targeting BlueprintReadOnly, Transient nullptr Transient on purpose. Target Indicator Material TargetIndicatorMaterial TObjectPtr<UMaterialInterface> XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly The indicator drawn on the targeted enemy - XC1 marks the enemy itself, not the ground. Target Acquired Sound TargetAcquiredSound TObjectPtr<USoundBase> XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly Played each time a target is acquired or cycled to. Null is legal and silent. Target Indicator Size TargetIndicatorSize float XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=0.0, UIMin=0.0 250.0 Size of the quad in world units - not of the diamond, which is drawn inside it. Strafe While Locked bStrafeWhileLocked bool XenoCore › TargetMode EditDefaultsOnly true No description. Strafe Max Range StrafeMaxRange float XenoCore › TargetMode EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=0.0 400.0 Beyond it the pawn returns to orient-to-movement and free-roam locomotion, even though the lock is still held. Strafe Range Release Scale StrafeRangeReleaseScale float XenoCore › TargetMode EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=1.0 1.2 Hysteresis, so standing exactly on the boundary does not flip facing every frame. Retreat Dot Threshold RetreatDotThreshold float XenoCore › TargetMode EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=-1.0, ClampMax=0.0 -0.9 How directly the player must be moving away from the target before facing locks to it. Strafe Stationary Speed StrafeStationarySpeed float XenoCore › TargetMode EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=0.0 20.0 Below this speed the player counts as standing still, and keeps facing the target. Target Indicator Height Fraction TargetIndicatorHeightFraction float XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly 0.35 Height above the target's origin, as a fraction of its capsule half-height. Lock Acquire Range LockAcquireRange float XenoCore › Targeting › Range EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, Units=cm 3000.0 No description. Lock Keep Range LockKeepRange float XenoCore › Targeting › Range EditDefaultsOnly, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0.0, Units=cm 3000.0 Must be at least Lock Acquire Range; set it higher so a target at the edge is not dropped the moment it steps back. Target Indicator Screen Space Size bTargetIndicatorScreenSpaceSize bool XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly false Keep the indicator the same size on screen regardless of distance. Offscreen Arrow Material OffscreenArrowMaterial TObjectPtr<UMaterialInterface> XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly The arrows drawn at the screen edge when the target is off screen, pointing back at it. Arrow Screen Edge Inset ArrowScreenEdgeInset float XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=0.0, ClampMax=1.0, UIMin=0.0, UIMax=1.0 0.88 How far in from the viewport edge the arrows sit, as a fraction of half-width/height. Arrow Camera Distance ArrowCameraDistance float XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=1.0, UIMin=1.0 200.0 Distance in front of the camera to place the arrows. Size is scaled with it. Arrow Screen Size Fraction ArrowScreenSizeFraction float XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=0.0, UIMin=0.0 0.16 Apparent size, as a fraction of ArrowCameraDistance. Invert Arrow Direction bInvertArrowDirection bool XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly false Flips which way the chevrons point, if the plane's UVs run the other way. Offscreen Arrow Mesh OffscreenArrowMesh TObjectPtr<UStaticMesh> XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly Plane the arrows are drawn on. Engine unit plane unless overridden. Target Plate Class TargetPlateClass TSubclassOf<UXenoCoreTargetPlateBase> XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly The top-centre badge naming the target. Owned here for the same reason the diamond and the arrows are: it is part of the lock, so its lifetime is the lock's lifetime and it cannot be left on screen by a path that forgot to clear it. Player Plate Class PlayerPlateClass TSubclassOf<UXenoCorePlayerPlateBase> XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly The upper-left player readout. Arts Palette Class ArtsPaletteClass TSubclassOf<UXenoCoreArtsPaletteBase> XenoCore › Targeting EditDefaultsOnly The arts palette. Same lifetime as the badge and the player plate. Approach Timeout ApproachTimeout float XenoCore › Targeting › Approach EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=0.1 4.0 Give up running in after this long - an unreachable target must not hold the input forever. Approach Arrive Margin ApproachArriveMargin float XenoCore › Targeting › Approach EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=0.0 60.0 Stop this far inside the art's Distance before striking, so the target stepping back during the windup still leaves it within reach plus the contact tolerance. Approach Stick Cancel ApproachStickCancel float XenoCore › Targeting › Approach EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=0.0, ClampMax=1.0 0.35 Pushing the stick past this during a run hands control back: the run ends and nothing is cast - no cooldown, no gauge. Approach Move Action ApproachMoveAction TSoftObjectPtr<class UInputAction> XenoCore › Targeting › Approach EditDefaultsOnly The move action whose value is read to tell the player's stick from the run's own steering. Camera Focus Duration CameraFocusDuration float XenoCore › TargetMode EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=0.0 0.3 Seconds the focus takes. Zero disables it entirely. Strafe Evaluate Interval StrafeEvaluateInterval float XenoCore › TargetMode EditDefaultsOnly, ClampMin=0.01 0.05 Poll interval. Facing interpolates at RotationRate, so this need not be per-frame.

docs.title: Curve tables
docs.text:
Designer · reference · No code

XenoCore keeps its level-driven numbers in five curve tables in Battle/Attributes/. Each row is a curve: the X axis is a level (or a level difference) and the value is read at that X. Nothing in C++ holds these numbers, so balancing is a data job.

Table X axis What reads it What it controls CT_XenoCore_PartyStatlines Character level Each sample character's own stats effect (GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_Kael ... _Tamsin) That character's Max HP, Strength, Ether, Agility: rows <Name>.<Stat>, read at ×1.0 CT_XenoCore_BaseStats Character level The stock members' stats effects (GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_Shulk, _Party_*) Their Max HP, Strength, Ether, Agility: shared rows with a coefficient per character CT_XenoCore_EnemyStats Enemy level The enemy stats effects (GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_Minion_Melee, _Minion_Skirmisher, _Minion_Bulwark, _Minion_Brute, GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_Dummy; the other types scale the same rows by a multiplier on their effect), and the enemy's Experience Level Scale Enemy Max HP, Strength, Ether, Agility, defences; how kill EXP grows with the enemy's level CT_XenoCore_RewardLevelDiff Party level minus enemy level Game/BP_XenoCore_Progression › Reward Multiplier Curve EXP multiplier for a kill CT_XenoCore_DamageLevelDiff Attacker level minus target level Battle/Attributes/BP_XenoCoreDamageExecution › Level Difference Curve Damage multiplier by level gap

EXP needed per level is not a curve table

It is the Data Table Game/DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves, one row per curve, picked per character. See Tune levelling.

docs.title: How a table is read
docs.text:
There are two ways, and they fail differently.

Stats tables (BaseStats, EnemyStats). A stats Gameplay Effect has one modifier per attribute. Each modifier's magnitude is a scalable float: a number multiplied by a curve-table row evaluated at the effect's level. The character's level is passed as the effect level, so the row is read at that level. The effect is picked per character by the pawn's Stats Effect property (XenoCore › Combatant on party pawns, XenoCore › Enemy on enemies).

Fails silently: the number in the table is not always the number in the game

A scalable float multiplies its curve by its own coefficient. If the coefficient is not 1.0, the game uses a different number from the one you see in the table, and nothing says so. The shipped minion types use this on purpose: the melee minion reads its rows at 1.0, and the Brute (1.45), Bulwark (1.15) and Skirmisher (0.9) scale the same rows. Before you rebalance a row, open the effect that reads it and check the coefficient on each modifier.

Lookup tables (RewardLevelDiff, DamageLevelDiff). C++ looks the row up by name on the table assigned in a Blueprint (Reward Multiplier Curve, Level Difference Curve) and evaluates it at X.

If… You get Logged? The table property is empty Reward and damage multipliers read 1.0. No The table is set but the row name is wrong Same fallbacks as above Yes, a warning naming the row

Fails silently: an empty curve property

If Reward Multiplier Curve is cleared, every kill pays its flat reward. If Level Difference Curve is cleared, level gaps stop affecting damage. Neither logs anything. Keep a table assigned, even if you flatten its values.

docs.title: The rows
docs.text: Row names must match exactly: C++ or the stats effects refer to them by name.

docs.title: CT_XenoCore_BaseStats
docs.text:
Shulk.MaxHealth
Shulk.Strength
Shulk.Ether
Shulk.Agility

One set of rows, read by every stock party member's stats effect (GE_XenoCore_BaseStats_Shulk and the eleven _Party_* effects). Members differ only through their own stats effect: each _Party_* effect multiplies the same rows by its own coefficient per stat (between 0.8 and 1.2 when last measured), so the number in the table is not the number that member gets.

Scheduled for renaming

These row names are placeholders and will be renamed before release. When that happens every stats effect that reads them is updated in the same change. If you add your own character, add your own rows (for example MyHero.Strength) rather than editing these.

Physical and Ether Defence, critical rate and block rate are not in this table: party members have none of their own, and all of it comes from equipment.

docs.title: CT_XenoCore_EnemyStats
docs.text:
Minion_Melee.MaxHealth      Minion_Melee.Strength     Minion_Melee.Ether
Minion_Melee.Agility        Minion_Melee.PhysicalDefence  Minion_Melee.EtherDefence
Minion_Melee.CharacterLevel
Minion_Ranged.*   Minion_Siege.*   Minion_Super.*   (same seven stats each)
Minion.ExperienceScale

Enemy stats grow linearly with level. The melee minion's HP and Strength follow an XC1 field enemy's line (Max HP 900 + 100 × (level − 1), Strength 69 + 10 × (level − 1)). Only the Minion_Melee.* rows are read by a shipped stats effect: all seven sample enemy types read them, through their effect's multiplier. The Minion_Ranged, Minion_Siege and Minion_Super rows are not read by anything. *.CharacterLevel is not read by any effect.

Minion.ExperienceScale is read by the minion's Experience Level Scale (XenoCore › Enemy): the kill's Experience Reward is multiplied by this row at the enemy's level, so a same-level kill is worth about the same share of a level all the way up. An enemy with the property empty pays a flat reward.

Defence means different things on the two sides

On an enemy, PhysicalDefence and EtherDefence are fractions (0 to 0.9): damage is multiplied by 1 − defence. On a party member the same attributes are flat points subtracted from the attacker's stat. Author enemy defence rows as fractions. The execution clamps a fraction to Max Defence Fraction (default 0.9).

docs.title: The level cap
docs.text:
The level cap is not any table's length: it is MaxCharacterLevel on UXenoCoreStatSet, default 99. It is a config value, so you can raise it without touching C++. Add this to your project's Config/DefaultGame.ini:

[/Script/XenoCoreRuntime.XenoCoreStatSet]
MaxCharacterLevel=120

Then extend the stats rows to the new cap (past its last key a stats curve holds its final value), and lengthen every row of the Data Table DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves. A character whose EXP row is shorter than the cap stops levelling at the end of the list; validating the table warns about a row shorter than the cap.

docs.title: CT_XenoCore_RewardLevelDiff
docs.text:
Reward.LevelDiffMultiplier

X is party level minus enemy level. A positive X (you out-level the enemy) should give a multiplier below 1; a negative X above 1. Keys run from −20 to +20; outside that the curve's end values hold.

docs.title: CT_XenoCore_DamageLevelDiff
docs.text:
Damage.LevelDiff.Physical
Damage.LevelDiff.Ether

X is attacker level minus target level. The execution picks the Ether row for ether attacks and the Physical row otherwise, and multiplies damage by the result.

docs.title: Editing a table
docs.text:
1. Duplicate the table into your own folder, for example Content/MyGame/Data/.
  2. Open the duplicate. Edit values in the curve table editor, or add rows with the same naming pattern.
  3. Point the reader at your duplicate: the stats effect's modifiers, or the Blueprint property in the table above.

Keep row names when you duplicate

The lookup tables are found by row name (Reward.LevelDiffMultiplier, Damage.LevelDiff.Physical, Damage.LevelDiff.Ether). A duplicate with renamed rows falls back to the defaults above, with only a warning in the log.

The shipped tables were imported from CSV files that are not part of the template, so Reimport will not find a source. Unreal then asks whether to specify a new source file: Yes lets you pick your own CSV, No skips the reimport. Edit the tables in the editor, or export to CSV and reimport from your own file.

This page is written by Docs/Manual/tools/gen_reference.py from the plugin's headers. Edit the source comment and re-run the generator instead. See Docs/Manual/tools/README.md.

The data asset types a designer creates and fills in, and the three item fragments that go on an item definition. To make a new one, right-click in the Content Browser, choose Data › Data Asset, and pick the class from the list.

Duplicate, don't start blank

For item definitions especially, duplicate a working shipped asset into your own folder (Content/MyGame/...) rather than creating an empty one. A blank asset has none of the links the shipped ones carry, and several of those fail without an error.

Weak Level Gap WeakLevelGap int32 Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0 3 Battle start reads "weak" when the nearest enemy is at least this many levels below the speaker. Low Health Fraction LowHealthFraction float Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, ClampMax=1 0.3 A party member says LowHP when a hit takes them below this fraction of their max HP. Enemy Low Health Fraction EnemyLowHealthFraction float Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, ClampMax=1 0.25 Enemy.Low is said when a party hit takes the enemy below this fraction of its max HP. Close Victory Health Fraction CloseVictoryHealthFraction float Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, ClampMax=1 0.25 A win is Close when someone was downed in the fight, or the leader ends below this fraction of max HP. Victory Line Delay VictoryLineDelay float Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, Units=s 1.2 Delay after the win before the victory line, so it lands over the fanfare's tail rather than its first note. Field Banter Interval FieldBanterInterval float Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, Units=s 20.0 How often out-of-battle banter is considered. The Field rules decide whether anything is said. Field Scenery Chance FieldSceneryChance float Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, ClampMax=1 0.3 Of the idle remarks, the share that are about the scenery (Field.Scenery) instead. Field Exchange Chance FieldExchangeChance float Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, ClampMax=1 0.35 Chance a banter tick is a two-person exchange (Field.Exchange, then Field.Reply) rather than a remark. Field Watch Interval FieldWatchInterval float Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, Units=s 1.0 How often the party looks around for enemies and stragglers (Field.EnemySighted, Field.WaitUp). 0 = never. Enemy Sighted Radius EnemySightedRadius float Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, Units=cm 2500.0 An enemy, not yet fighting, this close to the leader is announced once (Field.EnemySighted). Wait Up Distance WaitUpDistance float Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, Units=cm 1500.0 A companion this far behind a moving leader calls out (Field.WaitUp). Reinforcement After Seconds ReinforcementAfterSeconds float Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, Units=s 5.0 An enemy engaging this long after the fight started counts as reinforcements (Enemy.Reinforcement). Aid Given Chance AidGivenChance float Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, ClampMax=1 0.5 Of heal and buff casts, the share that say an Aid.Given line ("Hang on, I've got you!") instead of the art's name. Field Travel Speed FieldTravelSpeed float Triggers EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, Units=cm/s 150.0 Above this leader speed the party is travelling (Field.Travel), below it idle (Field.Idle). Exchange Max Distance ExchangeMaxDistance float Who Is Speaking EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, Units=cm 500.0 Two members further apart than this are never paired for a Field.Exchange. 0 = any distance. Listener Glance Chance ListenerGlanceChance float Who Is Speaking EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ClampMin=0, ClampMax=1 0.6 The chance each of those companions does glance at the speaker. docs.title: Editor tools
docs.text:
Programmer · reference · C++

Designers: the two things on this page you will use

  • Tools › XenoCore › Apply XenoCore Project Settings writes the project settings XenoCore needs. Run it once after installing, and again if a recipe tells you to. It never overwrites a setting you changed yourself. See Project setup.
  • Save-time checks: saving an Art definition or a pawn Blueprint can show an error or warning in the Message Log. The messages are listed in Save-time checks.

That is the whole menu: XenoCore adds one entry to Tools. Everything else on this page is a Blueprint function library for programmers automating the editor.

XenoCore has a second C++ module, XenoCoreEditor, declared with type Editor in XenoCore.uplugin. It never loads in a packaged game. It holds Blueprint function libraries that automate editor tasks the engine's own scripting cannot reach: building anim-layer graphs, camera rigs, Gameplay Effect tag requirements and so on. It also holds the project setup that writes the settings XenoCore needs into your project (below), and two save-time asset checks. Apart from project setup, you don't need any of it to use the template.

docs.title: How to call them
docs.text:
Every function is a static BlueprintCallable on a UBlueprintFunctionLibrary, so you can call it from:

  • Editor Utility Blueprints and Editor Utility Widgets. Search the node name in the graph.
  • Python in the editor (Tools › Execute Python Script, or the Output Log in Python mode). Unreal exposes each library as unreal.<ClassName minus the U> with snake-case functions, for example:
import unreal
print(unreal.XenoCoreMapTools.get_default_gameplay_experience(
    unreal.load_asset("/XenoCore/Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym")))

Never call these from gameplay Blueprints

The module is editor-only and is not part of a packaged game, so a gameplay Blueprint that calls one of these nodes cannot work in a packaged build. Use them only from Editor Utility assets and Python.

Every function's full signature is listed in C++ classes › XenoCoreEditor.

docs.title: The libraries
docs.text:
Library Header What it does UXenoCoreAITools XenoCoreAITools.h Builds the companion combat-spot and positional-spot EQS queries, whose options cannot be set from script. UXenoCoreAnimLayerTools XenoCoreAnimLayerTools.h Builds and inspects Animation Blueprints from script: declares layers on an anim layer interface, adds linked-layer, slot, sequence-player, inertialization and stride-warping nodes to any named graph, wires node pins to variables, rewires state-machine transitions, sets a state's random sequence player, repoints blend spaces, reads and writes node comments, and describes a state machine or a child anim Blueprint's overrides as text. UXenoCoreCameraTools XenoCoreCameraTools.h Builds Gameplay Cameras rigs: creates camera nodes, sets the root node and a sequence's children, creates enter and exit transitions, builds the rig and reports its status, and describes a rig's node tree and transitions. UXenoCoreCosmeticTools XenoCoreCosmeticTools.h Fills in and describes a pawn Blueprint's cosmetic body-mesh rules (which body mesh each cosmetic tag picks). UXenoCoreEnvironmentTools XenoCoreEnvironmentTools.h Builds the procedural terrain, rock, bark and canopy materials, and the scanned-rock material. UXenoCoreGameplayEffectTools XenoCoreGameplayEffectTools.h Sets the tags a Gameplay Effect grants and the tags its target must or must not have, and reads them back. UXenoCoreMapTools XenoCoreMapTools.h Reads and sets which Experience a map opens with, and creates a landscape from a 16-bit greyscale heightmap. UXenoCoreMaterialTools XenoCoreMaterialTools.h Describes a material's wiring as text, and cuts a root input or a named expression input. UXenoCoreMinimapTools XenoCoreMinimapTools.h Builds the minimap disc material M_XenoCore_Minimap. UXenoCoreNiagaraTools XenoCoreNiagaraTools.h Lists and sets every colour constant in a Niagara system whose name contains a given string, across all emitters. Useful for recolouring an effect in one call. UXenoCoreProjectSetup XenoCoreProjectSetup.h Lists, applies and reports conflicts for the project settings XenoCore needs. See below. UXenoCoreReleaseTools XenoCoreReleaseTools.h Reads and sets an asset's preview mesh and a skeleton's preview attachments without loading them. Used to keep editor previews from pulling in development content. UXenoCoreSkyTools XenoCoreSkyTools.h Builds the night-sky star and moon materials and the rain streak material. UXenoCoreStateTreeTools XenoCoreStateTreeTools.h Recompiles a State Tree asset, which scripts cannot otherwise do after editing one.

Headers are in Plugins/GameFeatures/XenoCore/Source/XenoCoreEditor/Public/.

docs.title: Most useful to a buyer
docs.text:
Task Call Point a new map at XenoCore's Experience from a script UXenoCoreMapTools::SetDefaultGameplayExperience Recolour a copied Niagara effect UXenoCoreNiagaraTools::ListColorConstants, then SetColorConstants Add a status effect's granted tag from a batch script UXenoCoreGameplayEffectTools::SetGrantedTags Rebuild a State Tree after a scripted edit UXenoCoreStateTreeTools::CompileStateTree Check what a per-weapon anim layer overrides UXenoCoreAnimLayerTools::DescribeParentAssetOverrides

Verify scripted edits

A scripted edit can report success and still not reach disk. After any script that changes assets, save, then re-open the asset (or run a second script that reads it back) before trusting the result. The Describe… functions exist for exactly that.

docs.title: Project setup
docs.text:
UXenoCoreProjectSetup writes the settings a Lyra project needs to run XenoCore into the project's own Config/Default*.ini files. It never overwrites a value you have set yourself; it lists it as a conflict in the Output Log under LogXenoSetup. Run it any of three ways:

  • the notification that appears when the editor opens, while any step is pending;
  • Tools › XenoCore › Apply XenoCore Project Settings;
  • the console: XenoCore.ProjectSetup lists what is pending, XenoCore.ProjectSetup apply writes it.

The full list of settings is in Install › What Apply changes.

docs.title: Save-time checks
docs.text:
Two validators in this module run when you save an asset, and when you right-click an asset or folder and choose Validate Assets:

Check Runs on What it reports Art cooldown tags Every Art definition Error: "Cooldown Tag … is also used by …. Arts sharing a tag share one cooldown". Give each Art its own tag. (An Art with a cooldown and no tag at all is reported by the Art definition's own check.) Body meshes Pawn Blueprints with cosmetic body-mesh rules Warning: "Body Meshes has no Default Mesh", "Mesh Rules[n] has no Mesh", or a cosmetic part "matches no Body Meshes rule". Error when that part would make the pawn "INVISIBLE": add a rule for its tags, or set a Default Mesh

Many runtime assets (shop and trade tables, drop tables, member definitions, experience curves, Art definitions) carry their own checks, which run the same way. Each recipe lists the messages for its asset.

docs.title: Development scripts are not part of the template
docs.text: The repository that XenoCore is developed in has a Tools/ folder at its root, full of Python and shell scripts used to author the shipped assets. Those scripts are internal: they assume the developer's machine, a running editor bridge, and specific asset states. They are not supported, not documented, and not needed to use or extend the template. The package you receive holds only the plugin folder, so Tools/ is not in it.

docs.title: Removing the module
docs.text: If you do not want the editor tools, you can remove the XenoCoreEditor entry from XenoCore.uplugin's Modules list and delete Source/XenoCoreEditor. Nothing in the runtime module depends on it: its build file does not list XenoCoreEditor, and no shipped asset references it. You lose project setup (Tools › XenoCore) and the save-time checks with it.

docs.title: Folder map
docs.text:
All · reference · No code

Every folder in the XenoCore plugin's content, what it holds, and whether you can remove it when you replace the sample. In the Content Browser this is Plugins › XenoCore Content (turn on Show Plugin Content first). On disk it is Plugins/GameFeatures/XenoCore/Content/ in your project.

Kind tells you what removing a folder costs:

  • Framework: bases, shared effects and screens the systems need. Keep it. Duplicate from it.
  • Sample: example content that shows the framework working. Replace it with your own, then delete it once nothing of yours references it.

docs.title: Where is…?
docs.text:
The settings designers reach for most, and the one asset each lives on. Paths are inside XenoCore Content.

I want to change… Open Who is in the party at the start, how many fight, the leader Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party › Class Defaults Revive cost, recovery between fights, the defeat beat Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party › Class Defaults EXP per level Game/DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves Art slots, Art Points, starting gold, benched EXP Game/BP_XenoCore_Progression › Class Defaults One character's stats, Arts, AI pacing, portrait Its member definition, Characters/VRoid/<Name>/PartyMember_VRoid_* A character's learnset Characters/Party/Learnsets/DT_XenoCore_ArtLearnset_<Name> An Art Battle/Arts/DA_XenoCore_<Art> Lock-on range, strafing, the target marker Battle/Targeting/GA_XenoCore_TargetMode › Class Defaults Auto-attack speed and reach Battle/GA_XenoCore_AutoAttack › Class Defaults When enemies notice, chase and give up Characters/Enemies/Core/BP_AIC_XenoCore_Enemy › Class Defaults Enemy stats by level Battle/Attributes/CT_XenoCore_EnemyStats What an enemy drops Inventory/Loot/DA_XenoCore_Drops_* What a shop sells Shop/DA_XenoCore_Shop_* Item rarity colours UserInterface/Items/DT_XenoCore_ItemRarities Tutorial cards UserInterface/Tutorials/DT_XenoCore_Tutorials Which screen opens for the shop, save, quests… Project Settings › Game › XenoCore UI The new-game map, starting roster override, music, sounds Project Settings › Game › XenoCore Content A map's music, minimap and weather Actors placed in that map: XenoCore Area Music, XenoCore Map Area, XenoCore Environment Director

Delete with the reference viewer, not by eye

A folder marked Sample can still be referenced by a framework asset (an ability set that grants a sample art, a party roster that lists a sample member). Before deleting, right-click the folder › Reference Viewer, or use Delete and read the list of referencing assets the editor shows you. See Replace the sample content.

docs.title: Gameplay messages
docs.text:
Programmer · reference · No code

XenoCore announces changes through Lyra's Gameplay Message Router: a sender broadcasts a payload struct on a gameplay-tag channel, and any number of listeners receive it without knowing who sent it. This is how the HUD, menus and quests stay up to date. For the idea behind it, see Events and messages.

To listen from a Blueprint, use Lyra's Listen for Gameplay Messages latent node, set Channel to the tag and Payload Type to the struct below. From C++, use UGameplayMessageSubsystem::Get(this).RegisterListener(...) and keep the returned handle so you can unregister in EndPlay or NativeDestruct. Every payload struct is BlueprintType.

docs.title: Rules and traps
docs.text:
Fails silently: Lyra's own inventory message never fires here

Lyra's Lyra.Inventory.Message.StackChanged is only sent from network-replication callbacks. XenoCore is single-player, so it never arrives. Listen to XenoCore.Inventory.Message.Changed instead.

Changing the bag behind XenoCore's back

UXenoCoreInventoryStatics (the XenoCore › Inventory nodes) sends the inventory message directly. A change made through Lyra's inventory manager is noticed by UXenoCoreInventoryWatchSubsystem, which sends the same message for it one frame later and logs it to LogXenoBagWatch. So listeners still hear it, but a frame late, and with none of the statics' protections (carry caps, never removing a worn item). The message's Owner is then the controller that owns the bag.

Screens should re-read, not accumulate

Several messages carry only "something changed". Treat every message as a prompt to re-read the owning component, never as a delta to add up. A running total drifts the first time a change arrives without a message.

  • Add your own channel rather than reusing one: each XenoCore channel has one sender by design, so listeners can trust where it came from. Declare the tag in your own tag file and your own payload struct.
  • Unregister in EndPlay or NativeDestruct. A widget that is pooled and re-shown should register once, not on every show.

docs.title: Gameplay tags
docs.text:
Designer · reference · No code

Generated from source — do not edit by hand.

This page is written by Docs/Manual/tools/gen_reference.py from the plugin's headers. Edit the source comment and re-run the generator instead. See Docs/Manual/tools/README.md.

Every gameplay tag XenoCore declares. There are two kinds:

  • Native tags are declared in C++ (XenoCoreGameplayTags.h / .cpp) because code names them. C++ uses the symbol in the C++ symbol column, for example XenoCoreGameplayTags::Status_XenoCore_InBattle.
  • Ini tags are declared in the plugin's Config/Tags/XenoCoreTags.ini because only data (abilities, input data, state trees) picks them.

Both kinds appear in the editor's tag picker. Matching is hierarchical: a check for Status.XenoCore.Reaction also matches Status.XenoCore.Reaction.Break.

Fails silently: a tag declared twice, or renamed

Declare a new tag in one place only. If C++ looks a tag up by its string name and the tag is later renamed, the lookup returns an empty tag. Nothing is logged; the feature that depends on the tag simply stops. Add your own tags to your own tag .ini or native file, and never edit XenoCore's in place.

170 native tags, 99 ini tags.

The palette matches granted abilities against this to build its row, so adding an art needs no HUD edit - only an Ability.XenoCore.Art.* asset tag. This is the lookup handle: match this asset tag and take Spec.GetPrimaryInstance(). Ability.XenoCore.Art.Topple native Ability_XenoCore_Art_Topple Inflicts Topple. Green. docs.title: GameplayCue
docs.text: Tag Declared C++ symbol Description GameplayCue.XenoCore.DamageTaken ini XenoCore's copy of Lyra's GCNL_Character_DamageTaken, adapted for pawn instigators, ally hits and crits shown as weak-spot hits. GE_XenoCore_Damage fires it; Lyra's own cue stays untouched for Lyra's weapons. GameplayCue.XenoCore.Heal native GameplayCue_XenoCore_Heal The blue bloom on a heal. Executed on the ally - the effect belongs where the HP went, not on the caster - and the cue notify lives in Content/GameplayCues/ because that is the plugin's registered cue path. GameplayCue.XenoCore.Hit native GameplayCue_XenoCore_Hit Cosmetic feedback for a landed hit - camera shake and force feedback. Invoked with explicit cue parameters so Instigator is populated, which the GE-driven cue path never does. GameplayCue.XenoCore.Hit.Blocked native GameplayCue_XenoCore_Hit_Blocked Particles on a blocked hit, on the defender. GameplayCue.XenoCore.Hit.Evaded native GameplayCue_XenoCore_Hit_Evaded Particles on an evaded hit, on the defender. GameplayCue.XenoCore.LevelUp native GameplayCue_XenoCore_LevelUp Burst on each body that gained a level. Executed by UXenoCoreProgressionComponent. GameplayCue.XenoCore.Reaction.Break ini Pink burst while Break is applied. GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Break. GameplayCue.XenoCore.Reaction.Daze ini Looping over the head while Dazed. GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Daze. GameplayCue.XenoCore.Reaction.Topple ini Burst at the feet as Topple lands. GE_XenoCore_Reaction_Topple. GameplayCue.XenoCore.Revive native GameplayCue_XenoCore_Revive Burst on a party member brought back to life. GameplayCue.XenoCore.Status.Buff ini Looping aura while any buff status (bIsBuff) is active. Shared: removing one buff ends it. GameplayCue.XenoCore.Status.Debuff ini Looping aura while any debuff status is active. Shared: removing one debuff ends it. GameplayCue.XenoCore.Swing native GameplayCue_XenoCore_Swing The swing: whoosh and blade trail. A cue rather than montage notifies, because notify object references would not persist through scripted authoring and the cue path is already proven. Same effect asset as damage - the art's EffectType picks the channel. XenoCore.Art.School.Ether native XenoCore_Art_School_Ether Present on the spec when the attack is ether. Absent means physical. XenoCore.Battle.Message.Notification native XenoCore_Battle_Message_Notification Battle text over an actor - miss, break, topple, daze, critical, a buff name. One channel for all of them, so a new notification is a caller, not a system. Broadcast once per fight by UXenoCoreBattleVictorySubsystem, which also plays the fanfare and the party's victory emotes. GCNL_XenoCore_DamageTaken treats it like a weak-spot hit: crit number style and the weak-spot hit-confirm sound. docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
All · 5 min · No code

Find what you see in the table, then follow the link. Most entries are failures that log nothing and mark nothing red, which is why they are written down. Each entry says what you see, why it happens, how to fix it, and which recipe prevents it.

If your problem is not here, start with Diagnostics: where the logs are, the XenoCore log categories and console commands, and how to check a Blueprint really compiled. If that does not explain it, see Reporting a bug.

Entries marked (C++) only happen to someone compiling the project's C++; everything else can be fixed in the editor.

docs.title: Animation
docs.text:
All · 15 min · No code

Problems with the animation Blueprints, anim layers, montages and imported clips. For the model behind them, read Animation.

docs.title: Play refuses to start with "Blueprint failed to compile", and no error is shown anywhere
docs.text:
Fails silently

The anim Blueprint shows no red node, the Message Log is empty and the Output Log says nothing. Only its compile status is wrong.

Why: the anim Blueprint compiler checks some graph nodes in a silent pass and then discards the messages, but keeps the error count. The most common cause is a Get node for a variable that a programmer added to the C++ anim instance without making it readable from Blueprints.

Fix:

  1. Compile each anim Blueprint you changed and look at the Compile button: a red icon means it failed, even with an empty log. The last one you edited is the likely culprit.
  2. Undo your last graph change, or delete Get nodes for variables added recently, until it compiles. Then ask whoever added the variable to fix it (below).

For programmers

The variable is a UPROPERTY marked EditDefaultsOnly or EditAnywhere without BlueprintReadOnly or BlueprintReadWrite. Add BlueprintReadOnly, rebuild C++ (a reflected change cannot go through Live Coding), and restart the editor. A normal Blueprint shows this error; an anim Blueprint swallows it.

Avoid it next time: Choose an animation style.

docs.title: Equipping a weapon never changes the character's stance
docs.text:
Why: the stance is an anim layer, chosen by the weapon when it is drawn or sheathed. The weapon instance Blueprint (for example Weapons/GreatSword/B_WeaponInstance_GreatSword) has two settings: Equipped Anim Set (drawn) and Uneuipped Anim Set (sheathed; the spelling is Lyra's). If both name the same layer, drawing the weapon links the same layer again and nothing changes.

Fix: set Equipped Anim Set to your weapon's layer (like ABP_XenoCore_GreatSwordAnimLayers) and Uneuipped Anim Set to the unarmed layer. To check a layer is used at all, right-click it and choose Reference Viewer: an unused layer has no referencers.

Avoid it next time: Add a weapon.

docs.title: The pose pops when switching between armed and unarmed
docs.text:
Why: this happens only if you changed how the weapon instance Blueprint links its layer (its Set Drawn function). The switch is smoothed by an inertialization request made right after the layer is linked. It pops when:

  • the layers are unlinked and then linked: unlinking drops every node to its fallback for a frame. Link Anim Class Layers replaces the old layer on its own.
  • the layer is linked every frame from the anim Blueprint instead of once, on the draw or sheathe event.
  • the slot group name passed to Request Slot Group Inertialization does not match the Slot node's group. A wrong name fails silently.

Fix: link once per change, from the weapon's draw or sheathe, with no unlink. Keep the group name DefaultGroup unless you changed the Slot node, and keep the Inertialization node downstream of it in ABP_XenoCore_Base.

Avoid it next time: Add a weapon.

docs.title: A montage slot I added inside an anim layer never plays anything
docs.text:
Why: montages play on the character's main anim instance. A linked anim layer is a separate instance, and it only sees the main instance's montages if Use Main Instance Montage Evaluation Data is on in its class settings. It is off by default.

Fix: put montage slots in ABP_XenoCore_Base, not in a layer. If a layer truly needs one, turn that setting on for the layer class.

Avoid it next time: Choose an animation style.

docs.title: I reparented an anim Blueprint to another one and its graph is gone
docs.text:
Why: an anim Blueprint whose parent is another anim Blueprint becomes a child anim Blueprint, which has no AnimGraph of its own. The graph is discarded on save.

Fix: restore the asset from source control. To share logic between anim Blueprints, give each one the parent class XenoCoreAnimInstance instead (logic shared that way is C++, a programmer's job). Child anim Blueprints are only right for override-only layers, like the weapon layers, which replace assets but keep the parent's graph.

Avoid it next time: Choose an animation style.

docs.title: Feet slide or float between walk and run speeds
docs.text:
Why: stride warping is applied once, in ABP_XenoCore_Base's AnimGraph. A second Stride Warping node, for example in an anim layer's move graph, sits on the same chain and scales the stride twice. A Stride Warping node missing its thigh bones is inactive, and warns Stride Warping - Thigh bone definition is required on compile; "fixing" that warning on a duplicate node is what switches the double warp on.

Fix: keep exactly one Stride Warping node, the one in the base. Delete others rather than completing them. To compare with warping off, run a.AnimNode.StrideWarping.Enable 0 in the console.

Avoid it next time: Choose an animation style.

docs.title: The character's feet snap or jitter only while a weapon is equipped
docs.text:
Why: foot placement traces down to find the ground. A weapon mesh with blocking collision, attached to the character's back, is hit by those traces instead of the floor.

Fix: on your weapon actor's mesh, set the collision preset to NoCollision and turn off overlap events.

Avoid it next time: Add a weapon.

docs.title: Imported Paragon clips play in place and don't move the character
docs.text:
Why: the Paragon animation library animates in place. Its clips carry no root motion, so a montage that relies on root motion to lunge or dodge leaves the character standing still.

Fix: move the character in the ability instead (for example with a root motion task), or use clips that carry root motion.

Avoid it next time: Create an attack art.

docs.title: The idle break never plays, or an armed stance plays the unarmed fidget
docs.text:
Why: the idle break is set per anim layer, on the layer's Class Defaults: Idle Break Anim, Idle Break Delay and Idle Break Jitter (XenoCore › Idle Break). An empty Idle Break Anim means that stance never breaks. A layer child that does not set it inherits its parent's clip, so a new armed layer made from the unarmed one plays the unarmed fidget. The unarmed default, MM_Unarmed_IdleBreak_Fidget, is set on ABP_XenoCore_UnarmedAnimLayers; the layer base, ABP_XenoCore_ItemLayersBase, leaves it empty.

A character with an Anim Profile overrides that clip with its own lists: Idle Breaks with the weapon away, Armed Idle Breaks with it drawn. If a character plays the wrong fidget, look there first: an unarmed clip in Armed Idle Breaks plays straight through the sword. The profile is read once, when the body spawns, so an edit made during Play shows only after you press Play again.

Fix: set Idle Break Anim on every layer child, or clear it to opt out. For one character's own fidgets, fill its profile's Idle Breaks and leave Armed Idle Breaks empty unless you have clips made for the weapon. If you rebuild the idle graph, remember Blend Poses by bool's top pose is the True pose; wired backwards, the fidget becomes the idle.

Avoid it next time: Choose an animation style and Give a character its own idle breaks and faces.

docs.title: A companion's face never changes expression, or one expression never shows
docs.text:
Fails silently

Nothing is logged for a missing curve or a misspelt expression name.

Why: expressions are rows of the face's Expression Table (Characters/Core/Face/DT_XenoCore_FaceExpressions by default). A name that is not a row is tried as a single face curve, and a curve the VRoid model does not have does nothing. So a typo in a profile's Social Expressions, a face rule or a Play Expression On Actor call shows a neutral face. Only VRoid members have a face at all: a Mannequin-bodied character never shows one.

Fix: copy the row name exactly from the table. Build new rows from the VRM preset curves (happy, angry, sad, relaxed, surprised, aa, ih, ou, ee, oh, blink, blinkLeft, blinkRight), and check any raw Fcl_* curve in Play before relying on it. If the downed or victory face is missing on one character only, its retarget anim Blueprint has its own Expression Rules list; add the missing rule there, or reset the property to its default. The seven shipped retarget anim Blueprints keep the default list.

Avoid it next time: Give a character its own idle breaks and faces.

docs.title: A feminine or armed character stands in the masculine unarmed idle, but moves correctly
docs.text:
Why: a layer child swaps clips with asset overrides, and each override is tied to one node in the layer base, ABP_XenoCore_ItemLayersBase. If that node is deleted and rebuilt, for example while you rework the FullBody_Idle graph, every child's override for it is dropped when the child is next saved. Nothing warns you. The child then plays the base's own clip, MM_Unarmed_Idle_Ready. Locomotion keeps working because the blend-space override sits on a different node, so the fault only shows when the character stands still.

Fix: open the layer child, for example ABP_XenoCore_UnarmedAnimLayers_Feminine, and in the Asset Override Editor tab (it opens by itself for a layer child; if you closed it, reopen it from the Window menu) set the idle again: MF_Unarmed_Idle_Ready for the feminine layer, AS_Kwang_Idle for the greatsword layer. Compile and Save. Set it once only (see Choose an animation style).

Avoid it next time: after any edit to the layer base's graph, open each layer child and check its overrides are still listed. Right-click the child in the Content Browser and choose Reference Viewer: its idle clip must appear among its references.

docs.title: A character's own Topple (or flinch, block, dodge, death) never plays; the shared clip does
docs.text:
Why: the character's Anim Profile never reaches the reaction. Nothing warns you, because an empty profile slot is supposed to fall back to the shared clip. The usual causes: Anim Profile is set on a parent Blueprint the character does not spawn as; the profile row's key is a reaction this character is never granted; or a reaction ability you made yourself has an empty Profile Key.

Fix: press Play and run XenoCore.Anim.Describe in the console (add enemy or part of a pawn's name for someone other than the leader). The Output Log lists every reaction slot as PROFILE or default, says profile: None when the pawn has none, flags a profile row that matches no granted reaction, and shows no ProfileKey on an ability that never reads a profile.

Avoid it next time: Give a character its own combat animations.

docs.title: Hits knock a character back but its flinch barely shows, or a hit cuts its swing short
docs.text:
Why: the flinch montage shares a slot group with the attack montages. Montages in one group stop each other, so the flinch interrupts the swing and the next swing interrupts the flinch. Compiling an anim Blueprint with a new slot puts that slot in DefaultGroup, which is how this happens. Less often: the flinch clip is not additive, or the montage is not on the AdditiveHitReact slot.

Fix: open the character's skeleton › Anim Slot Manager, add a group AdditiveGroup and move AdditiveHitReact into it (SK_Mannequin and SK_Minion_Core ship this way). Check the flinch montage's slot is AdditiveHitReact and its clip's Additive Anim Type is Local Space.

Avoid it next time: Add an enemy, step 2.

docs.title: Build and editor
docs.text:
All · 15 min · Building C++ section needs C++

Problems loading the right experience, Blueprint changes that do not behave the way the graph suggests, packaging, and building the C++ code. For where things live, read Architecture.

The first three sections are for everyone. Building C++, at the end, covers compile errors. Everyone compiles once, because XenoCore is delivered as source and builds the first time the project opens; after that, only whoever changes C++ sees those errors.

docs.title: Play loads the wrong experience, whatever the map's World Settings say
docs.text:
Why: an Experience Override in Lyra's developer settings beats the map's World Settings in Play-in-Editor. It is saved in your per-user settings under Saved/Config, which is not in source control, so it survives across sessions and differs between machines. A small toast, "Developer Settings Override", appears for two seconds when Play starts.

Fix: open Edit › Editor Preferences, find the category named after your project (Lyra for a project named Lyra), open Lyra Developer Settings and clear Experience Override. It is an Editor Preference, not a Project Setting, because it is saved per user. The Output Log confirms the result: Identified experience <name> (Source: <source>).

Avoid it next time: Tour of the project.

docs.title: The experience in my own Game Feature plugin can't be found
docs.text:
Why: Lyra finds experiences through the Asset Manager, and a plugin's experience folder is not scanned by default. A DefaultGame.ini inside the plugin does not help. The log says EXPERIENCE: Wanted to use <id> but couldn't find it, falling back to the default.

Fix: open your plugin's Game Feature Data asset (the one named after the plugin, at its content root) and add your experience folder under Primary Asset Types to Scan, the way the XenoCore Game Feature Data does.

Avoid it next time: Subclass a mechanic.

docs.title: A Blueprint uses a default value instead of the one I expected, with no error
docs.text:
Fails silently

The Blueprint compiles cleanly.

Why: an input pin with no wire and no typed value gives the function the type's default: empty text, zero, none. A getter node sitting right beside it, with its output going nowhere, is the tell.

Fix: follow each input pin on the node that behaves oddly and check it has a wire or a value. A column that is hidden on most screens can hide this for a long time.

Avoid it next time: Add a menu screen.

docs.title: A base Blueprint I made by duplicating a character won't compile after reparenting
docs.text:
Why: a duplicate carries all of the original's components and functions. When the original is reparented onto its duplicate, both define functions like Death or Ragdoll, and the names collide. Its specifics (tags, effects, cooldowns) also end up on every future child.

Fix: create the base Blueprint empty, from the C++ class, and move only what every child needs into it. Keep identity (mesh, pawn data, abilities, stats) on the children.

Avoid it next time: Add a party member.

docs.title: My replacement screen works in the editor, but the packaged game shows the shipped one
docs.text:
Fails silently

Nothing is shown to the player. The game log (not present in a Shipping build) says XenoCore UI setting '...' did not load - using the shipped ....

Why: a screen, HUD widget or asset named in Project Settings › Game › XenoCore UI or XenoCore Content is a soft reference, and the cooker does not follow soft references in settings. XenoCore's own folders /XenoCore/UserInterface and /XenoCore/Characters/NPC are always cooked; your folder is not, so your replacement is left out of the build and XenoCore falls back to the shipped asset. A menu entry's Screen or Action has the same problem.

Fix: add your folder (for example /Game/MyGame/UI) to Project Settings › Packaging › Additional Asset Directories to Cook (DirectoriesToAlwaysCook in DefaultGame.ini), or make sure a cooked asset references it.

Avoid it next time: Restyle the menus.

docs.title: The build says it succeeded, but my C++ change isn't in the game
docs.text:
Why: one of four:

  • The build failed, but reported success. Unreal's Build.bat can exit with success after a failure. Scripts and some IDE integrations trust the exit code.
  • Live Coding was used for a reflected change. Live Coding cannot add or change a UPROPERTY, UFUNCTION, UCLASS or USTRUCT. It patches what it can and the reflected part silently keeps its old shape.
  • The editor is still running. Closing the editor window does not always end the process. UnrealEditor.exe and LiveCodingConsole.exe can stay resident, holding the Live Coding lock, and the build then cannot replace the module.
  • The data is a cached function-local static, such as static const TArray<...> X = ...; in a function. It is built once per editor session, so new code runs with the old data.

Fix:

  1. Read the end of the build output, not just the exit code. Look for Result: Succeeded.
  2. For any reflected change: close the editor, confirm in Task Manager that no UnrealEditor.exe or LiveCodingConsole.exe remains, build, then reopen.
  3. Restart the editor after changing anything held in a function-local static.

Avoid it next time: Subclass a mechanic.

docs.title: The C++ build fails inside the VRM4U plugin
docs.text:
You see this on the first build of a new project if the install step Let Lyra's editor build compile VRM4U was skipped: Unreal compiles VRM4U's C++ from source along with XenoCore's.

The build stops with dozens of header-tool errors like:

VRM4U\Source\VRM4U\Public\VrmAnimInstance.h(74): Error: Native pointer usage in member
declaration detected [[[UVrmMetaObject *]]]. This is disallowed for the target/module,
consider TObjectPtr as an alternative.

Lyra's editor target refuses raw object pointers in reflected members, and VRM4U's public source still uses them.

Fix: open Source/LyraEditor.Target.cs in your project and change one line:

NativePointerMemberBehaviorOverride = PointerMemberBehavior.Disallow;

to

NativePointerMemberBehaviorOverride = PointerMemberBehavior.AllowAndLog;

Then build again. This only relaxes a code-style check for C++ that is compiled; it changes no behaviour and no data. If you do not use the VRoid characters, you can instead remove them and disable VRM4U; see Replace the sample content.

Avoid it next time: before updating VRM4U, read Compatibility.

docs.title: Linker error "unresolved external symbol" for a Lyra class
docs.text:
Why: several Lyra classes are not exported from the LyraGame module (they have no LYRAGAME_API), so C++ outside Lyra cannot derive from them or call their functions. It compiles, then fails at link. Examples: ULyraAnimInstance, ULyraButtonBase, ULyraGameplayAbility_Interact.

XenoCore's own classes are all exported (XENOCORERUNTIME_API), so this error on a UXenoCore* or AXenoCore* class means a missing module in your Build.cs instead.

Fix: check for LYRAGAME_API on the class before designing around it. A Blueprint can still derive from an unexported class, so keep that part in Blueprint. Do not add the macro to Lyra's headers: that is an engine-side change you would have to carry through every update.

Avoid it next time: Subclass a mechanic.

docs.title: A compile error points into a .gen.cpp file I never wrote
docs.text:
Why: Unreal Header Tool generated code that does not match your declaration. The usual causes:

  • A BlueprintImplementableEvent takes a pointer to a class declared UCLASS(..., Const), such as UXenoCoreQuestDefinition. The generated code makes the pointer const; declare it const yourself.
  • A UFUNCTION parameter on an actor is called Instigator, which shadows AActor::Instigator. Rename it, for example Interactor.
  • "redefinition; multiple initialization" of a gameplay tag appears only on a full build. Two .cpp files define the same UE_DEFINE_GAMEPLAY_TAG_STATIC; unity builds merge them into one file. Incremental builds compile the files separately, which hides it until a clean build.

Fix: as above. For tags that C++ names in more than one place, declare them once as native tags in a header, the way XenoCoreGameplayTags.h does.

Avoid it next time: Subclass a mechanic.

docs.title: A gameplay tag lookup in C++ returns an empty tag
docs.text:
Fails silently

It compiles, and fails at run time as a message nobody receives or a flag stuck false.

Why: FGameplayTag::RequestGameplayTag(FName("...")) looks a tag up by string. If the tag is renamed or misspelled it still compiles and returns an empty tag.

Fix: use the native tag symbols in XenoCoreGameplayTags.h, for example XenoCoreGameplayTags::Status_XenoCore_Arming. Add new tags your C++ uses there too; they still appear in the editor's tag picker.

Avoid it next time: Gameplay tags reference.

docs.title: Everything works in Play-in-Editor but a standalone or packaged game crashes on launch
docs.text:
Why: Play-in-Editor runs inside an editor whose game instance is already up, so it cannot show some startup problems. A common one: a world subsystem that registers a gameplay message listener in Initialize. That runs for every world, including a temporary one created before the game instance exists, and the message system asserts.

Fix: register listeners in OnWorldBeginPlay, not Initialize. Test with a standalone launch before believing a startup change works: run UnrealEditor.exe with the project, a map and -game -log. On Windows, launch it from PowerShell or a shortcut; some shells rewrite a map path that starts with /.

Avoid it next time: Package a build.
