docs.title: A packaged game halts on the title screen with "breaking Disregard for GC assumptions"
docs.text:
Why: in a cooked game, objects created at startup (project settings objects among them) live in a pool the garbage collector never walks. An asset cached in a variable on one of them is not kept alive by it. A Development build stops with "Encountered N object(s) breaking Disregard for GC assumptions"; a Shipping build frees the asset later and crashes on it. Play-in-Editor never shows this.

Fix: in your own settings class, keep any asset you cache alive explicitly; XenoCore's own settings caches go through XenoCoreSettingsCache::KeepAlive (in XenoCoreRuntime's private headers). Or do not cache: resolve the soft reference where it is used. Then test a packaged Development build.

Avoid it next time: Loading and ticking.

docs.title: The editor builds, but the packaged game fails to compile
docs.text:
Why: some engine functions exist only in editor builds (they sit inside WITH_EDITOR). The editor target compiles them happily; the game target used for packaging does not have them.

Fix: wrap the call in #if WITH_EDITOR, or use a runtime alternative. Build the game target (for example Build.bat LyraGame Win64 Development -Project=...) after touching engine APIs, rather than finding out at package time.

Avoid it next time: Package a build.

docs.title: Characters and party
docs.text:
All · 10 min · No code

Problems with party members: who appears, what stats they have, what happens when they level, die or swap. For the model behind them, read Characters and Party.

docs.title: A new party member never appears in the field
docs.text:
Why: only the first few members of the roster are fielded. The party component fields members in roster order until it reaches Max Active Members (on Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party, 7 in the sample), and benches everyone after that. A benched member has no body in the world at all. A member whose definition has no Member Class never spawns either.

Fix:

  1. Right-click your party member definition in the Content Browser and choose Asset Actions › Validate Assets. A missing Member Class, Controller Class, Display Name or Portrait, or a pawn with no Combatant Pawn Data, is reported in red.
  2. Open BP_XenoCore_Party and check where your member sits in Starting Roster. Move it higher, or raise Max Active Members (Characters/Party/BP_XenoCore_Party).
  3. Or swap the member in from the Party screen in play.

Avoid it next time: Set the starting party.

docs.title: A character can't attack, can't use Arts, and can't die
docs.text:
Why: the character's abilities, including death, come from the ability sets in its pawn data. With Combatant Pawn Data empty, the character spawns with no abilities and no stats. This error is logged: <name> has no CombatantPawnData. It will have no stats, no abilities and cannot die.

Fix: open the character's pawn Blueprint, Class Defaults, and set Combatant Pawn Data. Duplicate an existing party member's pawn data rather than starting an empty one.

Avoid it next time: Add a party member.

docs.title: Stats don't change when a character levels up, or every character has the same stats
docs.text:
Why: a character's stats come from its own Stats Effect, re-applied at its new level on every level-up and every spawn. Two mistakes break this:

  • Several characters share one Stats Effect. They then have identical stats. Each character needs its own statline effect.
  • The statline is granted by an ability set. An ability set applies its effects at one fixed Effect Level that never changes, so the stats freeze at that level forever while the level badge keeps rising.

A character with no Stats Effect logs <name> has no StatsEffect. It will run on attribute defaults, not its statline. If you see that error every run, your numbers come from somewhere else, and they will not scale.

Fix:

  1. Set Stats Effect on the character's pawn Blueprint (Class Defaults).
  2. Remove any statline effect from the character's ability sets.
  3. Give each character its own duplicate of a statline effect, reading its own curve rows (the sample characters read <Name>.* rows of Battle/Attributes/CT_XenoCore_PartyStatlines).

Avoid it next time: Author a character statline.

Level-up heals because of the statline

Levelling up restores full health. No code does this: it happens because every statline effect sets Health as well as Max Health with an Override modifier. If you remove the Health modifier, or change it to Add, level-ups stop healing and nothing tells you. For the same reason, never re-apply a statline for any reason other than a level or a spawn: every application is a free full heal.

docs.title: After making someone else the leader and swapping back, the controls do nothing
docs.text:
Why: when you hand a body back to its AI, Unreal throws away that body's input bindings, and Lyra only binds input the first time a body is possessed. XenoCore's own hero component binds it again on every later possession. A pawn whose Components panel has Lyra's stock hero component (class LyraHeroComponent) instead of XenoCore's (class XenoCoreHeroComponent) loses that. Nothing is logged. The camera may also look fine; only input is dead.

Fix: build party pawns as children of Characters/VRoid/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_Base or Characters/Party/B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base, which carry the right component. On a pawn of your own, replace the hero component with XenoCoreHeroComponent.

For programmers

The rebind runs from AXenoCoreCombatantCharacter::SetupPlayerInputComponent through UXenoCoreHeroComponent::RebindPlayerInputOnRepossession. A C++ pawn that overrides SetupPlayerInputComponent must call Super first.

Avoid it next time: Add a party member.

docs.title: A character turns invisible after I give it a cosmetic part
docs.text:
Why: when cosmetic parts change, Lyra's character-parts component always sets the body mesh from Body Meshes, chosen by the parts' tags. If no rule matches the tags (the part carries a tag with no rule, or has no Part Class and so no tag), it uses Body Meshes › Default Mesh. With no default mesh either, the body mesh is set to nothing.

Every shipped pawn has a Default Mesh, and a character derived from XenoCore's combatant class (every party pawn and the player) has a runtime safety net: if its Default Mesh is empty at Begin Play, it uses the mesh it spawned with and logs a warning once per class (see the next entry). So on those characters an unmatched tag gives the wrong body rather than none. A pawn that is not a XenoCore combatant, for example a plain Lyra character, has no safety net and still turns invisible, with nothing logged.

Fix:

  1. On the pawn's character-parts component, make sure Body Meshes has a rule for every Cosmetic.AnimationStyle.* tag you use, and a Default Mesh.
  2. In the pawn's graph, only add a part when its class is valid. The sample pawns check Is Valid Class before Add Character Part; keep that check.
  3. Save the pawn Blueprint and read its validation messages. The editor flags a missing Default Mesh, a rule with no mesh, and a Cosmetic Part whose tags match no rule; on a pawn with no safety net, that last one is an error.

Avoid it next time: Choose an animation style.

docs.title: The log warns that Body Meshes has no Default Mesh
docs.text:
Why: a XenoCore character's Body Meshes has no Default Mesh, so a cosmetic part whose tags match no rule would make it invisible. The character is protected for this session: it uses the mesh it spawned with. The warning (LogXenoCosmetics) names the class and that mesh: "... CharacterParts BodyMeshes has no DefaultMesh ... Falling back to the mesh it spawned with ...". It is logged once per class.

Fix: open the named Blueprint, select its character-parts component, and set Body Meshes › Default Mesh to the mesh the character normally uses (for a VRoid member, its invisible Mannequin mesh). The warning then stops.

docs.title: A party member at 0 HP ragdolls instead of kneeling, and can't be revived
docs.text:
Fails silently

The body falls and the weapon disappears as if it were an enemy; no revive prompt appears, and nothing is logged.

Why: a party member at 0 HP is downed by GA_XenoCore_Downed, which the party's ability sets grant in place of Lyra's GA_Hero_Death. A pawn whose ability sets grant GA_Hero_Death instead (for example a pawn data copied from Lyra's heroes) runs a real death: montage, ragdoll, weapon hidden, body gone. A party pawn that is not a child of B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base or B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_Base cannot kneel either.

Fix: grant Battle/GA_XenoCore_Downed, not GA_Hero_Death, in every party member's ability sets (AbilitySet_XenoCore_PartyMember already does), and build party pawns as children of Characters/VRoid/B_XenoCore_Party_VRoid_Base or B_XenoCore_PartyMember_Base.

Avoid it next time: Party Gauge, downed and revive.

docs.title: Pressing A over a downed ally doesn't revive them
docs.text:
Why: a revive costs one full bar of the Party Gauge (Revive Bar Cost on BP_XenoCore_Party). Without a full bar the press is refused on purpose: "Party Gauge not full" appears over the ally and the gauge shakes. You also have to stand within Revive Range (110 cm), on top of the ally. A downed member also gets up by itself, at 1 HP, once no enemy has been engaged for Battle Over Grace.

Fix: fill the gauge (critical hits and art bonus effects), or set Revive Bar Cost to 0 for free revives.

Avoid it next time: Tune revive and defeat.

docs.title: A recruit joins at level 1, or benched members never level
docs.text:
Why: benched members earn EXP at Reserve Experience Rate on Game/BP_XenoCore_Progression, which the sample sets to 0 (XC1 uses 90%, the C++ default). A recruit only catches up if it is recruited with Join At Party Level ticked, on the recruit trigger, the NPC, or the Add To Roster node; the node's default is off.

Fix: tick Join At Party Level where the member is recruited, or raise Reserve Experience Rate.

Avoid it next time: Recruit a party member by talking to them.

docs.title: After a party wipe, the party reappears stuck in the floor or falls through it
docs.text:
Fails silently

The wipe completes and logs where the party stands again; nothing says the point was wrong.

Why: the respawn point is a capsule centre, like a player start, and the leader is placed exactly there with no collision adjustment. A Get Wipe Respawn Transform override on your BP_XenoCore_Party, or a Set Party Respawn Point call, that passes a point on the ground puts the party half into it. A save point with Respawn Offset lowered, or a pad whose origin sits below its surface, does the same.

Fix: raise the point by the character's capsule half-height (about 100 units). On a save point, set Respawn Offset so its Z clears the pad's surface by that much.

Avoid it next time: Party, under Party wipe.

docs.title: Companions zig-zag or wobble while following the leader
docs.text:
Fails silently

Nothing collides and nothing is logged; the party just never walks in a straight line.

Why: Detour Crowd avoidance is on while travelling. Each companion re-steers round the others every frame, and each body turns to face its new heading, so the whole party wobbles. It happens at every Crowd Avoidance Quality, and the higher qualities make it worse. XenoCore turns avoidance off out of battle for exactly this reason; it is back on only if Crowd Avoidance While Travelling is ticked, or if your companion's AI controller is not a child of Characters/Party/BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember, which is what switches it.

Fix: open your party controller Blueprint and untick XenoCore › AI › Crowd › Crowd Avoidance While Travelling. If you made your own controller, make it a child of Characters/Party/BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember.

Avoid it next time: Tune companion AI, step 5.

docs.title: Companions walk, sprint to catch up, then drop back to a walk
docs.text:
Why: catch-up speed is capped relative to the leader: the leader's speed × Catch Up Ratio plus Catch Up Margin, eased by Pace Smoothing, all on XenoCore Party Follow Leader in ST_XenoCore_PartyMember. Raised too far, or with Pace Smoothing high, a companion behind a walking leader runs to close the gap and then brakes.

Fix: restore Catch Up Ratio 1.5, Catch Up Margin 120 and Pace Smoothing 3 in your copy of the tree.

Avoid it next time: Companion AI.

docs.title: Companions stare straight ahead and never look around
docs.text:
Why: the head turn needs three things: the XenoCore Party Gaze task on the party StateTree's Active state, an AI controller that is a child of BP_AIC_XenoCore_PartyMember, and the ABP_XenoCore_Base Animation Blueprint (which turns the neck and head). A copy of the tree made before the gaze task existed, or a custom controller or anim Blueprint, loses it without a word. A player-controlled body never has a gaze, by design. The head also faces forward while the character is downed, celebrating, toppled or dazed (Look Blocked By Tags).

Fix: add XenoCore Party Gaze to the Active state of your tree, or start again from a copy of Characters/Party/AI/ST_XenoCore_PartyMember.

Avoid it next time: Companion AI.

docs.title: Companions stand still between fights and never chat or wander
docs.text:
Why: the rest activities run in XenoCore Party Hold, and none starts while the leader moves faster than Leader Moving Speed (60 cm/s). If you never stop for more than a few seconds, they never begin. With Stroll Chance, Social Chance and Solo Chance all 0 they never begin at all.

Fix: stand still for ten seconds and watch. If nothing happens, check those chances on XenoCore Party Hold in the tree your controller actually uses.

Avoid it next time: Tune companion AI, step 5.

docs.title: A skill is learnt but nothing changes
docs.text:
Fails silently

The skill shows as learnt on the Skills screen, "Skill Learnt" floated over the character, and no stat moves.

Why: one of these, most common first:

  • The skill is a stand-in: it works, but does something simpler than its name suggests. Check what it actually does in that table.
  • Your own skill has no effect. A skill with no Stats, Bonus or Ability is only reported as a Data Validation warning.
  • Its Timing is In Battle Party and its owner is benched.
  • Its Condition is not met (for example, HP is above the threshold, or the character wears armour).
  • It is a Scale skill on a stat that is 0, such as a party member's defence with no armour equipped.
  • It is a Bonus skill. It changes nothing on the stat sheet; it only matters when the system that asks for that bonus runs (a heal, a quest turn-in, a hit).
  • Its Scope is Self and you are looking at another character.

A Stats entry naming a stat that GE_XenoCore_SkillStats has no channel for is the one case that is logged: a LogXenoSkills warning naming the skill.

Fix: give the skill an effect, or check the conditions above. Run Validate Assets on the tree table to list every skill that does nothing.

Avoid it next time: Add a skill or a skill tree.

docs.title: Skill points stop filling the Skills screen
docs.text:
Fails silently

Kills pay SP (the HUD plate shows it) but no icon fills, or XenoGiveSP changes nothing.

Why: SP only ever flows into the selected branch, and once all five of its skills are learnt, further SP is thrown away. The branch header reads ---- / ----. Two other causes: XenoGiveSP always pays the leader, so another character's tree does not move; and if Skill Point Reward Table on BP_XenoCore_Progression is empty, kills pay no SP at all and nothing is logged.

Fix: on the Skills screen, focus another branch and choose Change Trait. For the cheat, make the character you are testing the leader. Check Skill Point Reward Table is set.

Avoid it next time: Skills.

docs.title: A character lost their skill progress after I edited their tree
docs.text:
Fails silently

After loading a save, a branch is back at the start, or the wrong skills show as learnt.

Why: a save stores each branch by its row name and only a count of learnt skills. Renaming a row makes the old progress unreachable and seeds the renamed row fresh. Reordering skills inside a branch keeps the count but changes which skills it covers. Neither is logged.

Fix: put the old row name back to recover the progress. Rename branches with Display Name only, and reorder skills only before release.

Avoid it next time: Add a skill or a skill tree.

docs.title: The Skills screen says "No skill tree"
docs.text:
Fails silently

The screen opens for the character but draws no branches.

Why: Skill Tree (XenoCore › Skills) is empty on the Blueprint the character spawns as, which is the member definition's Member Class. If the table is set but was made with the wrong row structure, LogXenoSkills logs an error instead. A tree whose branches are all locked also draws no columns.

Fix: set Skill Tree on the member's pawn class to a Data Table whose row structure is XenoCoreSkillBranchRow (duplicate a sample tree), with at least one row that has Unlocked At Start ticked.

Avoid it next time: Add a skill or a skill tree.

docs.title: Combat and Arts
docs.text:
All · 15 min · No code

Problems with Arts, cooldowns, hit feedback and the abilities you write yourself. For the model behind them, read Arts and Combat loop.

docs.title: Using one Art puts another Art on cooldown too
docs.text:
Why: an Art's cooldown is identified by its Cooldown Tag. Two Arts with the same tag share one cooldown. This almost always happens because the new Art was made by duplicating another one and the tag came along with the copy.

The editor catches this. Saving an Art definition, or right-clicking it and choosing Asset Actions › Validate Assets, fails with "Cooldown Tag ... is also used by .... Arts sharing a tag share one cooldown", naming the other Arts. The check runs only when the asset is saved or validated, so an asset that never was can still carry a shared tag.

Fix:

  1. Open each Art definition named in the error and check Cooldown Tag.
  2. Give every Art its own tag, for example Cooldown.MyGame.Art.StoneCleave, in your own tag file.
  3. If you made a base Art by duplicating a finished one, clear the base's specifics (cooldown tag, effects, montage) so its children must set their own.

Avoid it next time: Create an attack art.

docs.title: An Art never goes on cooldown and can be used again straight away
docs.text:
Why: one of three things:

  • Cooldown Duration is 0. Zero means no cooldown, which is meant only for Talent Arts.
  • The Art definition has a duration but no Cooldown Tag. The cooldown is applied, but nothing can see it, so the Art reads as ready. Saving the definition reports this as an error ("CooldownDuration is set but CooldownTag is not") whenever the duration is above zero at any level, and at runtime it logs a warning: <art> has a cooldown of <n>s but its art definition names NO CooldownTag.
  • It is your own ability Blueprint, and its graph never calls Commit Ability. A cooldown effect set on an ability does nothing on its own: the commit is the only thing that applies it. The shared Art ability and the auto-attack both commit; an ability you write from scratch must too.

Fix: set a duration and a unique Cooldown Tag on the Art definition. In your own ability's graph, call Commit Ability right after Event ActivateAbility, and end the ability if it returns false.

Avoid it next time: Create an attack art.

docs.title: An Art plays no animation and its effect lands at once
docs.text:
Why: the Art definition has no Montage. That is allowed: with no montage the Art applies its effect the moment it is used and ends. Saving the definition shows a warning, "No Montage - the art plays no animation", not an error, so it is easy to miss.

Fix: set Montage on the Art definition, unless an instant Art is what you want.

Avoid it next time: Create an attack art.

docs.title: An Art starts and stops on its first frame, with no hit
docs.text:
Fails silently

The Art goes on cooldown, nothing plays and no damage lands. Nothing is logged.

Why: the Art's Montage is the same asset as the auto-attack's swing. When an Art starts, the auto-attack stops its own montage by asset, and that stops the Art's montage too.

Fix: duplicate the clip's montage under the Art's own name and set that on the Art definition. Never point an Art at an auto-attack montage asset.

Avoid it next time: Create an attack art.

docs.title: After an Art or a custom action, my character is frozen in place for good
docs.text:
Fails silently

The character stops responding to movement and nothing is logged.

Why: while an Art runs, it holds Gameplay.MovementStopped, and the tag goes away only when the ability ends. If your own ability plays a montage with Play Montage and Wait and leaves Allow Interrupt After Blend Out off, a montage interrupted during its blend-out reports neither completed nor interrupted. The ability never ends, and the character keeps the tag.

The same happens if your ability adds a tag with Add Loose Gameplay Tags and some exit path (cancel, interrupt) never removes it.

Fix:

  1. Tick Allow Interrupt After Blend Out on every Play Montage and Wait that ends the ability.
  2. Bind On Completed, On Blend Out, On Interrupted and On Cancelled, and end the ability from each.
  3. Prefer Activation Owned Tags over loose tags: they are removed automatically when the ability ends. If you must add a loose tag, remove it in On End Ability, which runs on every exit.

Avoid it next time: Create an attack art.

docs.title: After a fight my character can't turn, or keeps playing sideways and backwards walks
docs.text:
Fails silently

It looks like an animation problem. No animation asset is involved.

Why: three flags decide whether a character turns to face where it moves: Orient Rotation to Movement, Use Controller Rotation Yaw and Use Controller Desired Rotation. Target mode, the auto-attack and Arts each switch these off for a while. If your own ability saves "the current value" and restores it later, it can save another system's temporary value and write it back after that system has finished. The character is then left unable to turn, and the movement blend space plays its side and back clips forever.

Fix: never save and restore these flags yourself. Call Suppress Self Rotation to switch them off and Restore Self Rotation to put them back (both in XenoCoreLocomotionStatics, under XenoCore › Locomotion). The restore reads the values your pawn Blueprint was authored with, so whichever system restores last is still right. Restore on every exit path, including cancel.

Avoid it next time: Subclass a mechanic.

docs.title: A tag list I set on an ability Blueprint lost the tags the C++ class adds
docs.text:
Fails silently

The Blueprint shows exactly the tags you typed, which looks correct. The loss is invisible.

Why: when a Blueprint sets a list (an array or a tag container) that its C++ parent class already fills, the Blueprint's list replaces the parent's. It does not merge. For example, the flinch ability's C++ parent blocks the flinch while an Art is executing or a weapon is being drawn. A hit-react Blueprint that sets its own Activation Blocked Tags drops both, and flinches start interrupting Arts and weapon draws.

The same applies to Activation Owned Tags, Ability Tags and any other array a base class fills.

Fix:

  1. In the Blueprint, click the reset arrow next to the property to see what the class supplies, or compare the Blueprint's Class Defaults with its parent's.
  2. If you override the list, restate every tag the parent had, then add yours. For a hit-react Blueprint that means Status.XenoCore.ArtExecuting and Status.XenoCore.Arming.

Topple and Daze reactions are deliberately not blocked on the base

The player's Topple and Daze abilities activate because their reaction tag was added. If the base class blocked those tags, each would refuse to start. That is why the flinch Blueprint lists them itself.

Avoid it next time: Subclass a mechanic.

docs.title: My healing Art plays a blade trail, hit sounds or a hit reaction
docs.text:
Why: it was built from damage parts. An attack montage carries a melee-hit notify and a weapon trail; a damage gameplay cue plays hit sounds and a flinch. Emptying a cue's effect list removes the particles but not the sounds its graph plays.

Fix:

  1. Give the heal its own montage, with no notifies. An upper-body slot keeps the legs moving.
  2. Use a heal effect with its own heal cue, not a copy of a damage cue.
  3. Set Effect Type to heal on the Art definition.

Avoid it next time: Create a healing or support art.

docs.title: Hits land but there's no camera shake or controller rumble
docs.text:
Why: one of three:

  • You are on keyboard. Rumble is gamepad-only, and Lyra switches it off unless the active input type is Gamepad and the player's force-feedback setting is on.
  • The shake is played by a cue that a gameplay effect triggers. Such a cue has no player controller to shake, so camera shake and rumble silently do nothing. Particles and numbers still work, which hides the problem. XenoCore's GCN_XenoCore_Hit is invoked directly by the attack ability, on whichever side has a local player controller.
  • The cue is never found (next entry).

Fix: test on a gamepad. To force rumble while testing, run LyraPC.ShouldAlwaysPlayForceFeedback 1 in the console. Trigger your own shake the same way the auto-attack does: executed directly by the ability, not through the damage effect.

Avoid it next time: Add hit feedback.

docs.title: Hit numbers or hit sounds are missing
docs.text:
Fails silently

Sparks and blood decals still play, so the hit looks as if it landed normally. Nothing is logged.

Why: the number, the hit-confirm sound and the kill sound are drawn by XenoCore's damage cue, GameplayCues/GCNL_XenoCore_DamageTaken (XenoCore's own copy of Lyra's, which knows XenoCore's attackers are characters and that allies' hits count). It plays only when the damage effect carries the cue tag GameplayCue.XenoCore.DamageTaken. Lyra's own GCNL_Character_DamageTaken cannot draw these hits.

What you see Likely cause No number and no hit sound on hits from your own damage effect, while the sample's hits work The effect fires GameplayCue.Character.DamageTaken (Lyra's), not GameplayCue.XenoCore.DamageTaken No number on any hit GCNL_XenoCore_DamageTaken was moved out of XenoCore/Content/GameplayCues, or deleted CRITICAL HIT! shows, but the number is the normal colour Same as the first row: Lyra's cue does not hear about XenoCore's critical hits

Fix: open the damage effect, and in its Gameplay Cues section add an entry to Gameplay Cues and set its Gameplay Cue Tags to GameplayCue.XenoCore.DamageTaken. Simplest is to duplicate Battle/Attributes/GE_XenoCore_Damage for every new damage effect. If the cue asset itself is missing, restore it from your XenoCore download.

docs.title: My new gameplay cue never plays
docs.text:
Fails silently

The cue asset looks correct and nothing is logged.

Why: cues are only found in folders registered with the cue manager. The registered folders are XenoCore/Content/GameplayCues and the project's own Content/GameplayCues and Content/GameplayCueNotifies. A cue saved anywhere else is never loaded.

Fix: save your cues under Content/GameplayCues/MyGame/. If you keep them in a Game Feature plugin of your own, open that plugin's Game Feature Data asset (the one named after the plugin, at its content root) and add an Add Gameplay Cue Path action. Paths are relative to the plugin's content root: /GameplayCues, not the full /MyPlugin/... path.

Avoid it next time: Add hit feedback.

docs.title: My code can't find an ability the character definitely has
docs.text:
Fails silently

The lookup returns nothing and logs nothing.

For programmers and advanced Blueprints.

Why: Find Ability Spec From Class compares classes for exact equality. Every granted ability in XenoCore is a Blueprint child, so asking for the C++ parent class matches nothing.

Fix: find abilities by tag instead. For the current target, use Get Current Target or Get Target Mode Ability from XenoCoreTargetingStatics. For your own abilities, give each an Ability Tags entry and search the granted specs for it.

Avoid it next time: Subclass a mechanic.

docs.title: A tag-relationship row doesn't block my ability
docs.text:
Why: XenoCore blocks abilities during states such as looting or dialogue with rows in Game/TagRelationships_XenoCore. Two things make a row miss:

  • The ability is a plain Gameplay Ability, not a Lyra Gameplay Ability. Only Lyra's ability class reads the mapping.
  • The ability has no Ability Tags. Rows match on ability tags, so an ability with none cannot be reached by any row.

Fix: base your ability on LyraGameplayAbility (or a XenoCore ability), and give it an ability tag. A row keyed on a parent tag, such as Ability.XenoCore.Art, covers every child tag, including Arts you add later.

Avoid it next time: Subclass a mechanic.

docs.title: A skill for a new percentage stat makes it 100 %
docs.text:
Fails silently

You added a new stat channel to GE_XenoCore_SkillStats for an attribute that stores a 0–1 fraction, and the first point of a skill or trait maxes the stat out.

Why: skill data uses whole percentages (a trait of +2 means +2 %). The conversion to a 0–1 fraction is applied only to Critical Rate and Block Rate, so on any other fractional attribute +2 lands as +2.0, which the attribute clamps to 100 %.

Fix: store your stat as a whole percentage and convert where it is read. The list of fraction stats is fixed in C++, so adding yours to it needs a programmer (AddStat in XenoCoreProgressionComponent_Skills.cpp). The Skills screen shows a "%" after any stat whose tag ends in Rate, so name the tag to match.

Avoid it next time: Skills.

docs.title: The God cheat doesn't stop the player taking damage
docs.text:
Why: Lyra's God command gives god mode to the player state's ability system. XenoCore characters carry their own ability system on the pawn, so the command changes nothing.

Fix: to keep a character alive while testing, add the Gameplay.DamageImmunity tag to the pawn's ability system (Lyra's health set honours it), for example with Add Loose Gameplay Tags on the pawn's ability system component from a debug Blueprint.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
All · 15 min · No code

Tools for finding out what is actually happening: where the logs are, which log categories XenoCore writes, the console commands it adds, and the engine commands worth knowing. Most of the problems in this section log nothing, so the first question is often which log line is missing.

docs.title: Where the logs are
docs.text:
Where you run Log file Editor and Play-in-Editor Saved/Logs/<project name>.log in the project folder, beside the .uproject (Lyra.log for a project named Lyra) A second editor open on the same project Saved/Logs/<project name>_2.log (the newest file is the live one) Packaged build <project name>/Saved/Logs/<project name>.log inside the packaged folder (Windows/Lyra/Saved/Logs/Lyra.log for a project named Lyra)

In the editor, Window › Output Log shows the same lines live. Type a category name, such as LogXenoParty, into its search box to filter.

Read the newest log

Unreal renames old logs with a timestamp when it starts. If two editors are open on one project, each saves over the other's changes, and the second writes <project name>_2.log while the first log keeps its old contents. Close every editor but one.

docs.title: XenoCore log categories
docs.text:
Every category logs at Log level by default. To see a category's verbose lines, run Log <Category> Verbose in the console, for example Log LogXenoEnemy Verbose.

Category What writes to it LogXenoCore General: saving and loading, title screen, reaction test commands, boot screens, collectable orbs LogXenoParty The party: roster, fielding, leader swaps, recruitment, party wipe and respawn LogXenoCombatant Party character setup: missing pawn data or stats effect, revive, camera LogXenoHero Player possession: ability grants, input rebinding after a leader swap LogXenoProgression Experience, levels, Arts learned LogXenoLevelUp The level-up banner LogXenoDamage Every damage calculation: stat, weapon, defence, level multiplier, hit roll LogXenoAttack Auto-attack LogXenoEnemy Enemy setup, death and chest drops LogXenoCoreEquipment Equip refusals (with the blocker number), starting gear, inventory dumps LogXenoDrop, LogXenoLoot, LogXenoLootFind, LogXenoLootPopup, LogXenoLootUI Drop tables, chests, finding the nearest chest, the loot panel LogXenoInteract The interaction prompt and presses, including out-of-range verbs LogXenoPrompt The interact prompt widget LogXenoNpc NPCs LogXenoDialogue, LogXenoDialogueNode, LogXenoDialogueAnchor Conversations, the dialogue nodes, the speech box anchor LogXenoQuest, LogXenoQuestNode, LogXenoQuestUI, LogXenoQuestLog, LogXenoQuestTracker, LogXenoQuestReward, LogXenoQuestStatics Quest state, quest nodes, and each quest screen LogXenoShop, LogXenoShopNode, LogXenoShopScreen Shops LogXenoTrade, LogXenoTradeNode, LogXenoMerchant Trading and the shared merchant screen LogXenoCoreSavePoint Save points placed in maps LogXenoDamageNumbers Damage-taken and heal numbers LogXenoCoreBuildStamp The build stamp shown on screen LogXenoSkills Skill trees: skills learnt, branch selection, missing SP bands, stat skills with no channel, a wrong or missing table or stats effect. See Skills

Editor-only tools also write LogXenoCoreAnimLayers and LogXenoCoreMapTools. Some older setup errors are written to LogTemp with a [XenoCore] prefix, for example an enemy with no pawn data. Search for [XenoCore] as well as the categories.

Lyra's own categories matter too. LogLyraExperience names the experience each map loaded and where the choice came from: Identified experience <name> (Source: <source>).

docs.title: XenoCore console commands
docs.text: Open the console with the backquote key (`, above Tab) in Play-in-Editor.

docs.title: Testing combat
docs.text: Command What it does XenoCore.Reaction 1 Applies one reaction to the player, on its own: 1 Break, 2 Topple, 3 Daze, 0 clears. Useful for testing hit reactions without an enemy. XenoCore.Reaction 2 enemy The same, on your locked-on target, or the nearest living enemy if nothing is locked. Use it to check an enemy's knock-down and that it stops acting. XenoCore.Art.MaxStage 1 Caps enemy Art escalation: 1 Break only, 2 up to Topple, 3 or 0 the full chain. The earlier stages still run, so the chain builds normally and stops where you set it. XenoCore.Arts.DrawArea 1 Draws every area Art's shape, and who it hit, at impact. Development builds only XenoCore.Anim.Describe, XenoCore.Anim.Play Topple front Lists every reaction clip a character plays and where it comes from; previews one clip XenoCore.Aggro.Describe Logs every enemy's aggro ring: whether it shows, on whom, and the threat and engage state behind it XenoCore.Battle.Victory Runs the battle-won sequence (fanfare, disarm, emotes) without a fight XenoCore.Enemies.Defeat <name>, XenoCore.Enemies.RespawnAll Defeats a named enemy; refills every enemy spawner XenoCore.Loot.Simulate <table> [level] [chests] Opens many chests from a drop table at a level and prints what came out XenoCore.Weapon.Describe [name] Prints a character's weapon type and what it can wield

docs.title: Progression cheats
docs.text:
Command What it does XenoAwardExp 5000 Gives experience to the party, as if from a fight XenoAwardGold 500 Gives gold XenoArts Prints the leader's learned Arts and palette XenoSetArt 2 AirSlash Puts a learned Art in a palette slot XenoGiveAP 1000 Gives the leader Art Points XenoCastArt AirSlash Casts an equipped Art the same way the palette does XenoGiveSP 500, XenoSkills Pours Skill Points into the leader's selected branch; prints the leader's branches and progress XenoLevelUpLeader, XenoLevelUpParty Exactly enough EXP for the leader's next level; enough for every active member to level once

These are cheat-manager commands, so they work wherever cheats are allowed (Play-in-Editor and Development packaged builds, not Shipping).

docs.title: Party, inventory, quest and save commands
docs.text:
Command What it does XenoSetLeader 1 Makes an active slot the leader XenoDownMember 1 Downs an active member through the real damage path: it kneels and can be revived XenoWipeParty Downs every active member, which runs the party wipe XenoReviveMember 1 Brings that member back at full health XenoHurtParty 0.3 Sets every standing member to that fraction of max HP, to watch out-of-battle recovery XenoGaugeAdd 100, XenoGaugeSpend 1 Adds Party Gauge points (negative removes); spends whole bars XenoCoreDumpInventory Prints the bag, the leader's loadout and the totals. Changes nothing XenoCoreTestInventoryEvents Changes the bag: adds and removes one item and reports both change messages XenoQuestStatus Prints every quest the party has touched XenoSave 1, XenoLoad 1 Saves to or loads a slot (default 1) XenoSaveDump Prints every slot without loading it

These are cheat commands too, so they run wherever the progression cheats do.

docs.title: Other console variables
docs.text: Command What it does XenoCore.Boot.ForceShaderScreen 1 Shows the shader-compile boot card with a simulated 4-second compile, for previewing it in the editor XenoCore.Tutorial.Reset, XenoCore.Tutorial.Show <Row>, XenoCore.Tutorial.Trigger <Tag>, XenoCore.Tutorial.Tips 0/1 Forget seen tutorial cards; show one; fire a trigger; switch tips XenoCore.Time.Set <hour> [fade], XenoCore.Time.Scale, XenoCore.Weather.Set <Weather>, XenoCore.Environment.Freeze Time of day and weather. See Time of day and weather XenoCore.Minimap.Rotate, XenoCore.Minimap.Hide Minimap rotation and visibility. See Minimap XenoCore.ProjectSetup [apply] Lists (or applies) the project settings XenoCore still needs. Editor only

docs.title: Engine and Lyra commands worth knowing
docs.text:
Command Use it to see showdebug abilitysystem The viewed character's attributes, owned tags and active effects. Answers "is the cooldown tag on?", "is Gameplay.MovementStopped stuck?", "did the stats effect apply?" Press Page Up / Page Down to change the character viewed. stat fps, stat unit Frame rate, and game / render / GPU time a.AnimNode.StrideWarping.Enable 0 Turns all stride warping off, to compare foot sliding with and without it LyraPC.ShouldAlwaysPlayForceFeedback 1 Plays controller rumble whatever the input type and setting Log <Category> Verbose Turns on a log category's detailed lines

For the AI, open the enemy's StateTree asset and use its Debugger tab, or Tools › Debug › Rewind Debugger, while playing to watch which state each enemy is in. In 5.8 the StateTree's recordings are shown in the Rewind Debugger.

docs.title: Checking a Blueprint really compiled
docs.text:
An anim Blueprint can fail to compile with nothing in the Output Log or Message Log, and no node marked red. Play then refuses to start with "Blueprint failed to compile" and no more detail. See Animation.

  1. Open the Blueprint and click Compile.
  2. Look at the icon on the Compile button itself: a green tick means it compiled, a red icon means it failed, whatever the logs say.
  3. If it failed with nothing logged, undo your last graph change and see Animation.

docs.title: Asset validation
docs.text:
Several XenoCore data assets check themselves. Right-click the asset and choose Asset Actions › Validate Assets (or right-click a folder and choose Validate Assets in Folder) and read the Message Log.

Asset What validation catches Party member definition Missing member class, controller class, display name or portrait; a pawn with no pawn data Art definition No palette glyph; a heal Art aimed at enemies Quest definition No objectives; an objective with no item or enemy target, a bad required count, no counter label, or a kind not implemented yet; no title or summary Shop and trade tables No offers; a row with no item; duplicate rows; a price of zero; an item that cannot be bought Art definition (cooldowns) Two Arts sharing a Cooldown Tag; a cooldown with no tag. See Combat and Arts Drop table An item in a lower pool than its rarity's lowest chest tier (a warning) Skill tree, cost curve, trait ladder tables A branch without five skills, a missing cost curve or ladder, a skill that does nothing (warning). See Skills DT_XenoCore_ExperienceCurves An empty row or a 0 entry; a row shorter than the level cap (warning) Placed XenoCore Map Area (Map Check) No area, no image, or backwards bounds

docs.title: Enemies and AI
docs.text:
All · 10 min · No code

Problems with enemies: damage, death, stats, Art choice, movement and loot. For the model behind them, read Enemies and AI.

docs.title: An enemy takes no damage and can't die
docs.text:
Why: one of three:

  • Enemy Pawn Data is empty. Damage and death come from the abilities its pawn data grants. This one logs an error: <name> has no EnemyPawnData. It will have no stats, no abilities and cannot die.
  • Its pawn data's ability sets grant no death ability. Nothing is logged.
  • It is possessed by the wrong AI controller. Lyra only lets a character damage another on a different team, and an enemy gets its team from its controller. Only Characters/Enemies/Core/BP_AIC_XenoCore_Enemy and its children supply one. A plain AI controller leaves the enemy on no team, and every hit on it is applied with zero effect. Nothing is logged.

Fix:

  1. In the enemy Blueprint's Class Defaults, set Enemy Pawn Data. Duplicate PawnData_XenoCore_Minion_Melee rather than starting empty; its ability set (AbilitySet_XenoCore_Enemy_Common) carries death.
  2. Set the enemy's AI Controller Class to BP_AIC_XenoCore_Enemy or your child of it.
  3. Keep the controller's Team Id (XenoCore › Teams) different from the party's. The default is 2.

Avoid it next time: Add an enemy type.

docs.title: An enemy's stats aren't what the curve table says, or they double after a level change
docs.text:
Why: an enemy's stats come from its Stats Effect, which reads rows of CT_XenoCore_EnemyStats at the enemy's level. Two things change the result:

  • A modifier's magnitude is the curve value times the modifier's own coefficient. The minion types share the Minion_Melee.* rows and differ only by that coefficient: Brute 1.45, Bulwark 1.15, Skirmisher 0.9 (Melee 1.0). A stats effect duplicated from one of them inherits its multiplier.
  • Every modifier must use Override. An Add modifier stacks on the old value each time the effect is re-applied.

Fix: open the stats effect, check each modifier's coefficient and set it to the multiplier you want (1.0 for the table's own number), and set every modifier's operation to Override.

Avoid it next time: Author an enemy statline.

docs.title: An enemy takes almost no damage, whatever the party does
docs.text:
Why: enemy and party defence work differently. On a party member, Physical Defence and Ether Defence are flat points subtracted from the attacker's stat. On an enemy, they are fractions from 0 to 0.9: damage is multiplied by 1 - defence. A value typed as points, such as 40, is clamped to 0.9, so the enemy shrugs off 90% of every hit.

Fix: set enemy defence rows in CT_XenoCore_EnemyStats as fractions, for example 0.15 for 15%. The 90% cap is fixed in C++.

Avoid it next time: Author an enemy statline.

docs.title: An enemy ignores the party and walks past
docs.text:
Why: one of three things.

  • Its Detection (XenoCore › AI › Detection) is None (passive): it only fights once hit.
  • It detects by Sound and the leader is walking: only a running leader is heard.
  • It is too far below the party: an enemy Ignore When Levels Below (6) or more levels under the leader notices nothing. The threshold is on its AI controller (XenoCore › AI). Such an enemy still fights back if attacked.

Fix: change its Detection, raise its Enemy Level (or the spawner's level range), or tick Unique Monster on it or Always Aggro on a child controller for bosses and unique enemies.

Avoid it next time: Place enemies.

docs.title: An enemy never uses its Arts, or uses one and never the other
docs.text:
Fails silently

The enemy keeps auto-attacking normally, so nothing looks broken.

Why: enemies choose Arts with the same scorer as companions, from the Art definitions on the enemy Blueprint's Arts list (XenoCore › Enemy › Arts). One of these is usually the cause:

  • The Art is not on the Arts list. Nothing in the ability set or the StateTree grants enemy Arts.
  • Usable By AI is off in the Art's Art › Companion AI section.
  • The Art's Distance is shorter than the distance the enemy fights from, so it is never in reach.
  • The Art plays the same montage asset as the enemy's auto-attack. The auto-attack's swing is stopped by montage, so the Art is stopped on its first frame and never lands.
  • A Topple or Daze Art with AI Wait For Reaction on is held until the target is Broken (or Toppled). With no Break Art on the enemy, it is never used.
  • Two Arts share one Cooldown Tag, so using one puts both on cooldown.

Fix: press the backquote key (`) in Play to open the console, type log LogXenoAI Verbose, and fight the enemy. Each decision prints as <enemy>: decision - <Art>=<score> .... An Art that never appears there is not on the body or not usable; an Art that appears but never wins needs a higher AI Priority or a condition bonus. Give every Art its own montage and its own Cooldown Tag.

Avoid it next time: Give an enemy Arts.

docs.title: An enemy uses Arts back to back
docs.text:
Why: each Art waits for its own cooldown, and the enemy also waits its AI Profile › Post-Art Cooldown after any Art. An Art with no Cooldown Duration, on an enemy with a short post-art cooldown, is ready again almost at once.

Fix: give the Art a Cooldown Duration and its own Cooldown Tag, and raise Post-Art Cooldown on the enemy (XenoCore › Enemy › Arts › AI Profile).

Avoid it next time: Give an enemy Arts.

docs.title: A state I added to a StateTree is never entered
docs.text:
Fails silently

The StateTree compiles with no errors and looks correct in the editor.

Why: a new state's Selection Behavior defaults to Try Select Children In Order. That behaviour looks for a child to enter, so a state with no children finds nothing and is never entered. The tree sits in its parent doing nothing.

Fix: on every leaf state (one with no children), set Selection Behavior to Try Enter. Keep Try Select Children In Order only on states that have children.

Avoid it next time: Enemies and AI.

docs.title: A Toppled or Dazed enemy stands still instead of falling, or keeps attacking
docs.text:
Fails silently

The TOPPLE or DAZE popup still appears, and nothing is logged.

Why:

  • Stands still: its ability set has no knock-down ability for that reaction, or the ability still plays the minion's montage on a different skeleton. The rule that stops it acting is on the auto-attack, so it cannot act, but nothing plays the fall.
  • Keeps attacking: its auto-attack Blueprint sets its own Incapacitated Tags (XenoCore › AutoAttack). A list set on a Blueprint replaces the default (Topple and Daze) rather than adding to it, and an empty list turns the rule off.

Fix: grant copies of GA_XenoCore_Minion_Topple and GA_XenoCore_Minion_Daze with your enemy's montages, with Hold Until Montage Ends and Hold While Trigger Tag Present on. Reset Incapacitated Tags to its default, or list Topple and Daze in it. Test with XenoCore.Reaction 2 enemy while locked on.

Avoid it next time: Add an enemy.

docs.title: An enemy slides sideways or backwards in an idle or forward-running pose
docs.text:
Fails silently

The enemy fights correctly; only its legs are wrong.

Why: its anim Blueprint plays a blend space with no direction. A forward-only (1D) blend space has nothing to play when the enemy strafes round its attackers or backs off, so it plays a forward clip, or half-blends into idle, while the body moves sideways. The minion's anim Blueprint uses a 2D blend space for this reason.

Fix:

  1. Give the enemy a 2D blend space with Direction (-180 to 180) on the horizontal axis and speed on the vertical axis, with forward, left, right and back clips. Copy the layout of Characters/Enemies/Minion/Animations/BS_XenoCore_Minion_Locomotion2D.
  2. In its Animation Blueprint (whose parent class is XenoCoreAnimInstance), drive the blend space's two axes from the Direction and Ground Speed variables.
  3. Drive the Idle and Move transitions from Ground Speed too, with a gap between them: enter Move above 20, return to Idle below 8. One threshold both ways makes the legs flicker between idle and run while the enemy shuffles.

Avoid it next time: Add an enemy type.

docs.title: An enemy never patrols
docs.text:
Why: the enemy has no Patrol Points, or it is provoked. An enemy walks its route only while unprovoked. With no points it wanders within Wander Radius of home, or stands still if that is 0. An enemy made by a spawner takes the spawner's Wander Radius and has no patrol route.

Fix: select the placed enemy and add Patrol Points (XenoCore › AI › Patrol). Each point is relative to where the enemy stands, and shows as a handle you can drag in the viewport. Check the route is on the navigation mesh (press P).

Avoid it next time: Place enemies.

docs.title: A defeated enemy drops no chest, or the chest opens empty
docs.text:
Why:

  • No chest at all: the enemy has a Drop Table but no Chest Class. Logged as an error: <name> has a DropTable but no ChestClass. Its loot is unreachable.
  • No chest from most of a group: the enemy came from a spawner with Squad Loot Rule on (the default), so only the last member killed drops a chest, at least silver, with the leader's loot (the first enemy of the first Members entry). Untick it on the spawner for one chest per enemy.
  • A squad's chest holds the wrong enemy's loot: it is the leader's, not the last kill's. Reorder the spawner's Members so the type you want is first.
  • Empty chest: the drop table has no pool, or no usable entries, for the tier the chest rolled (Wooden, Silver or Gold). Logged as a warning: <table> has no pool for tier <n>. The chest will be empty.
  • Fewer items than expected, or empty at some levels: the pool's entries have Min Level / Max Level bands, and none (or too few) cover the dying enemy's level; with No Duplicate Equipment on, a small pool can also run out of pieces. Run XenoCore.Loot.Simulate <table> <level> to see what a table pays at a level.

Fix: set Chest Class on the enemy (XenoCore › Loot), and give the drop table a pool with at least one entry for every tier. Always Gold Chest forces the Gold tier.

Avoid it next time: Author a drop table.

docs.title: Items and equipment
docs.text:
All · 10 min · No code

Problems with items, the party bag, weapons and armour. For the model behind them, read Items and inventory and Equipment.

docs.title: My new item shows in the list, but choosing it does nothing
docs.text:
Why: the item definition was created blank instead of duplicated. A blank item definition has no Equippable Item fragment naming an equipment definition, so the equip is refused. The list still draws the row and the click does nothing on screen. A warning is logged: Refused to equip <item> into slot <n> - blocker 2. Blocker 2 means not equippable.

A second warning, <item> has no UXenoCoreFragment_EquipSlots, means the item has no XenoCoreFragment_EquipSlots fragment, so it names no slot it can go in.

Fix: delete the blank item and duplicate a working one of the same kind instead: a sword from Weapons/, an armour piece from Inventory/Armour/. Then change its name, stats and mesh. Saving the item, or Asset Actions › Validate Assets, now reports a missing fragment or equipment definition as an error; see Items and inventory › Checks on save.

Blocker Meaning 1 No item 2 Not equippable: no equipment definition 3 Wrong slot for this item 4 This character already wears it in another slot 5 Another character wears it 6 This character cannot wield this weapon type: the item's Weapon Type is not in the character's Allowed Weapon Types

A weapon of the wrong type is also left out of that character's swap list, so a weapon that never appears there for one character is usually blocker 6.

Avoid it next time: Add a weapon, Add an armour piece.

docs.title: Armour equips and shows its name, but gives no stats
docs.text:
Fails silently

The slot fills, the loadout row names the piece, and the character sheet does not change. Nothing is logged.

Why: equipment stats are applied by the ability GA_XenoCore_EquipmentStats. It is granted by the ability sets of the item's equipment definition. Shipped armour all points at Inventory/Armour/ED_XenoCore_Armour, which grants AbilitySet_XenoCore_EquipmentStats. An equipment definition of your own with no ability set, or with the wrong one, equips without stats.

Fix: point your armour's equippable fragment at ED_XenoCore_Armour, or make sure your own equipment definition grants AbilitySet_XenoCore_EquipmentStats.

Do not give armour a weapon's ability set

A weapon's ability sets (Weapons/AbilitySet_XenoCore_SwordCommon and the swords' Talent sets) also grant GA_XenoCore_WeaponDrawSync. On armour, the character tries to draw its armour like a weapon.

Avoid it next time: Add an armour piece.

docs.title: My weapon no longer draws or sheathes
docs.text:
Fails silently

The weapon stays where it is. Nothing is logged.

Why: drawing and sheathing are driven by GA_XenoCore_WeaponDrawSync, granted through the weapon's equipment definition's Ability Sets to Grant (the sword base, Weapons/ED_XenoCore_Sword_Base, grants AbilitySet_XenoCore_SwordCommon, which carries it). The Junk, Blue, Gold, Green and Red Swords replace that list with AbilitySet_XenoCore_JunkSword alone, which carries it too, so nothing is granted twice. That grant is also what lets the ability find its weapon. Emptying the list, for example while tidying up stat effects, breaks draw and sheathe.

Fix: keep an ability set that grants GA_XenoCore_WeaponDrawSync on every weapon's equipment definition.

Avoid it next time: Add a weapon.

docs.title: Menus show old item counts after my script adds or removes items
docs.text:
Why: screens refresh when they hear XenoCore.Inventory.Message.Changed. The XenoCore inventory nodes (XenoCore › Inventory) send it at once. A change made with Lyra's own inventory nodes, such as Add Item Definition, is noticed by XenoCore's bag watcher and announced one frame later (the Output Log shows LogXenoBagWatch: The party bag changed outside the XenoCore inventory functions ...). So a stale count now means one of these:

  • The screen does not listen for the message at all. Your own screens must, or must re-read the bag when they open. See Events.
  • Your graph reads the count in the same frame it changed the bag through a Lyra node, before the watcher has announced it.

Fix: add and remove items with Add Item To Party, Add One Item To Party, Remove Item From Party, Remove Item Instance From Party and Consume Items From Party (XenoCore › Inventory). They announce the change at once.

Two more reasons to avoid Lyra's own nodes here:

  • XenoCore stores one bag entry per item: twelve crystals are twelve entries, and Lyra counts entries, not Stack Count. An entry added with a stack count above one still counts as one, so counts and item-priced ability costs come out wrong. Never set Stack Count yourself.
  • Lyra's removal nodes do not check whether a character is wearing the item. See the next entry.

Avoid it next time: Add a consumable item.

docs.title: An equipped item vanished from the bag, and the log shows an error
docs.text:
Why: Lyra's Remove Item Instance (or its Consume Items By Definition) removed an item a character was wearing. The character's slot still shows it, but the bag no longer holds it, so it is not saved and menus that list the bag do not show it. XenoCore cannot undo the removal; it logs an Error to LogXenoBagWatch: "... was removed from the party bag while ... was wearing it, by something other than the XenoCore inventory functions (Lyra's Remove Item Instance?)."

Fix: replace the node with Remove Item Instance From Party, which refuses a worn item and returns false (it logs a warning naming the wearer), or Consume Items From Party, which never takes a worn item. To remove a worn item on purpose, unequip it first.

Avoid it next time: Items and inventory.

docs.title: The editor stops when my graph calls Add Item Instance
docs.text:
Why: Lyra's Add Item Instance is not implemented in stock Lyra; calling it halts the editor or the game.

Fix: add items by definition with Add Item To Party or Add One Item To Party. There is no supported way to put an existing item instance back into the bag.

docs.title: An ability with an item cost never activates
docs.text:
Fails silently

Nothing is logged; the input simply does nothing.

Why: the ability's Additional Costs uses Lyra's Inventory Item cost. In stock Lyra 5.8 it is switched off inside Lyra and its check always fails, so the ability can never activate. The other causes: the party has too few copies that nobody is wearing, or the cost names a different item definition from the one in the bag.

Fix: use Party Item (XenoCore) instead, with the right Item Definition and Quantity. Get Free Party Item Count shows how many copies the cost can see.

Avoid it next time: Add a consumable item.

docs.title: A screen shows zero stats for the weapon a character just equipped
docs.text:
Why: equipment stats must be applied during the equip itself. If your own stats ability waits a frame (for example with a Delay Until Next Tick) before applying, any screen that redraws on the equip reads the character before the stats arrive, and shows the item's name with zeros.

Fix: apply stats in the same frame. From inside an ability granted by the equipment, get the character's equipment component and call Get Item For Equipment for the item being equipped; it answers during the equip. Test by opening a screen that refreshes on an equip.

Avoid it next time: Add an equipment stat.

docs.title: A character spawns without its starting weapon
docs.text:
Why: a character's starting gear is created in the party's bag, which lives on the player controller. A pawn that cannot reach the player controller when its abilities come up, for example one placed in a level with no player yet, cannot create its items. This is logged as an error: <name> could not reach the party inventory, so it cannot create item instances.

The same error appears when the map is not running the XenoCore experience, because the experience is what adds the bag to the player controller.

Fix: spawn party members through the party (its roster), not by placing their pawns in the level. Check the map's World Settings use a XenoCore experience (see Build and editor for an override that can silently replace it).

Avoid it next time: Add a party member.

docs.title: An item's name is not in its rarity colour
docs.text:
Symptom: a Rare or Legendary item is drawn white, or has no diamonds.

Check, in order:

  1. The item's Rarity. In its XenoCoreFragment_ItemCategory fragment, an empty Rarity means Common, which is white.
  2. The table. Project Settings › Game › XenoCore UI › Item Rarity Table must name DT_XenoCore_ItemRarities or your own table. A cleared setting turns rarity off.
  3. The row. The table needs a row whose Rarity column is the item's tag. If it has none, the log warns once: Rarity '...' has no row in .... Check Tint Name and Pips on that row too.
  4. Your own widget. A restyled row needs a call to Apply Item Rarity after it sets the name, and a Horizontal Box named RarityPips for the diamonds. A button labelled with Set Button Text needs Apply Item Rarity To Button.
  5. The outline vanished. The name's dark outline lives on its font, so a Set Font after Apply Item Rarity strips it. Set the font first, then apply rarity.

docs.title: Reporting a bug
docs.text:
All · 5 min · No code

If a problem is not in this section and Diagnostics did not explain it, report it. A report that lets us reproduce the problem on the shipped sample is usually fixed fastest.

docs.title: Before you report
docs.text:
1. Check the Troubleshooting index for your symptom.
  2. Try it on the shipped sample: open Maps/L_XenoCore_Gym and see whether the same thing happens with the sample party and minions. If it does not, the difference between the sample and your content is often the answer.
  3. Close every editor, check Task Manager that no UnrealEditor.exe is left running, reopen the project once, and try again. Several problems on the Build and editor page come from a stale editor process.

docs.title: What to include
docs.text:
Include Why XenoCore version and Unreal Engine version (for example 5.8.1) Fixes are per release. The XenoCore version is shown on the XenoCore entry in Edit › Plugins (the VersionName in XenoCore.uplugin). The build number on the title screen is your project's own version, not XenoCore's. What you did, step by step Start from opening a named map: "Open L_XenoCore_Gym, press Play, lock on to a minion, use the second Art." What you expected, and what happened One sentence each. Every time, or sometimes? And whether it also happens on the shipped sample. The log Saved/Logs/<project name>.log in the project folder (beside the .uproject) from the session where it happened. Attach the whole file; the lines that matter are often the ones before the problem. What you changed Which shipped assets you edited, and which of your own assets are involved. Name them with their folder. Screenshots or a short video Especially for animation, UI and camera problems. C++ changes If you changed or added C++, say so, and whether the problem happens without your change. Crash details If the editor crashed, the call stack from the crash window, plus the log.

Remove anything private from logs before you send them. Logs contain file paths, which can include your Windows user name.

docs.title: Where to report
docs.text:
Open an issue at github.com/baremetalrt/xenocore-dist/issues (the Support link on the XenoCore entry in Edit › Plugins goes to the same page). You need a free GitHub account.

  1. Search the open and closed issues first: your problem may already have an answer.
  2. Click New issue. Give it a title that names the symptom, for example "Companion never draws its weapon after a leader switch".
  3. Fill it in with everything in What to include above: the XenoCore and Unreal Engine versions, the steps from a named map, what you expected and what happened, the log, and what you changed.
  4. Drag the log file, screenshots or a short video into the issue to attach them. For a log too big to attach, zip it first.

Issues on that page are public. Do not post anything private, such as your licence details, your own project's unreleased content, or logs you have not checked for personal paths.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text: We reproduce the problem on the shipped sample. If it is a template bug, the fix goes into a future release, and this Troubleshooting section gains an entry so the next person finds the answer here.

docs.title: UI and input
docs.text:
All · 20 min · No code

Problems with buttons, menus, popups, HUD widgets and input. For the model behind them, read UI shell and HUD and Input and camera.

docs.title: One tap of a button does the action several times
docs.text:
Fails silently

It looks like the feature is broken: a conversation skips lines, then closes and reopens.

Why: an Enhanced Input action with no triggers fires on every frame the key is held. A normal tap lasts several frames. An ability that runs for a while (a jump, an Art) ignores the repeats because it is still active; an ability that ends on the frame it starts activates again on the next frame, once per frame of the tap.

Fix: open the input action and add a Pressed trigger to Triggers. Every one-shot action in Input/InputActions/ has one; copy that.

Avoid it next time: Show an input action prompt.

docs.title: A button does nothing, even though its input action is mapped
docs.text:
Fails silently

The action never fires, so there is nothing for the ability to log.

Why: two input mapping contexts map the same key at the same priority, and the other one's action consumes the input. Enhanced Input settles the conflict before any ability is asked, so blocking abilities with tags cannot fix it. XenoCore adds its own context, IMC_XenoCore, at priority 2 and Lyra's IMC_Default at 1, so they win ties against contexts added at the default 0, such as those from another Game Feature you add.

Fix:

  1. List every key your new mapping shares with IMC_Default and IMC_XenoCore.
  2. Give your context a higher Priority in the Game Feature Data's Add Input Mapping action, or move the action to a free key.
  3. On the winning action, leave Consume Input off if the other action must still work.

Avoid it next time: Show an input action prompt.

docs.title: One press of a button also opens the menu
docs.text:
Why: the Escape key is bound twice. It is a gameplay key in a mapping context and CommonUI's UI.Action.Escape UI action (in Config/DefaultInput.ini), which the HUD layout answers by opening its Escape Menu Class. Both fire on one press. XenoCore's UI.Action.Escape is on the Escape key only, so pad Select (View/Back) is free for the quest tracker; the menu opens from Y, Start, I or Escape.

Fix: do not map a gameplay action to a key listed under UI.Action.Escape's Key Mappings in Config/DefaultInput.ini, or take that key off the UI action.

Avoid it next time: Show an input action prompt.

docs.title: Holding a trigger switches at once instead of opening the party cursor
docs.text:
Fails silently

The hold looks exactly like a tap: control changes hands and no cursor appears.

Why: the Hold trigger on IA_XenoCore_PartySelect has Is One Shot ticked. A one-shot hold reports the press as released on the frame after it fires, so the cursor opens and commits in the same moment.

Fix: untick Is One Shot on that trigger. Keep the Hold Time Threshold on IA_XenoCore_PartySelect equal to the Tap Release Time Threshold on IA_XenoCore_PartySwitch and IA_XenoCore_PartySwitchPrev (0.25 s), or a press between the two values does both or neither.

Avoid it next time: Input and camera.

docs.title: Tapping a trigger shows "Can't switch"
docs.text:
Why: the switch was refused, on purpose. The leader is toppled or dazed, an ally-targeted Art is choosing its target, the party is being wiped, or nobody else can take control (everyone else is downed, toppled, dazed or in the air, or there is only one active member). The Output Log has a LogXenoParty line starting switch refused.

Fix: none needed. To change the message or its sound, set Switch Refused Text and Switch Refused Sound on BP_XenoCore_Party. See Party.

docs.title: The triggers do nothing at all
docs.text:
Fails silently

No "Can't switch", no cursor, nothing in the log.

Why: the switch abilities are granted only through the party's Leader Only Ability Set (Game/AbilitySet_XenoCore_Interact). If you replaced that set with your own, or cleared the field on your copy of BP_XenoCore_Party, nothing holds the abilities. With an empty starting roster the party component never hands the set to the player's pawn either.

Fix: add GA_XenoCore_PartySwitch, GA_XenoCore_PartySwitchPrev and GA_XenoCore_PartySelect, with their input tags, to the set named in Leader Only Ability Set.

docs.title: The character jumps or acts while a menu is open, or when it closes
docs.text:
Why: gameplay input stops under a menu because every gameplay mapping context only matches while the input mode has InputMode.Game, and CommonUI removes that tag while a menu is up. The project sets this once, as the default query in Config/DefaultInput.ini. A mapping context of yours with its own Input Mode Query instead of Use Project Default Query keeps working under menus.

Separately, when a menu closes while its confirm button is still held, gameplay input comes back and can read the held button as a fresh press.

Fix: leave Use Project Default Query on for gameplay contexts. If gameplay input works under every menu, the project's default query was never set: run Tools › XenoCore › Apply XenoCore Project Settings, which writes it to Config/DefaultInput.ini. For the close, add a short delay before re-enabling anything the confirm button also triggers, or block the ability with a state tag until the menu has faded.

A HUD element that takes Menu mode kills its own inputs

The Arts palette works in combat because it is a HUD plate, not an activatable screen. A widget that sets Menu mode filters out the gameplay contexts, including its own keys.

Avoid it next time: Add a menu screen.

docs.title: Enter doesn't press menu buttons on keyboard
docs.text:
Why: CommonUI's Common Button Accept Key Handling is not TriggerClick in the project you are running. XenoCore's project setup writes it to the project's Config/DefaultGame.ini ([/Script/CommonUI.CommonUISettings], CommonButtonAcceptKeyHandling=TriggerClick). If the setup was never applied, or the project already had its own value (setup never overwrites one), the engine's older default applies, where buttons ignore the Enter key. Arrow keys still move focus. Gamepad and mouse work.

Fix: run Tools › XenoCore › Apply XenoCore Project Settings (see Install) and check the Output Log (LogXenoSetup) for a conflict on that line. Or set it yourself: Project Settings › Plugins › Common UI Framework, Button section, Common Button Accept Key Handling = Trigger Click.

Avoid it next time: Restyle the menus.

docs.title: Pad A on a focused button does nothing, but the mouse works
docs.text:
Fails silently

Keyboard tests pass, which hides it.

Why: a gamepad's A press on a CommonUI button becomes a simulated click at the centre of the focused widget. Anything hit-testable drawn over the button at that point, such as a text label or icon in an Overlay above it, takes the click instead.

Fix: set every text block and image layered over a button to Not Hit-Testable (Self & All Children).

Avoid it next time: Restyle the menus.

docs.title: A prompt glyph shows the wrong key
docs.text:
Why: most prompts come from rows in UserInterface/Foundation/DT_XenoCore_Actions, which name their keys directly. A few rows exist only so a widget can draw a glyph for an Enhanced Input action. If you rebind the input action and not its row, the prompt names a key that does nothing.

Fix: when you rebind an action, update its row in DT_XenoCore_Actions to the same keys.

Avoid it next time: Show an input action prompt.

docs.title: A button's prompt stays in the action bar when the button shouldn't be usable
docs.text:
Fails silently

The bar draws a live-looking prompt that does nothing when pressed.

Why: the bottom action bar draws a prompt for every bound action, and it never looks at the button that bound it. Set Is Enabled and collapsing the button do not remove its prompt.

Fix: to show and hide a contextual prompt, call Set Triggering Input Action on the button: pass the action's row to show it, and an empty row handle (Make DataTableRowHandle with nothing set) to remove it. The loadout screen's Unequip prompt works this way.

Avoid it next time: Show an input action prompt.

docs.title: Pressing Back on a popup closes the whole screen behind it
docs.text:
Why: a popup only receives Back if it is a back handler. Is Back Handler is off by default, so Back falls through to the screen underneath, which closes and takes the popup with it. It looks exactly like "No closed the popup".

Fix: tick Is Back Handler on the popup widget. After it closes, give focus back to the row the player was on, because nothing does it for you. XenoCore's W_XenoCore_ConfirmPopup does both.

Avoid it next time: Add a confirm popup.

docs.title: Pressing Back on a loot or choice panel loses what it offered
docs.text:
Why: a panel that must be answered cannot let Back simply close it. Turning Is Back Handler off is not enough: Back then goes to whatever else is listening, such as the screen underneath. XenoCore's loot panel takes Back and ignores it.

Fix: for your own mandatory panel, keep Is Back Handler ticked, then in the widget's My Blueprint panel override the function On Handle Back Action and make it return true (ticked) without doing anything else. Back is then taken by the panel and goes nowhere.

Avoid it next time: Add a menu screen.

docs.title: A screen works the first time and misbehaves when opened again
docs.text:
Why: CommonUI layers reuse screen widgets instead of creating new ones. Anything a screen sets once in Construct or its constructor, such as a "finished" flag, is still set the next time it opens.

Fix: reset per-visit state when the screen is shown (On Activated), not in Construct. Bind button clicks in Construct, though: binding in On Activated adds another handler every time the screen opens.

Avoid it next time: Add a menu screen.

docs.title: A screen doesn't update after something changes
docs.text:
Why: most screens redraw only when they are told to. Equipment and inventory changes are broadcast as XenoCore.Equipment.Message.SlotChanged and XenoCore.Inventory.Message.Changed, but a screen that listens to neither only changes when you call its refresh.

Fix: after your own action (an unequip, a purchase), call the screen's refresh yourself, or have the screen listen for the message. See Events.

Avoid it next time: Add a menu screen.

docs.title: A Delete or other screen action acts on the wrong row
docs.text:
Why: a row that reports itself only on On Hovered is never reported by keyboard or gamepad navigation, which moves focus without hovering. The screen then acts on whichever row the mouse last touched.

Fix: report the row from On Focus Received as well, and have destructive actions ask which row has focus at the moment of the press.

Avoid it next time: Add a menu screen.

docs.title: A list is missing its "none" or "empty" row
docs.text:
Fails silently

The list looks normal, with one row missing.

Why: Set List Items on a List View drops null entries. A null used to mean "nothing equipped" never reaches the list.

Fix: use a real object for the empty row, or show "nothing" outside the list. For unequipping, XenoCore uses a footer prompt instead of an empty list row.

Avoid it next time: Add a menu screen.

docs.title: A shipped menu entry disappeared after I added mine
docs.text:
Fails silently

The menu still looks complete, with one button changed or missing.

Why: menu entries are merged by Id. An entry in Menu Entries or in an Additional Menu Entry Sets asset that reuses a shipped Id (Equipment, Arts, Skills, Collectables, Party, QuestLog, ChangeTime, Save, Load, Tutorials, Settings, ReturnToTitle, QuitGame) replaces that entry where it stands.

Fix: give your entry its own Id. Reuse a shipped Id only when you mean to replace or hide that entry.

Avoid it next time: Add a menu screen.

docs.title: A menu entry shows but does nothing when pressed
docs.text:
Why: the entry has neither Action nor Screen, or the one it names did not load, or it is not the right class (a screen must be a Common Activatable Widget, an action a XenoCoreMenuAction). The Output Log says which (LogXenoMenu: "has neither an Action nor a Screen", "did not load as a ..."). In a packaged build, the usual cause is that the screen was not cooked; see Build and editor.

Fix: set Screen or Action to a class of the right type, and make sure it is cooked.

Avoid it next time: Add a menu screen.

docs.title: A widget above a character never appears, or disappears and never comes back
docs.text:
Fails silently

Nothing is logged.

Why: three causes:

  • A screen-space Widget Component that starts hidden may never get onto the screen; unhiding it later does not help.
  • Its widget class was set in Begin Play. Set it in the construction script so it is ready at registration.
  • The widget hides itself by setting Collapsed. A collapsed widget stops ticking, so it can never notice it should reappear.

Fix: start widget components visible and hide them with Render Opacity. HUD plates built on XenoCoreHudPlateBase already fade with opacity; use Set Shown on them rather than changing visibility.

Avoid it next time: Restyle the menus.

docs.title: A world widget is enormous, cropped or invisible
docs.text:
Why: with Draw at Desired Size on, the widget is as big as its own layout says, and a Size Box override on any parent in the widget decides that, even on a collapsed branch. With a fixed draw size smaller than the layout, the widget is cropped, often to nothing. An Image whose brush has no size has a desired size of zero, which is invisible on a desired-size component.

Fix: size the widget in the widget Blueprint, not on the component. Walk up from the element to the root and clear any Size Box overrides you did not mean. Give images a brush size, or wrap them in a sized Size Box.

Avoid it next time: Restyle the menus.

docs.title: A tutorial card never appears
docs.text:
Why: a card shows only the first time its trigger happens in a save, and only if the player's Tips switch is on (main menu › Tutorials). With tips off, cards are still recorded as seen, so turning tips back on does not replay them. A card also waits while any menu, conversation, loading screen or Change Time fade is up. A card whose row has no Triggers never shows by itself.

Fix: to test, run XenoCore.Tutorial.Reset to forget every seen card, or XenoCore.Tutorial.Show <RowName> to show one now. Check the row's Triggers in UserInterface/Tutorials/DT_XenoCore_Tutorials.

Avoid it next time: Tutorial cards.

docs.title: The dialogue box jumps around the screen during a conversation
docs.text:
Why: the dialogue box is anchored in the world, above the speaker's head. Stopping the character (Gameplay.MovementStopped) does not stop the camera, so looking around sweeps the box across the screen. XenoCore's dialogue locks the look input for the conversation.

Fix: if you build your own world-anchored conversation or cutscene UI, call Set Ignore Look Input on the player controller as well as stopping movement. It is a counter, not a switch: every true needs exactly one matching false, on every exit path, or the camera stays locked.

Avoid it next time: Write an NPC conversation.

docs.title: World and maps
docs.text:
All · 10 min · No code

Problems with maps, terrain, surfaces, pack content and the things you place in a level. For the model behind them, read Interaction, NPCs and dialogue and the map recipes, including Give a map its music.

docs.title: Footsteps sound like concrete on grass
docs.text:
Fails silently

The footstep system works; the ground simply never says it is grass.

Why: footstep sounds and effects are picked by the surface type under the foot, through Lyra's context effects (ContextEffects/CFX_XenoCore). A landscape with no physical material reports the default surface, and the default surface is mapped to concrete. Unless the landscape's material has a physical material output per layer, the landscape's only surface comes from its Default Phys Material.

Fix:

  1. Select the landscape in your map and set Default Phys Material to Environment/PM_XenoCore_Grass, or your own physical material.
